sources.authors: Koulakov and Chklovskii
sources.title: Orientation Preference Patterns in Mammalian Visual Cortex: A Wire Length Minimization Approach
sources.evidence_type: analytical and computational layout optimization
sources.read_scope: Results, model definition and Experimental Procedures; full primary PDF available
locators: pp. 519–521: prescribed orientation-dependent connection function and layout optimization
p. 525: uniform-function salt-and-pepper argument and model assumptions
sources.finding: Prescribes connection counts by orientation difference, then minimizes wiring length on a periodic square lattice. Changing that functional requirement yields different optimal maps. Uniform requirements favor salt-and-pepper organization in the stated idealization.
sources.application_inference: An anatomical map can be modeled as a consequence of functional wiring requirements and a material cost. This does not justify introducing physical proximity as our partner-selection rule.
transfer_limits: Orientation has a meaningful angular metric; embedding dimension labels do not.
The objective is anatomical wire length, not semantic recall or our fixed five-byte slot cost.
The calculation neither validates arbitrary interleaving for us nor proves this developmental mechanism in animals.

sources.authors: Raj and Chen
sources.title: The Wiring Economy Principle: Connectivity Determines Anatomy in the Human Brain
sources.evidence_type: human macroconnectome analysis and constrained optimization
sources.read_scope: Results, model and limitations; targeted methods
sources.finding: Human diffusion-MRI networks from 14 participants were compared with rewired networks and optimized node placements. Fixed connectivity plus constrained placement reproduced aspects of anatomy; cheaper rewiring could increase graph path length.
sources.application_inference: Supports investigating function-first versus anatomy-first explanations. Neither the title nor an optimization fit establishes causal development or a microcircuit locality requirement.
transfer_limits: Large brain regions, not neurons inside one CC.
Undirected tractography-derived weights and Euclidean cost are proxies.
Placement uses hemispheric, spherical-surface and noncoincidence constraints; it is not unconstrained emergence of anatomy.

sources.authors: Zenke, Agnes and Gerstner
sources.title: Diverse synaptic plasticity mechanisms orchestrated to form and retrieve memories in spiking neural networks
sources.evidence_type: spiking-network simulation and plasticity analysis
sources.read_scope: Assembly results, ablations, balanced-network methods, stimulation and inhibitory-plasticity methods
locators: Methods: Long-term plasticity of inhibitory synapses
Results: Blockage of individual plasticity mechanisms
sources.finding: Uses random sparse recurrent connectivity in 4096 excitatory and 1024 inhibitory neurons. Coordinated plasticity supports assembly formation and recall; removing heterosynaptic stabilization causes runaway activity. Some demonstrations use spatially structured input receptive fields, while supplementary cases use random input connectivity.
sources.application_inference: Recurrent anatomical distance is not required for the demonstrated assembly mechanism. This is not evidence that geometry never matters.
transfer_limits: Learned input receptive fields are not our fixed semantic roles.
Multiple plasticity processes, adaptation and a hypothetical population-level inhibitory signal are assumed.
The ablations do not show every omitted mechanism prevents all recall; inhibitory plasticity can be unnecessary during recall after tuning.
No application activity band or FP4 implementation follows.

sources.authors: Gallinaro and Rotter
sources.title: Associative properties of structural plasticity based on firing rate homeostasis in recurrent neuronal networks
sources.evidence_type: structural-plasticity simulation
sources.read_scope: Network, synapse creation/deletion and fixed-preference stimulation methods; association results and discussion
sources.finding: In a 12500-neuron E/I model, free synaptic elements pair randomly without a physical-distance rule. Firing-rate homeostasis changes their availability; shared stimulation creates lasting connectivity associations. A visual example assigns each neuron a fixed preferred orientation before learning. Synaptic efficacy and transmission delay are fixed.
sources.application_inference: A closer comparison to fixed response roles with learned connectivity than models that learn a replacement feature map. The associative effect emerges from network dynamics, not a prescribed geometric metric.
transfer_limits: Orientation inputs and per-neuron target firing rates differ from dense signed vectors and broad per-CC occupancy bounds.
Variable synaptic elements, multapses and rewiring are study mechanisms, not approved static-pool algorithms.
No evidence for our three regimes or for sufficient sustained autonomous recurrence.

sources.authors: Gallinaro, Gašparović and Rotter
sources.title: Homeostatic control of synaptic rewiring in recurrent networks induces the formation of stable memory engrams
sources.evidence_type: spiking simulations and mean-field structural-plasticity theory
sources.read_scope: Memory and silent-versus-persistent results; discussion and model methods; selected stability and oscillation sections inspected, not an independent mathematical reproduction
locators: Results: Engrams represent silent memories, not attractors
Discussion: persistent activity versus homeostatic deletion
Methods: Network model and Plasticity model
Results: stability and oscillatory dynamics (XML sec007, sec008)
sources.finding: Random pairing of homeostatically regulated synaptic elements produces associations and partial-cue recall in a 12500-neuron E/I model. The learned memories are normally silent; pattern completion depends on stimulation. Persistent overactivity can trigger deletion and pathological oscillatory behavior.
sources.application_inference: Assembly formation, pattern completion and self-sustaining semantic recurrence are different acceptance properties. A successful nonspatial memory model is not automatically a solution for immersion or DMN.
transfer_limits: Fixed synaptic weights, per-neuron set points, explicit element counts and uniform delays differ from our open learning contract.

Near-fixed-point linear stability does not ensure global stability; calcium and structural-growth timescales, strong drive and within-ensemble recurrence matter. Numerical boundaries are model-specific.
The authors’ broader claims about exclusive mechanisms for persistent activity require independent comparison.

sources.authors: Miller, Miehl and Doiron
sources.title: Homeostatic Plasticity Enables Stable yet Tunable Neuronal Assemblies
sources.publication_status: PRX Life accepted 2026-10-06; inspected full text is the PMC-hosted preprint, not an asserted version of record

Methods: Hawkes process network model and Linear-response propagator
sources.finding: Compatible excitatory and inhibitory plasticity targets permit a continuum of weight configurations with the same mean rates but different gains and response times. Correlated inputs can cause weight drift. The studied Hawkes network includes all-to-all population coupling and autapses.
sources.application_inference: Mean activity control does not uniquely determine recurrence or response dynamics. This is relevant to distinguishing the requested broad activity envelope from semantic behavior.
transfer_limits: Dense linear point-process assumptions do not establish behavior of sparse FP4 cells.
Per-neuron firing-rate targets are not the same as a broad per-CC active fraction.
Preprint details may differ from the accepted or eventual published version.

sources.authors: Vargas-Barroso et al.
sources.title: Developmental emergence of sparse and structured synaptic connectivity in the hippocampal CA3 memory circuit
sources.evidence_type: mouse CA3 paired physiology plus associative-memory simulation
sources.read_scope: Main results, Figure 7, simulation methods and slice limitations; supplement and code pending
locators: Results: distance dependence across developmental groups
Figure 7d and Methods: circular arrangement with fixed mean connectivity
sources.finding: Mouse slice measurements become less distance-dependent over development in the sampled range. In a 100000-cell binary memory model, broader connectivity improves recall capacity at fixed mean connection probability 3%. The ring models compare exponential ranges with uniform connectivity.
sources.application_inference: A direct counterexample to treating stronger locality as universally better for memory; the computational result isolates mean edge count more carefully than an unmatched comparison.
transfer_limits: Hippocampal CA3 is not human neocortical CC.
Sampled transverse slices do not establish absence of long-range distance effects.
Sparse random binary patterns, clipped weights, global inhibition and roughly 3000 inputs/cell differ substantially from our representation and capacity.
Developmental observation does not by itself prove experience caused the change.

sources.authors: Nolte, Gal and Markram
sources.title: Impact of higher order network structure on emergent cortical activity
sources.evidence_type: detailed reconstructed neocortical microcircuit simulations and controlled rewiring
sources.read_scope: Rewiring construction, spontaneous/evoked results, cloud and NMC* control methods; supporting analyses pending
locators: Results: Reducing Higher Order Network Structure
sources.finding: A 31346-neuron morphology-based model was compared with a cloud-overlap rewiring model. Similar distance profiles and cell-type connection totals did not preserve evoked-response reliability. Controls addressed small connection losses and shuffled delays. Individual degree distributions and higher-order topology also changed.
sources.application_inference: A fitted distance profile is insufficient to specify computational behavior, even within an anatomically detailed model.
transfer_limits: This is a simulated microcircuit, not a causal in-vivo rewiring experiment.
It does not isolate a single motif independently of degree heterogeneity.
Only excitatory rewiring was instantiated; inhibitory connectivity remained fixed.
Neither shared neighbors nor a contact graph is thereby selected for our application.

sources.authors: Chen, Maex, Adams, Steuber, Calcraft and Davey
sources.title: Clustering Predicts Memory Performance in Networks of Spiking and Non-Spiking Neurons
sources.evidence_type: controlled network simulations
sources.read_scope: Connectivity, learning and retrieval methods; clustering and spiking results; discussion limitations
locators: Methods: network connectivity, neuron models, learning and performance
Discussion: wiring cost and biological limitations
sources.finding: At fixed neuron count and incoming degree, strongly clustered wiring generally impaired completion of random uncorrelated patterns. Gaussian locality became attractive when physical wire cost entered the objective. Fixed-delay and artificial distance-delay spiking comparisons showed similar tendencies.
sources.application_inference: A locality benefit depends on the task and cost function. Graph triangle clustering is distinct from learned weighted assemblies, so this counterexample does not rule out useful recurrent semantic groups.
transfer_limits: Perceptron training, not the proposed coactivity learning; spiking weights are transferred from threshold-network training.
Incoming degree is fixed, but outgoing degrees and all higher-order properties are not separately matched.
Random stationary patterns, absent Dale-separated populations and an imposed retrieval criterion differ from autonomous semantic sequences.
The paper does not prove clustering universally determines computational performance.

sources.authors: Kaiser and Hilgetag
sources.title: Nonoptimal Component Placement, but Short Processing Paths, due to Long-Distance Projections in Neural Systems
sources.evidence_type: anatomical network analysis and graph optimization
sources.read_scope: Rearrangement and rewiring results; methods for minimal wiring and path metrics; discussion
locators: Results: component placement and minimally rewired networks
sources.finding: Macaque-area and C. elegans networks can reduce modeled wiring cost by rearrangement. At fixed node and total-edge counts, replacing connections with a short-wire connected graph increases graph-hop distances.
sources.application_inference: Physical wiring minimization can trade against topological reach. It is not a sufficient objective from which to infer the application learning rule.
transfer_limits: The rewired control uses a minimum spanning tree plus shortest remaining edges; it does not preserve each neuron’s degree.
Graph-hop distance is a proxy, not measured signal latency or task performance.
Mixed species and anatomical scales do not establish a within-CC cortical law.

sources.authors: Kim, Song, Jang and Paik
sources.title: Spontaneous Retinal Waves Can Generate Long-Range Horizontal Connectivity in Visual Cortex
sources.evidence_type: developmental computational model
sources.read_scope: Retinal and cortical model, feedforward and horizontal learning methods; salt-and-pepper and shuffled-activity results
locators: Methods: feedforward and horizontal connection development
sources.finding: After feedforward development, fixed feedforward weights and wave-driven covariance learning produce feature-specific horizontal connections, including in a salt-and-pepper orientation arrangement. Shuffling the driving activity removes that specificity.
sources.application_inference: Role-preserving recurrent learning can exploit structured coactivity without requiring a smooth map of the represented feature.
transfer_limits: Retinal geometry, retinotopy and sampling locations remain explicit: salt-and-pepper organization is not absence of geometry.
The feedforward representation is learned before it is frozen; the complete model does not begin with our fixed semantic basis.
Clustering and spontaneous-dynamics analyses were not performed for the salt-and-pepper variant.
Structured retinal waves cannot be equated to independent white-noise drive.

sources.authors: Ko and colleagues
sources.title: The emergence of functional microcircuits in visual cortex
sources.publication_status: published, Nature; archived author manuscript inspected
sources.evidence_type: mouse V1 development, functional imaging, paired recording and modeling
sources.read_scope: Experimental results, recording methods, AdEx neuron, voltage-based plasticity and both network simulation variants inspected
locators: Results: connectivity and visual-response similarity across age
sources.finding: Receptive-field organization is largely present at eye opening, while preferential connectivity among similarly responding nearby neurons strengthens later. Sampled pairs are within 50 micrometres, with similar mean separation in the compared age groups.
sources.application_inference: Existing response roles and later recurrent organization are experimentally distinguishable. Physical closeness alone does not describe which sampled cells become selectively connected.
transfer_limits: Narrow, age-matched distance sampling does not remove every anatomical or developmental confound.
The experiment does not identify a unique causal plasticity rule.
Computational variants also change feedforward weights and therefore are not literal fixed-semantic-role implementations.

sources.authors: Peng and colleagues
sources.title: Directed and acyclic synaptic connectivity in the human layer 2-3 cortical microcircuit
sources.evidence_type: human surgical tissue recordings, graph null models and reservoir simulations
sources.read_scope: Six-page main article; Figs. 2–3 visually checked; repository README and selected spatial-null, network-generation, reservoir and task code inspected; supplementary PDF pending
sources.finding: Human temporal L2–3 recordings show lower connectivity with lateral separation but greater probability toward deeper cells. Heterogeneous sampling-group connectivity explains common-neighbor enrichment; a spatial null explains some directed motifs, while short cycles remain underrepresented. Reservoir comparisons rescale weights to a common stability boundary.
sources.application_inference: An isotropic proximity rule or a common-neighbor rule is not a universal consequence of these anatomical data. Directionality and recurrence must be distinguished from distance.
transfer_limits: Main cohort: 23 temporal-lobe-epilepsy patients; tumor tissue gives partial corroboration, not healthy whole-cortex coverage.
Groups contain at most ten simultaneously recorded cells; missing short local cycles does not exclude larger or interregional loops.
Effective tanh reservoirs use stability normalization and trained classification readouts; no literal SNN learning or autonomous-recurrence validation. See AUD-001 for released-code limits.
Anatomical depth has no given counterpart in our semantic layout.

sources.authors: Watson and colleagues
sources.title: Human hippocampal CA3 uses specific functional connectivity rules for efficient associative memory
sources.evidence_type: human and rodent circuit recordings, anatomical estimates and analytic associative-memory model
sources.read_scope: Connectivity and modeling results; STAR Methods distance sampling, anatomical caveats and model assumptions; Fig. S3 visually checked; equations inspected but not independently reproduced
locators: STAR Methods: Morphological analysis, Caveats of anatomical connectivity predictions, Mathematical modeling of CA3 function
sources.finding: Human CA3 recordings identify sparse recurrent connectivity and no detected distance trend in the sampled connected groups. A theoretical fixed-total-synapse comparison favors more neurons with lower connection probability for random-pattern storage.
sources.application_inference: Circuit-specific evidence challenges a universal local-distance law. Its memory advantage cannot be directly imported into our fixed-neuron-count, bounded-slot CC.
transfer_limits: Only ten connected human CA3 pairs; distance analysis includes recording groups containing connections. Absence of detection is not proof of spatial independence.
Surgical tissue, slice truncation and anatomical input estimates limit generalization.
Binary neurons, random patterns, clipped Hebbian learning, global inhibition and iterative cue recall differ from the three requested regimes.
The capacity comparison varies neuron count and degree; it does not isolate locality at fixed architecture.

sources.authors: Ko, Mrsic-Flogel and Hofer
sources.title: Emergence of Feature-Specific Connectivity in Cortical Microcircuits in the Absence of Visual Experience
sources.evidence_type: mouse dark-rearing intervention, functional imaging and paired recording
sources.read_scope: Full main-text methods, results, figure captions and discussion via PMC web text; XML endpoint unavailable
locators: Discussion: patterned endogenous drive and causal ambiguity
sources.finding: Dark rearing preserves substantial development of feature-selective recurrent connectivity, but natural-movie selectivity and pruning of nonresponsive cells differ from normally reared controls. The distance-restricted paired samples have similar separation across groups.
sources.application_inference: Pre-existing input roles can guide recurrent refinement without external task stimulation. This does not mean unstructured white noise alone supplies semantic learning structure.
transfer_limits: Endogenous patterned input and shared feedforward drive are proposed explanations, not directly isolated mechanisms.
Higher coactivity can influence connectivity or result from it; the authors acknowledge this ambiguity.
Mouse V1 development, a narrow sampling radius and partly maturing response properties differ from fixed LLM coordinate roles.

sources.authors: Watson, Vargas-Barroso and Jonas
sources.title: Cell-specific wiring routes information flow through hippocampal CA3
sources.evidence_type: mouse slice physiology, morphology and cell-subclass analysis
sources.read_scope: Published connectivity results, discussion, study limitations and classification/distance methods; no full supplement audit
sources.finding: Superficial and deep CA3 pyramidal subclasses show asymmetric local connectivity, with very few deep-to-superficial connections. A depth bias can largely reflect this subclass structure even when overall soma separation shows no detected relationship.
sources.application_inference: A spatial coordinate can be a proxy for cell identity and routing. Importing a geometric bias without those roles may fail to preserve its biological meaning.
transfer_limits: Primarily young mouse mid-to-ventral CA3; targeted sampling is not an unbiased subclass census.
Local slices miss long-range connections and underestimate connectivity; room-temperature physiology differs from in vivo conditions.
Subclass-specific inhibition is inferred from correlated input, not a complete inhibitory connectome.
These subclasses have no established equivalence to our positive/negative semantic populations.

sources.authors: Dahmen, Recanatesi and colleagues
sources.title: Strong and localized recurrence controls the dimensionality of neural activity across brain areas
sources.evidence_type: mouse population recordings, linear-response theory, spiking simulations and mouse/human synaptic-data analysis
sources.read_scope: Primary results/methods, published29-page PDF and32-page supplement; targeted SI covariance/input controls, motif derivation, multi-population approximation and layer/cell-type comparisons. Figure3 visually inspected; eight released source files audited.
locators: Results: local tuning of recurrency and synaptic motifs
Methods: Network models and linear response theory
Methods: Numerical validation of motifs theory
Methods: Extraction of connection probabilities and motif statistics
sources.finding: Effective coupling and two-edge motif statistics influence modeled covariance dimensionality. Excitatory/inhibitory gain changes can alter the contribution of the same structural motifs. The human evidence concerns sampled synapses, while state-dependent population dynamics are measured primarily in mice.
sources.application_inference: Local graph structure can affect computation without supplying a physical-distance variable. Structural recurrence, effective gain, activity fraction and covariance dimensionality must remain distinct.
transfer_limits: Theory linearizes stationary asynchronous states and uses large-network approximations; reciprocal motifs give only qualitative dimensionality agreement in one validation.
Human synaptic data reuse the Allen/Campagnola dataset, not an independent replication of that anatomy.
The motif null pools connection statistics by cell category; sampling-group heterogeneity needs comparison with LOC-013 before interpreting differences.
No application plasticity rule, semantic map or broad activity controller is established.
supplement_findings: The dimensionality relation concerns stationary linear-response covariance, with controlled spiking-model comparisons. The scalar R is implemented as the largest real part of connectivity eigenvalues in the motif simulation.
The Gaussian motif construction couples chain, convergence, divergence and reciprocal parameters; they cannot all be varied independently while preserving a valid covariance ensemble.

The multi-population motif expression uses an explicit approximation averaging population-specific terms. The overall strength term and motif term can predict opposite layer trends; cell-type comparisons are also conditional on assumed efficacy and population ratios.

Low-rank factor subtraction is a sensitivity analysis for shared external input. Its validation uses specified random external drives; it does not generally identify the origin of all low-rank activity.

The motif analyses condition on probed edges and pool statistics across recordings. Selected code allows postsynaptic-type probabilities for reciprocal/chain nulls, but its random-baseline generator replaces each experiment by eight fully probed cells.

sources.authors: Pyle and Rosenbaum
sources.title: Spatiotemporal Dynamics and Reliable Computations in Recurrent Spiking Neural Networks
sources.publication_status: published, Physical Review Letters; author-hosted combined article and supplement inspected
sources.evidence_type: spatial spiking-network simulations and stability theory

locators: Main Figs. 1–3: spatial modes and readout grouping
Main Fig. 4: input heterogeneity and readout training
sources.finding: Changing relative excitatory/inhibitory projection widths creates temporal spatial modes. Reliable trained outputs additionally require heterogeneous input; global random readouts average away much of the mode structure. Similar population-average dynamics coexist with different local dynamics.
sources.application_inference: This is a positive locality example with explicit input, neuron-dynamics and readout dependencies. It does not show that adding a distance kernel alone benefits our semantic CC.
transfer_limits: A 50000-cell E/I torus, anatomical readout patches and trained linear readouts differ from assigned semantic populations.
The instability depends on spiking-neuron resonance that a simpler rate equation misses; FP4 state dynamics are not yet specified.
Recurrent weights are not learned by the proposed coactivity scheme, and driven output reproduction is not autonomous semantic recurrence.
Supplementary delayed-output recall improves after adding adaptation; spatially heterogeneous input alone performs poorly after the driving signal ends.

The nonspatial comparison changes recurrent organization and input organization together. The readout is a separately trained100-group linear RLS mapping with no output feedback, frozen after50trials. It is not a controlled test of geometry alone or a demonstrated autonomous semantic loop.

sources.authors: Rosenbaum, Smith, Kohn, Rubin and Doiron
sources.title: The spatial structure of correlated neuronal variability
sources.publication_status: published, Nature Neuroscience; online 2016-10-31, issue January 2017
sources.evidence_type: balanced-network theory and simulations with macaque V1 recording analysis
sources.read_scope: Main input-heterogeneity and spatial-width results, network methods, supplementary tuning-similarity analysis and connectivity generation; complete supplement derivation not independently reproduced
locators: Main Fig. 1: two shared-input groups without rewiring
Online Methods: dense EIF networks and contact sampling
sources.finding: Changing shared-input group structure alters correlations without changing recurrent wiring. In spatial models, relative feedforward/recurrent widths determine whether correlations can cancel. The supplement explicitly treats its tuning-space comparison as inconclusive and fitted rather than predictive.
sources.application_inference: Assigned semantic inputs can matter before any geometry is introduced. Anatomical separation, functional tuning and correlations are not interchangeable definitions of distance.
transfer_limits: Dense networks, fixed outgoing contact counts, sampling with replacement and balanced weight scaling differ from our bounded sparse slots.
The spatial model assumes aligned input and cortical sheets; our semantic arrangement does not provide them.
A circular orientation metric and tuning fits do not establish a metric between LLM coordinate labels.
Near-zero mean correlation can conceal structured positive and negative correlations; it does not establish unstructured dynamics.

sources.authors: Fiete, Senn, Wang and Hahnloser
sources.title: Spike-Time-Dependent Plasticity and Heterosynaptic Competition Organize Networks to Produce Long Scale-Free Sequences of Neural Activity
sources.evidence_type: binary and conductance-based sequence-formation models with indirect songbird comparison
sources.read_scope: Main pp. 564–570, 573–575; Fig. 5 visually checked; supplement and full weight-growth variant pending
locators: Summed-weight limit rule; Experimental Procedures Eqs. 1–5
sources.finding: Uncorrelated drive plus timing-dependent plasticity and incoming/outgoing weight competition forms autonomous loops without geometry. Wider chains require shared inputs; excessive input-group overlap impairs formation.
sources.application_inference: This demonstrates a nonspatial route to recurrence, not a validated algorithm for distributed semantic patterns.
transfer_limits: Learning starts with all-to-all weak weights; illustrated networks are small. Sparse final connectivity does not establish sparse-start learnability.
Strong competition tends toward disjoint chains. Wide chains contain within-group recurrence; groups are not anatomical minicolumns.
The summed-weight variant uses global inhibition. Exact timing, weight competition and group allocation remain unchosen for our application.
The predicted chain-length distribution uses a random-permutation hypothesis; songbird stimulation provides indirect evidence.

sources.authors: Litwin-Kumar and Doiron
sources.title: Formation and maintenance of neuronal assemblies through synaptic plasticity
sources.evidence_type: spiking-network learning and reduced stochastic assembly model
sources.read_scope: Main assembly formation/persistence, discussion and Methods pp. 3–4, 9–11; Figs. 3–4 visually checked; supplement pending
locators: Discussion: fixed feedforward inputs and alternative homeostasis
Methods: stimulation protocols and non-recurrent control
sources.finding: With fixed feedforward inputs, learning produces overlapping assemblies whose spontaneous reactivation slows connectivity loss and repairs a small perturbation. Matching mean firing rates without recurrent excitation does not reproduce this maintenance.
sources.application_inference: Fixed input roles permit learned recurrent structure without a physical metric; this supports separating semantic assignment from learned coactivity.
transfer_limits: The 5,000-cell model uses 20% random connectivity, inhibitory plasticity and incoming-weight normalization. Those details are not our accepted design.
The non-recurrent control also changes external drive, inhibitory targets and weight bounds; matching rates is not matching every dynamical variable.
The result concerns trained assembly switching and persistence, not guaranteed semantic loops from white noise alone.
Homeostasis must be sufficiently fast relative to excitatory learning; biological timing and sparse-degree transfer remain open.

sources.authors: Rost, Deger and Nawrot

Binary-state occupancy differs from physiological spike rate; asynchronous updates introduce a specific noise process.
State switching relies on finite-size fluctuations and is not a demonstrated ordered semantic loop.
Typical E connectivity is 20%, inhibitory connectivity 50%; large sparse CC transfer is unverified. Biological justification for the exact inhibitory structure remains incomplete.

sources.title: Modeling somatic and dendritic spike mediated plasticity at the single neuron and network level

sources.authors: Cai, Kfir, Jamali, Huang, Kim, Cash and Williams
sources.title: Mapping the neuronal building blocks of human language with language models
sources.evidence_type: human single-unit and local-field recordings during speech production
sources.read_scope: Sec2, Sec6–7, recording/isolation and site-comparison methods, syntactic/static/contextual embedding construction, ridge prediction, random-token and sentence-swap controls, temporal mapping methods. Published figure 5 visually inspected. Full raw-data and fitting-code reproduction not performed. Released2026 analysis source and Figure5 ordering inspected in AUD-086.
locators: Sec7 and Fig. 5: site-aligned AP/LFP selectivity
Sec11–13: eight patients, arrays, separate session sorting
Sec19 and Sec24: comparisons and embedding construction
sources.finding: Linguistic selectivity is distributed across sampled frontotemporal regions, while modulation differs by region and hemisphere. Single-unit and local-field selectivity at the same recording contact often differ.
sources.application_inference: A local population signal does not directly identify the semantic role of every constituent cell. This does not prescribe a coordinate layout.
transfer_limits: Eight epilepsy patients, 14 sessions, 579 sorted units; repeated sessions were sorted separately. Reported channel observations are not all unique physical sites.
Arrays have 400-micrometre spacing over about 4×4 mm; electrode dimensions do not establish neuron-to-neuron spatial resolution.
The study does not identify a complete CC, reconstruct its synapses or estimate a semantic-distance wiring rule.
Production, contextual embeddings and syntactic features differ from our static input-table representation.

Contextual prediction uses Vicuna-7B v1.1 and other model controls, PCA to 30 components per layer, ridge regression with alpha=0.01, and sentence-held-out predictions. This is a fitted mapping from contextual representations, not a one-coordinate-to-one-neuron identification.

The population predictivity is defined from the mean firing rate across sampled neurons in a session; individual-neuron predictivity is a separate reported quantity. These summaries must not be equated with reconstructing every neuronal population pattern.

Figure 5 sorts single-unit modulation scores and applies the same ordering to matched local-field recordings. Its horizontal contact order is not anatomical order. Differences between sorted-unit and local-field selectivity neither identify a physical semantic-axis map nor demonstrate absence of spatial organization.

Released default code loads precomputed PCs; its fallback fits PCA across session embeddings before sentence-held-out regression. Provenance of supplied PCs and quantitative evaluation effects remain unverified; no general invalidation follows.

sources.title: Semantic encoding during language comprehension at single-cell resolution

This is targeted methods review, not an independent raw-data reanalysis. Recording/isolation, context results and discussion deepened; public analysis source inspected in AUD-085.

transfer_limits: The displayed low-dimensional maps are projections of fitted representations, not tissue maps.
A regression coefficient for each input dimension is not evidence that biological neurons instantiate one dimension each.

The hierarchical analysis concerns distances between word projections and responses; its semantically selective subgroup contains 19 neurons.
