sources.evidence_type: fly central-complex electron-microscopy reconstruction and connectivity-based calculations
sources.read_scope: Full-text sections 2.6.1, 2.7.1 paragraphs 0–4, 3.2, 3.3.4 and 4.5; broader connectome and complete simulations not audited.
locators: Delta7 input profiles and sinusoidal transformation
sources.finding: Several cell types form direct and indirect recurrent loops supporting the heading system. Anatomical mappings duplicate and shift represented angles across compartments; Delta7 pathways add a different transformation rather than a single distance-decay rule.
sources.application_inference: Anatomical adjacency, functional adjacency and effective interactions need not coincide even in an explicit biological ring. The computational relation is carried by identified pathways, not a universal soma-distance metric.
transfer_limits: Many proposed functions remain hypotheses. Synaptic counts and target-normalized relative weights approximate functional strength; they are not measured conductances.
Analyses discard edges with fewer than three synapses; the connectome omits gap junctions, glial networks and some modulatory effects.
Sinusoidal propagation calculations assume linearity and weight proportionality to counts, ignoring Delta7 recurrence.
This specialized navigation circuit supplies no arrangement for a general semantic-vector CC.

retrieval.title: A connectome of the Drosophila central complex reveals network motifs suitable for flexible navigation and context-dependent action selection

sources.authors: Davis and colleagues
sources.title: Spontaneous travelling cortical waves gate perception in behaving primates
sources.evidence_type: marmoset visual-cortex LFP/spiking recordings and detection behavior
sources.read_scope: Published author-hosted PDF: selected p. 3, p. 4, data inclusion/task methods p. 7 and conditional-probability methods p. 8.
sources.finding: Pre-target wave phase predicts evoked responses and detection probability; whole-array wave information is more predictive than a single-electrode phase in the reported analyses.
sources.application_inference: Measured propagation and sensory-gain association motivate studying coordinated excitability; they do not supply a physical metric for semantic roles.
transfer_limits: Two animals and a visual task with retinotopic targets; this is not a language CC or a causal manipulation of wave phase.
Selected responsive units and wave-defined trial subsets; no independent reanalysis of time-of-peak selection or prediction performance was performed.
Speed compatible with horizontal axons is suggestive of a pathway, not a direct measurement proving the generating circuit.

sources.authors: Davis, Benigno, Fletterman and colleagues
sources.title: Spontaneous traveling waves naturally emerge from horizontal fiber time delays and travel through locally asynchronous-irregular states
sources.evidence_type: conductance-based spiking-network comparisons and relation to cortical recordings
sources.read_scope: Full-text sections 4–5, 7, 9 paragraphs 0–2, 10 and 17–19.
sources.finding: Within the tested model family, local connectivity supports spatial organization and distance-linked delays support propagation. Individual firing-rate distributions can remain similar while large-scale activity organization differs.
sources.application_inference: A biologically grounded locality benefit here involves coordinated timing and excitability, rather than lower firing rates alone. Transfer requires specifying a meaningful relation between our assigned roles and these dynamics.
transfer_limits: Main network exceeds one million cells with 3000 contacts per cell; this is much denser per neuron than our allocated mean-slot budget.
Detailed conductance, E/I and delay assumptions are not the specified FP4/FP8 representation.
The study compares local/no-delay and random/delay variants, but does not establish universal necessity of spatial geometry or an exact degree/weight/delay-structure-matched alternative.
Analysed simulations last 1 s after a 200 ms transient; initialization derives from a 10 s run. These observations do not establish indefinite stable semantic recurrence.
Sparse-wave state refers weak participation in coordinated fluctuations; different sparsity definitions must not be conflated.

AUD-005 identifies a spatial-pitch calibration issue in one public cropped-array analysis path; exact published-figure provenance is unresolved. Qualitative wave propagation remains distinct from numerical speed calibration.

retrieval.title: Spontaneous traveling waves naturally emerge from horizontal fiber time delays and travel through locally asynchronous-irregular states

sources.authors: Davis, Busch, Steward, Muller and colleagues
sources.title: Horizontal cortical connections shape intrinsic traveling waves into feature-selective motifs that regulate perceptual sensitivity
sources.evidence_type: fixed-tuning spiking-network model and observational primate physiology
sources.read_scope: Full-text sections S3–S4, S12 and S21; v0.2 connection/tuning construction and example parameters inspected in AUD-004. Complete motif-analysis pipeline remains unaudited.
sources.finding: With assigned tuning, adding patchy like-tuned long-range connections to a local network yields more differentiated, feature-selective wave motifs than the random long-range comparison. Cortical motif states correlate with perceptual sensitivity.
sources.application_inference: A fixed assignment of response roles can coexist with structured recurrent motifs; learning the input roles is not necessary in this comparison. The result does not establish that a physical map is required for our semantic assignments.
transfer_limits: Model assumes a repeated motion-direction pinwheel map, 450000 cells, 1000 outgoing contacts, conductance dynamics and distance-linked delays. Circular motion tuning is not proximity among arbitrary embedding axes.

The local and feature maps use90/10 coefficients before sampling, not a guaranteed90/10 contact split. This comparison changes functional wiring and associated delays; it does not isolate geometry from all structural alternatives.
No wave/motif manipulation was performed in the primates; the authors explicitly limit causal behavioral inference.
Simulation analysis covers 1 s after transient; no actual coactivity learning or long-duration semantic regime is established.

retrieval.title: Horizontal cortical connections shape intrinsic traveling waves into feature-selective motifs that regulate perceptual sensitivity

sources.authors: Misawa and colleagues
sources.title: Awake cortex stabilizes traveling waves for global and reliable information routing
sources.evidence_type: rat ECoG state comparison and simulated propagation/common-input controls
sources.finding: Similar delayed evoked waveforms can be generated with or without a direct link in the illustrative model. Recorded wave directions align with directional statistical dependence, with state-dependent differences.
sources.application_inference: Wave appearance alone does not demonstrate inter-neuron transmission. Shared input from a token can also induce temporal relationships, so causal propagation and coactivity learning need separate interpretations.
transfer_limits: Ten male rats, awake versus isoflurane contrast and ECoG electrode populations; no single-cell semantic topology.
Pairwise transfer entropy is a predictive-dependence measure and can be confounded by unobserved common inputs; the authors explicitly acknowledge this.
The estimator uses single-lag approximations, parametric entropy and trial ensembles; no independent data reproduction was performed.
Hypothesized cellular mechanisms remain proposals, and anesthesia contrast is not evidence for the model’s three cognitive regimes.

retrieval.title: Awake cortex stabilizes traveling waves for global and reliable information routing

sources.authors: Benigno and colleagues
sources.title: Waves traveling over a map of visual space can ignite short-term predictions of sensory input
sources.evidence_type: complex-valued recurrent reservoir with supervised readout and video forecasting
sources.read_scope: Full-text sections 8–10 and 14, section 4 selected main results and section 6 paragraphs 0–3.
sources.finding: A spatially mapped recurrent reservoir can generate closed-loop forecasts after learning linear readouts of individual movies. Best recurrent length in the moving-bump example matches the input’s spatial scale.
sources.application_inference: This is a concrete computational benefit when the input already has spatial correlations. Our semantic dimension labels provide no corresponding image-plane neighborhood.
transfer_limits: All N-squared recurrent weights are positive, symmetric and include self-connections; dynamics are complex-valued and modulus-normalized, with distance-linked delays.
Readout regression and parameter search are not local spiking Hebbian learning; exact selection/evaluation independence was not audited.
Forecasting is tested on learned individual movies and selected multi-movie combinations, not arbitrary semantic streams or indefinite cyclic stability.
The authors leave general applicability of spatial topography to other recurrent networks open.

retrieval.title: Waves traveling over a map of visual space can ignite short-term predictions of sensory input

sources.authors: Gonzales and colleagues
sources.title: Touch-evoked traveling waves establish a translaminar spacetime code
sources.evidence_type: mouse surface/depth recordings, calcium imaging, feedback perturbations and spiking model
sources.read_scope: Full-text sections on L2/3 sparsity, recurrent model, motor feedback/L5 calcium spikes and traveling-wave simulations.
sources.finding: Late sensory waves depend on motor-cortical feedback and are linked to layer-5 dendritic calcium activity. Strong late waves accompany fewer but stronger inferred functional edges in small layer-2/3 ensembles.
sources.application_inference: A large field-potential wave need not mean broadly elevated somatic spiking. Dendritic, feedback and population measurements cannot be collapsed into one activity-fraction or connection-count variable.
transfer_limits: Functional edges inferred from calcium relationships are not reconstructed synapses or evidence for rapid anatomical rewiring; ensemble size did not significantly differ between the compared conditions.
Causal perturbations affect feedback and dendritic excitability; they do not uniquely establish the detailed proposed recurrent mechanism.
The illustrative model uses up to 450000 neurons and 1000 contacts per cell with conductance dynamics and delays, exceeding our mean slot budget.
No semantic vector representation, plasticity learning or autonomous immersion cycle is tested.

retrieval.title: Touch-evoked traveling waves establish a translaminar spacetime code

sources.authors: Branco, Clark and Häusser
sources.title: Dendritic Discrimination of Temporal Input Sequences in Cortical Neurons
sources.evidence_type: cortical slice glutamate-uncaging experiments and compartmental modeling
sources.read_scope: Main paper pp.1671–1675; supplementary methods not retrieved.
sources.finding: Permuting the activation order of the same synapses changes somatic responses. NMDA receptor blockade strongly reduces this discrimination; impedance gradients and nonlinear conductances explain it in the model.
sources.application_inference: Receiver-side temporal integration can distinguish sequences without defining proximity among the presynaptic neurons or semantic dimensions.
transfer_limits: Experiments manipulate dendritic synaptic sites, not a cortical layout or recurrent learning rule.
Patterns distributed across several dendrites were also discriminable; a single contiguous input cluster is not a universal requirement.
Detailed conductances and compartmental state are not supplied by the current FP4 state/FP8 edge proposal.
No autonomous semantic recurrence or resource-matched point-neuron comparison is established.

sources.authors: Harvey and Svoboda
sources.title: Locally dynamic synaptic learning rules in pyramidal neuron dendrites
sources.evidence_type: hippocampal slice single-spine plasticity perturbations
sources.read_scope: Main pp.1195–1200, preparation/electrophysiology methods; visual inspection of Figs.5–6.
sources.finding: Potentiation at one spine temporarily lowers the induction threshold at nearby stimulated spines. Nearby unstimulated spines remain unchanged. Spines physically close on different branches did not show the same crosstalk.
sources.application_inference: The relevant locality is intracellular path/branch proximity, not Euclidean proximity alone and not a metric between source neurons.
transfer_limits: Young mouse CA1 slices (postnatal days14–18), with uncaging, depolarization or reduced extracellular magnesium; not adult cortical semantic learning.
The approximately10-minute/10-micrometre effect is a measured plasticity interaction, not a prescribed partner-selection radius.
Strong-before-weak ordering mattered; the study distinguishes this effect from synaptic tagging and indiscriminate spreading potentiation.
No dendritic representation or extra metadata is adopted for the application.

sources.authors: Wright, Hedrick and Komiyama
sources.title: Distinct synaptic plasticity rules operate across dendritic compartments in vivo during learning
sources.evidence_type: longitudinal mouse motor-cortex imaging and somatic-output suppression
sources.read_scope: PMC author-manuscript main results/discussion and figure captions; supplementary methods PDF returned a download challenge and was not read.
sources.finding: During early motor learning, local synaptic coactivity predicts apical spine enlargement, whereas input coincident with somatic activity predicts basal enlargement. Soma-targeted Kir2.1 suppresses basal potentiation while apical plasticity persists.
sources.application_inference: A single whole-neuron coactivity rule is not an exhaustive biological account. Receiver compartments distinguish forms of locality without assigning distances to semantic axes.
transfer_limits: Spine area and calcium/glutamate indicators are measurement proxies; the imaging could not resolve small spike-timing differences.
Somatic suppression is a causal intervention; the precise molecular cause of apical clustering remains unresolved.
Kir2.1 also changes spine size, density or event rates, so it is not an otherwise identical replay of normal learning.
This is motor learning, not autonomous semantic-state cycling; supplementary analysis details remain unaudited.

retrieval.supplement_access: Public PDF route returned non-PDF download challenge

sources.authors: Hawkins and Ahmad
sources.title: Why Neurons Have Thousands of Synapses, a Theory of Sequence Memory in Neocortex
sources.evidence_type: HTM theoretical model, sparse-pattern calculations and sequence simulations
sources.read_scope: Main pp.2–6 and11–12, simulation parameter passages and replay-related text search.
sources.finding: Minicolumns share feedforward identity while constituent cells distinguish learned temporal contexts. Dendritic segments recognize sparse contextual patterns; predicted cells activate when their column receives winning feedforward input.
sources.application_inference: The source separates semantic/input identity, context, and prediction. Its displayed update equations alone do not produce input-free recurrent activation.
transfer_limits: This is a proposed theory with simulations, not experimental verification that every CC implements it.
Illustrative network:2048 columns,32 cells/column,40 active input columns, up to128 segments/cell and40 contacts/segment; these are not our resource or encoding assumptions.
Permanence controls binary connectivity and differs from the proposed FP8 weight semantics.

Potential partners are randomly selected across cells in the mathematical initialization; software creates segments and samples currently active cells. Neither establishes a physical metric for our semantic arrangement.

sources.authors: Hawkins, Ahmad and Cui
sources.title: A Theory of How Columns in the Neocortex Enable Learning the Structure of the World
sources.evidence_type: HTM sensorimotor column theory and object-recognition simulations
sources.read_scope: Model-description passages, discussion of location signals, and methods pp.14–16.
sources.finding: Columns combine sensory features with externally supplied object-relative location codes and cooperate through lateral support to identify objects. Learned output representations pool over feature/location combinations.
sources.application_inference: A location represented by neural activity is not a physical location of the neurons carrying that representation.
transfer_limits: The paper explicitly treats cortical grid-like location computation as a hypothesis without direct empirical evidence at publication.
Methods encode locations as random10-of-2400 binary vectors; these recognition experiments do not establish a cortical embedding metric.
Output identities are selected during object learning, and activity retains feedforward gating; this is not our fixed semantic-coordinate recurrence.
Column-specific input/output layers, segment rules, permanence and object-boundary resets are substantial assumptions, not inherited authorization.

sources.authors: Giannakakis, Vinogradov, Buendía, Levina and Gjorgjieva
sources.title: Structural influences on synaptic plasticity: The role of presynaptic connectivity in the emergence of E/I co-tuning
sources.evidence_type: spiking-network simulations, reduced model and simulation-based parameter optimization
sources.read_scope: Results sections sec003 andsec005–007; network input and weight-normalization methods sec011/sec018.
sources.finding: Prescribed input-group connectivity can restore downstream E/I co-tuning lost under noisy unstructured recurrence. The beneficial E/I assembly strengths vary with connection sparsity.
sources.application_inference: Functional circuit organization can change the statistics available to learning without supplying a physical neuron metric.
transfer_limits: The1000-cell input population has predefined groups with shared Poisson drive; these groups are not automatically semantic dimensions or cortical minicolumns.
Assembly parameters are optimized for high within-group/low between-group correlations. This objective is supplied externally, not discovered by the local plasticity.
Triplet excitatory STDP, inhibitory plasticity and competitive normalization are combined; the result is not bare coactivity learning.
The plastic recurrent comparison uses p=0.25 and learned selectivity; no autonomous fixed-role semantic cycles or our large-network slot budget is demonstrated.

retrieval.title: Structural influences on synaptic plasticity: The role of presynaptic connectivity in the emergence of E/I co-tuning

sources.authors: Auer, Chen, Stubenrauch, Lindner and Kempter
sources.title: Population sparseness determines strength of Hebbian plasticity for maximal memory lifetime in associative networks
sources.evidence_type: binary heteroassociative-memory theory and simulations
sources.read_scope: Network model sec003 first7 blocks; input/output sparsity discussion sec011; plasticity meanings sec015; Hebbian/homeostatic transition derivation sec021.
sources.finding: The optimal probability of binary synaptic potentiation depends on input/output activation fractions and available connections. Excessively sparse input can fail to supply enough signal for retrieval.
sources.application_inference: An activity band, connection count and plasticity strength cannot be transferred independently from a sparse-memory model.
transfer_limits: Feedforward one-way associations of uncorrelated random binary patterns, each presented once; no temporal spiking dynamics or autonomous recurrence.
Morphological candidate edges are fixed, functional edges binary, and each output preserves its functional count through selective random silencing.
The stated fin<=c assumption is sufficient for its normalization probabilities; it is not a universal neural constraint.
Transition probability is a learning parameter, not FP8 weight scale or static pool capacity. The study does not select our phase fractions or a topology.

retrieval.title: Population sparseness determines strength of Hebbian plasticity for maximal memory lifetime in associative networks

sources.authors: Lynn, Holmes and Palmer
sources.title: Heavy-tailed neuronal connectivity arises from Hebbian self-organization
sources.evidence_type: connectome-strength analysis and self-organization models
sources.read_scope: Publisher abstract/correction and seven publication-linked source files inspected; full paper XML and preprint were unavailable. Detailed findings here are bounded to the public code in AUD-006.
sources.finding: The analyzed observable aggregates strength across contacts between each neuron pair. The models redistribute conserved total strength through random pruning and preferential or correlation-dependent growth.
sources.application_inference: A heavy tail in pairwise connection strength does not determine distinct-partner indegree or the number of slots a neuron requires.
transfer_limits: Mouse-retina weights denote contact area; other supplied datasets aggregate unit synaptic contacts. Neither directly equals an FP8 conductance.
The activity-dependent example is symmetric and nonnegative, using a stationary mean-field correlation calculation across all pairs.
A network without explicit coordinates can exhibit these statistics, but this does not establish autonomous semantic dynamics or a scalable local learning implementation.
The publisher correction restores minus signs in clustering-minus-density labels; it does not provide a different biological degree exponent.

retrieval.full_text_status: unavailable through checked public XML/preprint routes

sources.authors: Lu, Doerig, Bosch, Krahmer, Kaiser, Cichy and Kietzmann
sources.title: End-to-end topographic networks as models of cortical map formation and human visual behaviour
sources.evidence_type: trained feedforward visual models and human visual-behaviour experiment
sources.read_scope: Full XML retrieved; model architecture, training, classification results, energy methods, behavioural comparison and discussion read. Three publication-linked code files inspected in AUD-007; no models executed.
sources.finding: A smoothness penalty on neighbouring receptive-field weight kernels produces topographic feature maps in locally connected networks without weight sharing. Compared with the matched locally connected control, topographic models better match human spatial visual biases but do not improve categorization accuracy. Their biological energy proxy is lower.
sources.application_inference: This is evidence about learned visual response preferences under image statistics and an imposed smoothness objective. It does not establish a physical metric or a runtime advantage for the existing fixed semantic-coordinate populations.
transfer_limits: The six-layer model is feedforward, with learned feature preferences, ReLU, layer normalization and L2 regularization. It does not test autonomous semantic recurrence.
The 2D sheet retains receptive-field organization inherited from image coordinates; LLM dimension labels do not supply those coordinates.

Energy is estimated from absolute weighted presynaptic activity and absolute postsynaptic activity, with coefficients two-thirds and one-third. It is not measured CPU time, RAM, joules on the target hardware, or axonal cable length.
The reported comparison against TDANN uses different architectures and training data; the authors explicitly limit interpretation of that cross-model comparison.
The control comparison supports a contribution of smoothness to visual-behaviour alignment, not a requirement that our fixed-role model learn a replacement feature basis.

sources.authors: Margalit, Lee, Finzi, DiCarlo, Grill-Spector and Yamins
sources.title: A unifying framework for functional organization in early and higher ventral visual cortex
sources.evidence_type: topographic visual representation model; detailed evidence here from 2023 preprint and public code
sources.read_scope: Published abstract/metadata and 18 May 2023 author-hosted preprint inspected. Read preprint pp.5,13-14,18-19,23, and visually inspected Fig.7 on p.14. Three current publication-linked code files inspected in AUD-008. Final full text was inaccessible through checked routes; preprint details are not certified as final-version details.
sources.finding: The preprint initializes positions from retinotopy and response-based swaps, freezes positions, randomly reinitializes all network weights, then jointly optimizes task and spatial objectives. Spatial constraints improve several brain-alignment measures and reduce an inferred inter-layer wiring proxy while trading off categorization performance.
sources.application_inference: Frozen coordinates in this workflow do not mean frozen semantic response roles. The intermediate swap procedure can arrange existing responses, but the reported trained model subsequently relearns those responses.
transfer_limits: Preprint task accuracy is 43.9% for the selected TDANN versus 48.5% for task-only models. Better biological alignment is a distinct outcome from better classification.
The network lacks intra-layer recurrent connections. The study does not demonstrate the requested DMN, task-flow or immersion dynamics.
The wiring estimate clusters highly active units separately for each input and assigns hypothetical inter-layer fibers; it is not a sum over the actual nonzero trained synapses.
Every layer has its own 2D sheet. The preprint averages four relative sheet placements because their mutual physical placement is not defined by the model.
Response correlations and inherited visual retinotopy guide placement. Neither licenses distance from semantic dimension indices or matched cell indices across minicolumns.
Current code has a one-half factor in its Pearson spatial loss relative to the displayed preprint formula; numerical alpha values cannot be transferred without identifying the exact version.

retrieval.preprint_title: A Unifying Principle for the Functional Organization of Visual Cortex
retrieval.final_full_text_status: not read; XML unavailable, PMC browser challenge and author sharing link inaccessible

sources.authors: Wingert, Parida, Norman-Haignere and David
sources.title: Convolutional neural network models describe the encoding subspace of local circuits in auditory cortex
sources.evidence_type: ferret cortical recordings and fitted nonlinear sensory-encoding models
sources.read_scope: Final full XML retrieved; local-subspace, layer/cell-type, discussion and recording/similarity methods read. Archived figure notebook and helper file inspected without execution; no raw recordings or sound archive downloaded.
sources.finding: Neurons recorded at the same cortical location share a spectrotemporal subspace more strongly than neurons across sites, yet their response profiles within that subspace differ. Subspace similarity varies substantially with cell type and mean cortical depth; depth separation has a weaker reported association.
sources.application_inference: Shared represented dimensions, correlated firing and nearby cell bodies are separate relationships. This supports analyzing local functional diversity rather than treating anatomical proximity as one universal similarity or connection score.
transfer_limits: The study records 2874 units across 67 sites in four awake, passively listening ferrets; it concerns sensory sound encoding, not human semantic-vector replicas.

The within/across comparison controls a shared-CNN architecture bias by pooling matched-stimulus sites in one fitted model. The reported median subspace indices are 0.55 versus 0.35, while predicted signal correlations are 0.17 versus 0.14.
Narrow spike width is a putative inhibitory-cell label, not direct transmitter or synapse identification.

The response-subspace and layer associations are observational. Inhibitory competition and top-down circuit explanations are hypotheses discussed by the authors, not causal interventions in this experiment.
A cortical tuning subspace does not imply that each model minicolumn must change its assigned semantic dimension or that every CC should be restricted to a learned low-dimensional subspace.

The exact numerical implementation of the published SSI was not independently reconstructed. The archived plotting notebook consumes a precomputed sscc column; its full upstream computation was not found in the inspected files.

retrieval.archive_resolution: The publication-linked record17211353 resolves through its API to version18331549.
retrieval.scope_note: The archive README says64 sites, while the final paper specifies53 A1 plus14 PEG sites. Final-paper scope is used here; no dataset-level reconciliation was performed.

sources.authors: Karkowski, Kehl, Qin, Darcher, Karkowski, Borger, Surges, Hebart, Reber, Dehaene, Lakretz and Mormann
sources.title: Semantic Tuning of Single Neurons in the Human Medial Temporal Lobe
sources.evidence_type: human single-neuron recording preprint with adaptive concept-image sampling
sources.read_scope: 27 October 2025 preprint pp.3-4,8-14,16-17,32 read; Fig.2 on p.24 visually inspected. No peer-reviewed final version identified in the checked routes.
sources.finding: Adaptive sampling of semantically related object images reveals graded responses around preferred concepts in responsive medial-temporal neurons. Continuous vector similarities describe the sampled population better than the tested category/feature and WordNet graph alternatives.
sources.application_inference: The distance is between represented concepts, not between neurons in tissue. The study supplies semantic response evidence but no neuron-placement rule for our assigned coordinates.
transfer_limits: Fifteen epilepsy patients contributed 36 sessions and 2835 recorded units;333 were responsive single units. This is MTL sampling, not a complete neocortical column.

Stimulus selection uses THINGS object embeddings derived from word2vec/WordNet, reduced from 300 to 25 dimensions; a 66-dimensional behavioural embedding is another comparison. These are not DeepSeek token embeddings.
The figures map concept stimuli using 2D t-SNE and interpolate response magnitudes. Neither those maps nor the connected heatmap fields are measured neuron locations.

The reported coactivation probability asks whether two concept stimuli evoke responses in the same neuron. It is not simultaneous activity of a neuron pair and cannot directly supply a Hebbian pair-selection rule.
Embedding-guided adaptive sampling may influence inferred tuning. Diverse pictures per concept help but do not fully separate visual and semantic features, as the authors acknowledge.

The authors explicitly leave peak-versus-axis coding unresolved for sufficiently general models and stimulus spaces. Their illustrative axis comparison does not justify assigning each biological neuron to one embedding coordinate.
No physical distance, connection probability, autonomous recurrence or SNN phase-code parameter is measured.

sources.authors: Lazar, Pipa and Triesch
sources.title: SORN: A Self-Organizing Recurrent Neural Network
sources.evidence_type: binary recurrent-network model with multiple plasticity mechanisms
sources.read_scope: Network-definition section first eight blocks; plasticity, counting-task results, internal-representation results and appendix parameter analysis read. No numerical reproduction.
sources.finding: Spike-timing plasticity, incoming-weight normalization and intrinsic threshold plasticity improve next-symbol/count-position readout compared with static reservoirs. Input letters drive fixed groups of neurons; internal state trajectories become more separable.
sources.application_inference: Fixed input assignments can coexist with learned recurrent temporal context without a neuron-distance rule. The reported result concerns driven prediction and does not by itself establish autonomous semantic recurrence.
transfer_limits: Excitatory-to-excitatory connectivity is sparse, but both cross excitatory/inhibitory connection classes are fully connected. Inhibitory population size is 20% of excitatory population size.
The readout is supervised using a pseudoinverse after recurrent training. While recurrent plasticity continues, representations drift and the authors say the readout needs retraining.
Each symbol drives a small fixed group, unlike our dense signed coordinate vector spread across 5120 minicolumns.
Intrinsic plasticity regulates each neuron toward a target mean rate. This is a stronger and different constraint than a broad per-CC activation band.
The illustrated 200-excitatory-neuron setting and binary time steps do not establish scaling, FP4 dynamics or static incoming-slot feasibility.

sources.authors: Zheng and Triesch
sources.title: Robust development of synfire chains from multiple plasticity mechanisms
sources.evidence_type: spontaneous sequence formation in a binary recurrent-network model
sources.read_scope: Network/plasticity methods, results sections3.2-3.5 and discussion read; figures described by their text, not independently digitized.
sources.finding: Several synfire rings emerge from random connectivity under unstructured noise. Recurrent excitation supports repeated propagation; global inhibition and homeostatic adaptation can produce competition and switching between rings. No physical coordinates are used.
sources.application_inference: This is a positive example of autonomous repeated activity without geometry, closer to our recurrence question than a driven readout task. It does not show that the cycles encode fixed semantic roles or preserve the desired semantic trajectories.
transfer_limits: The studied network has 200-800 excitatory neurons in most examples, inhibitory count0.2 times that count, initial EE probability0.1, IE probability0.2 and fully connected EI pathways.

STDP, structural growth, synaptic normalization, excitatory intrinsic plasticity and inhibitory plasticity jointly shape the result. Their ablations do not establish that coactivity alone is sufficient.
A global event adds one random absent EE edge with probability0.2 per step. This is neither a demonstrated scalable proposal rate nor bounded per-target slot management.
Per-neuron firing targets, default mean0.1 with optional heterogeneity, are not our broad per-CC band. Conduction delays are uniformly one discrete step.
The authors report fragmentation below the tested initial EE probability0.1. This is a limitation of their tested settings, not a universal lower density bound for all sequence networks.
Activity plots sort cells using resulting activity correlations. That plotted order is not physical position.
Established rings become resistant to newly added connections. The paper does not measure continual semantic learning, overlapping dense embeddings or FP4/FP8 operation.

sources.authors: Miner and Triesch
sources.title: Plasticity-Driven Self-Organization under Topological Constraints Accounts for Non-random Features of Cortical Synaptic Wiring
sources.evidence_type: spiking structural-plasticity model fitted to cortical connectivity statistics
sources.read_scope: Network/plasticity methods, reciprocity analysis and discussion read. No numerical reproduction or digitization.
sources.finding: A 400-excitatory/80-inhibitory LIF network starts without EE edges and grows distance-biased EE connections. Plasticity and topology reproduce several non-random wiring statistics. Removing distance bias changes reciprocity and motif statistics.
sources.application_inference: The study identifies a way a shared pairwise opportunity distribution can create structural enrichment. Its explicit geometric construction and structural observables do not demonstrate a computational advantage for our coordinate-assigned semantic recurrence.
transfer_limits: The model supplies a1x1mm sheet and a Gaussian growth kernel with half-width200micrometres. These coordinates are model inputs; our current neuron organization supplies no such physical metric.

Growth probabilities are precomputed over neuron pairs; mean growth920synapses/s is manually tuned toward EE density0.1. Starting with zero functional EE edges does not establish a bounded sparse candidate representation.
Short-term synaptic dynamics, weight normalization, per-neuron3Hz target regulation, STDP and structural growth all contribute. The paper explicitly leaves task/metabolic advantages for future work.
Their reciprocal-pair argument uses a shared symmetric latent pair probability. Arbitrary directed heterogeneity need not produce the same enrichment.
Spike-nearest-neighbour STDP refers to pairing nearby spike times, not nearby physical neurons.
Comparison with the binary SORN ring model is not a geometry-only ablation: neuron dynamics, delays, plasticity, connectivity and outcome measures also differ.

sources.authors: Yuan, Zhu, Wang, Li, Xu, Fang, Huo, Wan, Li, Liu and Yang
sources.title: Incorporating structural plasticity into self-organization recurrent networks for sequence learning
sources.evidence_type: reward-modulated recurrent sequence model with public implementation
sources.read_scope: Architecture, structural plasticity, reward-modulated STDP, training protocol, generation task and structural-plasticity comparisons read; targeted implementation audit AUD-009.
sources.finding: Structural plasticity improves the studied small-network sequence tasks. A closed output-feedback loop generates learned symbolic sequences without continuing external teaching inputs during inference.
sources.application_inference: Autonomous generation is a real positive result, but it depends on a trained readout/feedback circuit and a specified symbolic sequence reward. It is not evidence that an unconstrained recurrent reservoir spontaneously develops our semantic loops.
transfer_limits: Both cross excitatory/inhibitory connection classes are dense. The public implementation allocates full matrices for weights, masks and eligibility traces despite sparse EE connectivity.
The tested recurrent sizes200 and400 and small symbol alphabet do not cover our614400-neuron dense-vector representation or static pool allocation.
The source code scores generated sequences by a longest-common-subsequence calculation. That observable is not a semantic vector error or a general temporal precision measure.

The paper describes repeated alternating recurrent/readout training; the inspected generation example instead selects a recurrent checkpoint and then trains its readout. Exact publication-code version equivalence remains unresolved.
The generation example disables reward modulation of recurrent synapses while retaining output reward learning; paper-level reward claims should not be attributed indiscriminately to every pathway.
No source-distance rule is needed by this example, but neither its storage nor its learning-work cost meets our budget by demonstration.

sources.authors: Bouhadjar, Wouters, Diesmann and Tetzlaff
sources.title: Sequence learning, prediction, and replay in networks of spiking neurons
sources.evidence_type: continuous-time spiking implementation extending HTM temporal memory
sources.read_scope: Network structure, structural plasticity, potential-connectivity constraints, replay and limitations read; Table2 checked; Figs5 and11 visually inspected in final PDF pp16 and23.
sources.finding: Fixed stimulus-specific neuron groups learn context-dependent sequences through potential synapse maturation, dendritic plateaus and group-specific inhibition. In replay mode, a cue triggers a learned sequence without continuing external sequence elements.
sources.application_inference: This provides a constructive bridge from fixed input roles to autonomous replay, beyond the input-gated equations in LOC-061. It does not supply a physical-distance metric or demonstrate our dense multi-coordinate semantic loops.
transfer_limits: Default model has2100 excitatory cells in14 groups of150, plus one inhibitory cell per group. One symbol maps to one group; dense simultaneous semantic-coordinate input is not evaluated.
Potential EE indegree420 corresponds to connection probability0.2; immature synapses retain permanence state even though their current functional weight is zero.

The paper chooses probability0.2 using a divergent-convergent motif calculation:20 active source cells must recruit at least20 of150 candidate target cells, each needing at least5 coincident inputs. This is parameter-dependent, not a universal minimum density.
Group inhibition uses very strong and fast connections. Dendritic-event homeostasis is adjusted to task episode duration, a biological limitation explicitly acknowledged by the authors.

Replay parameters in Table2 differ in somatic threshold20to5mV, dendritic-current threshold59to41.3pA, and excitatory-to-inhibitory strength581.19to77.49pA. The evidence is not merely the original predictive dynamics with external input removed.
The illustrated replay is a short cued sequence. Sustained semantic cycling, broad per-CC band regulation and valence-biased DMN drift are not demonstrated.
High background noise disrupts context specificity; timing limits and overlapping first sequence elements create further constraints discussed by the authors.

sources.authors: Jun and Jin
sources.title: Development of Neural Circuitry for Precise Temporal Sequences through Spontaneous Activity, Axon Remodeling, and Synaptic Plasticity
sources.evidence_type: spiking synfire-chain development model with silent synapses and axon remodeling
sources.read_scope: Model overview, cycles, and network/synapse/inhibition/silent-synapse/axon-remodeling methods read; no supplementary simulation reproduced.
sources.finding: Repeated stimulation of a starter group recruits convergent successors through STDP and synapse activation. An outgoing supersynapse limit prevents the first group from recruiting the entire network. Developed chains can reconnect to earlier groups and repeat within a trial.
sources.application_inference: A graph-only recruitment mechanism can form cyclic propagation, but the specific learning substrate is far more permissive than a fixed small set of stored incoming candidates.
transfer_limits: All neuron pairs initially have a tracked synaptic strength. Only10% are initially functional; silent synapses still undergo STDP. Sparse functional connectivity is not sparse potential storage.
Axon withdrawal after reaching the supersynapse limit stops transmission and STDP for other edges, but their strengths continue to decay and remain available if withdrawal reverses.
The default model has1000 excitatory neurons and an idealized global inhibitory event delivered after every excitatory spike.
Each2-second trial resets neuronal variables and spike histories. The reported cycling therefore does not establish an uninterrupted steady regime across trial boundaries.
Training stimuli identify a starter group; the model does not assign every neuron a fixed signed semantic-coordinate role.
The outgoing supersynapse cap is a learning mechanism in this paper, distinct from our provisional incoming capacity classes. No such cap or withdrawal rule is adopted.

sources.authors: Shao, Riquelme and Gjorgjieva
sources.title: Spontaneous emergence and evolution of neuronal sequences in recurrent networks
sources.evidence_type: eLife reviewed preprint v1, published14April2026; spiking-network simulations
sources.read_scope: Sequence-emergence results, motif analysis, structured-input results, network/plasticity/sequence-testing/structured-input methods and discussion read; Table2/3 visually inspected; targeted public-code audit AUD-010. Paper equations are image-rendered and are not all independently re-derived.
sources.finding: A fixed random graph with sparse connections in all four E/I classes develops broad weights and reliable ordered followers under unstructured-input training. Strong connections and follower identities turn over more slowly than weak connections, while overall weight statistics stabilize.
sources.application_inference: This is useful evidence that distance-free fixed candidate graphs can support learned sequential responses with all connection classes sparse. The demonstrated outcome and the candidate densities still differ from our required continuously active semantic regimes.
transfer_limits: Default size is1200 excitatory and240 inhibitory AdEx neurons. Table2 gives connection probabilities EE0.06, EI0.19, IE0.20, II0.11; these are not fixed degree limits as neuron count grows.

Sequence testing freezes plasticity, injects a source spike every400ms for1000 trials, lowers external Poisson drive, and detects followers in the next300ms. Reliable trial-evoked propagation is not an uninterrupted self-sustaining loop.
Both incoming and outgoing weights are normalized, and excitatory thresholds target a common0.45Hz firing rate. A broad CC-wide activation band does not imply these per-neuron constraints.
Spatially structured input here means correlated drive to twelve random groups of100 neurons, not a measured or modeled physical-distance kernel.

Fan-in/out motif enrichment among followers is an association. The random comparator matches strong-edge probability, not all degree heterogeneity; enrichment is not a causal proof that this motif should become an independent wiring rule.
The hub comparison changes presynaptic normalization and intrinsic plasticity and also adjusts parameters. Its strong-weight hubs are not our allocated high-capacity classes.
Reference code updates stored sparse edges but constructs dense intermediate matrices during initialization. It does not demonstrate memory-bounded setup at our scale.
No fixed semantic-vector assignment, FP4/FP8 arithmetic, learned continuous vector recurrence, or task-independent regulation of the three proposed regimes is evaluated.
Public code and reviewed-preprint text differ in the stated null-rate construction for follower detection; the audit does not quantify the effect or invalidate the reported result.

sources.authors: Bellec, Kappel, Maass and Legenstein
sources.title: Deep Rewiring: Training very sparse deep networks
sources.evidence_type: published ICLR2018 paper, author-hosted conference PDF; supervised sparse network learning
sources.read_scope: Algorithm and representation discussion pp2-4, recurrent/transfer experiments pp6-7, convergence summary pp8-10, initialization discussion p15 and theoretical/practical distinction p24 read. Algorithm1 p3 visually inspected. Source audit AUD-011.
sources.finding: DEEP R updates active connections and replaces those crossing its deletion boundary with newly sampled partners, maintaining a hard total active-connection budget. The paper explains that dormant connections need not retain parameters, and reports feedforward/CNN/LSTM classification results.
sources.application_inference: Bounded stored connectivity does not logically require a permanently fixed potential-contact graph or physical coordinates. This is an existence example for budgeted partner exploration, not evidence that the same rule solves our semantic recurrence task.
transfer_limits: Learning uses supervised gradients or backpropagation through time, regularization and stochastic updates. Coactivity-only learning is not tested by this paper.
The hard constraint is global or per weight matrix in the examples, not the current per-neuron incoming capacity-class allocation.
The authors distinguish hard-budget DEEP R from soft-DEEP R, which continues updating dormant parameters and has no hard active-count bound.
A fixed synapse budget does not bound all training memory: activations, optimizer state and temporal differentiation remain separate costs. CPU performance at CC scale was not measured here.
Initial allocation among layers matters; smaller output matrices can be dense. Classification and LSTM speech recognition do not demonstrate autonomous semantic loops or per-CC steady activity.

AppendixD explicitly distinguishes the proven formal Markov operator from the practical rule that resets dormant parameters to zero. The stationary-distribution result is not an exact finite-step convergence guarantee for every implementation.
Fixed connection signs in this model concern excitation/inhibition of weights, not positive/negative semantic coordinate populations.
No rewiring distribution, gradient method, stochastic temperature or additional data structure is adopted for the application.

sources.authors: Gillett, Pereira and Brunel
sources.title: Characteristics of sequential activity in networks with temporally asymmetric Hebbian learning
sources.evidence_type: published theoretical and simulation study; full main-article XML
sources.read_scope: Rate/learning equations, retrieval, capacity, nonlinear learning, spiking translation and discussion sections read; Fig1/3/4/7 captions checked. Supplement was not retrieved. Targeted author-code audit AUD-012.
sources.finding: A nonspatial sparse network retrieves distributed sequences after a cue using temporally asymmetric Hebbian weights. Fig1 uses 40000 rate units and mean degree 200. A separate translation uses 20000 excitatory and 5000 inhibitory spiking units.
sources.application_inference: Sparse candidate access can support distributed sequence retrieval without physical coordinates. Failure of a small-group coincidence motif does not imply failure of every distributed representation.
transfer_limits: Weights are constructed from prescribed random input patterns, neglecting recurrent activity during learning; online biological learning is left for future work.
Retrieval is a transient sequence, not a demonstrated sustained semantic loop. The code stores successive transitions without a last-to-first term.

Independent Gaussian patterns, transfer functions, nonlinear learning and near-uniform random degree are assumptions. The example capacity near 0.47 times degree is parameter dependent and cannot be applied to allocated slot counts.
Spiking conversion rectifies excitatory weights and calibrates fast inhibitory feedback. Semantic coordinate polarity is not excitation/inhibition.
Reported pattern correlations permit imperfect reconstruction. No FP4/FP8 precision, heterogeneous capacity classes or per-CC activity band was validated.

sources.authors: Hopfield
sources.title: Neurons with graded response have collective computational properties like those of two-state neurons
sources.evidence_type: published continuous-rate network analysis; author-institution-hosted scan
sources.read_scope: PDF pp2-4 and first part of p5 read; printed p3090 equations visually inspected. ANA-026 states a zero-input version of the Lyapunov argument.
sources.finding: Under symmetric interactions, monotone continuous response functions and passive first-order dynamics, a decreasing energy function constrains autonomous behavior to exclude nonconstant periodic orbits.
sources.application_inference: Changing only which symmetric edges are near cannot produce sustained cycles in this particular dynamical class. Temporal behavior must be evaluated alongside connection selection.
transfer_limits: This is not a theorem about arbitrary spiking, delayed, stochastic, adaptive or synchronously quantized networks.
Coactivity learning need not produce symmetric effective interactions when masks, cell rules or history differ.
Adaptation can invalidate the static-energy argument even with symmetric weights; asymmetry is not asserted to be universally necessary.
No neuron dynamics, energy objective or temporal learning rule is adopted.

sources.authors: Billaudelle, Cramer, Petrovici, Schreiber, Kappel, Schemmel and Meier
sources.title: Structural plasticity on an accelerated analog neuromorphic hardware system
sources.evidence_type: published hardware experiment; final Neural Networks133 pp11-20 PDF; online2020
sources.read_scope: Final PDF pp1-8 read, particularly algorithm, address filtering, learning, task, sparsity controls and timing. Algorithm1 and Fig7/8 visually inspected. Related arXiv1912.12980v2 overview was also read but final experimental report governs this card.
sources.finding: Fixed incoming synaptic circuits can replace their source labels while retaining constant fan-in. Causal STDP, rate-dependent decay, noise and pruning learn informative connections in a teacher-driven Iris classification task; about92% test accuracy is reported with six incoming synapses per label neuron.
sources.application_inference: Budgeted incoming slots and exploration of a larger candidate universe are compatible. No physical neuron metric is needed for the illustrated replacement operation.
transfer_limits: Random disjoint receptor bundles restrict each slot to one source from its bundle; two useful sources in the same bundle cannot both connect to that target.
The two-dimensional coordinates are predefined petal features used to set receptor firing, not anatomical neuron positions or an embedding of semantic dimension labels.
This is a small feedforward supervised task, with120 training and30 test samples,20 initializations and frozen test weights. It does not establish autonomous recurrence.
Larger candidate pools slow discovery. Hardware parallelism and measured update times cannot be transferred to CPU simulation.
Six-bit source labels and weights, teacher inputs, bundles, counters and correlation traces are not adopted as application fields or algorithms.

sources.authors: Gillett and Brunel
sources.title: Dynamic control of sequential retrieval speed in networks with heterogeneous learning rules
sources.evidence_type: eLife Version of Record,28 August2024; main XML and publisher PDF; PDF running header retains2023 volume year
sources.read_scope: Learning equations, heterogeneous populations, nonlinear learning, persistent-to-sequential transition, spiking translation, reward adaptation and limitations read. Figure4 visually checked. Mean-field derivation was not independently reproduced.
sources.finding: Changing external inputs to populations with different temporal learning rules controls recall speed and switches between persistent and sequential retrieval on the same nonspatial graph. The illustrated rate network has80000 units and connection probability0.005.
sources.application_inference: Mode and temporal scale can depend on cell dynamics, learning asymmetry and drive without being encoded as physical separation.
transfer_limits: Recurrent weights are constructed from prescribed independent Gaussian patterns. The paper explicitly leaves learning with recurrently shaped responses for future work.
Persistent recall of one pattern and transient ordered recall are different from continuous autonomous cyclic activation.
The control inputs target specified neuron subpopulations; these are not the application's positive/negative semantic populations.
Nonlinear plasticity binarizes training patterns. Its fixed-point and speed results do not directly describe the unchosen FP4 population encoder.
The reward example adjusts two external drives using an explicit target speed; it does not learn the recurrent sequence weights online.
No controller, cellular subtype, reward, timing rule or distance metric is adopted.

sources.authors: Jézéquel et al.
sources.title: Cadherins orchestrate specific patterns of perisomatic inhibition onto distinct pyramidal cell populations
sources.evidence_type: published primary experimental study; main full-text XML and publisher PDF
sources.read_scope: Input specificity, conditional knockdown, developmental injections, bouton quantification and discussion read. Figure 3 visually inspected. Transcriptomics and rabies tracing were read for context, not independently reanalyzed.
sources.finding: In mouse somatosensory cortex, postsynaptic Cdh12 knockdown reduces CCK-marker perisomatic inputs to L5 IT cells, while Cdh13 knockdown reduces PV-marker inputs to L5 ET cells. The effects depend on target cell type; the same perturbations do not have the same effects in the other target population.
sources.application_inference: Partner identity and cellular context can matter among intermingled neurons. A rule based only on soma separation does not describe all measured inhibitory specificity.
transfer_limits: The measured synaptic endpoint is marker-positive bouton density near reconstructed somata, not a complete pairwise functional connectome; somata without the relevant inputs were excluded.
Spatial controls concern cortical sublayers and cell positions, not a complete intervention holding every axon/dendrite contact fixed.

Cdh13 knockdown also changes excitatory miniature currents. Compensation or additional excitatory functions remain possible; Cdh12 knockdown does not significantly change aggregate miniature inhibitory currents.
The experiment does not identify a semantic similarity metric or equate biological IT/ET/PV/CCK identities with fixed embedding-coordinate roles.
No cell-type field, molecular rule, inhibitory subtype or anatomical layout is adopted.

sources.authors: Zhu, Deng, Fan, Wang, Zhou and Xu
sources.title: Combinatorial expression of γ-protocadherins regulates synaptic connectivity in the mouse neocortex
sources.evidence_type: published primary experimental study; main full-text XML and publisher PDF
sources.read_scope: Knockout, overexpression, combination-similarity experiments, positioning control, discussion and bootstrap method read. Figure 4 visually inspected. PDF identifies the March 2024 Version of Record despite its 2023 volume header.
sources.finding: Among nearby mouse L2/3 pyramidal cells, removing γ-protocadherins increases detected connectivity. Overexpressing identical combinations in two neuronal groups decreases their connection rate; a fully overlapping combination gives 5/134 connected pairs versus 19/151 controls, while nonoverlapping combinations approach controls.
sources.application_inference: The biological meaning of similarity depends on the property being compared. Similar molecular identifiers can discourage excitatory contact, which is different from inhibitory synaptic action or semantic opposition.
transfer_limits: The combination experiment uses overexpression and a few chosen isoform mixtures. It does not establish a universal quantitative similarity kernel under physiological expression.
Laminar cell positioning was unchanged in the reported control, but the authors leave direct synapse formation versus pruning or axon/dendrite growth as unresolved mechanisms.
Effects differ with isoform family, cortical layer, developmental age and brain region; molecular homophily cannot be substituted for similarity of functional responses.
Pair connectivity is not interchangeable with a directed-edge probability or total synapse count. Bootstrap-derived trend plots do not add independent biological observations.
No semantic avoidance metric, identity code or minimum-distance exclusion is adopted.

sources.authors: Cadwell et al.
sources.title: Cell type composition and circuit organization of clonally related excitatory neurons in the juvenile mouse neocortex
sources.evidence_type: published primary experimental study; main full-text XML and publisher PDF
sources.read_scope: Vertical/lateral connectivity, distance-matched controls, GLM, power-analysis summary and discussion of prior studies read. Figure 4 and contextual discussion visually inspected; no raw-data reanalysis.
sources.finding: Across 2049 tested potential excitatory connections, related cells show higher connection probability across layers (6.0% versus 2.7%), but no demonstrated increase within a layer (5.6% versus 8.1%). Matching both vertical and tangential distances within 20 micrometres preserves this distinction.
sources.application_inference: A developmental relationship is not a uniform pair-affinity rule. Its association with connectivity depends on connection class even after measured distance is controlled.
transfer_limits: Clones contain about two radial-glial lineages on average and differ from narrowly labeled sister-cell clones. This is a refinement of earlier claims, not a direct replication using identical labels.
No detected within-layer increase is not proof of zero effect at every age or in every subtype; the authors discuss potentially transient effects and different tracing methods.
Distance matching does not hold developmental contact history, neurite trajectories or every transcriptomic subtype fixed.
A weak conditional distance effect here does not establish that physical distance is biologically irrelevant.
Cortical layers and biological clones are not the application’s semantic dimensions or positive/negative populations. No mapping between them is proposed.

sources.authors: Mathieu et al.
sources.title: Uncovering the molecular logic of cortical wiring between neuronal subtypes across development through ligand–receptor inference
sources.evidence_type: published primary experimental study; main full-text XML and publisher PDF
sources.read_scope: Inference pipeline, adult morphological prior, classifier task, targeted CBLN4/cadherin validation, discussion and limitations read. Figure 3 caption and accompanying classifier description visually inspected. Not all atlas predictions were validated.
sources.finding: The study combines expression-based interaction scores with developmental and adult-morphology priors, then validates selected candidates. Cdh13 knockdown reduces L5 perisomatic PV-marker coverage, whereas Pcdh8 knockdown increases L2/3 coverage; axon-initial-segment inputs are unaffected in these comparisons.
sources.application_inference: Selected molecular effects can be context-specific and opposite in direction. The atlas is useful for generating hypotheses, but its imposed anatomical prior cannot independently establish a new geometry for semantic roles.
transfer_limits: The connectivity prior places 1000 reconstructed neurons in a prescribed 3D column. Same-type morphology scores are replaced by 0.5 to address an artifact; this is a modeling choice rather than a direct connectome measurement.
The classifier predicts source/target cell-type identity from ligand–receptor expression products, not whether an individual neuronal pair has a synapse. See ANA-030.
RNA abundance does not determine protein localization or functional binding. Selected knockdowns support specific gene involvement, not validation of every predicted ligand–receptor edge.
Developmental predictions use adult morphology; transient connections, non-neuronal cells and generalization beyond somatosensory cortex remain limitations.
No anatomical prior, molecular identity mapping or connectivity classifier is adopted.

sources.authors: Li, Lu, Cheng, Ge, Xu, Shi and Dan
sources.title: Clonally Related Visual Cortical Neurons Show Similar Stimulus Feature Selectivity
sources.evidence_type: published primary imaging and developmental-intervention study; accepted-manuscript XML
sources.read_scope: All nine main-body paragraphs, methods summary and Figure2/3 captions read. Supplement and PDF were not retrieved.
sources.finding: In juvenile mouse V1, sparsely labeled putative sister neurons show more similar orientation preferences than nearby nonsisters. Disrupting gap-junction communication reduces this similarity; systemic blockade also reduces overall visual responsiveness.
sources.application_inference: Functional similarity can depend on developmental communication among cells that are intermingled with differently tuned neighbors. It need not be a monotone map of nearest soma position.
transfer_limits: The comparison includes 34 visually driven sister pairs, with 23 pairs passing orientation-selectivity criteria, under anesthesia shortly after eye opening. Sparse labeling and radial alignment infer sister relationships rather than directly sequencing lineages.
The selective connexin perturbation and systemic blocker have different specificity; electrical coupling versus exchanged small molecules is unresolved.
This measures response selectivity, not the entire synaptic graph. Later evidence in LOC-084 questions uniformly increased within-layer connections as its explanation.
The authors discuss common inputs and experience. The experiment does not show that a particular feature value is genetically assigned or that LLM coordinates correspond to cortical columns.
No gap junction, developmental protocol or reassignment of the application’s fixed semantic roles is proposed.

sources.authors: Perin, Berger and Markram
sources.title: A synaptic organizing principle for cortical neuronal groups
sources.evidence_type: published multi-neuron slice recordings plus graph-model extrapolation; university-hosted published PDF
sources.read_scope: Main PDFpp1–5 read, including distance profiles, matched-position null, common neighbors, cluster extrapolation, discussion and brief methods. Figure1 and Figure3 visually checked. Supplement remains unavailable: publisher403 and PMC download challenge; neither was bypassed.
sources.finding: Recordings from up to 12 juvenile rat L5 pyramidal cells at once find decreasing pairwise connection probability with distance, but additional group clustering and common-neighbor associations beyond a null using measured positions and connection profiles. An iterative 2000-node graph model reproduces several statistics.
sources.application_inference: A distance law, a conditional common-neighbor association and the spatial extent of an assembly are different observations. Their coexistence does not define physical coordinates for the application.
transfer_limits: The experiment samples 1345 cells and 3446 pairs across 270 sessions, not a complete large-neuron connectome.
Approximately 53 cells per cluster and small-world path lengths are model extrapolations using affinity propagation, not direct measurements of an anatomical minicolumn’s size.
The model’s common-neighbor update is sufficient for selected statistics, not a demonstrated biological learning rule or proof that experience must obey that update.
The proposed genetic preconfiguration is explicitly speculative; shared statistics across animals do not establish identical memberships or fixed semantic meanings.
The small-sample/model degree result does not determine the application’s static capacity-class allocation.
No common-neighbor prior, assembly membership, physical layout or exclusion radius is adopted.

sources.authors: Udvary, Harth, Macke, Hege, de Kock, Sakmann and Oberlaender

sources.finding: A model based on axodendritic overlap, synaptic-site density and cellular diversity predicts many nonrandom connectivity patterns without an additional activity-specific partner rule. Pairwise predictions correlate with 89 literature measurements across 29 studies; several motifs and compartment-specific effects remain unexplained.
sources.application_inference: Biological anatomy can contribute more structure than soma distance alone. Conversely, a motif associated with a common-neighbor rule can have another generative explanation; neither explanation automatically establishes a useful learning rule for semantic recurrence.
transfer_limits: The model assumes equal partner opportunity within cubic subvolumes, normally 50 micrometres wide, and Poisson synapse counts; it does not resolve every neurite trajectory inside a voxel.
Anatomical cell types, arbor shapes and site densities are measured or assigned inputs. They are not derived from semantic vectors.
Empirical comparison pools heterogeneous studies, including rat and mouse data. A prediction lying within a broad model distribution is not the same as an independently precise prediction.
The human extension uses a preliminary EM reconstruction and conditions on its pre/post site locations. It does not infer anatomy without anatomical data.
Some motifs, dendritic targeting and inhibitory subtype specificity are explicitly outside the successful explanation.
Recurrent graph motifs are static wiring patterns; the study does not demonstrate sustained activation loops, learning performance or a per-CC activity band.
No anatomical opportunity graph or morphological field is adopted for the application.

sources.title: Establishment of high reciprocal connectivity between clonal cortical neurons is regulated by the Dnmt3b DNA methyltransferase and clustered protocadherins

Clonal origin is inferred from sparse chimeric labeling and distribution controls, not individually proven for every pair; these early progenitors differ from narrowly defined radial-glial sister clones.
Morphology and physiology controls do not hold every axodendritic contact fixed. Dnmt3b regulates genes beyond cPcdhs.
Reciprocity uses connected pairs as its denominator; 83% is not the fraction of all tested pairs. No semantic representation or autonomous activity loop was tested.

sources.title: Patterned cPCDH expression regulates the fine organization of the neocortex

Language experiments use GPT-Neo/NanoGPT125M and target feed-forward c_fc layers; this is not the fixed Flash token-embedding table or a spiking recurrent CC.

Orientation supplies a known circular feature relation. Flash dimension labels have no corresponding orientation difference; directly substituting axis indices would violate the current boundary.

This phase transition concerns spatial organization of feature preferences, not active/inactive/predictive FP4 states or DMN/flow/immersion transitions.

Population counts and anatomical map evidence were compiled across heterogeneous studies, with some estimates. The paper predicts maps in large rodents; later direct agouti and small-primate measurements are queued to assess those predictions rather than treating them as established.

sources.application_inference: Displaced identity can coexist with substantial local circuit organization and altered dynamics. Functional substitution in another experiment should not be interpreted as proof that every spatial arrangement is dynamically equivalent.
transfer_limits: Recordings use P12–P15 slices; calcium imaging runs at7.4Hz. The main synchronous-event comparison uses5micromolar gabazine to block GABAA receptors. These are not measurements of normal adult resting-state recurrence.

Baseline activation frequencies are reported similar to controls, with fewer spontaneously active cells in Eml1 slices; disinhibition exposes altered activity. The source does not establish spontaneous seizures in every tested preparation.

The256-site uncaging grid has75micrometer spacing. Mean evoked current is measured in a100ms window starting7ms after stimulation, with short-latency direct responses excluded. This maps functional input origins, not a complete set of individual synaptic edges or a universal connection-probability law.

Figure5 morphology overlays17 RhoA and22 Eml1 neurons; these reconstruction counts are not the sample size for every experiment. Slice truncation and developmental manipulation limit whole-brain transfer.
The earlier recruitment of Eml1 heterotopia under gabazine is an activity-timing result, not proof that a specific geometric term alone causes the difference.
Different ages, preparations, tasks and manipulation contexts prevent treating this study and LOC-106 as a direct replication or contradiction.

sources.authors: Shalev Itzkovitz, Leehod Baruch, Ehud Shapiro and Eran Segal
sources.title: Geometric constraints on neuronal connectivity facilitate a concise synaptic adhesive code
sources.evidence_type: Primary theoretical encoding model, synthetic graph comparisons and C.elegans connectome analysis
sources.read_scope: Six-page author-hosted published PDF main text and methods read; Figures1–2 visually inspected on page2. Online supplementary derivations not retrieved. EuropePMC XML returned500.
sources.finding: Restricting possible partners permits reuse of molecular-address labels, and repeating wiring patterns further reduces the labels needed in the proposed deterministic binary wiring code. Simulated scaling depends mainly on neighborhood size, with comparable1D/2D results.
sources.application_inference: Biological locality can serve the economy of specifying connections, separately from recurrent computation. This offers a concrete reason not to assume that a biological distance law is automatically a computational requirement for our explicitly stored incoming slots.
transfer_limits: A pre-existing potential-neighbor relation is supplied to the code; address-pair rules determine actual binary edges only within that relation. Potential neighborhood sizeD differs from actual degreeK and from allocated slot capacity.

The approximate square-root scaling is a counting/heuristic result for stated regimes, not a measured cortical neuron-degree scale law. The label-minimization problem is NP-complete and reported counts use greedy search, not certified global optima.
The authors explicitly generalize the argument beyond Euclidean lattices to restricted target sets. This does not select or justify any particular nonspatial eligibility rule for our application.

The C.elegans analysis uses281 nodes and derives proximity from the union of existing directed chemical and gap-junction contacts because anatomical reach is unavailable. This may omit nearby unconnected pairs and is not independent anatomical validation of the proximity mask.

The real network requires80 heuristic labels versus85±1.5 in1000 randomizations preserving in/out degrees and the supplied reach constraints. The reported effect is modest and does not establish a neuronal coordinate metric.

Address diversity, per-neuron label assignment, the address-pair rule table and the cost of specifying the potential-neighbor relation are different resources. Fewer labels do not automatically reduce our4-byte source-ID plus1-byte weight storage.

The model omits activity-dependent rewiring/weights and recurrent performance. Its2008 protocadherin estimates and adhesive-code hypothesis are historical assumptions, not current proof of a complete molecular wiring code; later molecular interventions are separately reviewed in LOC-082–091.

sources.authors: Francis Normand, Mehul Gajwani, Trang Cao, Jace Cruddas, Arshiya Sangchooli, Stuart Oldham, Alexander Holmes, P. A. Robinson, James C. Pang and Alex Fornito
sources.title: Geometric constraints on the architecture of mammalian cortical connectomes
sources.publication_status: Final Cell article metadata/abstract verified; detailed results below refer to the separately identified 2025 preprint, not a claimed full reading of the final version.
sources.read_scope: PMC12458297 version5 full main-text sections S1–S5 and figure captions read. The supplement containing methods timed out, and final publisher access was unavailable. No claim to independently inspect supplementary controls. Five public source files audited separately in AUD-022.
sources.evidence_type: Geometric neural-field generative model fitted to group cortical connectomes, with cross-validation and cross-species comparisons
sources.finding: The preprint reports substantial prediction of cortical connectivity from anatomical geometry using a truncated, zero-frequency neural-field Green function. Geometry contributes more than a simple exponential distance rule under the reported comparisons.
sources.application_inference: This is positive evidence that an existing cortical surface constrains anatomical wiring. It does not derive a surface from fixed semantic-coordinate roles or establish that the resulting static graph supports the application’s autonomous activation regimes.
transfer_limits: The supplied cortical mesh carries substantial measured anatomical structure. The two fitted parameters are the spatial range and retained eigenmode count; two parameters does not mean the model has only two quantities of prior anatomical information.

For the 339-subject group-average left hemisphere with 4386 surface vertices, the preprint reports optimized range9.53mm,108modes, intersection-edge weight Spearman correlation0.81, binary degree0.52, rank-strength0.47, and true-positive rate75%. Optimization uses a sum of union-edge weight, degree and rank-strength correlations; the reported intersection-edge correlation is a distinct statistic.

Split-half cross-validation, individual-versus-average geometry, smoothing/resampling controls and binary-objective comparisons are explicitly reported. Their supplementary implementation and exact split unit were not independently read and are not assumed absent.

Community structure and normalized-Laplacian statistics provide additional comparisons outside the optimization sum. At vertex resolution none of the tested models captured nodal clustering well; long, weak and rare edges remain difficult.

The 150-region parcellated result and mouse, marmoset, macaque and chimpanzee comparisons use different graph scales and separately fitted parameters. They are not neuron-level tests or unchanged-parameter cross-species transfer.

The theoretical Green function is static. Diagonal removal, clipping, symmetrization and empirical-density thresholding further transform its kernel in the public implementation. Shared geometric eigenvectors of the unprocessed Green function cannot automatically be attributed to the final adjacency.

The framework supplies a single-hemisphere intracortical physical geometry and a uniform spatial range. The authors explicitly identify temporal dynamics and broader anatomical components as further work. Semantic role assignment, activity-dependent learning, sparse slot budgets and per-CC autonomous stability are not tested.
