sources.authors: Jacob Tanner, Joshua Faskowitz, Andreia Sofia Teixeira, Caio Seguin, Ludovico Coletta, Alessandro Gozzi, Bratislav Misic and Richard F. Betzel
sources.title: A multi-modal, asymmetric, weighted, and signed description of anatomical connectivity
sources.evidence_type: Structural-mask-constrained regression of human fMRI activity, with subject/state comparisons and graph controls
sources.read_scope: Published XML sections3,7,9,14,19,22 read, including list-form null-model definitions; Figure1 visually inspected on PDF page3. Supplement retrieval returned502; supplementary results are distinguished from independently inspected evidence.
sources.finding: Fitting directed signed regression coefficients on a fixed structural mask predicts next-sample activity, distinguishes individuals and changes between rest and movie viewing. Real structural neighborhoods outperform several randomized or minimally wired alternatives.
sources.application_inference: A fixed set of input/output roles and structural eligibility does not force fixed functional responses or state-independent effective weights. This supports separating assigned roles, learned interactions and physical geometry, without importing the regression scheme into the SNN.
transfer_limits: The primary group fit pools95 participants; subject specificity uses three scans to predict a fourth. The reported group correlation0.76 is a one-step explanatory fit, not demonstrated autonomous rollout stability.

The five nulls include a shortest-edge-only graph, arbitrary reordering, approximate distance-preserving spin reordering, degree-preserving rewiring and time-series circular shifts. Additional equal-distance edge replacement, regularization, lag and global-signal controls are reported in the supplement; their plots were not independently read.
The117-participant7T rest/movie comparison holds the structural mask fixed. Differences in fitted coefficients do not show that anatomical synaptic strengths physically changed over the scan.

The authors explicitly treat regression signs and asymmetries as statistical constructs. A negative coefficient is not an identified inhibitory synapse, and directionality is not by itself established causal influence. Their mouse supplementary comparison reports no correlation with tracer-derived directed weights.

The regression is described as explanatory rather than generative. Separate Galan and reduced Wong-Wang neural-mass comparisons are reported and their equations were read; their supplementary numerical performance was not inspected. These must not be conflated with free-running use of the fitted regression.
For shortest-path calculations negative weights are shifted to positive values. Graph efficiency after that transformation is not a direct measure of signed excitatory/inhibitory propagation.

The spatial relations belong to measured macroscopic brain regions. The study supplies no physical-distance rule between our semantic dimensions, no cell-level learning algorithm and no evidence for the three requested autonomous/driven regimes.

sources.authors: Caio Seguin, Maciej Jedynak, Olivier David, Sina Mansour L, Olaf Sporns and Andrew Zalesky
sources.title: Communication dynamics in the human connectome shape the cortex-wide propagation of direct electrical stimulation
sources.evidence_type: Human intracranial electrical-stimulation propagation compared with structural-network communication measures
sources.publication_status: Final Neuron metadata, summary and targeted publisher-indexed control passages verified. Detailed methods and figures inspected in the author-deposited July2022 preprint, which is not assumed equivalent to the final article.
sources.read_scope: HAL19-page PDF pages2–11 main text/methods and page19 supplementary captions read; Figure3 and supplementary FigureS5 visually inspected. Final publisher full-page access unavailable; indexed final passages explicitly report additional nonlinear-distance, latency, individual-network and held-out-center controls.
sources.finding: Structural-network measures, especially search information and communicability, explain stimulus propagation beyond Euclidean distance. The final abstract reports46% variance explained for held-out medical centers; the2022preprint reports54% under region-pair cross-validation. These are different validation settings.
sources.application_inference: This provides intervention-based evidence that actual graph topology matters beyond a near-neighbor distance rule. It supports studying pathways and recurrent interaction structure separately from coordinates, while leaving the microscopic learning rule and autonomous regimes open.
transfer_limits: The stimulation dataset includes550 epilepsy patients across20 centers and29055 stimulations. Normative structural/functional graphs come from1000 healthy HCP participants, rather than subject-matched complete anatomical wiring.

In the2022version the principal comparisons include4989 probability and857 amplitude region pairs, generally requiring100 stimulations/significant responses and at least5 patients per pair. Pairs closer than20mm are excluded in the main analysis to reduce measurement confounds; this is an analysis exclusion, not evidence of biological near-neighbor avoidance.

A significant response is a z-scored evoked potential above5 within800ms in that preprint. Millisecond recording resolution does not make every response monosynaptic or identify a specific neuronal transmission mechanism.
The preprint uses nested lasso cross-validation over region pairs. The final held-out-center result is separately recorded; the full final splitting implementation was not read in the retrieved PDF.

Standard and cost-preserving Maslov-Sneppen nulls preserve degree sequence and edge-weight distribution; the cost-preserving variant also preserves approximate length distribution and weight-length relationship.1000 nulls are compared, with each connection rewired once on average. FigureS5 shows heterogeneous outcomes across metrics and subsets, not uniform superiority of every metric.

The final publisher-indexed text additionally reports piecewise regression of nonlinear distance effects, short/medium/long distance strata, latency analysis, and independent MICA normative-network replication. These controls should not be omitted merely because the older preprint lacks all of them.

Electrical stimulation is an intervention, but fitting communication metrics to its outcomes does not uniquely identify the biological signaling policy. Search-information/communicability success does not establish random-walk neurons or prescribe an SNN update.

Macroscopic geometry and tractography biases, incomplete sampling, clinical population and group aggregation limit transfer to a single CC. No static semantic-role layout, finite-degree learning or autonomous activation band is tested.

sources.authors: Richard F. Betzel, Maria Grazia Puxeddu, Caio Seguin and Bratislav Misic
sources.title: Cascades and convergence: Dynamic signal flow in a synapse-level brain network
sources.evidence_type: Stochastic independent-cascade propagation on an adult Drosophila synapse-level connectome
sources.read_scope: Published XML sensory wiring, edge contributions, additional analyses, cascade/cooperation/competition definitions read; PDF discussion and methods pages17–19 read, with Figure1 visually inspected on page4. Supplement captions inspected selectively; no simulation or bulk connectome download.
sources.finding: A measured directed synaptic graph produces modality-specific propagation followed by convergence, and different cascade responses to joint or competing sensory seeds. Graph structure is sufficient to generate these transient model effects without an explicit distance term in the update.
sources.application_inference: This illustrates that anatomy can influence computation through the stored graph without requiring physical coordinates at runtime. It is a transient propagation result and cannot supply the sustained-loop mechanism required by the application.
transfer_limits: The model uses138639 neurons, approximately54million synapses, independent transmission probability0.01 per synaptic contact and16 seeds per modality. A multi-contact pair transmits with probability1-(1-p)^m; synapse multiplicity is not the same as our singleFP8 slot weight.

Every neuron transitions inactive→active→permanently refractory for that cascade. It fires at most once and cannot sustain a closed loop. These three states are not the application’s inactive/predictively preactivated/actively activated phases.

Connectivity comes from a real fly with pre-existing anatomy; omitting coordinates from the update is not evidence that its graph was generated without geometric constraints. Cell locations are mainly used for visualization. Spatial delays, inhibition and transmitter-specific dynamics are explicit future extensions.

Joint-modality seeding doubles the number of initial active neurons. Faster mean arrival can arise from pooling independent opportunities; it is not by itself evidence of nonlinear synaptic cooperation or learned semantic association.
The main text reports weak early dynamic-versus-structural centrality correlation (maximum0.15), rising above0.9 later. This is more specific than the broad introduction’s statement about early hubs.

Thresholding to pairs with at least5 synapses yields correlations0.80,0.56 and0.82 for activation/cooperation/competition summaries. This supports some robustness but does not prove that filling missing synapses only rescales time.

Equal seed counts across sensory modalities imply very different overlap across repeated trials because modality population sizes differ greatly. The authors recognize this issue for overlap/dominance statistics.

No observed neural recordings or behavioral scores validate the cascade trajectories here; the study presents testable hypotheses. No choice of coordinates, incoming pool distribution, phase code or learning algorithm follows for our model.

sources.authors: Andrea I. Luppi, Yonatan Sanz Perl, Jakub Vohryzek, Hana Ali, Pedro A. M. Mediano and colleagues
sources.title: Competitive interactions shape mammalian brain network dynamics and computation
sources.evidence_type: Signed generative whole-brain oscillator modeling and a separate reservoir-computing memory benchmark across three species
sources.read_scope: Published results sections3,4,6,8,10–12, discussion, Hopf equations, connectivity optimization and reservoir methods inspected; equation3 and Figure8 visually inspected on PDF pages20 and12. Main-text descriptions of supplementary controls read, not all supplement plots. Five implementation files audited in AUD-023.
sources.finding: Allowing competitive effective interactions improves fitted and several unoptimized brain-dynamics measures. Reusing the inferred graphs in a separate tanh reservoir improves a delayed-input memory score across human, macaque and mouse comparisons.
sources.application_inference: Signed interaction organization has demonstrated computational consequences beyond simple anatomical resemblance. The result motivates keeping graph structure, interaction sign, phase dynamics and task performance distinct; it does not justify a physical layout for semantic-coordinate populations.
transfer_limits: The primary model is a noisy two-state-variable Hopf oscillator per anatomical brain region, with diffusive coupling G_np*(z_p-z_n), a=-0.02 and noise scale0.01. A negative edge changes both cross-node influence and the diagonal coupling term; it is not equivalent to an isolated inhibitory synapse.

Signs and weights are fitted to zero-lag and lagged fMRI connectivity on an anatomical structural mask. The inferred competition is macroscopic effective influence, not recovered cell-type polarity, semantic-coordinate sign or negative emotional valence.

The positive findings include split-half generalization, stable inferred weights, simulation-based recovery, larger positive-weight range, more positive-only edges, L1 regularization, temporal surrogates and topology/weight controls. These controls are explicitly reported and not treated as absent.

Synthetic recovery is conditional on data generated by the same model family; it does not establish a unique microscopic mechanism for empirical fMRI. Metastability here is standard deviation of phase synchrony, not a per-CC fraction of active FP4 neurons.

Competitive edges are relatively longer, weaker, less modular and less clustered than cooperative edges. This is a fitted organization over a given anatomy, not a universal near-neighbor preference or a prescribed interaction between our positive/negative populations.

The separate memory benchmark uses x(t+1)=tanh(W_in*u+W*x), fixed reservoir weights, visual input nodes, motor readouts and ridge regression. It is driven delayed-input reconstruction, not autonomous semantic-sequence replay, and it does not use the Hopf update equation.

The score sums absolute Pearson correlations over20lags, not the conventional sum of squared correlations. Reported means increase4.27→4.35 in humans (~1.87%),4.31→4.63 in macaques (~7.42%), and4.15→4.45 in mice (~7.23%). Human standardized effect magnitude is0.30; the larger fitting gains must not be substituted for this modest task gain.

Reservoirs are spectral-radius normalized and swept across16values0.1–1.6. Methods use4050input points,70:30train/test,50-step washout,10input-node selections and retain the best test performance across radii. A separate radius-selection validation split is not described in these methods, so this is an optimized comparative benchmark rather than untouched final-test performance.

Reported degree-preserving topology controls matter differently by endpoint: metastability fit can be reproduced once degree is preserved, whereas FC, cognitive-pattern and memory outcomes are more topology-sensitive. The denser positive-only macaque reservoir is an explicit exception to one memory comparison.
No CC-scale sparse learning, Flash input basis, FP4/FP8 quantization or long-lived low-activity band is tested. No interaction rule or runtime structure is adopted.

sources.authors: Jessica Royer, Casey Paquola, Raul Rodriguez-Cruces and colleagues
sources.title: Human cortical dynamics reflect graded contributions of local geometry and network topography
sources.publication_status: Published online26December2025; Nature Communications volume17/article1002 in2026.
sources.evidence_type: Intracranial electrophysiology spectral-similarity gradients compared with geometry, microstructure and connectivity across discovery and replication cohorts
sources.read_scope: Published results sections3–5 and methods9,11,12 read; discussion read selectively. Figure2 and its caption visually inspected on PDF pages5–6. Supplement controls are recorded from main descriptions rather than independently inspected plots.
sources.finding: Physical geodesic proximity is the strongest global correlate among the tested predictors of spectral-profile similarity, while microstructure and connectivity add more explanatory value in transmodal regions. The result varies with cortical region and cohort.
sources.application_inference: Even within biological cortex, a single distance law does not capture all functional relationships equally. The learned coordinate space of spectral similarity must not be mistaken for the cortical sheet or a mapping of individual semantic dimensions to neuron positions.
transfer_limits: Discovery uses106 epilepsy patients with over1700 non-epileptic channels and separate MRI cohorts of50 at3T and10 at7T. Replication uses18 patients with within-cohort multimodal imaging. This is macroscale group inference, not a single-CC neuronal map.

The embedding is derived from log power spectra and partial correlations controlling the cortex-wide mean, followed by normalized-angle affinity and diffusion maps. Fourteen gradients retain50% of the selected variance; the displayed two dimensions retain17.37%. The paper does not demonstrate a faithful two-dimensional physical realization of response space.

Geodesic distance is multiplied by−1 for the Figure2 comparison. The reported−0.376 correlation is therefore between embedding distance and negative anatomical distance, not an inverse relationship between two raw distances. The caption resolves this sign convention.

Across-edge adjusted R-squared ranges approximately0.147–0.171, with90/10edge-resampling median ranges0.142–0.161. The strongest predictor among those tested does not explain most variation. Edge resampling is distinct from the independent-cohort and leave-patient-out analyses also reported.

Regional gains from microstructural similarity/connectivity concentrate in transmodal areas, and replication shows somewhat different modality contributions. This supports heterogeneous relationships rather than a universal distance-only mechanism.

Main preprocessing reflects left channels to the right hemisphere, extrapolates each channel spectrum within5mm and averages into100right-hemisphere parcels. Bilateral, parcellation, coverage and embedding-parameter controls are reported. These choices and spatial autocorrelation-preserving nulls belong to the inference, not to a neuronal learning rule.

Spectral-profile similarity does not measure semantic tuning, connection probability, directed influence or a stable recurrent attractor. The study is correlational and supplies no missing physical coordinates for our assigned semantic roles.

sources.authors: Jordan K. Matelsky and colleagues
sources.title: Physical contact reveals a hidden layer of cortical architecture
sources.publication_status: bioRxiv preprint, version 1; not peer-reviewed evidence
sources.evidence_type: Segmentation-derived physical-contact graphs compared with synaptic graphs in two mouse visual-cortex volumes
sources.read_scope: XML results S3/S4, discussion S7, methods S9–S14, Tables1–3 and all figure captions. Glial result sections and supplemental queries not fully reviewed; no PDF/figure visual verification.
sources.finding: Physical cell appositions greatly outnumber synaptic partnerships. The Pinky halo analysis finds that many cells near an existing arbor already contact it.
sources.application_inference: Anatomical opportunity and selected functional influence are different relations. This does not supply a contact graph for the application.
transfer_limits: Contacts are undirected segmentation-boundary adjacency at coarse voxel resolution, not necessarily axon-to-dendrite synapse candidates. Whole-arbor halos are not soma-centered distance neighborhoods.

Pinky/Minnie contact-to-synapse density ratios11.74/3.853 and synaptic filling fractions3.41%/2.81% cannot be combined under a common simple-graph universe without additional definitions; ANA-050 checks this.
Full contact degree includes untyped partners. It is neither incoming synapse degree nor a justified slot capacity.
Area units remain unresolved between methods normalization to nm² and table labeling. Numerical membrane-area estimates are excluded from application sizing.
Snapshot appositions do not establish remodeling probability, electrical coupling or useful recurrent dynamics.

sources.authors: Lee Cossell, Maria Florencia Iacaruso, Dylan R. Muir and colleagues
sources.title: Functional organization of excitatory synaptic strength in primary visual cortex
sources.evidence_type: In-vivo response characterization followed by in-vitro paired electrophysiology in mouse V1 L2/3
sources.read_scope: Primary PMC author manuscript: all main results/discussion paragraphs; paired recording, RF fitting, connection-prediction statistics and input-to-single-cell simulation methods. Main Figure 4 and Extended Data Figure 4 visually inspected. No author-code execution or raw-data reproduction.
sources.finding: In a local mouse V1 L2/3 sample, response correlation and RF similarity predict excitatory connection probability and strength more strongly than soma distance. The strongest measured inputs provide feature-matched drive; a stimulus-driven single-target model qualitatively reproduces selective subthreshold modulation.
sources.application_inference: The strongest transferable distinction is selective functional coupling among anatomically nearby candidates, rather than interpreting index proximity as semantic similarity.
transfer_limits: The sample includes 203 matched pyramidal cells from seventeen P22–26 mice and 75 detected connections among 520 assayed directions. Imaging covers about260×260×56 micrometres; slice cutting and the local sampling range limit conclusions about distant alternatives.

The 7% most response-correlated sampled pairs carry50% of total measured weight. Among the45 transformed connected RF pairs, the strongest quartile contributes78% of weight. These are distinct denominators, neither a whole-brain input fraction nor a pruning guarantee.

Prediction performance here is a univariate Pearson association with measured weights and a permutation comparison. It is not a joint causal estimate or held-out prediction of every synapse. RF estimation itself uses repeated75/25 image splits and a smoothness-regularized fit.
RF similarity includes visual position, phase and ON/OFF overlap. Visual coordinates differ from soma coordinates, and neither maps automatically to embedding-coordinate indices.

The simulation pools4,633 measured RFs, aligns experiment RF centers, assigns RF-dependent input weights and normalizes total weight. Presynaptic responses are independently stimulus-generated and summed into one passive R–C target per instance. It is not a closed-loop recurrent simulation, despite the anatomical origin of the modeled inputs.

Removing weak inputs preserves most modeled phase modulation but changes broad depolarization. The paper leaves contextual and plasticity roles for weak connections; it does not establish that weak or low-degree cells are functionless.
The data support selective functional influence within available anatomy, not an invented software distance or autonomous semantic recurrence.

sources.finding: At fixed expected outgoing total strength, modular organization adds competitive modes. Increasing spatial/functional confinement makes local excitation–inhibition fluctuations more consequential.
sources.application_inference: Structured coupling can matter even when global strength is controlled. Its benefit or danger depends on dynamics, not a universal preference for shorter edges.
transfer_limits: The spatial case prescribes uniformly sampled coordinates on a hypertorus and a Gaussian kernel. Functional dimensions are assumed to behave similarly; this does not establish a metric for Flash dimensions.
Equal-sized excitatory modules and linear/threshold-linear stability assumptions constrain transfer. Nonlinear gain functions can change operating regimes.
Global inhibitory feedback cannot generally suppress competitive modes that leave total excitation unchanged; ANA-051 provides a separate exact illustration.
The result is not an autonomous semantic-memory task, a measured cortical-distance law, or a selected homeostatic algorithm.

sources.evidence_type: Equivariant bifurcation analysis and heterogeneous firing-rate network examples

sources.title: A cortical semantic map integrates fractions and integers in the human brain

sources.read_scope: Participant/task/PCA/RSA/tuning methods, vector and topographic results, discussion limitations; Figures3/7 visually inspected on PDF pages12/17. Supplement figures not independently audited.
sources.finding: Numerical magnitude organizes both multivoxel responses and an anterior parietal preference map across fractions and integers.
sources.application_inference: This is positive evidence for learned abstract meaning having spatial organization. The meaningful ordering belongs to represented quantities and task context, not the labels of embedding coordinates.

Cross-run tuning, native-subject maps and smoothed-noise nulls are reported. Voxel acquisition is1.2mm isotropic; tuning uses4mm smoothing. This is not a single-CC cellular wiring map.

Existing local weights are 1/m and interregional weights 1/total incoming degree. The total incoming strength is therefore not constant across the distance sweep (ANA-057), even before firing rates and correlations change.

Structural complexity is a weak-coupling expansion of an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck approximation. Dynamical complexity uses covariance log determinants of mean regional voltages. Pooled ISI skewness/kurtosis alone do not establish joint Gaussian regional voltages, and this Gaussian complexity is not a universal penalty against synchrony (ANA-058).

The main model uses excitatory inputs and sustained Poisson external drive. The paper reports robustness to delays, weak local inhibition and 16/25 regions; these controls must be retained. It does not test semantic roles, sparse slot migration, Hebbian learning or autonomous learned content sequences.

Printed equation 3 has a conductance sign inconsistent with the stated excitation from rest (ANA-059). This is an equation-level reproducibility issue; without implementation evidence it is not a claim that the actual simulations used that sign.

sources.title: Autapses enhance bursting and coincidence detection in neocortical pyramidal cells

sources.read_scope: Results on functional isolation, cell-type selectivity, strength, short-term plasticity, receptor kinetics, bursting and coincidence detection; slice-preparation methods. Published figures 1/2 visually inspected. Full supplementary experiments not independently reviewed.
sources.finding: Excitatory self-connections selectively occur in particular cortical cell classes and can enhance subsequent responsiveness and burst firing; their timing and receptor composition differ from connections between neighboring cells.
sources.application_inference: Self-feedback is a distinct physiological mechanism, not simply the zero-distance endpoint of a universal pairwise locality rule. A recurrent connection can shape transient timing without supporting persistent autonomous activity.

Among projection-defined layer-5 populations the rates ranged from 2.6% for contralateral-PFC-projecting cells to 84.8% for habenula-projecting cells. These are sample- and protocol-dependent frequencies, not application probabilities.

Human evidence consists of 28 cells from two adult epilepsy patients with pathological frontal tissue; eight showed autaptic currents. It establishes existence in that preparation, not healthy-human cortical prevalence.

Functional autapses were stronger on average than sampled PC-to-PC connections, showed short-term depression and no detected NMDA component under the tested conditions. The main dynamic-clamp manipulation used 1.4 ms delay and conductances including values above the measured maximum; the source distinguishes these ranges.

The authors explicitly did not observe persistent activity outlasting evoked spikes in their tested autaptic cells, even near threshold (n=6). Positive burst/coincidence effects should therefore not be relabeled as a demonstration of autonomous memory loops.

No rule to include or exclude self-edges, no near-neighbor exemption, and no additional state or receptor variable is adopted. These findings constrain biological analogies rather than define the application neuron model.

sources.title: Exact linear theory of perturbation response in a space- and feature-dependent cortical circuit model
sources.evidence_type: Analytical recurrent-circuit theory, numerical simulations and constrained fits to mouse V1 perturbation measurements
sources.read_scope: Final PNAS article main formulation, spatial/feature response and gain results, fitting and discretization methods; targeted source audit AUD-029. Published PDF text was accessible through web indexing; local publisher PDF download was blocked. Released author figure panels 1C, 2C and 4C were downloaded at a pinned commit, hash-verified and visually inspected. Supplementary proofs were not independently reproduced.
sources.finding: An exactly solvable spatial kernel permits stable strong-coupling response analysis beyond the convergence regime of a path-series expansion. Excitation/inhibition and gain can alter the sign, width and feature dependence of net influence without corresponding changes of anatomical connection width.
sources.application_inference: Measured influence range is an emergent circuit property. It cannot alone identify a direct wiring-distance preference, especially when only a subset of cell types is stimulated or observed. The positive fit and sparse controls make this a substantive alternative explanation, not merely a theoretical objection.
transfer_limits: The analysis assumes a spatial continuum, translation-invariant factorized space/feature kernels, fixed feature preferences and small perturbations about a stable operating point. It is not a learned semantic-loop model.

Continuous-time stability and convergence of the Neumann path expansion are different conditions; see ANA-064. Unequal time constants require checking the full dynamical Jacobian; the general analysis invokes sufficiently fast inhibition.

The two-dimensional Green-function kernel is singular at zero separation. The numerical grid sets same-location connections to zero as a discretization convention. This is not a biological exclusion zone to transfer to the application.

The empirical fit constrains the circuit to be stable overall with an unstable excitatory-only subcircuit, and imposes anatomical bounds. Thus its inhibition-stabilized character is a fitting assumption, not an unconstrained discovery from the perturbation curves.

The 24,000-neuron fit omits selectivity variability by assigning full tuning, uses an 85/15 excitatory/inhibitory mix and tau_I=tau_E/2, and analyzes the best 50 of 200 accepted parameter fits. Similar response curves admit substantial parameter variation.

Connectivity-product fits combine connection probabilities and strengths from different experiments; unmeasured portions use stated interpolation/extrapolation and symmetry assumptions. Sparse and heterogeneous-gain controls are present and must not be described as absent.

The sparse control can impose monotone conditional connection strength and preserve a chosen norm of the expected kernel rather than its entire pointwise shape. This tests robustness to an additional change; it is not an exact same-mean sparse realization in every configuration.
questions: Which circuit properties remain identifiable when perturbation responses are observed only in selected populations, and which are inherited from the model constraints?

sources.title: Single-neuron network topology governs neural computation and learning in primate cortex
sources.evidence_type: Longitudinal primate calcium imaging, inferred functional graphs and statistical prediction
sources.read_scope: Main network, hub, modularity and selected learning-prediction results; imaging, cell matching, graph construction, spatial controls, null models, causality-index and regression methods. Published figure 1 visually inspected. Raw recordings and supplementary figures were not independently reanalyzed.
sources.finding: Functional hubs and modules are associated with stronger task encoding and coordinated learning-related changes. Hub/non-hub populations overlap spatially, while functional modules show spatial clustering. Most fields show no significant relationship between inferred pair weight and soma distance.
sources.application_inference: Spatially overlapping functional roles and spatially structured modules can coexist. Functional organization can change without moving cells; this is relevant to distinguishing learned relationships from fixed semantic assignments, but supplies no physical coordinates for the application.
transfer_limits: Two monkeys contributed 59 sessions across 12 fields, unevenly distributed as 7 versus 52 sessions. Each field was tracked over 3–7 days. The reported 8,537 neuronal observations should not be treated as that many independent cells from independent animals.

Typical inferred networks contain 144 plus/minus 22 neurons and density 0.048 plus/minus 0.013. Edges are undirected partial correlations of pre-cue activity, thresholded at P<0.001, not reconstructed synapses. Positive weights define core status; signed weights enter modularity; shortest paths use inverse absolute weights.

The core/periphery partition uses a conventional resolution parameter and gives roughly equally sized groups. This is not evidence for a rare anatomical high-degree class or a particular incoming-degree exponent. The heavy-tailed comparison does not estimate the application’s static capacity law.

The causality index is a lagged partial correlation, often using condition-averaged activity. Classical Granger analysis supports the reported directionality pattern, but neither is a controlled neuronal intervention. Graph ablation is analytical node removal, not biological ablation.

Strength/degree-preserving randomization, trial shuffling, tracking-quality and fluorescence/size controls are reported and retained. Statistical functional-network structure must nevertheless be interpreted with estimator-specific nulls; LOC-134/135 do not directly invalidate this study’s partial-correlation results.

Some encoding-prediction analyses use an unthresholded matrix, unlike the principal sparse graph. Within-session and next-day regressions are not evidence that the same physical synapses or wiring capacities were measured.

Absence of a significant pairwise weight-distance effect in these 800-by-800-micrometer fields is not proof that anatomical locality is absent; the authors explicitly discuss indirect influence and spatial sampling limits.
questions: Which reported functional graph properties remain under alternative estimators and matched observation models, and which have direct anatomical or perturbational support?

sources.title: Constructing mesoscale functionomics by neural dynamics subspace clustering
sources.evidence_type: Activity-based clustering benchmarked on known simulated modules and large-scale mouse calcium recordings
sources.read_scope: Main framework, simulated-module benchmark, anatomical-area comparison, decision-making application and discussion; anchor and multi-session methods. Eight released source files audited in AUD-030. XML equations encoded as images were not available as readable formula text; released code establishes the audited optimization. Publisher full PDF was blocked, and no bypass was attempted. Supplementary simulation details and raw calcium data were not reproduced.

sources.application_inference: Functional grouping can be investigated without presupposing a spatial metric. The resulting groups are descriptions of recorded dynamics, not synapse lists, physical coordinates or mandatory replacements for assigned minicolumn roles.
transfer_limits: The main simulation contains five predefined modules with sparse within-module and still sparser between-module connections. Reported accuracy remains about 98 percent at inter-module probability 0.2; multiple alternative clustering methods and cluster-number sensitivity controls are included.

The initial atlas comparison records about 10,000 cortical neurons in two mice; the learning-related cue-cluster expansion uses three mice. Repeated algorithm runs are not independent animal replications.

Clustering is unsupervised with respect to behavioral labels and spatial positions, but requires a cluster count, anchor count and regularization setting. The paper acknowledges empirical cluster-number selection for smooth spectra. The released simulation demo obtains the number of clusters from ground-truth labels.

The code performs box-constrained L2-regularized linear reconstruction on K-means anchor traces, then takes absolute coefficients and applies SVD/K-means. This does not generally yield sparse coefficients or a directed synaptic graph; see ANA-067.

Body-movement signals remain strong in leading cluster components, while other components carry differentiated task information. This is evidence for coexistence of shared and specialized dynamics, not complete removal of movement effects.

State-shift simulation rewires selected neurons by design. Recovering these shifted labels does not establish a biological learning rule, and changing a learned functional grouping must not be conflated with changing the application’s fixed coordinate/polarity identity.

The logical-gate analogy requires distinguishing signed correlation, absolute dependence and joint information. ANA-068 gives explicit conditional examples; it does not claim to reproduce the inaccessible figure’s input distribution or information calculation.
questions: Can functional groups provide explanatory or predictive value beyond the same activity used to construct them, while preserving fixed semantic roles and independently testing the desired recurrent behavior?

Threshold/density changes have large effects. Very large small-world ratios can involve disconnected graphs or small null clustering; a connected-only control still shows substantial effects up to roughly ten in the reported range.
Degree-preserving nulls weaken but do not eliminate the effect. Matching graph degree does not automatically match the dependence constraints of a correlation estimator.

The main result concerns thresholded Pearson correlation. It must not be applied unchanged to signed, partial, lagged or intervention-based measurements; LOC-135 specifically reports that partial-correlation null effects can differ.
The finding does not show that coactivity is useless as a learning objective or that a useful learned graph must reconstruct biological wiring.

Lagged correlation is effective in selected sparse nonlinear cases; derivative covariance performs better for the tested linear systems. sources.authors: Gaspar Cano and Richard Kempter
sources.title: Conditions for replay of neuronal assemblies
sources.evidence_type: Spiking-network simulations and analytical population model
sources.read_scope: Sequence retrieval and minimal-model results; analytical replay conditions; principal assumptions and limitations; assembly and plasticity discussion; replay measurement methods. Published figure 1 and equation (9)/Condition 3 on PDF pages 4 and 16 visually inspected. Selected released source reviewed in AUD-032; no author simulations executed.
sources.finding: Within-assembly recurrent excitation can amplify weak feedforward activation enough to propagate a sequence. This occurs with assembly-specific inhibition, global inhibition, or no inhibitory neurons in a suitable parameter regime. The required connection strengths and replay speed depend on the membrane-potential distribution, synaptic timing and leak. The abstract population model supplies useful necessary conditions and accurate fast-pulse approximations under stated assumptions.
sources.application_inference: Provides a concrete computational role for functional recurrent grouping without a physical coordinate metric. The relevant unit is an activity assembly, not necessarily one semantic dimension or minicolumn. It motivates distinguishing propagation success from repeated autonomous cycling, without selecting an assembly mechanism.
transfer_limits: The principal spiking experiment embeds one open chain of ten non-overlapping assemblies, each with 500 excitatory cells. The full E/I network has 20,000 excitatory and 5,000 inhibitory cells; the minimal model has 5,000 excitatory cells. Assembly edges are prescribed rather than learned; interference and memory capacity are outside the study.

All cells of the first assembly are triggered simultaneously after an asynchronous baseline. In the first two models, inhibitory STDP prepares that baseline and is then disabled. The no-inhibition model uses tuned background current and Poisson input; it is not an undriven autonomous loop.

Replay acceptance includes ordered activity peaks, appropriate delay, 90–110% as many spikes as assembly neurons in the fitted pulse interval, and limited background activity. Parameters are accepted when at least 80% of 25 attempts succeed. The spike-count criterion does not independently prove that 90% of distinct cells each fired once.

The population approximation assumes effectively one spike per cell during replay and omits reset, leak and inhibition. Its analytical conditions do not predict the high-connectivity bursting region or failure of very slow pulses due to leak; the authors explicitly describe these limits.

The 90–110% pulse criterion is a temporal per-assembly spike count, not the application’s per-CC active-fraction band. Theoretical minimum assembly-size estimates are conditional on biological PSP/distribution parameters, not a reason to equate a minicolumn with an assembly or change its 60+60 allocation.
questions: Which experimentally useful grouping and recovery mechanisms would preserve fixed semantic roles while permitting repeated loops and overlapping represented states?

retrieval.title: Conditions for replay of neuronal assemblies

sources.authors: András Ecker, Daniela Egas Santander and colleagues
sources.title: Assemblies, synapse clustering, and network topology interact with plasticity to explain structure-function relationships of the cortical connectome
sources.evidence_type: Biophysically detailed cortical simulation with selected MICrONS structural/functional comparisons
sources.read_scope: Model overview, stability, dendritic clustering, selected topology and before/after functional results; assembly detection, synapse-cluster selection, control STDP/random walk, MICrONS and simulation-cost methods. Figure 8 on PDF page 16 visually inspected. Publisher canonical Version-of-Record page links a PDF named elife-101850-v1.pdf; that filename is not treated as a preprint version claim.
sources.finding: In a 211,712-neuron model, calcium-dependent plasticity produces sparse synaptic changes and stable firing during ten simulated minutes. Stimulus-specific assembly sequences become more reliable for most tested patterns, while single-neuron reliability slightly decreases. Dendritic synapse clustering, co-firing and higher-order connection structure help explain where changes occur. Selected topology/strength and topology/correlation associations also occur in MICrONS.
sources.application_inference: Useful evidence that group-level functional reliability can improve without increased average firing or improved individual-cell reliability. Dendritic input grouping supplies a distinct computational mechanism; it is not physical distance between assigned semantic-role cells.
transfer_limits: The detailed model includes active dendritic compartments, calcium dynamics, multivesicular synapses and coupled short-/long-term plasticity. Its 312,709,576 plastic synapses and reported computation cost do not transfer to the application’s flat FP4 cell state and five-byte logical connection slot.

The stimulus protocol repeats ten thalamic input patterns in random order at 500-ms intervals. Improved driven response sequences do not establish self-sustaining semantic loops or long-term stability under the application’s three regimes.

The pair-based STDP control processes spikes recorded from the calcium-plasticity simulation offline. It compares weight changes under those spike trains, not two fully closed-loop networks with separately evolving activity.

Assembly detection uses 20-ms bins, activity/significance thresholds, Ward clustering and a selected number of clusters. A forced-equal-cluster-count control preserves the reported splitting result. This control is useful but does not establish held-out recurrent task performance.

The dendritic cluster analysis selects ten highly innervated/high-clustering L5 thick-tufted cells per assembly. Within-assembly clustered synapses are not uniformly the most plastic: many early/middle-assembly clusters begin potentiated and remain stable; non-clustered within-assembly synapses change more consistently, and clustered cross-assembly synapses can potentiate.

MICrONS synapse volume is a structural proxy for strength; calcium/spike correlations are observations, not measured direct causal coupling. Its comparisons validate selected associations rather than every detail of the rat simulation or a universal cortical mechanism.
questions: Which group-level functional measure would be useful independently of mean active fraction, and would any dendritic abstraction justify its extra state and semantics?
