sources.authors: Michael W. Reimann, Daniela Egas Santander, Lida Kanari and Natalí Barros-Zulaica
sources.title: Spatial continuity of neurons explains non-random network architecture
sources.evidence_type: Anatomical connectome analysis and stochastic graph-generation model
sources.read_scope: Central hypothesis, selected morphology/MICrONS and generative-model results, limitations, graph model/customizations/null models and nearest-neighbor statistical methods in full-text XML. Six tagged source/config files inspected in AUD-033. No figure image, full supplement or raw connectome reproduction is claimed.
sources.finding: Knowing that a neuron connects to a physical neighbor of a candidate predicts increased connection probability. The study separates a global contribution from heterogeneous degree and a spatially structured contribution beyond its configuration-model control. A stochastic spread graph over a geometric base graph can reproduce several anatomical graph statistics better than the compared simple distance-dependent and preferential-attachment models.
sources.application_inference: Biological locality can induce dependencies between edges, not merely a scalar decay in independent pairwise probability. Heterogeneous allocation alone does not establish those dependencies, and statistical associations caused by degree heterogeneity should not be mistaken for a physical-neighborhood effect.
transfer_limits: The main MICrONS analysis uses one anatomical volume, with 1,680 axon-proofread presynaptic cells and 45,598 excitatory candidate targets. Many sampled pairs are not independent animals. Potential morphology-derived contacts and actual synaptic edges are separately analyzed.

The configuration control preserves degrees only approximately: self and duplicate edges are removed after endpoint shuffling. Its spatially specific excess should be retained as a positive finding, while exact-degree matching is not claimed.

The fitted model starts from actual soma positions and adds axis scaling, directional bias and empirical cell-class propensities. Layer-2/3 transfer retains d and p but changes other settings; it is not a parameter-free test.

The study reports structural motif and degree fits, not a recurrent task or autonomous-loop advantage. Lognormal/heavy-tailed degree descriptions do not determine the application’s provisional capacity-class law.

The released generator has unresolved differences from the printed candidate-exclusion and multiplicity rules (AUD-033). This limits reuse of the exact algorithm/theoretical limits; it does not undo the independently reported anatomical associations.
The physical coordinates and axonal morphology presupposed here are absent from the application. No base graph, geometric spread rule, synthetic positions or contact graph is adopted.
questions: Which higher-order connectivity features carry an independently measured functional benefit, beyond matching an anatomical graph?

retrieval.title: Spatial continuity of neurons explains non-random network architecture

sources.authors: Ilenna Simone Jones, Maceo Richards, Houman Safaai, Elom Amematsro and Bernardo Sabatini
sources.title: Synaptic clustering emerges from learning and supports covariance discrimination
sources.evidence_type: arXiv preprint v1: task-trained dendritic network and conditional analytical argument; no peer-reviewed publication verified
sources.read_scope: Task, architecture, optimization, ablations, null-normalized clustering, selected results, discussion and limitations; theorem 3.1 and final proof steps on page 25. Figure 2 on page 8 visually inspected. No author-code execution or empirical biological experiment is claimed.
sources.finding: On a synthetic four-class covariance-discrimination task, learned sparse inputs to nonlinear dendritic subunits improve parameter efficiency over the compared matched MLPs. Rewiring at a fixed neuron-wide synapse budget leads to task-dependent excitatory/inhibitory input grouping. Shuffling learned synaptic organization damages held-out accuracy even while preserving nonlinearities.
sources.application_inference: A concrete example of useful learned functional grouping with input identities held fixed, and without defining a physical distance between those inputs. Its mechanism is nonlinear joint integration within a branch, which would require an explicit representational/update decision before any transfer to our cells.
transfer_limits: This is a feedforward classifier, not a recurrent SNN. It uses four readout neurons with binary trees of subunits, 200 input channels and four predefined covariance-block permutations. It does not test token semantics, DMN/flow/immersion or autonomous activity.

Gaussian-copula inputs have identical uniform marginal distributions across classes; latent within/between-block correlations are 0.9/0.3, not the exact Pearson correlations after the CDF transform. These are constructed task statistics, not measured Flash or cortical correlations.

Training uses Adam/backpropagation, separate learning rates, weight decay, gradient clipping, early stopping and task labels. The main seven-compartment setting has 140 excitatory and 140 inhibitory synapses per readout neuron; branch fan-in changes under that total budget. This does not validate a local Hebbian training rule or the application’s static class distribution.

Forty seeds per ablation condition, held-out test samples, parameter/depth/sparsity comparisons and a fan-in/weight-preserving entropy null are meaningful controls. Dense parameter counts are not direct CPU/FP4 memory-cost measurements.

The post-training shuffle changes other learned connectivity properties in addition to functional clustering, as the authors acknowledge. Figure 2F shows several ablated conditions above chance; the defensible result is a large relative loss, not a universal impossibility of above-chance computation without all three components.

The clustering theorem concerns binary supports with s no greater than block size, a linearized variance ratio and an expected random competing partition. It is not a global optimality proof for the nonlinear dendritic tree, arbitrary signed weights or the three realized competing classes.

Branches are discrete computational subunits; continuous synaptic distance and temporal dynamics are absent. Excitatory/inhibitory input labels are not the application’s positive/negative semantic-coordinate populations.
questions: Can a useful grouping objective be established for fixed semantic roles and recurrent tasks before introducing any new compartment or location representation?

sources.authors: Tristan Geiller and colleagues
sources.title: Local circuit amplification of spatial selectivity in the hippocampus
sources.evidence_type: Primary experimental study and rate-network model; PMC author manuscript; published online December 2021, issue January 2022
sources.read_scope: Introduction/results, recruitment criteria, photostimulation, rate model and plasticity methods, discussion and limitations. Main Figure 4 visually inspected. Not a complete supplement or raw-data reproduction.
sources.finding: Inducing a place field in one CA1 pyramidal cell can recruit a small local group whose subsequent fields favor the induced represented location. Presynaptic inhibitory populations become anti-tuned to established fields. Successful induction, failed induction, pre-induction activity, and light without an electroporated starter provide important controls.
sources.application_inference: A positive example of recurrent amplification and experience-dependent functional cooperation while external input preferences are specified. The represented belt location, physical soma separation and network membership are three different quantities; none supplies a distance between our assigned semantic dimensions.
transfer_limits: Successful field induction occurred in seven of fourteen sessions in six mice. Recruitment averages about 12.6 cells and later field changes are assessed after rest. The result is not immediate universal field conversion or a self-sustaining autonomous loop.

The recruitment analysis explicitly excludes cells already tuned to the induced belt location. Presynaptic labeling followed imaging to limit rabies-related physiological confounding; nineteen starter networks were examined, eight with stable fields.

The rate model starts with random baseline connectivity and a designated strongly coupled seed subnetwork. Feedforward place preferences are assigned, while recurrent and inhibitory effects change through specified potentiation/depression stages; these are not learned physical coordinates or an online local STDP demonstration.

The model uses separate excitatory and inhibitory populations, graded rates and additional state. The authors explicitly discuss stability problems that potentiation and disinhibition may require other processes to counteract. Its assumptions are not adopted for FP4 application cells.
The experimental circuit has actual anatomy. Local causal recruitment does not show that arbitrary software coordinates would preserve its computation. No code or datasets were executed.
questions: Can a comparable functional amplification benefit be stated for fixed semantic I/O roles without redefining their meaning or assigning anatomy?

sources.authors: Bert Vancura and colleagues
sources.title: Inhibitory control of sharp-wave ripple duration during learning in hippocampal recurrent networks
sources.evidence_type: Primary simultaneous calcium/LFP and behavioral observations; PMC author manuscript
sources.read_scope: Subtype-specific ripple dynamics, learning comparisons, limitations, LFP/imaging methods, modulation index, duration bins and statistics. Printed main Figure 5 is HTML F14 and was visually inspected; HTML F5 is Extended Data Figure 5, also inspected. Full supplement not reproduced.
sources.finding: CA3 CCK-cell suppression before sharp-wave ripple onset and PV basket-cell activation after onset correlate with longer events. Learning-related duration increases and subtype changes differ from simple increases in event occurrence. Passive sensory controls increase occurrence without the same duration effect.
sources.application_inference: The timing and type of inhibition can matter separately from an overall activity fraction. This supports distinguishing event initiation, extension and termination when evaluating the requested regimes, without deciding a controller or interneuron representation.
transfer_limits: Despite the title, these subtype-duration relationships are observational. The authors call for necessity and sufficiency interventions. They do not establish that one subtype alone sets duration.

The before/after measures average calcium over 500-ms windows around onset; calcium and recording rates do not resolve each synaptic interaction. Ripple durations are defined from LFP events, not from individual-neuron activation windows.
Learning and nonlearning days are distinguished by anticipatory-lick improvement. CA2 and CA3 differ; a universal cortical inhibitory law cannot be inferred.
Only awake animals and the studied CA3a region are sampled. Contralateral CA1 LFP can miss local ipsilateral events; imaging samples limited cells and is not a complete recurrent-state measurement.
No prospective power calculation or blinding; exclusions and normality assumptions are stated. The study supplies neither semantic valence nor a physical metric for our cells.
questions: Which observable should separate state-dependent sequence duration from the per-CC active-fraction band?

sources.authors: Luis Carrillo-Reid, Shuting Han, Weijian Yang, Alejandro Akrouh and Rafael Yuste
sources.title: Controlling Visually Guided Behavior by Holographic Recalling of Cortical Ensembles
sources.evidence_type: Primary two-photon ensemble perturbation and behavior; PMC author manuscript
sources.read_scope: Ensemble/CRF identification, optical specificity, random disruption, low-contrast and no-cue recall, photostimulation, behavioral session selection, analytical methods and statistics. Main Figures 6 and 7 visually inspected. Associated general CRF source selectively audited as AUD-034.
sources.finding: Holographic stimulation of two functionally selected pattern-completion cells can recall a larger visual ensemble and improve low-contrast Go performance. Random non-Go activation disrupts ensemble identity and degrades behavior. These interventions provide positive evidence that functionally defined ensembles can be causally useful, beyond a correlational graph description.
sources.application_inference: A functional statistical model can identify useful intervention targets without itself being a map of anatomical synapses or requiring a physical-distance objective. This supports examining cooperation among fixed semantic-role cells while preserving the distinction between selection evidence and wiring inference.
transfer_limits: Low-contrast performance improves from about 58.3% to 82.6% in six mice with visual drive present. This is driven completion, not a demonstration of autonomous sustained recurrent activity.

Without visual or behavioral cues, full ensemble recall occurs in only about 5% of photostimulation trials. The reported roughly 70.8% behavioral response is conditional on successful recall; partial recall has about 18.3%. These are not unconditional success rates.
Ensembles are intermingled or dispersed within the imaged local field. This does not establish absence of anatomical constraints across the cortex or justify arbitrary geometry in the application.
Calcium population vectors use approximately 200-ms frames; stimulation is 20 Hz for one second. The experiment does not resolve exact spike-order learning or establish loop lengths.
Optical controls compare targeted and nearby untargeted responses and spontaneous activity across target counts. Random disruption is not selective necessity testing of the identified ensemble alone.

The first and last three of ten recording sessions are discarded by a stated motivation criterion; conditions occur on different days. Sample-size planning and data collection were not blinded. The paper describes a 90/10 CRF split, but the generic repository is not verified as the exact experimental pipeline.
questions: Can functional selection predict useful cooperation for the specified regimes without importing synapse-map or spatial interpretations?

sources.authors: Antonio Fernández-Ruiz and colleagues
sources.title: Long-duration hippocampal sharp wave ripples improve memory
sources.evidence_type: Primary closed-loop optogenetic ripple-duration manipulation and memory behavior; PMC author manuscript
sources.read_scope: All main-body paragraphs and main Figures 2 and 3, both visually inspected. Full supplementary methods and raw recordings not independently reviewed.
sources.finding: Event-triggered stimulation prolonging ongoing hippocampal ripples improves the memory-dependent outbound component of a maze task relative to unstimulated and randomly delayed stimulation controls. A separate interruption protocol impairs that component. Longer events recruit additional low-baseline-rate cells and route representations.
sources.application_inference: A concrete causal benefit of extending an appropriately timed recurrent event, distinct from increasing stimulation or event count indiscriminately. It motivates separating sequence extent, participating identities and timing from a scalar activity-fraction constraint.
transfer_limits: The intervention uses bilateral CA1 excitation triggered by naturally initiated events and calibrated light; random control stimuli are delayed 400–1000 ms. The effect is state/timing dependent, not a generic benefit of more excitation.

Three cohorts each contain five experimental and five sham rats; the interruption experiment uses five previously trained rats. The memory-independent inbound component, running speed, trial counts and several broad LFP measures serve as controls.
The experiment operates inside an intact hippocampal system. It does not identify a self-contained autonomous CC mechanism or distinguish all local and upstream contributions.
A roughly doubled finite ripple duration is not evidence that unlimited persistence, longer loops of any length, or near-fixed activity fractions are optimal.

No physical-distance learning rule, semantic representation, inhibitory subtype mechanism or application controller follows from the result. Some HTML unit rendering is inconsistent, so unverified percentage details are not reused.
questions: What task-level outcome would establish a useful duration range for the application rather than treating persistence alone as success?

sources.authors: Luis Carrillo-Reid, Weijian Yang, Yuki Bando, Darcy S. Peterka and Rafael Yuste
sources.title: Imprinting and recalling cortical ensembles
sources.evidence_type: Primary optogenetic ensemble-imprinting experiment; PMC author manuscript
sources.read_scope: All main text, embedded supplementary captions S1–S7 and main Figures3/4 visually inspected. Supplement PDF retrieval failed; its full methods and images are not claimed as reviewed.
sources.finding: Repeated coactivation creates a cortical photoensemble that later recurs spontaneously and can be recalled by stimulating a suitable member cell. Existing visual ensembles and activity in nonphotostimulated cells remain broadly stable in the reported controls. Recall and enhanced coactivity persist to the next day.
sources.application_inference: Positive evidence that learning can add recurring cooperative patterns within an existing circuit without replacing all prior patterns. It supports distinguishing an input-driven training phase from later spontaneous recurrence, while leaving the application learning rule undecided.
transfer_limits: Population training uses whole-field raster stimulation over4–6 seconds with5–10-second intervals,60–90 trials. Single-cell recall uses a roughly20-Hz spiral protocol. These are controlled interventions, not the application’s token or white-noise encoder.
Only a subset of ensemble members are successful triggers; reported post-training recall is about64.5% with substantial variation. The result is not universal single-cell recall.

Training expands the distribution of recruited cells relative to pretraining single-cell stimulation, yet recalled ensembles remain more spatially restricted than ongoing ensembles. Both spatial comparisons matter; neither demonstrates geometry-free biological connectivity.

The evidence measures coactivity and perturbational recruitment rather than directly measuring every altered synapse. The authors interpret it as Hebbian imprinting; it does not uniquely identify a molecular or numerical weight-update formula.
Spontaneous reappearances on consecutive days are distinct from a continuously self-maintaining activation loop, a calibrated semantic sequence, or a specified per-CC activity fraction.

The novel ensemble overlaps subsets of existing ensembles. Failure to observe the same full pattern before training is not proof of an empty initial circuit; the authors acknowledge recruitment of pre-existing motifs.
questions: Which recurrence outcome should distinguish learned pattern availability from continuously sustained semantic cycling?

sources.authors: Mo Shakiba, Rana Rokni, Mohammad Mohammadi and Nima Dehghani
sources.title: Harnessing cortical geometry, wiring, and function as inductive biases for recurrent neural networks
sources.evidence_type: arXiv preprint v1; task-trained recurrent models with MICrONS-derived priors; no peer-reviewed version verified
sources.read_scope: Main task/ablation results, model/initialization/regularization/training/task methods, network metrics, discussion and selected supplementary tables. PDFpage6 tables visually inspected. Six released text/notebook files selectively inspected in AUD-035 without execution.
sources.finding: The reported function-derived initialization substantially improves task learning; real-coordinate regularization adds gains in some comparisons. Strong performance can survive a joint row/column permutation of initial recurrent weights, and high-performing variants need not share the same modular or small-world metrics.
sources.application_inference: A relevant positive computational comparison, rather than anatomy alone. It motivates asking which aspects of initial weight structure, regularization and geometry produce useful learning. Released-control differences prevent attributing the full gain uniquely to biological placement.
transfer_limits: Although the resource contains nearly12,000 coregistered neurons, the main RNN has312 units; auxiliary fields have70 and160. All are dense trainable ReLU RNNs with learned input/readout weights, Adam supervision and synthetic decision tasks, not614,400 fixed semantic-role FP4 cells.

Biological initialization multiplies lognormal weights by min–max-scaled correlation and STTC, applies a nonzero floor, then rescales spectral radius to0.95. Baselines use orthogonal initialization. This changes several dynamical properties, not just one anatomical prior.

In the released notebook real coordinates are independently normalized to[0,1] per axis, whereas grid coordinates remain raw integer coordinates. With equal nominal coefficients the distance penalties have different scales (ANA-074). The plain-L1 baseline also omits its stored coefficient in __call__. These are source/formalism/control issues to resolve, not proof that all reported benefits disappear.

W! is a node relabeling of the full weighted graph, preserving its spectrum and motifs, rather than an independent edge-value shuffle. Its success cannot establish that the marginal weight histogram alone is sufficient (ANA-075). The paper separately reports a worse ECDF-resampling control.

The EMD term matches flattened communicability-value distributions, not labeled connections. Graph metrics are computed after absolute-value conversion, top10% thresholding and undirected conversion; they are distinct from signed dynamics and live synaptic sparsity.

The notebook and paper differ in task2/3 ordering and the first task’s listed cases; the notebook creates an extra validation dataset not used in the inspected fit/report path. Exact table-generation provenance is unresolved; no independent held-out replication is claimed.

Precision matrices condition zero-lag statistics; they do not in general eliminate all dynamical indirect effects, as already shown in ANA-069. Positive-only recurrence does not identify the application’s positive semantic population with excitation.
questions: Does a benefit remain after matching distance units, effective penalty strength, initialization spectra and evaluation provenance while preserving fixed semantic roles?

sources.authors: Manuel Beiran and Ashok Litwin-Kumar
sources.title: Prediction of neural activity in connectome-constrained recurrent networks
sources.evidence_type: Primary theoretical and computational teacher–student study; PMC author manuscript of published Nature Neuroscience paper
sources.read_scope: Teacher–student setup, output/activity constraints, size/dimensionality results, mismatch controls, empirical-connectome examples, limitations, model/training definitions and selected linear-theory setup. Figure5 visually inspected. Full mathematical proof and released code/data not independently audited. Additional stiffness/susceptibility and optimal-cell-observation sections reviewed: low-rank illustrative examples and linearized observation selection, without treating the selected-model10-cell result as a universal sampling bound.
sources.finding: Networks sharing a synaptic matrix can fit the same task output while exhibiting different single-cell dynamics. Adding recordings from sufficiently many identified neurons can constrain unrecorded activity much more effectively when connectivity is known, even though some neuronal parameters remain unidentified.
sources.application_inference: Structural resemblance and matched output are different validation targets. A wiring prior can be informative without determining dynamics by itself; cellular gains, biases, input and initial state also matter. This supports evaluating the actual requested regimes rather than accepting anatomical graph statistics alone.
transfer_limits: The main cycling teacher has300 rate neurons; a representative activity-recovery threshold is about30 observed cells. Rank-two examples require few recordings because their dynamical dimension is held fixed, not because a universal fixed observation count suffices for every large network.

Empirical connectomes constrain synthetic teachers for fly premotor circuitry, the fly heading system and a zebrafish integrator. These are not simultaneous ground-truth whole-circuit physiological recordings.

Teacher/student inputs and initial conditions are known and matched; teacher measurement noise is absent in the main setup. Unknown external drives, neuromodulation, dendrites and synchrony can invalidate transfer.
The limited analytical model has linear units, unknown additive biases and rank-constrained connectivity. Its exact parameter/dynamics results do not automatically cover all nonlinear SNN states.

The application seeks meaningful semantic recurrence, not exact replication of a particular animal’s single-neuron activity. This paper therefore supplies a distinction and possible evidence standard, not an obligation to reproduce an anatomical connectome.
questions: Which behavioral and state observables actually identify the application’s desired recurrence, beyond matching an aggregate output?

sources.authors: Andrew J. Mocle and colleagues
sources.title: Excitability mediates allocation of pre-configured ensembles to a hippocampal engram supporting contextual conditioned threat in mice
sources.evidence_type: Primary imaging, activity tagging and optogenetic allocation/silencing study; PMC author manuscript
sources.read_scope: Allocation and pretraining tagging interventions, baseline activity/connectivity, task/retrieval comparisons, higher-order ensemble results, NMF/correlation methods and nested-statistics methods. Figure1 visually inspected; Figure4 downloaded but not yet visually reviewed. Full supplementary dataset/code not audited.
sources.finding: Increasing excitability before learning biases a sparse population into a memory-supporting ensemble; silencing that allocated population impairs later recall, unlike silencing a small random control group. Recently active endogenous populations and pre-existing functional subgroups also predict allocation, while higher-order task patterns become more context-specific after training.
sources.application_inference: Partner cooperation can depend on current excitability and prior functional organization as well as coincident input. This is positive evidence for context-sensitive learning within a pre-existing circuit, without giving software semantic-role cells physical coordinates.
transfer_limits: Pretraining tagged populations at10minutes and3hours, unlike24hours, affect later recall. The visual Figure1 confirms10minutes despite an inconsistent1m label in one text sentence; the training-tag comparison is marginal in that figure and should not be overstated.

The two-photon baseline population contains about5% tagged engram cells, while the one-photon retrieval-based definition yields about9% of all imaged cells. Different definitions and observation denominators must not become one universal active-fraction target.
The reported cycling of relative excitability occurs across sampled baseline days. It is not a measurement of continuous short-timescale autonomous loops or proof of a specific oscillator.

Functional connectivity is calcium Pearson correlation compared with1000 circular shuffles. Higher-order groups use sparse NMF of1-second bins with a permutation-based component count and shuffled cell-ID activation control. These are functional analyses, not direct synapse maps.

Engram groups are identified from retrieval activity and then traced retrospectively. Higher-order training/test similarity, unlike pairwise similarity, is not above chance in pretraining homecage sessions. The useful result concerns selective stabilization, not a wholly prewritten memory.

Mixed models account for nested neuron/animal observations where appropriate. The task is aversive contextual memory in hippocampus; semantic coordinate polarity, valence and inhibitory sign remain distinct, and no application excitability state or controller is selected.
questions: Can contextual cell selection and learning preserve coordinate meaning while allowing the functional participation of same-role cells to differ?

sources.authors: Geoffroy Delamare, Douglas Feitosa Tomé and Claudia Clopath
sources.title: Intrinsic Neural Excitability Biases Allocation and Overlap of Memory Engrams
sources.evidence_type: Primary computational rate-network study; published full XML and institutional published PDF
sources.read_scope: All six results subsections; rate, weight, excitability, stimulation, readout, exclusion and integration methods and parameter table; discussion on single-memory learning and inhibition. Figure7 visually inspected. Targeted author-source audit AUD-037; no simulation executed.
sources.finding: A small recurrent network with fixed feedforward preferences, learned recurrent weights, global inhibition and slowly changing excitability produces cue-triggered pattern completion and greater overlap of memories trained close in time. Suppression and reduced-inhibition conditions model earlier biological interventions.
sources.application_inference: Fixed input roles need not prevent learned recurrent cooperation or context-sensitive participation. This is a constructive nonspatial example, but its dense contextual inputs and excitability mechanism do not become an approved semantic-neuron algorithm.
transfer_limits: The network has60 rate cells and30 input cells representing three contexts. Preferred feedforward weights are0.3 and nonpreferred weights0.2; fixed preference is not exclusive one-coordinate drive. Fifteen of the60 cells have no preferred context.

The recurrent matrix is initially zero, all-to-all and plastic with bounds0..1. Homogeneous inhibition depends on total activity. There is no learned physical position or distance kernel and no test at the application static sparse degree distribution.

The model reproduces hours-long allocation/overlap effects using an extra excitability state, activity threshold and12/24-hour decay parameters. These are not short recurrent sequence lengths or application FP4 state semantics.

The claimed behavioral memory strength is an ideal-observer sum of firing during a recall cue. The authors do not evaluate pattern separation and explicitly do not model spontaneous firing except a background-noise control. Quiescent intervals preserve recurrent weights; recall is not autonomous immersion.

Approximately10% of simulation trials are excluded if any rate exceeds100Hz. Figure7 gives explicit exclusions, including11 of100 runs for its size/overlap comparison. Reported successful behavior is therefore not an unconditional stability guarantee.

Overlap requires a bounded range of nonpreferred feedforward drive. Too little fails to recruit the earlier ensemble; too much causes indiscriminate overlap, including a novel context. Inhibition, thresholds, plasticity and excitability jointly affect this trade-off.

The parameter table labels tau_w750/500ms, while Figure7e labels its750-axis in seconds. The pinned public code uses milliseconds, but predates publication and differs in other parameters. Do not silently infer a complete corrected parameter set.

Euler integration uses0.5ms near stimulation and20-second steps during quiescent gaps, with rates below1e-5 set to zero. This is not a resolved continuous simulation of spontaneous inter-event dynamics.
questions: Can same-coordinate cells learn context-specific cooperation while preserving fixed signed coordinate meaning, without importing broad nonpreferred input or an unapproved excitability state?

xml.title: Intrinsic Neural Excitability Biases Allocation and Overlap of Memory Engrams

sources.authors: Toshitake Asabuki and Tomoki Fukai
sources.title: Predictive learning rules generate a cortical-like replay of probabilistic sensory experiences
sources.evidence_type: Primary spiking-network modeling paper, Version of Record16June2025; PDF retains2024 volume footer
sources.read_scope: Main predictive-learning architecture, probability replay, recurrent-strength interventions, inhibitory and homeostatic controls, conditioned priors, distinct inhibitory pathways and Dale-compliant extension; complete neural-model/learning/stimulation/assembly-measure methods and discussion. Figures3 and7 and equation5 page17 visually inspected. Behavioral-fit details and all figure supplements not fully reviewed. Public two-file sample audited without execution.
sources.finding: Predictive plasticity in feedforward and recurrent pathways produces assemblies whose spontaneous total firing reflects stimulus occurrence probabilities. Learned within-assembly excitation and two forms of inhibitory interaction support assembly-specific activity and competition. A Dale-compliant extension retains the central result.
sources.application_inference: This provides a positive nonspatial example of learned spontaneous ensemble activity and distinguishes stabilizing within-assembly inhibition from between-assembly competition. Its statistical measure, learned input roles and additional homeostasis differ from the proposed application.
transfer_limits: The main model uses500 Poisson units, all-to-all modifiable feedforward inputs and two recurrent matrices, one sign-mixed and one inhibitory. The Dale-compliant extension uses500 excitatory plus500 inhibitory cells and two inhibitory pathways; no universal biological E:I ratio is established.

Feedforward selectivity and assembly membership are learned. Even50%-overlapping input patterns form nonoverlapping output assemblies in the reported example. This cannot directly serve as evidence for fixed signed semantic-coordinate cells with distributed overlapping token patterns.

The probability estimator sums mean firing across all cells in each assembly. Neither per-cell rate nor assembly size alone matches the input probabilities. This is neural activity-mass coding, not a demonstration that discrete event visits or ordered loops have those probabilities; see ANA-076.

Fixed-order input does not generate stereotyped sequential transitions in the reported control. The authors explicitly contrast their within-assembly coding with Markovian between-assembly transition learning. Strong positive evidence for stochastic reactivation remains distinct from the required immersion sequences.

Removing structured feedforward input leaves intrinsic Poisson stochasticity and a dynamic gain/threshold variable with10-second history. Homeostasis improves probability accuracy and avoids trivial learning; its proposed intracellular implementation is an open biological question.

Holding inhibition fixed, or disabling it after learning, impairs assembly formation or maintenance in the tested model. Dual-path necessity is conditional on this architecture and objective, not a proof that every stable application requires two explicit inhibitory neuron types.

In the two-subnetwork conditional-prior experiment, activity in one subnetwork changes the other’s assembly firing ratios; assemblies can coactivate. This supports context-conditioned statistics, not exclusive one-state-at-a-time sampling.

Figure3 error bars are standard deviations over five trials; Figure7 bars are standard errors over five trials. These small numerical comparisons do not establish large-network sparse scaling or an activity-fraction acceptance band.

Published transfer-function equations and the pinned sample code differ materially, and the sample training schedule lacks its interval-counter increment. AUD-036/ANA-077 identify the exact limits. No paper result is declared false and no corrected simulation is substituted.
questions: Which of total firing mass, event occupancy, event frequency and transition order is the intended observable for each application regime?

xml.title: Predictive learning rules generate a cortical-like replay of probabilistic sensory experiences

sources.authors: Toshitake Asabuki and Claudia Clopath
sources.title: Embedding stochastic dynamics of the environment in spontaneous activity by prediction-based plasticity
sources.evidence_type: Primary spiking-network study, Version of Record11June2025; PDF retains2024 volume footer
sources.read_scope: Results on learned switching, inhibitory controls, task switching and complex transitions; full discussion; neural model, learning, stimulation, integration and transition-count methods; Figure2 supplement7 caption. Main Figures2 and4 and equation3 page13 visually reviewed. Songbird data-fit details, all supplements and exact figure reproduction remain incomplete. Three-file source snapshot inspected read-only in AUD-038.
sources.finding: With fixed nonoverlapping stimulus preferences, recurrent predictive excitatory plasticity and inhibitory balancing learn spontaneous assembly transitions resembling the trained first-order Markov chain. The model also adapts to changed transition statistics and develops functional communities reflecting a15-state temporal graph without a physical distance kernel.
sources.application_inference: This is a constructive example of fixed input roles plus learned recurrent transitions, closer to the desired self-driven state trajectories than aggregate firing-prior matching. Its units represent preassigned whole stimulus states, however, whereas application cells represent signed coordinates shared by many dense token vectors.
transfer_limits: The standard network has500 excitatory and500 inhibitory Poisson cells with random50% connectivity; a larger example and an800/200 E:I control are also reported. This is not a validation of the application614400-cell static heterogeneous sparse pool.

Every stimulus targets a fixed nonoverlapping excitatory group, lasts200ms and follows the previous one without a gap. During spontaneous measurement, structured stimulation is replaced by constant0.3 drive to excitatory cells and intrinsic Poisson randomness; all weights are frozen. Autonomy here means no structured sequence drive, not absence of sustaining input.

The model learns first-order transitions. The authors explicitly state that their rule does not learn higher-order transitions or transitions across temporally separated states without additional memory. Fixed role meaning and context-specific recurrent participation remain different questions.

Changing training-state duration from200 to100ms leaves spontaneous event-duration distributions nearly unchanged. Matching transition probabilities therefore does not recover the temporal duration of the learned input sequence.

Unequal assembly sizes1:1.5:2 work better than1:2:3. Weaker background drive reduces event rate and increases transition variance, while stronger drive makes transitions more uniform. Learning speed also changes event durations. These controls show substantive parameter dependence rather than a universal stable replay regime.

Only synapses onto excitatory cells are plastic in the base model. With all synapses plastic, replay can fail. The successful mixed-selectivity control specifically gives inhibitory neurons random responses to all states; it does not show that arbitrary overlap among fixed excitatory semantic-coordinate roles is already handled.

Published event detection thresholds each assembly at half its own maximum and counts successors within100ms. The released estimator uses50ms and additional argmax/adjacency conditions; row-normalized conditional transitions do not report all-event coverage, waiting times or self-transitions. See AUD-038 and ANA-078.

The temporal-community diagram is a graph over stimulus states, and PCA is a geometry of evoked population responses. Neither is a measured physical arrangement of the model neurons or a coordinate metric for embedding dimensions.

The paper’s contrast with Hebbian saturation concerns particular unnormalized/bounded rules. It is not proof that every Hebbian or STDP variant cannot learn stochastic sequences; the authors discuss earlier HMM and sequence models separately.

The printed excitatory sigmoid has the same gain/threshold placement discrepancy as LOC-151, while the source uses g(2*u/h). Published positive numerical results remain distinct from literal equation portability.
questions: How can context be retained among same-coordinate cells when a fixed semantic input pattern participates in several different successor sequences?
Which replay coverage, dwell time and transition statistics would express the application requirement without conflating them?

xml.title: Embedding stochastic dynamics of the environment in spontaneous activity by prediction-based plasticity

sources.authors: Ljubica Cimeša, Lazar Ciric and Srdjan Ostojic
sources.title: Geometry of population activity in spiking networks with low-rank structure
sources.evidence_type: Primary theoretical and numerical rate/LIF comparison with constructed connectivity
sources.read_scope: State-space and input-response results including sparse/Dale control; filtering/synchrony comparison; complete rank-two autonomous results and discussion; LIF model, low-rank subspace derivation, Gaussian projection, rank-two mean-field equations and relevant parameter tables. Figures5 and7 visually inspected. Perceptual-task details, full rank-one bifurcation sweep and author code not audited.
sources.finding: Constructed low-rank recurrence supports rich population-pattern dynamics in spiking networks, including out-of-phase oscillations with weak population-average oscillation and ring-shaped slow manifolds ending at fixed points. Low-pass filtered dynamics resemble corresponding rate-network predictions without a physical neuron layout.
sources.application_inference: This is positive evidence that structured recurrence can support state trajectories without spatial coordinates and that a stable population average can coexist with useful internal dynamics. State-space geometry is a geometry of population activity, not a physical metric over semantic-role cells.
transfer_limits: The standard LIF network has12500 cells, a random E/I component with1250 incoming partners per cell and an added constructed low-rank component. Baseline current, independent white noise, reset/refractory behavior and fixed synaptic delay remain present during autonomous dynamics.

The initial dense Gaussian low-rank addition breaks sparsity and can break Dale signs. The paper explicitly tests a masked, sparse/Dale-compliant variant for externally driven unit-rank responses and reports preserved qualitative geometry. That control must be retained, but it is not a demonstrated sparse heavy-tailed rank-two oscillation result at the application scale.

The masked addition is no longer exactly low rank. Small perturbations relative to the background E/I weights preserve signs in the tested setting; a general sign guarantee for arbitrary Gaussian samples or larger amplitudes is not established.

Low-rank vectors and input overlaps are prescribed, not acquired by a tested local learning algorithm. No fixed signed-coordinate semantic representation, FP4 states, FP8 weights or online slot migration is studied.

The rank-two comparison deliberately separates a limit cycle from a nearly degenerate ring of fixed points/slow manifold. Finite-size fluctuations select fixed points on the latter. Similar ring-shaped plots do not establish the same temporal behavior.

Firing-rate geometry depends strongly on the smoothing timescale. One-millisecond filtering exposes fluctuations and synchrony; longer filtering reveals dominant low-dimensional modes. The authors do not establish equivalence for ultra-sparse precise-spike coding.

Exact low-dimensional confinement applies to the activation variable in the constructed rate model. Claims about nonlinear firing-rate projections use weak-response or jointly Gaussian-axis assumptions; dominant PCA dimensions are not a universal exact covariance-rank bound. ANA-079 makes this distinction explicit.

The relevant LIF plots show limited simulated durations, specific noise/delay parameters and substantial rates. They are constructive dynamical examples, not long-term application stability or semantic replay acceptance.
questions: Which information must persist in population patterns while the per-CC activity band remains bounded?
Can an approved learning rule produce the required temporal organization under the existing sparse static capacity, without adding a physical metric?

sources.authors: David Kappel, Bernhard Nessler and Wolfgang Maass
sources.title: STDP Installs in Winner-Take-All Circuits an Online Approximation to Hidden Markov Model Learning
sources.evidence_type: Primary theoretical and numerical stochastic WTA/hidden-Markov learning study
sources.read_scope: Network equations and forward-sampling interpretation; local STDP rule and EM approximation; context-dependent prediction, mixed selectivity, stationary-input trajectories, grammar and rejection-sampling comparisons; principal simulation and correlation-analysis methods. Figures3 and5 visually inspected. Full rejection-sampling proof, every likelihood equation and source code not independently reproduced.
sources.finding: Stochastic WTA circuits learn recurrent context states and can complete cued sequences after afferent input is removed. Multiple interacting WTA groups develop mixed/context-dependent selectivity; a local weight-dependent STDP rule implements a forward-sampling approximation to HMM learning, with more accurate but costlier rejection-sampling extensions.
sources.application_inference: The same input meaning can participate in different temporal contexts carried by recurrent neuronal states. This is positive nonspatial evidence for context-dependent cooperation, not a justification for turning dimension indices into distances.
transfer_limits: Both feedforward and recurrent weights are learned. The basic example uses200 afferent and100 circuit neurons; input identity is encoded by stochastic distributed rate patterns. The model does not retain the application’s fixed per-neuron signed-coordinate assignments.

The theoretical inhibitory signal is an instantaneous log-sum-exp normalization giving a fixed total conditional firing rate within each WTA. This ideal softmax rate constraint is not a demonstrated phase-specific activation-fraction controller or a measured local cortical inhibitory circuit.

The circuit has lateral all-to-all excitation; multiple WTAs restrict competition within groups while permitting excitation across the network. Neither a physical distance kernel nor the application’s static heterogeneous sparse capacity is tested.

Cue patterns last50ms in the first example; a delay is extended to150ms before removing afferent spikes. Figure3 shows short autonomous completion, not arbitrarily long cycling. Numeric experiments include5ms lateral delay, double-exponential EPSPs and refractoriness, while the simplest theoretical analysis omits delay.

Replay similarity is a Spearman rank correlation between a spontaneous trial and100-trial evoked PETH, including only neurons that fired in that spontaneous trial. This measures retained order among observed participants, not complete neuron coverage, precise timing or a full transition-probability matrix.

A stationary500ms input experiment uses704 cells across multiple WTAs. A separate intrinsic-plasticity condition increases participation by regulating excitability toward uniform long-window mean use. That extra mechanism is not part of an approved application state model.

Basic forward sampling is a limited online approximation, not exact posterior inference or guaranteed full EM learning. More accurate rejection sampling requires repeated input presentation and a sequence-wide acceptance/modulatory mechanism.

The simpler grammar task can be distinguished by illegal bigrams; the authors explicitly identify this limitation and use a longer-context task to demonstrate rejection sampling’s advantage. Classification thresholds are derived from the tested sequence likelihoods, so this is not a separately calibrated deployment classifier.

The paper’s dynamics are stochastic and its HMM representation includes stochastic transitions. LOC-152’s contrast concerns the representation and demonstrated replay objective; it should not be generalized into a claim that WTA/HMM models inherently permit only deterministic trajectories.
questions: Can context-dependent neuronal participation be learned while the semantic observation map stays fixed, and what temporal memory is already present in the proposed neuron dynamics?

xml.title: STDP Installs in Winner-Take-All Circuits an Online Approximation to Hidden Markov Model Learning

sources.authors: Johanni Brea, Walter Senn and Jean-Pascal Pfister
sources.title: Matching Recall and Storage in Sequence Learning with Spiking Neural Networks
sources.evidence_type: Primary theoretical/numerical sequence-learning paper; author-hosted published PDF
sources.read_scope: Abstract and model/objective setup; deterministic learnability, Markov/higher-order sequence examples, stochastic targets, fast/slow synaptic-kernel comparison and discussion/limitations. Main Figures2 and4 visually inspected. Some extracted mathematical glyphs are defective; the full online-gradient derivation is not claimed as independently verified. No author code executed.
sources.finding: Learning matched to the assumed neuronal dynamics can reproduce deterministic and stochastic sequence distributions. The paper includes recurring last-to-first transitions and an online learned periodic example without further initial-state clamping. Hidden recurrent states enable examples that cannot be learned with the restricted visible-only one-step model.
sources.application_inference: This supplies a constructive learned-cycling example without a physical distance kernel and emphasizes that plasticity must be assessed together with recall dynamics. It is stronger than a one-pass replay demonstration, while still far from the application’s signed semantic, sparse, quantized and multi-regime requirements.
transfer_limits: Visible neurons receive a teaching signal specifying target activity; hidden neurons evolve without that direct teaching. This is not equivalent to merely adding ordinary token-driven excitation to fixed semantic-coordinate cells, and it does not authorize a new hidden-cell population.

The conditional firing model assumes neurons are independent within a time bin given their membrane potentials, with stochastic sigmoidal output and dynamics linear in synaptic weights. Different synaptic response and adaptation kernels materially change the recall problem.

The visible-only learnability argument concerns a binary one-step threshold/GLM model with specified coding and adjustable weights. Its capacity and linear-separability limits are not universal bounds for FP4 neurons, temporal traces or the current static connection pool.

Non-Markovian visible sequences can become Markovian in an expanded recurrent internal state. A separate hidden-neuron architecture is one constructive realization; the theorem does not prove that the application must add neurons beyond its existing context-capable state.

The stronger hidden-weight learning rule includes a global or semi-global modulation derived from how well visible activity is explained. Its proposed astrocytic implementation is a biological hypothesis, not directly measured validation or a simple pair-only Hebbian rule.

The optimized variational upper bound is not always identical to the desired KL divergence. The authors discuss possible differences of optima and do not establish arbitrary-task global convergence with hidden units.

Figures2A/E show cyclic recall in small binary examples, while Figure4 shows more realistic kernel-dependent spike/rate recall with initial clamping where marked. These conditions must not be merged into a claim that every spiking example is a long autonomous attractor.

Adding a fast synaptic component to a slower one improves one rate-coded replay example; precise spike timing can degrade and become unstable. No universal duration, activation band or distance exponent follows.

The comparison to shuffled fixed hidden weights is not a proof against all reservoirs. The authors explicitly note that a suitable hardwired delay line or sufficiently large random reservoir can remove the need to learn hidden weights, at a potential size cost.
questions: Which aspects of a desired trajectory must be reproduced—state content, duration, ordering, stochastic transitions or continued circulation—and what learning objective matches the chosen neuronal dynamics?
sources.access_note: EuropePMC fullTextXML returned500; the independent public author-hosted published PDF was available. No access restriction was bypassed.

sources.authors: Christian Klos, Daniel Miner and Jochen Triesch
sources.title: Bridging structure and function: A model of sequence learning and prediction in primary visual cortex
sources.evidence_type: Primary spatial spiking structural-plasticity model compared with visual-cortex sequence-recall measurements
sources.read_scope: Model summary, architecture, basic activity, cue recall, connectivity changes, spontaneous transition analysis, persistence, discussion, plasticity and stimulus methods; Figure7 visually inspected. No author code or network simulated.
sources.finding: Distance-biased growth plus temporally asymmetric STDP and stabilizing mechanisms learn directional structure from a moving stimulus. Cue-triggered sequence order and spontaneous forward transitions improve; the trained effect decays over minutes.
sources.application_inference: This positively links structural and functional adaptation, but its locality is supplied by an explicit visual-space-aligned sheet. It does not show how a metric should arise among fixed LLM coordinates or isolate a computational advantage of geometry over a matched nonspatial learner.
transfer_limits: 1000E/200I neurons are randomly placed on a2500×1000micrometre sheet; Gaussian200micrometre connection probabilities and a swept spatial input are explicit assumptions. Excitatory growth begins without EE edges.

Only recurrent EE synapses learn; inhibition is fixed. STDP is accompanied by once-per-second incoming-weight normalization, growth/pruning, per-cell3Hz threshold adaptation and short-term facilitation/depression. These are additional dynamics, not the application's selected state or learning rule.
The source explicitly rescales incoming normalization near sheet boundaries to avoid artificial corner-originating waves. Boundary geometry and normalization therefore interact materially.
The cue-order statistic is a Spearman correlation of smoothed cluster-rate first-peak times. Its reported mean increases0.26→0.30; this is not an almost-certain full sequence replay.

Spontaneous transitions order every relative maximum of each smoothed cluster rate. Figure7 shows a modest directional shift over30network realizations, not an event-defined repeated complete cycle or semantic transition distribution.

The cue-recall improvement decays in approximately5minutes in the model; cited rat data approximately7minutes. Recall speed differs from training speed. Neither timing preservation nor long-term autonomous circulation is established.
Midpoint/endpoint cue outcomes do not fully match the cited experiment. Multiple branching sequences, disparate assemblies and richer inhibitory plasticity remain outside the tested task.

sources.authors: Yann Sweeney, Jeanette Hellgren Kotaleski and Matthias H. Hennig
sources.title: A Diffusive Homeostatic Signal Maintains Neural Heterogeneity and Responsiveness in Cortical Networks
sources.evidence_type: Primary spiking-network and mean-field model of nitric-oxide-mediated homeostatic feedback
sources.read_scope: All Results and Discussion; network, diffusion, non-diffusive and mean-field homeostasis, mixed-mechanism, timing and orientation-decoding methods. Printed Eq11 visually checked on PDFp19; selected released source inspected separately. No simulation replication.
sources.finding: In finite network experiments, feedback influenced by other neurons permits heterogeneous firing while regulating mean activity and improves response linearity and a simple population-vector decoding task relative to the tested individual-cell homeostasis controls.
sources.application_inference: This isolates a useful candidate computational role of biological spatial signaling: share regulation across a population instead of independently forcing every cell to one rate. A nonspatial mean-field comparison captures part of the effect, so the result does not itself require adding physical positions. The application has not chosen a controller or extra state.
transfer_limits: The main5000cell80/20E/I network has sparse random connectivity independent of random positions. NO diffusion uses a2Dtorus; spatially decaying synaptic connectivity is an additional control with qualitatively similar results.
All modeled cells synthesize NO; nonlinear calcium/nNOS dynamics, diffusion, decay and threshold feedback are model assumptions. They are not a directly measured population homeostat in a CC.

Positive orientation-decoding comparison assigns preferred orientations independently of physical position. Homeostasis is frozen during the rapid-response tests. Errors remain substantial; the task is illustrative, not a biological visual-circuit fit.

Static-weight response linearity R² is reported0.85diffusive versus0.57non-diffusive and0.38variable-target; afterSTDP values are much smaller0.16versus0.01/0.02. Different drive/recurrent influence matters, so the high static value must not describe the plastic network.

The printed mixed local/global mean-field rule has a homogeneous interior stationary solution for every alpha<1 under fixed deterministic inputs and positive rates. Broader finite-time distributions cannot be treated as a proof of a heterogeneous infinite-time equilibrium of that exact reduction; ANA082 states the limited algebra.

Released spiking code clips thresholds, uses target concentration rather than instantaneous concentration in the feedback denominator, and has finite adaptation/measurement windows. Those distinctions and stochastic dynamics prevent treating the mean-field stationary calculation as a refutation of the full simulations.
Population firing rate is not the application's phase-specific active fraction. No rate target, diffusion length, dimensionality, position field or cell-state mechanism is adopted.

sources.authors: Edden Slomowitz, Boaz Styr, Irena Vertkin, Hila Milshtein-Parush, Israel Nelken, Michael Slutsky and Inna Slutsky
sources.title: Interplay between population firing stability and single neuron dynamics in hippocampal networks
sources.evidence_type: Primary long-duration mouse hippocampal culture electrophysiology, calcium imaging and synaptic physiology
sources.read_scope: Population and single-unit rate recovery, calcium confirmation, burst synchrony, short-term plasticity, AMPAR-blockade comparison, homeostasis discussion and MEA/rate/burst methods. Full XML text and publisher record checked; not a reanalysis of recordings or full source-code audit. Published PDF Figures2 and8 visually inspected.
sources.finding: After sustained GABAB-receptor activation, population firing and burst statistics recover over hours to days even though many individual cells change rates. Short-term synaptic facilitation does not recover with those population averages, and a different perturbation fails to restore mean firing.
sources.application_inference: Direct biological evidence supports separating population regulation from identical per-neuron activity, and from preservation of every computational property. It is compatible with discussing a broad per-CC activity band and diverse cell responses, without selecting a physiological controller or physical metric.
transfer_limits: Newborn-mouse CA3/CA1 cultures at15–22days in vitro, recorded with59electrodes, are not an intact cortical column. The population average is across sorted recorded units, not every anatomical neuron.

With10micromolar baclofen, mean rate initially falls to1.2±0.4% of baseline and reaches103±14% after48hours;5MEA cultures versus7controls. Potency, washout and receptor-response controls argue against simple drug loss/desensitization.

Only11±2% of314recorded units are statistically unchanged after baclofen; controls23±3% of490units. Independent calcium imaging finds54±6% of192cells changed, supporting the qualitative conclusion while not reproducing the exact unit percentage.

Rate recovery and burst recovery have different timescales. Burst detection uses smoothed pooled spikes and rate-conditioned thresholds; neither mean rate nor fraction of spikes in bursts is the application's instantaneous phase-specific neuron fraction.

Short-term facilitation measured by burst-versus-single-stimulus vesicle release is abolished after two days despite recovered population firing. This is a concrete functional distinction, not a direct measurement of semantic memory loss.
AMPAR blockade leaves mean rate around40±5% of baseline at48hours despite adaptive synaptic changes. Recovery is perturbation-dependent, not a universal stabilizing guarantee.

The experiments do not identify NO as the recovery mechanism, nor measure a physical-distance law for partner selection. Fixed semantic roles and learned response variability remain separate concepts.

sources.authors: Joern R. Steinert, Susan W. Robinson, Huaxia Tong, Martin D. Haustein, Cornelia Kopp-Scheinpflug and Ian D. Forsythe
sources.title: Nitric Oxide Is an Activity-Dependent Regulator of Target Neuron Intrinsic Excitability
sources.evidence_type: Primary juvenile-mouse brain-slice electrophysiology with synaptic conditioning, pharmacology and knockout controls
sources.read_scope: Conditioning effects in MNTB/CA3, Kv/nNOS knockout comparisons, post-slicing current decay, methodological and homeostatic-pathway discussion, electrophysiology methods. Full primary XML inspected; not all current-fit or molecular panels reanalyzed.
sources.finding: Sustained activity engages NO-dependent changes in intrinsic potassium currents and excitability, with region- and timescale-dependent effects on transmission fidelity. Knockout and pharmacological controls support the pathway.
sources.application_inference: Biological regulation includes activity-dependent cellular gain and recovery dynamics beyond connection weights. This supports investigating the required functional effect rather than assuming every locality benefit is a partner-distance preference. It does not add these cellular states to the application.
transfer_limits: Experiments use P12–16mouse slices and one-hour conditioning. MNTB auditory neurons and hippocampal CA3 are not cortical-column semantic neurons; their tested frequencies are not application rates.

Conditioning raises spike threshold; MNTB transmission becomes more reliable at very high frequencies, while CA3 burst output is reduced toward one spike per input. Reduced excitability need not mean reduced temporal fidelity.
Early Kv3 suppression and slower Kv2 potentiation have different effects and time courses. NO is not a universal scalar monotone gain knob.

The positive in-vivo-like current inference uses rapid postmortem recordings and knockout controls, not direct awake in-vivo voltage-clamp measurement. Measured currents decay with roughly15minute time constant after slicing.

Control and conditioned whole-cell recordings use separate neurons to avoid dialysis of signaling; this is explicitly justified in the paper. It is not a longitudinal within-cell measurement of the whole hour.

The60–100micrometre neighbor range in discussion is attributed to prior literature, including Steinert2008, not newly measured by this experiment. The older source is abstract-checked only; its distance/protocol must not be claimed independently verified.
No evidence here establishes population-wide setpoint control, fixed semantic role allocation, a distance exponent, or the three requested mental-state regimes.

sources.authors: Barna Zajzon, David Dahmen, Abigail Morrison and Renato Duarte
sources.title: Signal denoising through topographic modularity of neural circuits
sources.evidence_type: Primary spiking/rate circuit simulations, mean-field analysis and controlled structured-projection comparisons
sources.read_scope: Results on reconstruction, E/I effects, inhibitory controls, model variants, map size, multiple inputs and dynamical input; all Discussion; architecture, map definitions, reconstruction and multi-input metrics; AppendixA. Figures6,9,10 and AppendixA Eq13 visually checked. Full AppendixB proof not independently reproduced; selected2022archive readout code inspected.
sources.finding: Matched stimulus-group projections across recurrent populations can amplify selected signals and suppress noise at fixed overall feedforward density. Modularity changes gain, inhibition and competition; coexistence, winner-take-all and stochastic switching occur in different tested regimes.
sources.application_inference: The useful structure here is preferential correspondence between assigned stimulus groups across populations. It is a graph/group relation, not a soma-distance kernel or a metric over embedding dimension labels. It offers a positive functional comparison while exposing a potential conflict between winner selection and preserving many simultaneous semantic-coordinate values.
transfer_limits: The main architecture has six sequential10000cell80/20E/I subnetworks, random sparse within-subnetwork connectivity and fixed structured excitatory projections to both E and I in the next subnetwork. No weights or maps learn during the reported simulations.

Main reconstruction inputs activate one of ten channels for200ms, plus rectified Gaussian corruption and Poisson encoding. Linear readouts trained on membrane potentials reconstruct the clean signal; the circuit is only conceptually analogous to a denoising autoencoder.

The dynamical extension genuinely tests fast-changing scalar signals and overlapping input/maps: the scalar is discretized into one active bin among40channels mapped to20overlapping populations. This is not a test of arbitrary dense simultaneous5120coordinate amplitudes. Figure10 uses20s training and10s testing.

Randomizing feedforward input to inhibition destabilizes the original configuration, but additional uncorrelated inhibitory drive restores selective responses. Thus the paper contains a rescue demonstrating that precisely matched inhibitory projection geometry is not the only route to the required effective inhibition.

Two simultaneous inputs are explicitly tested. Weaker input can be suppressed; comparable inputs can coexist or fluctuate between dominant populations. Coexistence disappears with sufficient depth in the tested setting. Stochastic switching under continuous input is not learned autonomous semantic cycling.

Performance gain denotes relative reconstruction-error reduction, not percent-correct token classification. Delay selection and learned readouts are part of the measurement; AUD040 qualifies the released archived implementation.

Map overlap and small size limit some configurations, but larger receptive fields can improve intermediate-modularity performance. The tested variants and controls must not be reduced to a claim that all overlap fails.

AppendixA Eq13 contains a square root, lost in plain XML extraction. It is the full-modularity nonoverlapping-capacity boundary d>=sqrt(sigma/Nc). At finite modularity the admissibility condition differs; the small-map plotted sweep ends below the corresponding probability bound. No missing-square-root source error is alleged.
The cited modularity threshold near0.83 is model/drive-dependent. No map size, inhibition rule, delay, learning algorithm, inter-CC neuron-edge architecture or semantic denoiser is adopted.

sources.authors: Nicholas M. Timme, Shinya Ito, Maxym Myroshnychenko, Sunny Nigam, Masanori Shimono, Fang-Chin Yeh, Pawel Hottowy, Alan M. Litke and John M. Beggs
sources.title: High-Degree Neurons Feed Cortical Computations
sources.evidence_type: Primary organotypic cortical recording analysis, information decomposition and illustrative feedforward rewiring models
sources.read_scope: Recording/selection, transfer entropy and significance, all partial-information-decomposition methods, degree/computation results, selected toy-model setup and rewiring results, unused information and limitations. Figure5 visually checked. No experimental data or author code executed.
sources.finding: Among inferred functional connections, transmitter out-degree is associated with the information that pairs of transmitters jointly contribute to a receiver. Receiver in-degree is not comparably associated with bivariate synergy. A degree-modified coactivity rule qualitatively fits these associations in a toy network.
sources.application_inference: This distinguishes contribution through outgoing influence from computation attributed to incoming combinations. It supplies neither an anatomical degree law nor a reason to fill larger target-owned capacity sets. Pairwise edge selection also limits which joint computations enter the measurement.
transfer_limits: Recordings are25organotypic mouse somatosensory cortico-hippocampal preparations, with512electrodes spaced60micrometers and roughly309recorded units on average. Units firing fewer than100spikes in60minutes are excluded. Recorded units are a small observed subset, not a complete cortical column.

Edges are significant bivariate transfer entropy conditioned on receiver history, assessed against5000jitter surrogates at short1.6–6.4ms and3.5–14ms scales. They are inferred functional relations, not directly observed synapses; inhibitory/excitatory classes are not identified.

Primary synergy analysis selects triples with two individually significant transfer-entropy inputs. The XOR extension in ANA068 shows a conditional blind spot of such an edge gate; it does not claim that real observations implement XOR or invalidate detected associations.

Information synergy depends on the chosen decomposition and spike variables; it is not sensory or semantic task accuracy. Higher-order bounds sample at most six inputs and do not measure every joint computation.

Toy networks have20input and20output binary units,80edges, and a shared binary drive. The agreement score includes coincident silence. Rewiring globally replaces the lowest-scoring connected pair with the highest-scoring absent pair; this is not a bounded local partner-search algorithm.

The fitted degree score includes +0.05receiver in-degree and -1.75sender out-degree. It discourages repeated use of high-outdegree senders and spreads outgoing edges; it is not preferential growth of outgoing hubs. Parameters are manually fit and the authors caution against assigning biological significance to the small toy-model fit difference.
No physical distance rule, incoming capacity distribution, semantic representation or learning mechanism is selected.

sources.authors: Alex Roxin
sources.title: The Role of Degree Distribution in Shaping the Dynamics in Networks of Sparsely Connected Spiking Neurons
sources.evidence_type: Controlled spiking-network degree-distribution simulations and heuristic population-rate analysis
sources.read_scope: Degree generation, LIF parameters, inhibitory and E/I dynamical states, pairwise-correlation sections, selected rate-model stability derivation and Discussion. Figure8 and accompanying equations visually checked. Full appendix proof not reproduced.
sources.finding: At fixed mean degree, broadening incoming degree suppresses fast oscillations in the inhibitory example but generates slow oscillations in the tested E/I example. Outgoing heterogeneity increases shared-input correlations and can change dynamics near a bifurcation, despite weak effects in a balanced asynchronous regime.
sources.application_inference: Degree heterogeneity changes effective gains and recurrent feedback, not just memory consumption. The direction depends on cell response and circuit type; the static capacity-class law cannot establish the required active-fraction or dynamical stability.
transfer_limits: Graphs vary prescribed independent in- and out-degree distributions, interpolating from binomial to truncated heavy-tailed distributions while preserving their mean. This is actual connectivity, not reserved capacity.

Present synapses have constant strength by presynaptic E/I type; there is no learned inverse-degree weight compensation. Fixed delays, instantaneous currents and external Poisson drive are part of the examples.

The E/I example varies only E-to-E degree. Other projection classes remain random with fixed probability. Results do not establish a universal effect of broadening all incoming classes simultaneously.

The expected common-input fraction depends on the second moment of outgoing degree. Membrane filtering, reset and E/I cancellation can prevent increased input-current correlation from becoming increased spike-count correlation.
Near a transition, broader outgoing degree can induce aperiodic population bursts. The baseline observation of little outgoing-degree effect is not a general invariance.

The rate reduction is explicitly heuristic. Its predictions depend on the transfer curve; a threshold-linear approximation can give a different direction from a concave-up curve. Correlated in-/out-degree and additional motifs are outside the main model.
No weights, degree exponent, topology, activity controller or numerical SNN acceptance band is adopted.

primary_metadata.title: The Role of Degree Distribution in Shaping the Dynamics in Networks of Sparsely Connected Spiking Neurons

sources.authors: Raphaël Bergoin, Alessandro Torcini, Gustavo Deco, Mathias Quoy and Gorka Zamora-López
sources.title: Emergence and maintenance of modularity in neural networks with Hebbian and anti-Hebbian inhibitory STDP
sources.evidence_type: Primary nonspatial spiking-network learning, continual-plasticity recall and consolidation simulations
sources.read_scope: Model/protocol, inhibition comparison, resting dynamics, consolidation, capacity, larger networks, overlapping inputs, limitations, STDP and adaptation methods; full S6 and S9 supplements. Figures6/7 and equations7–11 visually checked; S9 visually checked. Selected archived and current source audited.
sources.finding: Co-stimulation learns modular recurrent weights. With both inhibitory plasticity classes, noise-driven rest exhibits asynchronous activity and intermittent recalls while plasticity remains active. Learned modules can persist for hours of simulated time, and overlapping stimulation can yield stable shared hubs without spatial embedding.
sources.application_inference: The positive result directly supports investigating learned cooperation and spontaneous maintenance within assigned input roles. Its functional group relations need no anatomical distance; transfer depends on inhibition, overlap, forgetting, sparsity and the meaning of a recall event.
transfer_limits: The main network has100QIF neurons,80excitatory and two10cell inhibitory classes, initially all-to-all without autapses. Stimulus groups are prescribed. The5sbaseline/35straining protocol uses800msdrive plus200ms gaps; the main paper illustrates a subsequent rest period. Weight adaptation remains enabled.

Excitatory timing-dependent plasticity and symmetric Hebbian/anti-Hebbian inhibitory rules jointly shape feedback and competition. Positive/negative semantic populations in this application have not been identified with biological E/I types or these extra classes.

The10stimulus example uses1000cells and4hours of simulated rest. Overlap examples explicitly assign shared excitatory cells; Figure6 uses eight shared cells and alternating training, with weight matrices shown through24hours. These are finite-duration simulations, not a proof of lifelong stability or arbitrary overlapping dense-vector recall.

S6 includes a20000cell fully connected example and a1000cell50%-connected example without additive noise. These useful controls do not test614400cells with the application's roughly183allocated slots per cell; even the paper's sparse control has very different density.

The forgetting offset is set to f=0.2/M using the externally specified number of memories. A memory requires enough spontaneous recall to offset decay. S9 uses a rough synchronized-versus-far-separated spike comparison; ANA086 examines a distinct explicit independent-Poisson case rather than treating its11second estimate as universal.

The storage bound min(NE,NHI,NAI) belongs to initialized or learned modules under this particular division of inhibition. Brain-wide numbers extrapolated from it are model hypotheses, not anatomical memory-capacity measurements.

Spontaneous ensemble recalls and preserved weights do not establish a learned ordered cycle, vector reconstruction accuracy, a per-CC active-fraction band or preserved independent simultaneous semantic content.
AUD041 identifies exact-version differences in released equations/code while retaining the positive nonspatial result. No author code was run; no corrected performance is asserted.
