sources.authors: Marina Vegué, Antoine Allard and Patrick Desrosiers
sources.title: Firing rate distributions in plastic networks of spiking neurons
sources.evidence_type: Primary mean-field derivation and spiking-network comparison with heterogeneous degrees and plastic weights
sources.read_scope: Connectivity and plasticity sections, neuronal-model setup, mean-field assumptions, trace moments, selected conditional-degree and plastic-network derivations/results, all Discussion. Published trace CV equation visually checked onPDFpage10. Full supporting derivation/code not inspected.
sources.finding: A self-consistent mean-field calculation predicts stationary rate and weight distributions in tested heterogeneous plastic spiking networks. It incorporates degree-dependent sampling of presynaptic and postsynaptic cells and provides good agreement in several irregular-firing regimes, with a reported failure near synchronized activity.
sources.application_inference: A weaker weight at a high-rate receiving cell can arise from plasticity, but it does not make capacity or mean degree a sufficient description of dynamics. Which cells supply the inputs and the assumptions needed to replace spikes by rates remain consequential.
transfer_limits: The binary graph is a fixed random scaffold with a prescribed joint in-/out-degree law. This is not structural learning or an anatomical locality model.

The main plasticity rule continuously depends on pre/post exponential spike traces and weight, with equilibrium weights factorizing into pre- and postsynaptic rate functions. It differs from event-gated pair/triplet STDP and does not cover their full timing dependence.

The theory assumes approximately Poisson firing, conditional independence of spike trains, many individually small inputs, and sufficiently large trace-time-constant times firing-rate products. Equalizing a broad population statistic does not establish these assumptions.

A presynaptic endpoint is sampled in proportion to its outgoing degree. Correlation between a cell's in- and out-degree therefore changes the incoming rate distribution. The theory permits this within-cell degree correlation but assumes that connected cells' in-degrees are independent; assortative pairing is not covered.

The mixed example uses1000E and1000I cells, an Oja-inspired excitatory rule and an analogous inhibitory sign reversal. A pure-excitatory extension sometimes matches too, but misses a synchronous/regular transition regime. This is a qualified positive result, not universal accuracy.
The paper explicitly leaves stationary-solution stability and multiplicity unanalysed. A self-consistent stationary distribution is not a dynamical-stability theorem or a per-CC activation bound.
ANA087/088 illustrate rate-estimation and compensating-weight limits under stated simpler assumptions; no trace array, precision, weight rule, topology or controller is adopted.

sources.authors: Yuxiu Shao, David Dahmen, Stefano Recanatesi, Eric Shea-Brown and Srdjan Ostojic
sources.title: Impact of Local Connectivity Patterns on Excitatory-Inhibitory Network Dynamics
sources.evidence_type: Primary random-matrix analysis and linear-rate network simulations of typed connectivity motifs
sources.read_scope: Arxiv2411.06802v3 main model, low-rank formulation, Gaussian/sparse eigenvalue results, strong/weak scaling, response definitions and Discussion; selected effective-connectivity formulas. Published finalPDF text independently checked for weak scaling, typed-response controls, effective-versus-transient distinction and degree discussion. Full appendices and author code not audited. V3page10 equations visually checked; finalPDF screenshot retrieval failed.
sources.finding: Chain correlations can add a positive feedback eigenmode and alter population responses beyond predictions from mean connectivity. Sparse sign-constrained controls and distinct scaling regimes delimit the result.
sources.application_inference: Directed arrangement and endpoint statistics can matter without a physical metric. Fixed-density growth differs from fixed incoming-count growth; steady-response matching does not establish semantic trajectories.
transfer_limits: Models are linear rate dynamics. Gaussian cases do not strictly constrain every outgoing sign; sparse cases use fixed positiveE/negativeI strengths. Their typed motif correlations differ, and inhibitory responses can change in opposite directions.
The paper includes a fixed-count weakly connected regime with size-independent outliers. It must not be reduced to a claim that increasing neuron count inevitably destabilizes every sparse network.

The effective matrix predicts stationary population responses but not generally transient spectra. Low-rank response predictions also use numerically measured eigenvectors; this is not a fully learned online rule.
Chain enrichment does not establish a power-law capacity distribution. ANA090 gives a bounded two-degree counterexample. No metric, motif target or controller is selected.
sources.version_note: Published20May2025;arxivv3dated15March2025 has the title Identifying the impact of local connectivity patterns on dynamics in excitatory-inhibitory networks and different section/page numbering. The final26page version is not asserted identical to the30page preprint. Local download of final publisherPDF returned403; public arxiv copy inspected independently.

sources.authors: Subhaneil Lahiri and Surya Ganguli
sources.title: A memory frontier for complex synapses
sources.evidence_type: Primary mathematical analysis of independent finite-state synapses under ongoing random plasticity
sources.read_scope: Main paper pages 1–8, Figure 4 visually checked; supplementary pages 1, 6 and 13 inspected for ergodicity, independent-input noise normalization and the serial-chain area bound. Not an independent verification of every proof or the entire supplement.
sources.finding: Within its ideal-observer model, synaptic internal-state structure trades immediate encoding strength against retention. The paper derives an area bound sqrt(N)*(M-1)/r and a late-time memory envelope; N counts independent synapses and M counts internal states, not distinct neurons or connection slots.
sources.application_inference: A locality or assembly mechanism that relies on hidden synaptic history must account for that history separately from the expressed weight. Its state count cannot be equated with the CC neuron count.
transfer_limits: The analyzed synapses have two expressed efficacy values, possibly many hidden states, independent identically distributed plasticity events, stationary initial states and ergodic forgetting. This is not a capacity formula for correlated semantic sequences with FP8-valued efficacies.

The area-bound supremum concentrates probability in sticky end states; perfectly absorbing end states cease to be ergodic. Improving long retention reduces fast acquisition. No single model is shown to attain the envelope at every age.
Ideal-observer overlap is not demonstrated autonomous recurrent semantic recall. A serial chain in this paper is a graph of internal synaptic states, not a physical arrangement of neurons.

sources.authors: Marcus K. Benna and Stefano Fusi
sources.title: Computational principles of synaptic memory consolidation
sources.evidence_type: Primary multiscale synaptic model with finite-state simulations and reported perceptron/recurrent retrieval controls
sources.read_scope: Main pages 1–9; Methods definitions and selected construction/discretization passages on pages 11–14. Figures 2 and 5 and equation 2 visually checked. Supplementary retrieval simulations are described by the main paper but their complete methods/data were not audited.
sources.finding: Bidirectionally coupled fast and slow synaptic variables preserve strong recent traces while extending retention. Finite-level stochastic rounding remains effective in their simulations. The main paper also reports successful noisy-cue retrieval in a perceptron and a fully connected recurrent network.
sources.application_inference: Low precision does not by itself rule out sustained memory, and nonspatial mechanisms provide positive controls. Their long retention depends on multiple internal variables and must not be attributed to a lone FP8 weight.
transfer_limits: The main scaling analysis uses balanced random uncorrelated synaptic modifications and an ideal observer. The authors explicitly leave sparse modular recurrent scalability and general correlated rehearsal statistics unresolved.

The approximate SNR is sqrt(N/t)*exp(-t/T)/sqrt(log(T)); T grows exponentially with the number m of internal variables. Near-linear lifetime requires choosing T with N; a fixed T eventually limits the improvement.

Quantized variables have independently rounded finite levels and hard bounds. Their joint internal-state space grows multiplicatively; several low-precision variables do not fit automatically in one low-precision weight.

The diffusion analogy concerns interactions among synaptic memory variables. It does not provide a physical coordinate system for this application. One-memory-per-minute labels are illustrative time conversions, not measured cortical retention rates.

sources.authors: Pablo Urbizagastegui, André van Schaik and Runchun Wang
sources.title: Stochastic rounding for memory-efficient digital simulation of synaptic plasticity using 8-bit floating-point
sources.evidence_type: Primary publisher abstract plus independently inspected public source code; full article unavailable through attempted routes
sources.read_scope: Publisher-indexed abstract and bibliographic metadata; nine selected repository text files pinned to the May 21, 2025 commit, predating the September 17 publication. Full article, result files and all simulation protocols not reviewed or executed.
sources.finding: The abstract reports recurrent-network plasticity with custom stochastic FP8 arithmetic. Public code implements such arithmetic and an excitatory STDP experiment; this inspection verifies a mechanism and its assumptions, not the reported quantitative performance.
sources.application_inference: FP8 online updates are a concrete research avenue. Represented precision, rounding behavior, additional neural state and actual allocated memory need separate evidence before transferring this result to a CC.
transfer_limits: Selected code uses a 1-sign/4-exponent/3-fraction format with maximum finite magnitude 480, three guard bits, saturation and custom stochastic alignment. It is not automatically interchangeable with every format called FP8.

The selected balanced-network script has 90,000 excitatory and 22,500 inhibitory cells with connection probability 0.1, external Poisson input, membrane/current/calcium states and excitatory-to-excitatory plasticity. This is not the application's fixed signed-coordinate population or sparse degree budget.
The code represents bit patterns using integer declarations and host arithmetic. Selected files do not establish a one-byte backing layout or measured end-to-end memory footprint.
Custom stochastic rounding must not be assumed exactly unbiased for every operand; ANA-093 gives a scoped exact case. This does not establish failure of the reported network statistics.

sources.authors: Won Chan Oh, Laxmi Kumar Parajuli and Karen Zito
sources.title: Heterosynaptic structural plasticity on local dendritic segments of hippocampal CA1 neurons
sources.evidence_type: Primary two-photon uncaging, structural imaging, receptor imaging and pharmacological perturbations in rat hippocampal slice cultures
sources.read_scope: Main results, Discussion and Methods, PDF pages 2–8; all four appended supplementary figure captions. Figure 4 pharmacological dissociation visually checked.
sources.finding: Stimulating a cluster of synapses caused nearby inactive spines to shrink, accompanied by reduced surface AMPA-receptor fluorescence. Pharmacological dissociation of stimulated-spine growth and neighbor shrinkage supports an active heterosynaptic signal rather than a requirement for growth to consume shared structural resources.
sources.application_inference: Biological proximity can mediate conditional competition among incoming synapses. This is a relation within a target dendrite, not a universal positive connection-probability kernel between source neurons.
quantitative_scope: P6–P7 rat hippocampal cultures, CA1 secondary/tertiary basal dendrites at 13–18 days in vitro; imaging in zero magnesium and TTX. Main multiple-spine protocol: 30 one-millisecond uncaging pulses at 2 Hz.

Average six stimulated spines; nearby unstimulated spine size fell 21±4% in the main 31-cell sample. Detectable shrinkage occurred with at least four successfully potentiated neighbors in this protocol; single/triple stimulation controls did not show it.

Effects depended on average distance to the stimulated cluster and position inside it. The 2–3.4 micrometer group showed shrinkage; distant groups did not show a significant effect. This does not establish a universal sharp distance cutoff.

Unstimulated spines were deliberately chosen at least 1.5 micrometers from stimulated spines to avoid glutamate spillover. That excluded interval is an experimental selection rule, not evidence for a biological very-near exemption.
transfer_limits: Surface SEP-GluA2 fluorescence is the functional proxy here, not a direct measurement of every synaptic current. The supplementary cross-synapse AMPA change correlation was not statistically significant (r=-0.46, p=0.16), unlike several structural associations.

KN62 prevented statistically significant growth while shrinkage persisted; calcineurin/IP3R/mGluR inhibition separated the opposite responses. These controls delimit a mechanism in this preparation, not every form of synaptic resource competition.
No recurrent-network stability, semantic storage capacity or neuron-pair anatomical distance law is established.

sources.authors: Arvind Govindarajan, Inbal Israely, Shu-Ying Huang and Susumu Tonegawa
sources.title: The dendritic branch is the preferred integrative unit for protein synthesis-dependent LTP
sources.evidence_type: Primary single-spine and multispine uncaging experiments with protein-synthesis perturbations in mouse hippocampal slices
sources.read_scope: Main experimental rationale, single-spine validation, temporal/spatial facilitation, competition, multispine controls, Discussion and Methods. Figure 4 distance/branch comparison visually checked; full external supplement not obtained.
sources.finding: A strong stimulus facilitated later weak synaptic potentiation over a limited time and dendritic distance, with weaker transfer across a branch point. Stimulated spines also competed when stimulated closely in time. The observed interaction is therefore history- and branch-dependent.
sources.application_inference: The useful candidate function is selective consolidation and competition, not static attraction of nearby neuron identities. Neither one Euclidean distance nor one positive multiplier captures all tested conditions.
quantitative_scope: Single-spine protocols used glutamate uncaging with forskolin or a D1 agonist; early potentiation decayed within about 2.5 hours while the protein-synthesis-dependent response persisted at least four hours in the reported conditions.

At a 45-minute separation, facilitation declined along a branch and was barely detectable near 70 micrometers; cross-sister-branch transfer was reduced and absent at 50 micrometers or more in the sampled conditions. Distance was measured along the dendrite.

Effective protein availability and tag lifetimes were inferred through stimulation timing and translation inhibition, not directly measured molecular concentrations. Forward and reverse temporal windows differed.

A physiological-magnesium multispine control produced potentiation in a minority of stimulated spines when more than ten inputs were activated on one branch; splitting sampled sets across sister branches failed. This is a protocol-specific control, not a universal neuron activation threshold.
transfer_limits: Most single-spine experiments used zero magnesium and pharmacological induction. The physiological-magnesium controls and acute-slice checks broaden the result but do not demonstrate memory content or recurrent semantic dynamics in vivo.
Long-duration synaptic strength comparisons partly use a spine-volume-to-current calibration from another cell; the early validation includes paired structural and electrophysiological changes.

The proposed explanation involves limiting plasticity-related proteins and local capture; a unique biochemical transport mechanism was not identified. The claim that branches are primary units of all long-term memory is broader than these experiments alone establish.

sources.authors: Jan H. Kirchner and Julijana Gjorgjieva
sources.title: Emergence of local and global synaptic organization on cortical dendrites
sources.evidence_type: Primary biophysical/generalized plasticity models compared with published developmental and adult synaptic organization data
sources.read_scope: Results on molecular competition/cooperation, generalized rule, retinal input, ferret/mouse clustering and somatic feedback; Methods for generalized dynamics, steady-state analysis, parameters, retinal input, receptive fields, turnover and backpropagating signal; functional-role Discussion. PDF Figure 4 and equations/table on page 13 visually checked. Not every supplement or simulation audited.
sources.finding: A local interaction between correlated incoming synapses and competition among uncorrelated neighbors produces different forms of synaptic clustering depending on the input ensemble. Ferret-like parameters favor orientation grouping; mouse-like parameters favor receptive-field overlap without orientation grouping.
sources.application_inference: Anatomical grouping need not correspond to one semantic feature label. Its computational role depends on input statistics and conditional plasticity, while the model's actual dendritic and visual-field coordinates are additional assumptions absent from our fixed semantic arrangement.
transfer_limits: The generalized rule combines a presynaptic trace with a distance-weighted sum of neighboring synaptic inputs and a heterosynaptic offset. It is not simply pairwise pre/post somatic co-firing multiplied by distance.

Six hours of modeled retinal waves are looped across development. The white-noise control uses independently sampled pixels followed by spatial Gaussian filtering; no-clustering in that protocol is not a universal result for every white-noise-driven recurrent system.

Turnover removes a weak synapse and samples a new dendritic position, orientation and receptive-field center. This resampling of input roles differs from the application's fixed coordinate roles, though selecting different existing inputs remains a separate possible mechanism.

The model includes traces, continuous bounded efficacy, an explicit dendritic interaction matrix and, in whole-cell experiments, a thresholded somatic feedback signal. That signal excludes its own contribution from the threshold accumulator to avoid immediate positive feedback.

The authors discuss computational benefits of clustering; these simulations establish organization and correspondence to selected data, not autonomous semantic cycling, task performance or a sparse CC memory budget.
The provided repository helper and figure scripts do not form a verified matching execution path in the inspected snapshot; see AUD-043. No simulated outcomes were reproduced.

sources.authors: David Kappel, Stefan Habenschuss, Robert Legenstein and Wolfgang Maass
sources.title: Network Plasticity as Bayesian Inference
sources.evidence_type: Primary stochastic-plasticity theory and generative spiking-network simulations
sources.read_scope: Posterior/online learning, spine model, changing sensory inputs and recurrent compensation Results; online-approximation and recurrent-scaffold Methods. Figure 5 visually checked in final PDF. Generalization benchmark and supplements not audited.
sources.finding: Stochastic parameter updates combine a specified structural prior with a likelihood gradient. A network of recurrently coupled winner-take-all circuits learns cross-modal associations and recovers partially after lesions without a neuron-distance rule.
sources.application_inference: Fixed input channels can coexist with learned recurrent associations and changing internal responses. Sampling connection configurations is distinct from the desired spontaneous sampling or cycling of represented semantic states.
transfer_limits: The exact stationary-distribution result concerns a batch Langevin process. The online rule uses an independent-input likelihood factorization and a slow-learning approximation; its exact convergence is not guaranteed.

The recurrent example has predefined input routing, WTA competition, homeostatic regulation and potentially all-to-all recurrent contacts. Learned hidden receptive fields are not fixed semantic-coordinate roles.

A parameter is assigned to each potential contact; negative values represent effectively absent contacts through tiny exponential weights. Statistical sparsity and a heavy-tailed efficacy distribution do not specify the application slot-capacity law.
The demonstrated output is stimulus association/reconstruction and compensation under continued experience, not autonomous semantic cycles or a per-CC activation-band guarantee.
sources.access_note: An incorrectly guessed PDF type=print returned 404. The publisher download link uses type=printable and supplied the final PDF.

sources.authors: David Kappel, Robert Legenstein, Stefan Habenschuss, Michael Hsieh and Wolfgang Maass
sources.title: A Dynamic Connectome Supports the Emergence of Stable Computational Function of Neural Circuits through Reward-Based Learning
sources.evidence_type: Primary reward-modulated structural/synaptic-plasticity theory and spiking-network simulations
sources.read_scope: Policy framework; recurrent task, prior and stochasticity Results; synaptic dynamics, online approximation, simulation and recurrent-task Methods. Figure 3 visually checked. Not every derivation, routing experiment or supplement reviewed.
sources.finding: A small recurrent E/I network learns a cue-triggered two-step action with fixed input/output groups and no neuron-distance preference. Continued rewiring supports relearning after a task change. Exponential waiting times for inactive contacts retain similar eventual task performance in an explicit approximation control.
sources.application_inference: Partner exploration can be separated from geometric nearness. The inactive-contact approximation is relevant evidence against assuming that every absent pair must always retain a continuously updated latent variable.
transfer_limits: The recurrent scaffold has 60 excitatory and 20 inhibitory cells, 200 input cells and multiple potential synapses per excitatory pair; inhibitory connections are fixed. This is not sparse CC-scale validation.

Plasticity uses eligibility and reward-gradient traces, exponential efficacy mapping, a tuned prior and stochastic parameter noise. These are additional algorithm requirements, not approved additions to the application memory layout.

Inactive contacts have zero transmitted weight. The tested approximation resumes a contact after an exponential wait with mean 12 simulated hours and resets traces; it is not an exact preservation of the heavy-tailed original return-time distribution.
The exact posterior interpretation and approximate online updates have different assumptions. Fast decay of initial-state influence relative to environmental change is used for the online estimator.

Statistical priors alter connection counts and can impair learning when too restrictive; they do not enforce heterogeneous hard per-neuron slot limits. No semantic valence drift, three-regime behavior or activation-fraction acceptance was tested.
The inspected public showcase and simulator source are not a verified reproduction of every figure or parameter setting; see AUD-044.

sources.authors: Manuel Beiran, Alexis Dubreuil, Adrian Valente, Francesca Mastrogiuseppe and Srdjan Ostojic
sources.title: Shaping Dynamics With Multiple Populations in Low-Rank Recurrent Networks
sources.evidence_type: Primary low-rank rate-network theory and finite-network demonstrations
sources.read_scope: Author arXiv v2 (2020-11-17), pages 3, 6-10, 19-23 and Appendices A/B: model, collective dynamics, single-population cycles, universality and oscillator construction. Figure 7 visually checked. Published 44-page version inspected through native browser for model, theorem statements and section 6/finite-size discussion; not claimed identical in every detail.
sources.finding: Connection-pattern distributions determine nonlinear collective dynamics without physical positions. A single zero-mean Gaussian population can support a stable oscillation; multiple populations provide more varied dynamics, including a demonstrated approximation to a Van der Pol oscillator.
sources.application_inference: Grouping in connection-parameter space can matter computationally without becoming a physical neighborhood. Existing semantic roles do not themselves specify the required recurrent loadings or population statistics.
transfer_limits: The network uses continuous tanh rate units and low-rank, generally dense signed connectivity; no neuron-distance rule or Dale constraint is supplied. This is not a sparse FP4/FP8 implementation result.

The universal-approximation construction concerns a vector field on a specified domain, with adjustable connectivity/input statistics and sufficiently many populations. It gives no population-count or memory guarantee for the application.

The zero-mean, autonomous single-Gaussian analysis can have at most a pair of stable nonzero fixed points under the stated nondegenerate real-eigenvalue conditions; this does not prohibit its separate complex-eigenvalue oscillatory solutions.

The oscillator demonstration uses 2000 units per population and compares 15 and 35 populations. More populations improve the mean-field fit but need not improve a finite sampled network; regularization controls large parameters and sampling sensitivity.
Those populations are not identified with our 120-cell minicolumns. Fixed semantic inputs, live-degree constraints, quantization and learned semantic loop content require separate justification.

Vector-field approximation is not by itself a guarantee of long-term orbit preservation; see ANA-097. The continuous-target approximation claim must not be silently extended to arbitrary discontinuous update rules; see ANA-098.

sources.authors: Alexis Dubreuil, Adrian Valente, Manuel Beiran, Francesca Mastrogiuseppe and Srdjan Ostojic
sources.title: The role of population structure in computations through neural dynamics
sources.evidence_type: Primary trained rate-network interventions and mathematical reduction, reviewed in an identified author-thesis chapter
sources.read_scope: Adrian Valente thesis, defended 2022-10-19, chapter III explicitly based on this paper: PDF pages 41, 43-45, 47, 51, 53-59, 61-63; Appendix A pages 110-115 and 117. Fixed-input alternative Figure A.6 on page 125 visually checked. Journal abstract verified, but journal full text/supplement not directly obtained; chapter includes adapted numbering and some unresolved cross-references.
sources.finding: Resampling that preserves overall connection-loading covariance but removes multi-population structure preserves some tasks and degrades context-dependent tasks. Population-specific gain modulation explains flexible routing. An alternative successful network keeps input directions fixed during recurrent training.
sources.application_inference: Fixed input roles and learned contextual computation are compatible in principle. Connectivity structure can be functionally relevant even when it has no physical layout; a measured cluster or nearest-neighbor statistic is not itself a connection-distance rule.
transfer_limits: The fixed-input control uses random distributed input patterns, not signed coordinate populations. Overall input/readout amplitudes can be trained even where individual directions are fixed.

Main context-dependent examples train input vectors; the alternative fixed-input solution has three functional populations plus one largely inactive population. Both positive cases are retained rather than treating learned input roles as mandatory.
Resampling includes input, recurrent and readout loadings jointly. Preservation of their statistical distribution does not preserve each individual neuron's assigned input/output role. See AUD-045.

Models use tanh units, backpropagation through time and unstructured initial connectivity without anatomical/Dale constraints. The authors explicitly do not identify the training procedure with biological synaptic learning.
The DMS mixture analysis includes retraining covariance factors to address finite-size fluctuations. Its success is not entirely a frozen-parameter shuffle control.

Reported dependence on population structure applies to the studied tasks, model classes and interventions; it is not a proof that every possible context computation requires the same groups, a physical metric or a particular minicolumn arrangement.
The work does not establish semantic autonomous cycling, the three requested regimes, sparse static-slot learning or FP4/FP8 robustness.

sources.authors: Stefan Klampfl and Wolfgang Maass
sources.title: Emergence of Dynamic Memory Traces in Cortical Microcircuit Models through STDP
sources.evidence_type: Primary stochastic spiking-network simulation with learning and ablation controls
sources.read_scope: Author-hosted published PDF: model and methods, assembly formation, spontaneous reactivation, context dependence and computational trade-off, pages 2-13. Figures 6 and 7 visually inspected; Figure 9/10/12 captions and surrounding results read. Parameter lambda not recovered as a numerical value.
sources.finding: Repeated temporal inputs induce stimulus-specific recurrent assemblies, partially compressed spontaneous replay, and context-sensitive responses. Fixed random input weights still permit assembly formation. Recurrence STDP and depressing short-term synapses are necessary in the examined protocol; a single large WTA circuit also produces sequences.
sources.application_inference: Fixed semantic input roles need not imply frozen recurrent responses, but the fixed-random-input control is not a demonstration using signed embedding coordinates. Learned sequence content and global distance are separable questions.
transfer_limits: The main model imposes 50 WTA circuits on a 10-by-5 grid and an exponential inter-circuit connection probability, citing LOC-178. This is an added physical geometry, not a metric obtained from input coordinates. No degree-matched geometry-removal comparison was identified.

Each WTA has 2-10 neurons, or 10-50 for the temporal-context example. The softmax normalization fixes the total instantaneous firing intensity per WTA, usually 100 Hz; it does not fix the realized fraction of active cells over an arbitrary time window.

The single-WTA control changes inhibition organization and uses 268 cells and a 2500-Hz total rate. It supports sequence formation without multiple spatial WTA groups but is not a clean, fully matched geometry-only ablation.

Replay can be incomplete and less precise than driven activity. A common stimulus in two contexts is represented differently only over limited durations in this protocol; the authors explicitly report instability for longer common inputs.
Assembly selection and replay alignment use response thresholds and expected learned-pattern durations. This is not an unconditioned proof of indefinite autonomous semantic cycles.

The learned specialization improves spoken-digit discrimination and gap completion while degrading the tested generic XOR and fading-memory tasks. Greater sequence stereotypy is not an unconditional computational improvement.
No transfer to the application static capacity, FP4/FP8 arithmetic, per-CC bands or three regimes is established.

sources.authors: Christos H. Papadimitriou, Santosh S. Vempala, Daniel Mitropolsky, Michael Collins and Wolfgang Maass
sources.title: Brain computation by assemblies of neurons
sources.evidence_type: Primary random-graph assembly model, theorem statements and simulations
sources.read_scope: EuropePMC main text: model, operations, theoretical statements, methods and simulation algorithm. NSF-hosted published PDF; Figure 2 visually checked. Supplementary proofs were not obtained, so detailed theorem parameter conditions were not audited.
sources.finding: Random directed connectivity, top-k firing and multiplicative Hebbian plasticity support assembly projection, association, pattern completion and merging without a neuron-distance metric.
sources.application_inference: Useful recurrent operations do not logically require a physical embedding. Their operational assumptions and learned assembly membership must be distinguished from existing fixed semantic-coordinate input/output identities.
transfer_limits: The model fixes exactly k excitatory winners each discrete step, assumes inhibition/disinhibition and read/fire control primitives, and invokes slower normalization. These are not consequences of a broad activation band or of coactivity alone.
Repeated parent stimulation produces a stabilizing support of participating cells; support convergence is not proof of an unchanging firing state or autonomous semantic loop.
Typical stated scales are n=10^6-10^7, p=10^-3, k=100-1000 and beta=0.1. They are not a calibrated model for one 614400-cell CC or a prescribed live-degree budget.

On-demand generation exploits statistical symmetry of ungenerated candidates. The inspected historical code uses tail approximations and growing dense arrays for seen supports; its laptop feasibility does not establish the application static-pool implementation.
Subsecond assembly formation and rapid plasticity are modeling hypotheses in the discussion, not direct experimental measurements supplied by this paper.
No independent validation of the published supplementary proofs or exact figure reproduction is claimed.

sources.authors: N. T. Markov, P. Misery and colleagues
sources.title: Weight Consistency Specifies Regularities of Macaque Cortical Networks
sources.evidence_type: Primary quantitative retrograde-tracer anatomy in cynomolgus macaque
sources.read_scope: EuropePMC full text: surgery and tracing, charting, local/extrinsic FLN definitions, intrinsic spatial result, technical considerations and connectivity discussion. Figure 2 caption read; figure image and technical supplement not obtained.
sources.finding: Intrinsic labeled inputs are highly local: mean intrinsic FLNt 79% (68-89%), an approximately exponential decline of labeled-neuron density with distance in small injections, and about 80%/95% of intrinsic labeled neurons within 1.2/1.9 mm in the reported measurements.
sources.application_inference: This is anatomical evidence for local investment in real tissue, not a distance rule for semantic-coordinate labels. Its tracer observable must be distinguished from pairwise neuron connection probability.
transfer_limits: FLNt divides labeled neurons in a source structure by all labeled neurons for the injection, including intrinsic sources; FLNe excludes intrinsic sources. Neither is a direct count of synapses, a weight magnitude or a probability over all possible source-target pairs.

A labeled source projects into a finite tracer uptake zone containing multiple possible targets. The observed source density is not directly the probability that two identified somata are monosynaptically connected; see ANA-099.

The study includes intrinsic spatial measurements and must not be dismissed as only a macro-area connectivity study. Nonetheless its millimeter distances cannot be assigned to embedding dimensions without an additional, justified model.
Reported distances refer to processed material without shrinkage correction. Injection extent, cell-density variation, tracer uptake and laminar/retinotopic organization constrain interpretation.
The exponential density finding alone does not justify importing the normalized kernel lambda*exp(-lambda*d) used in LOC-176, its amplitude, grid units or a very-near exclusion.

sources.authors: Henrike Planert, Franz Xaver Mittermaier, Sabine Grosser and colleagues
sources.title: Electrophysiological classification of human layer 2–3 pyramidal neurons reveals subtype-specific synaptic interactions
sources.evidence_type: Primary human temporal-cortex slice electrophysiology, morphology and public processed tables
sources.read_scope: Institutional copy of published 32-page PDF including methods and extended data: main cellular/synaptic results, subtype connectivity, individual-level checks, curation, clustering, truncation and statistical methods. Extended Data Figure 8 visually inspected and selected released data/code audited independently.
sources.finding: Four electrophysiological subtypes differ in connectivity and synaptic dynamics. LowRin neurons receive relatively frequent inputs with smaller initial somatic EPSPs and greater facilitation than SlowAP neurons, which receive fewer, stronger and more depressing inputs. Soma distance predicts overall connectivity, while measured subtype differences add structured heterogeneity.
sources.application_inference: This provides concrete, scoped support for distinguishing incoming degree from effective influence and excitability. It supplies neither a universal inverse-degree weight law nor physical coordinates for existing semantic roles.
transfer_limits: The study analyzes temporal tissue from 23 epilepsy-surgery participants and shares its dataset with LOC-013; it is not independent anatomical replication of that study.

Counts depend on curation: 1479 recorded pyramidal cells, 1214 meeting general quality criteria, 901 cells in the core cellular analysis, and 1094 connections among 6911 tested pairs after the reported anatomical exclusions. The e-type matrix is a distinct subset (AUD-047).

The four e-types arise from clustering 15 measured physiological properties. They are not semantic minicolumns, signed-coordinate populations or a prescribed discrete physiological taxonomy for the application.

Initial somatic EPSP combines release, potentially multiple contacts, dendritic filtering, membrane properties and recording conditions. Smaller EPSPs do not by themselves establish smaller individual synaptic conductance or a training rule.
Some subtype differences remain in participant-level comparisons; not every directional contrast reaches significance. Pair-type comparisons use a reported 15% FDR threshold.

The distance control in Extended Data Figure 8 uses group mean distances from connected, nondisynaptic pairs in the released script, rather than all tested pairs. AUD-047 reproduces its counts and correlation; this is not a full pair-level distance adjustment (ANA-101).
The observed latency-distance relation includes conduction and synaptic/measurement contributions. No edge-delay field, subtype metadata, extra state or geometry is approved for our model.
sources.access_notes: Institutional public PDF obtained after a browser timeout. Public processed tables and analysis scripts downloaded from the author-linked Figshare record. No restricted recordings requested.

sources.authors: Amir Levi, Lidor Spivak, Hadas E. Sloin, Shirly Someck and Eran Stark
sources.title: Error correction and improved precision of spike timing in converging cortical networks
sources.evidence_type: Primary freely moving mouse electrophysiology, optogenetic stimulation and data-driven transmission models
sources.read_scope: EuropePMC full-text XML: convergence, recruitment interventions, coincidence models, coding and limitations; stimulation, decoding, precision and synthetic-neuron methods. Author PDF Figure 4 visually inspected. Full supplementary figures were not individually audited.
sources.finding: Indirectly activated interneurons reconstruct a shared, filtered optogenetic signal more accurately and with finer spike timing than individual directly activated pyramidal inputs. Increasing recruited input populations improves transmission. Nonlinear coincidence models reproduce important features better than the tested single-input or linear-sum models under matched postsynaptic background firing.
sources.application_inference: A common receiving neuron supplies an experimentally meaningful relation among inputs without a global neuron metric. This motivates distinguishing target-local integration from anatomical distance and from pairwise coactivity alone; it does not select a nonlinear integration rule for the application.
transfer_limits: The same one-second Gaussian-noise realization, filtered with a 3 ms alpha kernel, is reused across trials and stimulation sites. It is a shared external signal, not independent noise at every model neuron or evidence of autonomous DMN-like semantic cycling.

The main neocortical sample comprises 1867 pyramidal cells and 563 interneurons from seven mice, with 239 directly activated pyramidal cells and 116 indirectly activated interneurons meeting response criteria. Recorded converging inputs are a subset of actual inputs, not an anatomical degree census.

Precision is the smallest spike-jitter half-window that significantly degrades cross-validated decoding quality. It is not a directly measured axonal delay, single-spike latency variance or guaranteed online decoding resolution.
Modified Wiener reconstruction uses an acausal filter. Better recovery than any individual presynaptic cell does not mean information is created beyond the joint presynaptic population.

Lower illumination and multiple simultaneous sites provide positive recruitment controls. Multiple sites preserve per-source illumination, not necessarily total drive; these interventions do not isolate input identity at a fixed total conductance.

With realistic background firing, the coincidence model yields reliable responses in 54 of 109 modeled targets, versus none for the tested labeled-line and summed-population models. It remains less precise than actual targets and does not identify the biological nonlinear mechanism uniquely.
Directly versus indirectly activated interneuron coding comparisons use different cell populations. No pyramidal-to-pyramidal transmission or formation of new anatomical edges is established.
No minicolumn correspondence, semantic-coordinate geometry, recurrent semantic-loop acceptance, auxiliary state or implementation allocation follows from this study.

sources.authors: Lidor Spivak, Shirly Someck, Amir Levi, Sarit Sivroni and Eran Stark
sources.title: Wired together, change together: Spike timing modifies transmission in converging assemblies
sources.evidence_type: Primary mouse CA1 closed-loop optogenetics and spike-transmission analysis
sources.read_scope: EuropePMC XML results and discussion; closed-loop stimulation, sample selection, transmission-gain measurement, prediction and grouped-validation methods. Published author PDF Figure 5 visually inspected. Supplementary PDF request returned 403; its figures were not independently inspected.
sources.finding: Connections from pyramidal cells converging on the same PV interneuron have correlated transmission gains and coordinated changes. The timing of peer inputs predicts a given connection's gain change better than that pair's timing alone. Real closed-loop stimulation supplies timing-related predictive information beyond a postsynaptic firing-rate proxy; virtual closed-loop controls do not show the same timing signal.
sources.application_inference: Learning evidence can be specific to a receiving cell and its existing input ensemble. Such a target-centered relation is relevant to evaluating incoming-slot computation, but does not establish spatial proximity, a new-edge proposal distribution or approval of target-owned slots.
transfer_limits: The selected stimulation dataset contains 1026 connected pyramidal-PV pairs, 689 pyramidal cells and 122 PV cells from 29 sessions in four mice. Controls retain 388 pairs from nine sessions in five mice. Many pairs share cells and sessions.

Spike transmission gain is estimated from deconvolved cross-correlograms with an identified causal peak; it is effective spike transmission rather than direct synaptic conductance or an anatomical contact count.
The population has no significant uniform direction of median gain change. Absolute changes are larger with stimulation, while coordinated peer changes also occur in controls.

Main pair-level classifiers use repeated random fivefold validation. Crucially, the paper also reports whole-assembly held-out validation and one-pair-per-assembly subsampling with similar qualitative findings. These controls must be retained; claiming that all prediction results leak assembly membership would be incorrect. Held-out-animal generalization is not established.

Peer timing classification AUC is about 0.673 versus 0.513 for the individual pair in the main analysis. Assembly-level real-stimulation timing and firing-rate predictors reach about 0.746 and 0.725, combined about 0.796; virtual-control timing is approximately chance. These are within-study prediction results, not a complete causal partition of cellular mechanisms.
Closed-loop triggering and illumination affect an ensemble, not an isolated synapse. Mean firing-rate change is a useful excitability proxy but does not exhaust intrinsic response-gain changes.

The study examines changes of detected existing pyramidal-to-PV connections. It neither demonstrates preferential formation between nearby semantic neurons nor prescribes a universal pairwise STDP rule, inhibitory learning rule, physical metric or state representation.

sources.authors: Ali Ghadiri, Saeed Taghavi, Hedyeh Rezaei, Ad Aertsen, Arvind Kumar and Alireza Valizadeh
sources.title: Delay Selection by Spike-Timing-Dependent Plasticity Shapes Efficient Networks for Signal Transmission
sources.evidence_type: Primary conductance-based spiking-network simulations
sources.read_scope: Published author PDF main model, delay-selection results, sparse and frequency-mismatch controls, limitations, and four-page supplement captions. Main Figures 4 and 5 visually inspected. No author simulation code executed or located from the paper's prospective availability statement.
sources.finding: Arrival-time STDP selects fixed-delay connections according to network dynamics. Forward connections favor short delays; reciprocal feedback pathways favor delays compatible with the coupled resonance period. Pulse-driven and spontaneously oscillatory conditions both show selection, with limited robustness to frequency mismatch and reduced projection density.
sources.application_inference: A learning preference based on transmission timing need not be a monotone function of anatomical distance, let alone semantic-index distance. A useful feedback route can be longer than an early-arriving forward route. Timing remains an unchosen modeling option requiring an explicit task benefit and state cost.
transfer_limits: Each layer contains 200 excitatory and 50 inhibitory cells, with 70 excitatory projection cells. Inter-layer projections are excitatory-to-excitatory. Main plastic conditions start with all-to-all projection connectivity; reduced densities of 75%,50%,25% are separate controls.

Individual axonal delays are fixed. Plasticity changes weights and a threshold defines the potentiated subset; the results are not direct adaptation of conduction delay or demonstrated formation and removal of physical synapses.

The all-pairs additive STDP rule uses hard weight bounds and specified millisecond kernels. NEST dummy neurons implement arrival-time bookkeeping. Neither these auxiliary cells nor per-edge delays are approved application state.

Sparse controls rescale initial weights, maximum conductances and survival thresholds inversely with density. They preserve potential total drive by construction and do not validate our fixed FP8 slot budget or a degree-distribution law.

The static-forward/plastic-feedback example improves signal-to-noise with similar mean feedback weight. When both directions learn, their mean weights change differently, including a substantial forward increase. The latter is not an exactly matched total-weight ablation; a blanket claim of no weight increase would overstate Figure 5.
Signal-to-noise is based on population-activity variance around pulse stimulation. It is not semantic-sequence fidelity, information capacity or a broad per-CC activity-fraction bound.

Moderate resonance mismatches retain the effect; larger mismatches largely suppress feedback potentiation. Authors explicitly leave persistence after removing pulse packets, unlearning and changing activity regimes for future study.

The oscillatory regime receives ongoing background drive and has synchronized rhythms. Neither indefinite autonomous semantic recurrence nor compatibility with all three requested regimes is established. No physical embedding is learned or required by the reported delay assignment.

sources.authors: Sebastian Spreizer, Ad Aertsen and Arvind Kumar
sources.title: From space to time: Spatial inhomogeneities lead to the emergence of spatiotemporal sequences in spiking neuronal networks
sources.evidence_type: Primary spatial spiking-network simulations with prescribed connectivity and independent external noise
sources.read_scope: Published PDF and EuropePMC XML: connectivity configurations, spontaneous and evoked sequences, correlation-scale variation, structural-path analysis, neuromodulator hypothesis, biological-evidence limits, network and detector methods. Figures 2 and 8 visually inspected. Selected published-date code audited without execution.
sources.finding: Spatially correlated directional biases in otherwise local recurrent connectivity produce propagating activity patterns in both inhibitory-only and excitatory-inhibitory models. Isotropic or independently random directional controls remain localized; a uniform direction creates common-direction waves. Locally varying coordinated directions produce more diverse paths.
sources.application_inference: This is positive evidence for a particular organization of directed pathways, beyond radial distance decay alone. It supplies an explicit spatial construction of spontaneous sequences but does not establish its necessity, a 2D advantage over matched nonspatial graphs, or compatibility with fixed dense semantic representation.
transfer_limits: The model starts from a square grid folded into a torus, with prescribed local kernels and a correlated directional field. These are added model ingredients, not recovered physical positions for our neurons.

The inhibitory model has 10000 cells and 1000 sampled outgoing contacts per source; the E/I model has 14400 E and 3600 I cells with nominal 720 E-target and 180 I-target contact draws per source. Multiple contacts are allowed, self-connections removed, and distinct partner degree is not equal to contact count.

Directional asymmetry affects all sources in the inhibitory-only model and only E-to-E contacts in the E/I model. Direction histograms and approximate degree distributions are controls, but spatial correlations of incoming connectivity vary with the directional field.

Independent Gaussian external drive sustains spontaneous activity. No short-term depression, adaptation or synaptic learning is needed for the reported patterns; this is a useful positive control, but the paths are prescribed by connectivity rather than learned semantic sequences.

Sequence detection uses two spatial dimensions plus rescaled time, with density-clustering parameters adjusted to activity level. Its count and speed measurements are not geometry-independent semantic evaluations.

The structural feedforward-path search repeatedly selects 64 maximally innervated cells from an initially local 8-by-8 patch and classifies paths partly by endpoint spatial separation. Failure of this search is not proof that the full graph has no directed paths or cycles.

In low-drive conditions a stimulus evokes a pattern reliably but persistence after stimulation is brief. In strong ongoing activity, the authors explicitly warn that overlap with spontaneous patterns can give a false impression of long stimulus-evoked persistence.

The neuromodulator mechanism is a proposed explanation rather than a demonstrated adaptive implementation. The authors state that anatomical asymmetry is known but the required spatial correlation of preferred directions still needs dedicated experimental validation.

No minicolumn assignment, signed-vector decoder, learned semantic ordering, valence bias, activity-fraction band or slot-capacity law is tested. The results neither establish nor rule out a useful application role for directed nonspatial structure.

correction.scope: Adds an author affiliation; no scientific result, model or code correction.

sources.authors: Lida Kanari, Ying Shi, Alexis Arnaudon and colleagues
sources.title: Of mice and men: Dendritic architecture differentiates human from mouse neuronal networks
sources.publication_status: Published online June18,2025; iScience28(7),112928,July18,2025. Review uses the published version rather than the earlier bioRxiv manuscript.
sources.evidence_type: Primary morphological reconstructions, synthetic anatomical circuit reconstruction and graph analysis
sources.read_scope: Published EuropePMC XML and institutional published PDF: morphology, network construction, hybrid control, pruning, simplex analysis, capacity assumptions and limitations. Main Figures3 and6 visually inspected; selected released notebooks and their saved outputs inspected without execution.
sources.finding: Human cortical pyramidal dendrites differ from mouse dendrites in branching organization beyond simple size scaling. In the reconstructed models, human morphology supports more directed-clique structure despite lower cell density. A hybrid model using human placement and axons with length-scaled mouse dendrites preserves much of the mouse-like pyramidal graph structure, providing a positive morphology control.
sources.application_inference: Physical anatomy constrains a structured set of possible contacts that cannot be reduced to soma distance or total neurite length alone. This supports distinguishing opportunity from learned connectivity and investigating useful graph relations, without assigning an anatomical layout to fixed semantic roles.
transfer_limits: Neurons are placed homogeneously in constructed hexagonal columns with species-specific thickness and density; seven columns reduce boundary effects. This is not a measured complete human cortical-column connectome.

Axon-dendrite proximity within2 micrometers defines possible contacts. Random reduction toward approximately4% total graph density then selects edges; no measured cell-type-specific or activity-dependent synapse-selection rule is recovered.

The4% reference is estimated using3750 distinct partners in a hypothetical100000-cell population. It is neither a universal local pair probability nor an application degree law. The instantiated graphs contain about15000–17000 cells, so the same density implies different actual degrees.

Incomplete human axons are repaired or paired with better-reconstructed axons; morphologies are cloned with small coordinate noise. These operations approximate missing anatomy and introduce assumptions rather than restoring the original complete cells.
The human/mouse analysis pools selected tissue sources and cell types. Basket cells dominate the interneuron subset; broad interneuron generalization is explicitly limited.

The hybrid and random-graph controls support a morphological structural difference. They do not directly measure task performance, learned semantic sequences, stable recurrence or human cognitive superiority.

Reported memory capacity is a combinatorial estimate for nonlinear dendritic inputs, not a trained recurrent-network memory measurement. Directed-simplex dimension alone does not establish recurrent feedback (ANA-104).

Published Figure3, main-text degree statistics and released notebook plots/counts are not fully consistent (AUD-049). Exact graph counts, degree values and largest simplex dimensions are not transferred to application sizing from this review.
No dendritic compartments, anatomical coordinates, contact-pool allocation, pruning algorithm, subtype field or auxiliary state is adopted.

sources.authors: Natalí Barros-Zulaica, Daniela Egas Santander, Lida Kanari and colleagues
sources.title: Uncovering the Basis of Human Connectome Complexity: The Role of Neuronal Morphology
sources.publication_status: bioRxiv preprint v1, posted February13,2026; not peer reviewed.
sources.evidence_type: Primary anatomical reconstruction and computational graph controls, with comparisons to published physiology and electron microscopy
sources.read_scope: Public author-manuscript text: structural and pruning results, distance/degree/reciprocity controls, conditional-neighbor and contact-count analyses, Discussion and limitations, Methods4.1–4.5. Published figures were not visually inspected and underlying connectome matrices were not downloaded.
sources.finding: Morphology creates correlated potential-contact opportunities; cooperative pruning constrained by bouton density and contacts per connection retains a structured subset. Distance-conditioned and degree-based graph controls explain different components of observed motif enrichment. Predicted human-versus-rat differences depend on morphology, pruning and sampling scale.
sources.application_inference: This strengthens the distinction between available partners, contact multiplicity, selective retention and functional learning. It supports examining structured opportunities and directed motifs without identifying semantic coordinates with anatomical locations.
transfer_limits: Human temporal tissue and juvenile rat somatosensory tissue differ in region, age, density and reconstruction completeness; species differences are not isolated experimentally.
The authors explicitly model statistical endpoints of development and pruning, not the complete causal processes. Biological coactivity-dependent learning is not recovered from the pruning rule.

CPC is constrained by bouton densities and contacts per connection. Agreement with those quantities is partly calibration, not wholly independent validation. Random-touch and random-edge controls separately match contact or edge totals.

The extracted central volumes contain20072 human neurons and20064 rat neurons; the reported connectivity analyses focus on excitatory pathways. Reported global probabilities are model-dependent and are not a degree prescription for614400 application cells.

A distance-dependent independent-edge control reduces reciprocal enrichment substantially; a configuration model approximately preserves degrees. The reciprocal-edge relocation control preserves the undirected skeleton and reciprocal count, but not every neuron degree or reciprocal-edge location.

Nearest-neighbor conditional connectivity in patch recordings uses the nearest recorded cell, not the nearest neuron in the tissue. The modeled offset analysis bins horizontal and vertical separation; broad sampling can alter apparent motif enrichment.

The discussion acknowledges that the strongest conditional effect in the Peng human recordings occurs beyond100 micrometers, which does not straightforwardly support the proposed special role of very close pairs.
Increasing conditional contact counts can indicate heterogeneous or correlated opportunity without identifying a causal reinforcement process (ANA-107).

The positive morphology/pruning controls concern structural statistics. No semantic decoder, autonomous recurrent regime, fixed-slot learning algorithm or functional advantage for the application is established.
No physical coordinates, dendritic compartments, contact-count fields, delay fields or additional memory allocation are adopted.

sources.authors: Samuel Eckmann, Edward James Young and Julijana Gjorgjieva
sources.title: Synapse-type-specific competitive Hebbian learning forms functional recurrent networks
sources.evidence_type: Primary rate-network simulations and analytical learning/stability calculations
sources.read_scope: Published PMC manuscript Results on lateral interactions and fixed-feedforward recurrent learning, Discussion, model/plasticity/input Methods; accepted author PDF including targeted supplement sections on L1/L2 normalization and eigencircuit stability. Figure5 visually inspected; selected released source audited without execution.
sources.finding: Separate competitive normalization of excitatory and inhibitory weights lets Hebbian plasticity organize recurrent interactions. Crucially, the Figure5 experiment fixes feedforward tuning while learning recurrent connectivity and obtains contrast-dependent response normalization; it does not require learning new feedforward identities. Other experiments learn receptive fields, which is a different scope.
sources.application_inference: This is a positive example of useful learned recurrent computation compatible with assigned input roles, without a supplied anatomical distance between recurrent cells. The relevant mechanism is competition among weights and structured E/I interactions, not proximity between semantic dimension labels.
transfer_limits: The cells are continuous rectified-power rate units, not FP4 spiking cells. The tested circuits use dense matrices and do not implement finite sparse connection slots, partner discovery or migration.
Biological excitatory/inhibitory populations obey distinct output signs. They are not the application's positive/negative coordinate populations or semantic valence categories.

The fixed-feedforward test uses orientation-selective input curves and single-grating training chosen to maintain feedforward dominance despite strong recurrence. Its success does not establish behavior for arbitrary multidimensional semantic trajectories or autonomous activity.
The center-surround experiment additionally supplies two sensory regions and correlated versus separate training; that sensory organization is not an anatomical map for our semantic coordinates.
Winner-takes-all suppression of a weaker competing stimulus is a reported behavior, not automatically desirable for legitimate simultaneous components of a dense semantic vector.

L1 weight competition is a training constraint; static allocated degree does not select its normalization constant. The supplement explicitly shows that changing to L2 normalization can introduce size-dependent variance divergence under its eigencircuit assumptions.

The released code predates the final paper and does not provide an identified Figure5 run/configuration artifact. Its fixed-feedforward switches and normalization path can be inspected, but published curves were not independently reproduced (AUD-051).
No E/I taxonomy, normalization law, firing-rate target, dense topology or application learning rule is selected.

sources.authors: Katya Tsimring, Kyle R. Jenks, Claudia Cusseddu and colleagues
sources.title: Large-scale synaptic dynamics drive the reconstruction of binocular circuits in mouse visual cortex
sources.evidence_type: Primary longitudinal two-photon spine/soma imaging and a phenomenological single-neuron plasticity model
sources.read_scope: Published PMC text and PDF: retention, soma alignment, local coactivity, model ablations, Discussion and experimental/analysis/model Methods. Figure6 visually inspected. Nine selected publication-linked source files read without execution.
sources.finding: During the mouse binocular critical period, retained spines have greater activity, especially at the soma's preferred stimulus, while correlations between nearby spines increase. In a supplied two-branch model, Hebbian and heterosynaptic terms can each improve binocular alignment, but local heterosynaptic interaction is needed for its spatial coactivity clustering.
sources.application_inference: Functional retention and within-target cooperation are separable candidate effects. The measured distance is along a receiving dendrite, not between presynaptic neuron identities or semantic dimensions.
transfer_limits: The experiment follows young mice aroundp22–34, not adult human CCs. Across all timepoints1574/1166/1384 spines were imaged; the fully tracked subset and individual analyses use smaller, partly overlapping samples.
Only40% of the449 D1 spines in the relevant tracked comparison remained atD10. Average spine density stays similar, but this does not measure a fixed-size software connection pool.

Correlation or distance to the nearest spine did not significantly distinguish lost versus retained spines in the reported comparisons. Retained-pair correlation increases mainlyD1→D5; average functional-cluster size and number were not significantly changed.

Spine fluorescence is corrected against the dendritic signal for backpropagating activity; responsiveness has an estimated4% false-discovery rate under scrambled stimulus times. Calcium events and trial-amplitude correlations are not direct presynaptic spike identities or pure noise correlations.

The within-field shuffle reference controls local recording context but does not establish an experimentally manipulated causal learning mechanism. Authors explicitly describe the molecular explanation as putative.

The model supplies dendritic positions, synthetic orientation-tuned inputs, separate pre/post traces and a somatic event accumulator. Replacement redraws input preferences at existing positions; it is not partner discovery among a finite recurrent neuron population.
Model ablations establish different roles for two terms within that model. Their parameter widths and turnover probabilities are not transferable physical constants or selected application rules.

sources.authors: Simone Tasciotti, Daniel Maxim Iascone, Spyridon Chavlis and colleagues
sources.title: Clustered inputs engage dendritic nonlinearities and calcium signaling to support efficient place-field formation in CA1 pyramidal neurons
sources.evidence_type: Primary mouse CA1 anatomical reconstructions and biophysical single-cell simulations
sources.read_scope: Published author-manuscript XML: morphology, noisy-input and place-field comparisons, input shuffling/restoration, limitations and detailed structural/input/model Methods. Six selected publication-release source files audited; figures not visually inspected and simulation datasets not downloaded.
sources.finding: With spine volumes and presynaptic activation preserved, clustered synaptic locations recruit local nonlinearities more efficiently than shuffled locations. Somatic amplification peaks over a limited input-density range. In place-field simulations, adding approximately13% more active inputs to the shuffled configuration restores comparable firing, while calcium/NMDA signals can still differ.
sources.application_inference: This supplies a concrete potential benefit of within-target grouping: input efficiency and access to nonlinear or plasticity-related events. It does not identify a global physical distance among our existing semantic neurons.
transfer_limits: Six reconstructed CA1 pyramidal neurons come from three adult mice; one reconstruction lacks an inhibitory map. The thousands of simulated connectivity patterns are not thousands of independently measured biological neurons.

Structural clusters are defined among spines above the80th volume percentile, separately within each branch, using complete-linkage path-distance clustering with a10-micrometer cutoff. This is not a general nearest-neuron rule.
Noise comparisons use independent5Hz Poisson inputs. The somatic advantage is largest around6% active synapses and diminishes at higher input density; calcium-related differences can persist.

The shuffled comparison preserves spine volume together with input identity, while relocation changes receiving compartments and their distance-dependent conductance compensation (AUD-053). It is not merely a relabeling of a fixed linear weighted sum.

Place-field information can remain similar despite a lower firing rate after shuffling. The restored condition matches activity by adding inputs; it supports an input-count efficiency effect, not unique semantic representability or a measured CPU/energy saving.
Place tuning is supplied by biased in-field input density or larger in-field synapses. Inhibitory spike trains are prescribed; no recurrent inhibitory feedback network or learning rule is simulated.
The model represents a post-learning state. Proposed implications for maintaining plasticity through calcium remain predictions, not measured learning or autonomous semantic-loop performance.

The discussion contrasts Basak/Narayanan2018, whose clustering confines the entire input load to one or two branches. Different definitions and nonlinear operating regimes must be compared before declaring clustered versus dispersed wiring universally superior.

sources.authors: Reshma Basak and Rishikesh Narayanan
sources.title: Spatially dispersed synapses yield sharply-tuned place cell responses through dendritic spike initiation
sources.evidence_type: Primary conductance-based single-neuron modeling with multiparameter search and virtual channel knockouts
sources.read_scope: Full published PMC text: synaptic normalization and input definitions, localization comparisons, search/selection and background-state methods, clustered/dispersed results, dendritic-event explanation, targeted potentiation and limitations. No author code or simulation output obtained; figures not independently visually inspected.
sources.finding: Within the tested model, place-field inputs dispersed across the apical arbor can produce sharp tuning and dendritic spikes, whereas placing the entire input load on one or two obliques performs poorly. Diverse channel parameterizations preserve successful dispersed configurations, and targeted potentiation can select one of several dispersed input patterns.
sources.application_inference: A useful nonlinear computation need not identify one unique anatomical grouping or globally favor maximal concentration. The result is a direct contrast to LOC188 only after distinguishing large whole-branch loading from small clusters distributed across branches.
transfer_limits: The principal comparison uses a fixed anatomical morphology. It contrasts all inputs at the soma, one oblique, two obliques, or randomized apical locations within300 micrometers; this is not an exhaustive comparison of every possible cluster size.

Synapse counts are swept from10 to500, with100 in the principal example. AMPA/NMDA strengths are adjusted so an isolated input gives about0.2mV at the soma, controlling first-order electrotonic attenuation without equalizing all nonlinear responses.

Each localization receives place-field-shaped stochastic inputs with an8Hz modulation and fixed Gaussian temporal envelope. Sharpness is judged by firing-rate peak and width, not arbitrary semantic decoding or recurrent behavior.

Each localization uses an independent5000-model conductance search over0.5–2times baseline. Best-tuned subsets are selected using firing rate and width, so their frequencies are conditional on the sampled parameter ranges and selection procedure.

Concentrated inputs can generate local spikes that fail to reach the soma at low drive and depolarization-induced block at high drive. Distributed inputs recruit coordinated dendritic events under the model conditions. This does not refute the small-cluster gain reported in LOC188.

The multiple-place-field example potentiates a chosen subset by an externally varied factor; it demonstrates feasible selective response, not a learned partner-selection or online plasticity algorithm.

Background conductance controls and virtual channel knockouts strengthen the model-specific mechanism. Detailed dendritic inhibition, several subcellular processes and stochastic ion-channel gating remain outside scope.
No source-neuron metric, semantic layout, dendritic compartment representation or application algorithm is selected.
sources.access_notes: Public EuropePMC XML read. Author-lab page timed out; no code or PDF was assumed available and no unavailable route was repeatedly retried.

sources.authors: Brett W. Larsen and Shaul Druckmann
sources.title: Towards a more general understanding of the algorithmic utility of recurrent connections
sources.evidence_type: Primary analytical task construction and trained artificial-network comparison
sources.read_scope: Full primary XML: connectedness definition and inequalities, architectural constraints, convolution/U-Net comparison, sample generation and training methods; selected discussion and competitive-foraging results. No figure visual inspection or author simulation execution.
finding: Each hidden unit can retain a fixed pixel-input association. Recurrent masks based on the task-defined four-neighbor adjacency permit learning effective propagation solutions, whereas merely sharing dense weights across time does not reliably discover them in the tested search.

At low allowed step counts, feedforward or hybrid solutions can outperform pure propagation; recurrent solutions become effective with enough processing time. This is a task-and-latency trade-off rather than a universal recurrent advantage.

Experiments use15×15 binary images with path-length distribution controlled over1–25 and explicit disconnected distractors. Most architectures receive Hyperband optimization; masked networks do not, with weight decay disabled. No claim that failed optimization proves mathematical impossibility.
A U-Net with substantially more units can reach similar accuracy. Nominal active parameters/neurons are the paper comparison, not a measured sparse CPU implementation.
sources.application_inference: A supplied relation can help when it expresses the computation required by the task, even with fixed input roles. Here adjacency belongs to the pixels and problem statement; it cannot be transferred to arbitrary embedding-dimension labels. Repeated reachability propagation converges to a classification and does not establish autonomous semantic cycling.
transfer_limits: Supervised gradient training, continuously presented input and real-valued tanh states differ from the requested learning setup.
The source uses dense matrices with masks; useful active connectivity does not establish proportional memory or runtime savings.
No matched1D-versus2D comparison under our fixed signed-coordinate roles.

sources.authors: Xinyu Qian, Amir Ozhan Dehghani, Asa Borzabadi Farahani and Pouya Bashivan
sources.title: Local lateral connectivity is sufficient for replicating cortex-like topographical organization in deep neural networks
sources.evidence_type: Primary trained visual-network modeling with brain-map comparisons and adversarial robustness evaluation
sources.read_scope: Full primary XML: architecture, lateral kernels, behavioral performance, robustness, effective dimensionality and discussion; Figure7 visually inspected in the published PDF page9. Selected released model and robustness source.
finding: ResNet18 filters are arranged on a supplied2D sheet. A kernel-pooling operation mixes channel activations, with preceding-layer padding; the principal simulations apply one step, not an autonomous iterative recurrent process.

Feedforward filters learn from ImageNet with top-down credit assignment. Step/Gaussian/Mexican-hat lateral profiles are prescribed and their extents shrink during training; a separate learnable variant exists.
Step-like coupling shows the strongest AutoAttack robustness; Gaussian coupling has more limited benefit. Larger ranges improve robustness in the tested evaluation, which uses500 validation images.

The selected Gaussian topographic model has53% ImageNet accuracy versus69.57% for ResNet18 and43.9% for the compared TDANN. The drop is16.57 percentage points, not16.57% relative. Accuracy-matched effective dimensionality largely removes the difference from non-topographic models.
The authors present an ensemble-averaging interpretation and identify long-range patchy connectivity and truly learned lateral adaptation as limitations.
sources.application_inference: Averaging related learned features can support robustness, but the study lets those features organize around a supplied sheet. Our assigned coordinate meanings cannot be assumed interchangeable or smoothed across neighboring dimension indices. Benefits require a computation-preserving grouping and an appropriate accuracy/robustness comparison.
transfer_limits: Not a matched test of fixed semantic-coordinate roles or sparse partner learning.
No inspected control establishes that the robustness gain uniquely requires Euclidean2D geometry rather than a different grouping architecture.
No recurrent-cycle, activity-band, FP4/FP8 or CPU-cost acceptance result.
