sources.authors: Ahmad Beyh, Jason Z. Kim, Waheed U. Bajwa and Linden Parkes
sources.title: Geometric constraints and cognitive inputs jointly shape emergent brain dynamics and topology
sources.publication_status: bioRxiv preprint, reviewed v2 as identified by PMC13484749.2 and its v2 self-PDF reference; not peer-reviewed publication.
sources.evidence_type: Primary task-trained RNN comparison with anatomical projection constraints and empirical fMRI subspace evaluation
sources.read_scope: Full primary EuropePMC XML: resultsS3–S6, architecture, projection constraints, regularization, training, PCA, fMRI projection, geometry nulls, variance decomposition and topology methods. Selected publication-date repository snapshot inspected. No PDF figure visual inspection or training/data reproduction.
finding: 100 recurrent units represent left-hemisphere cortical parcels, not individual cells. Masked and bioRNN conditions receive inputs only through14 visual parcels and read outputs through27 default-mode parcels; recurrent matrices remain dense. The allowed input/readout weights are learned, so fixed masks are not fixed feature identities.

The preprint v2 reports final accuracy92.00±1.52% vanilla,74.26±6.25% masked and75.92±10.23% bioRNN. Fitted95%-of-own-asymptote learning times are4019±615,21150±8348 and11729±4834 epochs respectively. The positive geometry advantage is relative to the same projection masks; unrestricted models remain faster and more accurate.

Spatial regularization adds1 minus the Pearson correlation of signed off-diagonal weights with1 minus normalized Euclidean distances, plus the same scaled squared-weight penalty. It is a global relative-pattern objective, not a per-connection wiring-length cost.

Five-dimensional spatial PC subspaces derived from task-driven networks capture more empirical fMRI variance for bioRNNs.1000 matched-training null networks across200 spin-permuted geometries preserve a stronger positive result for the veridical layout. Thus an arbitrary smooth geometry is not equivalent in their anatomically labeled comparison.

Noise-driven and task-driven network subspaces share most of the reported correspondence; task inputs contribute additional unique variance. This is a commonality decomposition, not direct causal isolation of geometry.

Topology is measured after keeping the strongest20% of absolute recurrent weights among intermediate nodes. Emergent topology tracks training; the reported temporal ordering is not a targeted motif-ablation experiment proving necessity.
sources.application_inference: This supplies a positive anatomical inductive-bias example under fixed input/output locations. It does not assign a geometry to semantic-coordinate cells, nor establish the requested autonomous recurrent regimes. Spatial fMRI projection and time-ordered behavioral prediction are different endpoints; both the positive null control and that distinction must be retained.
transfer_limits: Preprint; no application task or numerical-precision match.
Learning time is relative to each run’s own asymptote, not one common target accuracy.
fMRI variance projection is unchanged by time-row permutation and therefore cannot alone verify temporal sequence fidelity.
A symmetric signed proximity target also constrains directional and sign structure, not only length.

sources.authors: Xiaoyu Zhang, Mingyi Huang, Yixuan Cui, Xin Lu and Yuguo Yu
sources.title: Reciprocity coordinates a three-way trade-off in recurrent neural circuits
sources.publication_status: arXiv preprint 2610.19949v1, submitted 2026-10-14; not peer reviewed.
sources.evidence_type: Primary reservoir simulations, linear-system analysis and heterogeneous biological graph comparisons
sources.read_scope: Full primary HTML and selected supplementary sections S1–S7 in the 42-page PDF; Figure 8 and its numerical table visually inspected on PDF page 30; S5 constructive analysis read. No author code or simulations executed.
finding: In the main construction, increasing reciprocal excitatory support improves local restoration toward a bias-supported state while reducing several driven-task scores and cue margins. Thirty-two initial conditions converge to the same nonzero state; this is not evidence for multiple learned memory attractors or autonomous semantic cycling.

Reciprocal support edges have independently sampled weights. A dense off-diagonal inhibitory component and global excitatory/inhibitory cancellation produce the final signed matrix; the nominal 10% excitatory density is not the sparsity of the complete recurrent operator.

The main normalization fixes the largest real eigenvalue. A paired largest-modulus control removes the monotonic local-restoration result and can improve pattern retention instead. Recovery of a trajectory and retention of its label are distinct endpoints.

Linear examples show a real task trade-off: nonnormal shear can expand standardized driven-state volume for one input direction while increasing isotropic noise susceptibility. Isotropic drive gives a different baseline; the result is not a universal advantage of nonnormality.

Supplementary wording that performance consistently degrades across all tested densities/topologies is stronger than the displayed Figure 8 values support. The principal paired findings are retained without adopting that blanket statement.

Human recordings are represented as disjoint recording clusters with unobserved cross-cluster entries zero. Cross-species reciprocity enrichment and state-space-volume summaries are descriptive and have different observation opportunities; the manuscript itself limits inferential interpretation of the volume comparison.
sources.application_inference: Reciprocal feedback may trade responsiveness for restoration, but a restoration target must be specified. Neither an excitatory-support statistic nor convergence to one fixed point selects a topology for the requested semantic loops. Fixed connection budgets also couple reciprocity to distinct-partner coverage.
transfer_limits: Real-valued tanh reservoirs and trained readouts; no FP4/FP8, local learning, CPU throughput or semantic-role acceptance.
Global balance is neither a row-wise balance constraint nor a Dale-constrained cell model.
No released-code audit or exact numerical reproduction was completed.

sources.authors: Fabrizio Damicelli, Claus C. Hilgetag and Alexandros Goulas
sources.title: Brain connectivity meets reservoir computing
sources.evidence_type: Primary connectome-constrained reservoir comparison across memory tasks
sources.read_scope: Primary full XML: topology construction, task results, scaling, hyperparameter and task methods, selected discussion; six released source files. No figure visual inspection or simulations executed.
finding: Random signed weights on anatomical binary masks can perform comparably to random reservoirs. Ranking signed weights according to anatomical connection strength can impair the tested tasks; a preserved connectome mask alone does not guarantee a computational advantage.

Upscaling each anatomical area to several artificial neurons improves the ranked case when inter-area weights are partitioned heterogeneously; homogeneous partitioning lacks that benefit. This is a macro-area-to-unit mapping, not a neuron-level anatomical sheet.
One control matches global connection density; other controls use a fixed mean degree or full connectivity. These conditions do not all preserve the same degree distribution or edge budget.

Common selected hyperparameters include spectral radius 0.99, input scale 1e-5, leak 1 and bias 1. These are held across conditions rather than optimized separately for each topology. The result is conditional on tasks and operating point.

The scalar-memory endpoint sums squared correlations over delays; the cued sequence endpoint is scored during recall. Neither endpoint directly measures a self-sustaining semantic loop or an activation-fraction band.
sources.application_inference: Biological topology should be credited for a specific measured computation, not imported as a generally superior prior. Useful heterogeneity can depend on how node roles and weights are assigned, which matters for our fixed semantic roles.
transfer_limits: No trained recurrent partner selection, signed-coordinate minicolumns or quantized sparse execution.
No universal random-topology superiority is established.
The external bio2art upscaling implementation was not audited.

sources.authors: Laura E. Suárez, Blake A. Richards, Guillaume Lajoie and Bratislav Misic
sources.title: Learning function from structure in neuromorphic networks
sources.evidence_type: Primary published abstract/preview/figure captions and selected released analysis source; partial article access
sources.read_scope: Publisher metadata and abstract plus the primary publisher preview and figure captions displayed by ResearchGate; seven source files across the workflow and simulator repositories. Full final article text and figure images were not obtained.
finding: Published captions report a connectome advantage over rewired and spatial-label nulls around a near-critical gain regime; cost-adjusted performance has a broader reported advantage. This is a positive, operating-point-dependent finding rather than a topology-independent superiority claim.

The inspected workflow supplies subcortical input and uses cortical network modules as readouts. Its spin control permutes readout-module labels while retaining the graph and generated states; this is different from retraining a network under a permuted geometry.

The released simulator uses tanh dynamics despite its sim_lnm filename. The graph is a nonnegative symmetric connectome, and alpha scales recurrent weights; it is not the leak parameter used in some other reservoir studies.

Memory performance sums absolute correlations. A separate threshold-based capacity field also exists, but the inspected Figure 2 analysis selects the performance field. This cannot be equated numerically with squared-correlation memory capacity.

The cost calculation sums anatomical distance times raw connection weight over one triangle and normalizes scores for display. This is an anatomical wiring proxy, not measured CPU or communication cost in the proposed application.
sources.application_inference: Anatomical input/readout relationships can carry useful task structure. Their positive result does not establish a physical metric among our semantic dimensions, and its score and null model must remain distinct from other reservoir comparisons.
transfer_limits: Partial primary article access limits reconstruction of all final controls and methodological details.
Macro-connectome modules are not fixed embedding-coordinate roles.
Source snapshots are not certified exact reproduction environments; no author data, code or model was executed.
sources.access_notes: Primary preview: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353780963_Learning_function_from_structure_in_neuromorphic_networks . A separate third-party preprint PDF returned 403 and was not retried. The 4.2 GB data archive was not downloaded.

sources.authors: Ciana E. Deveau, Zhishang Zhou, Paul K. LaFosse, Yanting Deng, Saghar Mirbagheri, Nicholas Steinmetz and Mark H. Histed
sources.title: Recurrent cortical networks encode natural sensory statistics via sequence filtering
sources.publication_status: Published Neuron 114, 1489–1503.e4, 2026-04-15. Reviewed author-hosted publisher-formatted article-in-press PDF; an older 2025 bioRxiv v3 XML was identified separately and not substituted for the final methods.
sources.evidence_type: Primary two-photon perturbation and electrophysiology experiments with a trained fixed-input/readout RNN example
sources.read_scope: Publisher-formatted PDF main results, relevant discussion and STAR Methods, especially pp.5,7–13,19–20; Figure 5 visually inspected on PDF page 10. Four small released source artifacts inspected. No author model or neural data executed.
finding: Changing the preceding pattern changes responses to the same middle stimulation pattern. The middle pattern retains both input identity and ordinal position, strengthening the context interpretation beyond a generic first-versus-later effect.

Optogenetic patterns derived from a movie frame produce greater incremental responses in their matched preceding movie context than in an unmatched context. Matched responses are not on average greater than the optogenetic-only condition; the authors distinguish relative selectivity from unconditional amplification.

Earlier stimulation excites some non-target cells and suppresses others. Sequences constructed from these measured responses produce the predicted boosted versus attenuated responses; boosted populations also have a higher response-sparsity index. This is a positive designed-perturbation result.

For excited target cells, later incremental responses can be approximately linear; previously suppressed cells show sublinear responses. Electrophysiological responses persist long enough for inter-frame interactions, with approximately 70 ms excited and 210 ms suppressed response widths in the reported comparison.

The computational example trains recurrent weights while input weights and the identity readout remain fixed. It demonstrates context-sensitive driven responses without requiring learned reassignment of input/output roles.

Cells within 10 micrometers of prior stimulation targets are excluded to control off-target stimulation and pattern overlap. That experimental rule is not a biological near-neighbor exclusion zone or a learned partner-selection radius.
sources.application_inference: Fixed semantic roles can coexist with learned, history-dependent recurrent response modulation. The experiment supplies useful functional evidence without assigning physical coordinates to our semantic neurons. Filtering externally supplied sequences remains distinct from generating or sustaining autonomous semantic loops.
transfer_limits: The experiments perturb a local biological circuit and do not identify a monosynaptic excitatory graph or prove that geometry uniquely causes the computation.
The RNN uses dense real-valued tanh recurrence and supervised backpropagation, not the proposed bounded local learning system.
Released example settings differ from the publication in several details; no exact Figure 4 reproduction is claimed.

ScienceDirect returned403 and was not retried. Selected code was read by byte ranges from the public Zenodo archive; its 7.4 GB data payload was not downloaded.

sources.authors: Kisang Eom, Yujin Kim, Hyoung-Ro Lee, Yolguk Lee, Young-Eun Han, Jiwoo Shin, Jae Sung Lee, Jung Ho Hyun, Alan J. Park and Suk-Ho Lee
sources.title: The hippocampal CA3 area implements sequence learning of discontinuous episodes
sources.evidence_type: Primary ex vivo physiology, targeted genetic/behavioral comparison and spiking-network modeling
sources.read_scope: Full primary XML targeted results on intrinsic excitability, sequence modeling and behavioral controls; simulation methods/assumptions and discussion paragraphs0–9. Figures7 and8 visually inspected on PDF pages11–12. Nine selected released source files verified, relevant execution paths read without execution.
finding: The proposed mechanism uses input-specific priming and resetting of intrinsic excitability to recruit a subset of an earlier event ensemble during the next event. Coactivity then links successive ensembles while limiting merger of their main populations.

A CA3-specific Kv1.2 haploinsufficiency manipulation impairs improvement on a first-cue/three-probe sequential task while retaining performance on a fixed-probe-position association task. The latter is a useful control against a blanket inability to discriminate or obtain reward; it does not isolate every cellular consequence of the genetic change.

The model uses1000 excitatory and200 inhibitory cells, sparse nonoverlapping strong-input groups of200 and widespread weaker inputs. Recurrent excitatory connection probability is10%, while the authors note a lower in-vivo CA3 value. Coordinates or physical-distance partner preference are not part of that construction.

After training, a brief partial cue for the first event triggers a compressed one-pass sequence. Encoding and recall differ in recurrent effective strength; excitability/ion kinetics and learning are accelerated for computational convenience.

The authors explicitly state that the model does not encode elapsed time between events and that one-trial simulated learning differs from the gradual behavioral learning. Higher-order sequence extensions and sleep replay remain hypotheses.

An additional simulation includes intervening weak place-cell firing without forcing overt replay of those trajectories. This is a conditional modeling result, not proof that all biological event memory is independent of paths.
sources.application_inference: Transient context-dependent excitability can provide a functional relation between event populations without a new physical neuron metric. The distinctions among event identity, overlap, transition order, elapsed time and repeated cycling are directly relevant to the application.
transfer_limits: Hippocampal CA3-specific input pathways and Kv1.2 mechanism are not established as a universal cortical-column algorithm.
Orthogonal strong-input event groups differ from our dense signed-coordinate patterns.
The model includes multiple traces, conductances, thresholds and post-learning normalization not covered by the current FP4 state/FP8-slot budget; no additional fields are adopted.
First-event cue replay does not establish arbitrary middle-cue directionality, stable repeated loops or the requested regime transitions.

sources.authors: Shirin Shafiee, Sebastian Schmitt and Christian Tetzlaff
sources.title: Dendritic heterosynaptic plasticity arises from calcium-based input learning
sources.evidence_type: Primary compartmental/diffusion modeling with qualitative comparisons to earlier experiments
sources.read_scope: Full primary XML results, sequence selectivity, modeling equations, statistics and selected discussion; Figure5 visually inspected on PDF page7. Six selected source artifacts from the publication archive inspected without execution.
finding: Calcium spreading between spines can produce either cooperation or competition depending on stimulation frequency, relative input timing and plasticity thresholds. Greater distance reduces cross-spine influence in the tested1–3 micrometer range, but does not determine the sign of the resulting weight change.

An80-micrometer branch with16 spines includes a seven-micrometer cluster of seven stimulated and three unstimulated spines, plus six outer spines. Twenty placements and varying diffusion constants are compared; stronger diffusion also changes the stimulated spine response, not only its neighbors.

The model qualitatively matches selected experimental plasticity patterns extracted from published figures. It does not fit or validate against the original raw experimental datasets, which the authors did not have.

A two-input example learns different somatic peak responses for inward and outward sequences while spine positions remain fixed. This is a temporal selectivity example; the displayed firing criterion is a somatic threshold crossing, not an autonomous network cycle.

The model emphasizes early developmental conditions and omits backpropagating somatic action potentials, many calcium sources and inhibitory plasticity. Thresholds are deliberately adjusted between some figures, limiting universal parameter transfer.
sources.application_inference: Biological proximity can mediate a local, state-dependent learning interaction among inputs to one receiving neuron. Such an interaction is neither a globally ordered neuron layout nor simply a larger connection probability for closer cells. A useful computational abstraction would first need a justified function and state budget.
transfer_limits: The distance belongs to spines along a supplied dendrite, not to embedding-coordinate roles or storage order.
No evidence that a distance-only scalar weight can replace the modeled calcium history and threshold interactions.
Released Figure5 example settings differ from printed protocol parameters, so exact numerical reproduction remains unestablished.

sources.authors: Tibor Rózsa, Rémy Cagnol and Ján Antolík
sources.title: Iso-orientation bias of layer 2/3 connections unifies spontaneous, visually and optogenetically driven V1 dynamics
sources.evidence_type: Primary large-scale spiking model compared with previously published cortical recordings
sources.read_scope: Selected full primary Results, Discussion, network, connection, delay and analysis methods; Figure7 and Table2 visually inspected on PDF pages10–11. Eight source files at the publication-linked v1.1 tag inspected.
finding: A model with prescribed orientation preferences and orientation-biased long-range layer2/3 excitation jointly accounts for orientation-related spontaneous correlations, traveling waves, visual and optogenetic responses. Removing functional bias disrupts the correspondence with the orientation map.

Parameter comparisons for conduction delay, E-to-I connectivity and cell density adjust thalamo-cortical strength to match mean activity. This is a useful control against explaining the compared effects solely by average firing level; it does not match every dynamic statistic.

The architecture retains spatially local connectivity as well as a longer-range component weighted by orientation similarity. The supplied functional map, spatial kernel, conduction delay and recurrent E/I organization perform distinct roles.

Optogenetic radius comparisons keep total delivered power constant and exclude a nearby zone affected by light spread. Excitatory surround response and tuning can vary nonmonotonically with radius while inhibitory responses increase.
Comparisons draw on several species and developmental conditions. This is not a single experiment simultaneously validating all adult model regimes, nor a demonstration of semantic sequence learning.
sources.application_inference: Fixed input-response roles can coexist with functionally selective recurrence across spontaneous and driven conditions. That supports studying recurrent relations within assigned roles, while the biological orientation geometry supplies information that arbitrary embedding-coordinate labels do not.
transfer_limits: The model prescribes a feature map and anatomical positions; it does not derive them from a fixed dense semantic embedding.
Long-term partner learning is not modeled; short-term synaptic plasticity is included.
Mean activity matching is not an acceptance result for bounded semantic cycles or token order.
The cited young-ferret patterned stimulation includes an earlier report from the LOC-201 team; these are not independent replications.

sources.authors: Ana R. Inácio, Ka Chun Lam, Yuan Zhao, Francisco Pereira, Charles R. Gerfen and Soohyun Lee
sources.title: Brain-wide presynaptic networks of functionally distinct cortical neurons
sources.evidence_type: Primary single-cell tracing, functional imaging, perturbation and decoding experiments in mouse somatosensory cortex
sources.read_scope: Primary sections on local and long-range inputs, optogenetic suppression, discussion and decoding methods; Figure3 visually inspected. Five public source files inspected without executing analyses.
finding: One postsynaptic neuron per mouse was traced in11 movement-correlated and11 uncorrelated cases, with matched target depth and selection excluding sensory-responsive cells. The local input fraction was approximately79 versus81 percent, with no detected group difference in local counts, laminar composition or tested spatial distributions.

Functionally distinct targets nevertheless differed in long-range source composition: movement-correlated cells had a larger thalamic and smaller motor-cortical input fraction. Inputs from the groups were spatially intermingled within the studied distant areas.

Suppressing thalamic terminals reduced movement-related cortical activity more strongly than motor-cortical suppression or controls; combined thalamic pathways had a stronger effect. Analysis windows avoided the immediate light-triggered movement transient.
Whisker paralysis and trimming preserved the movement-related signal and cross-day decoding, arguing against ordinary peripheral sensory feedback as its principal source under these conditions.

Rabies tracing samples a subset of inputs and gives no synaptic strength. Similar tested local distributions are not proven anatomical equivalence. Distances reported among presynaptic cells describe their cloud spread, not a source-to-target connection probability with an opportunity denominator.
sources.application_inference: Input-source identity and composition can explain functional distinctions not captured by coarse local spatial distributions. This supports separating functional relations from a soma-distance prior; it does not assign semantic cells an anatomical position.
transfer_limits: Behavioral correlation and long-range anatomical areas are not embedding-coordinate roles.
Between-group null results have finite power and do not show all local connectivity is identical.
No autonomous semantic recurrence or neuron-level physical distance kernel is measured.

sources.authors: Haleigh N. Mulholland, Sigrid Trägenap, Matthias Kaschube and Gordon B. Smith
sources.title: Millimeter-scale selective amplification in the developing visual cortex
sources.evidence_type: Primary patterned optogenetic stimulation in developing ferret cortex, recurrent rate model and linear analysis
sources.read_scope: Primary XML Results and selected Discussion; full supplementary methods relevant to noise, mode selection, preprocessing and amplification; supplementary FigureS7 visually inspected. No published source-code release located.
finding: Patterns derived from spontaneous cortical correlations evoked more reproducible responses and greater stimulus-response similarity than random patterns. The advantage persisted when random-pattern spatial wavelength was matched; nine animals contributed to the main comparison.

Mean peak response amplitude was not significantly larger for endogenous patterns in the reported comparison. Reliability and pattern preservation are the central positive outcomes; they should not be paraphrased as a universal increase in firing.
Sustained five-second patterned stimulation produced more temporally stable responses for endogenous patterns. This is continued external drive, not persistence after input removal.

The model uses a supplied two-dimensional excitatory/inhibitory interaction kernel plus spatially correlated heterogeneity. Standard nonlinear gain is1.05 after normalizing the maximum real eigenvalue; mode extraction and the linear comparison use0.99. The linear fixed-point formula is not applied at the nonlinear model gain.

Standard spontaneous samples are independent fixed spatial-noise inputs integrated toward steady responses. Sustained simulations additionally use temporally correlated AR(1) noise. These are distinct protocols, neither interchangeable with an unspecified white-noise-driven SNN.

Input and output singular modes are distinguished in the analysis; approximate symmetry makes their leading patterns similar in the example. Spontaneous covariance is therefore a conditional proxy for preferred stimulation patterns, with a direct empirical test here rather than a general inverse-wiring theorem.
sources.application_inference: Circuit-compatible distributed patterns can be selected by functional response evidence beyond their spatial wavelength. That suggests a meaningful behavioral comparison within assigned semantic roles, but does not supply a distance between those roles or establish self-sustaining loops.
transfer_limits: Young pre-eye-opening visual cortex and widefield calcium patterns are not a validated adult semantic-column model.
Preprocessing includes spatial filtering and, for several measures, subtraction of the mean response across stimuli; amplitude and sustained analyses use different processing.
The spatially homogeneous comparison also changes wavelength, input filtering and integration time; it is not a perfectly isolated single-parameter removal of heterogeneity.
Pooled pattern-level correlations and their significance should not be treated as independent animal-level replication.
Source code is promised on publication and was not audited; the study remains a preprint.

sources.authors: Xinruo Yang and Brent Doiron
sources.title: Causal Spike Timing Dependent Plasticity Prevents Assembly Fusion in Recurrent Networks
sources.publication_status: Primary full text reviewed: arXiv v1, January2025. Related peer-reviewed article: PRX Life4:013011, 2026-01-27, DOI10.1103/9nv2-y63v; final abstract/metadata checked, final full PDF not accessed.
sources.evidence_type: Primary spiking-network simulation and motif-based mean-field theory
sources.read_scope: Preprint network and plasticity definitions, training, overlap/causality controls, motif cancellation, discussion and limitations; Figure4 visually inspected on page10.
finding: Two assigned, partially overlapping groups are trained with separate shared white-noise signals on initially random fixed connectivity. Plasticity continues after training; near-causal timing rules can preserve strong within-group and weak between-group weights despite substantial overlap.

The mechanism suppresses approximately even common-input correlation contributions with an approximately odd learning window. Near balance of potentiation and depression and a compatible timescale regime are explicit assumptions, not consequences of causality alone.

Inhibitory plasticity regulates excitatory firing around a target and supports the operating-point approximation used by the theory. Weight bounds, weak coupling and a random support with probability0.1 also matter.

The overlap parameter counts shared cells as a fraction of the whole network, including inhibitory cells. It is not the fraction of each assembly shared; varying it also changes each assembly size in the fixed-total-population construction.

Only two symmetric assemblies are modeled in the central theory. Pattern-completion capacity and extension to many unequal assemblies are left for future work. Preserved weight structure is not demonstrated autonomous sequence recall.
The authors acknowledge that additive pairwise plasticity tends toward boundary weights and that transfer to more detailed voltage/calcium rules remains unresolved.
sources.application_inference: The temporal structure of learning can protect overlapping functional relations without a physical metric. A near-odd timing rule is a concrete conditional mechanism to investigate, not a universal replacement for coactivity or a selected SNN learning rule.
transfer_limits: The primary derivation reviewed is the2025 preprint, not a verified final-text match.
Group membership and training correlations are supplied; fixed signed-coordinate encoding and many semantic sequences are not tested.
No finite-slot partner-search or capacity-migration algorithm is evaluated.

sources.authors: Toshitake Asabuki, Prajakta Kokate and Tomoki Fukai
sources.title: Neural circuit mechanisms of hierarchical sequence learning tested on large-scale recording data
sources.evidence_type: Primary compartmental spiking model and applications to previously recorded neural activity
sources.read_scope: Primary XML sections on overlapping chunks, mechanism, neural-data analysis, dendritic representations, additive recurrence and neural equations; Figures3 and8 visually inspected; three source files audited.
finding: The model discriminates sequences ABCD, DCBA and BDAC containing exactly the same components with equal frequency. Removing recurrent gating prevents the corresponding context discrimination, providing a stronger control than sequences with unique identifying symbols.
Recurrent signals gate transmission from dendrite to soma according to network history. Dendritic responses can retain component preference while somatic responses depend on sequence context.

For cued completion, an additional additive recurrent pathway is trained. A cue to the first component evokes a subsequent sequence; Figure8 repeats separate cues every five seconds. This is not an indefinite internally sustained cycle.

Afferent weights and recurrent gates are learned together. The network uses signed dense weights, filtered potentials, online mean/variance standardization, nonlinear gates and somatic inhibition. It is not an unchanged fixed-semantic-input model.

Applications sort452 hippocampal cells and6532 visual-cortex cells by learned temporal structure. Neural-data analysis supports utility as an unsupervised detector, not causal proof that the recorded brain uses the proposed dendritic mechanism.
Raster rows are sorted by response onset for visualization. Their apparent sequence slope is not a supplied anatomical coordinate or physical propagation speed.
sources.application_inference: Internally generated context can distinguish shared inputs without geometric ordering. The model separates context gating from excitatory recall, exposing distinct functional requirements that a fixed-role application would have to express and budget.
transfer_limits: Learning afferent identity is permitted in the source but not automatically in our assigned semantic roles.
Theoretical gating alone does not drive an inactive neuron; recall uses an additional pathway.
Memory traces, compartment variables and dense connections exceed a single scalar neuron/connection abstraction.

sources.authors: Viktoria Zemliak, Gordon Pipa and Pascal Nieters
sources.title: Ensemble synchrony reliably disentangles input drive and familiarity
sources.evidence_type: Primary recurrent spiking-network and readout comparisons
sources.read_scope: Primary PDF Results on drive, load, connectivity and synchronized input, Discussion and relevant Methods; Figure4 visually inspected; eight source files audited.
finding: Across varied input rates, population synchrony separates familiar from unfamiliar inputs more robustly than spike count in the tested models, while spike count better identifies which candidate pattern was stimulated.

The positive result appears both in an anatomically inspired V1 arrangement and in a nonspatial associative-memory model with overlapping distributed ensembles. Thus it is not evidence that the effect requires physical geometry.

Familiarity is pre-encoded by stronger recurrent connections, not learned during the reported experiment. The model contains mixed-sign outputs from each neuron rather than separate Dale-constrained excitatory/inhibitory populations.

Pattern identification maximizes activity over a supplied catalogue containing both familiar and novel candidate patterns. This is a meaningful readout comparison within that catalogue, not open-ended discovery of an unknown input support.

Increasing memory load also increases the union of stored connection supports. Inter-ensemble inhibition and within-ensemble excitation are swept, but the memory-load comparison does not hold total distinct degree fixed.

Rsync measures temporal covariance of filtered spikes, not oscillatory phase locking. Rate, synchrony, semantic identity and familiarity remain distinct observables. Multi-stage propagation is proposed but not directly tested.
sources.application_inference: A similar mean activity level can support different temporal coordination and readout quality; functional recurrence can supply this distinction without positions. It does not establish a familiar/negative semantic bias, a cyclic state, or an application synchrony controller.
transfer_limits: Binary100-cell patterns and known candidate groups differ from dense signed semantic coordinates.
Membrane noise was chosen to remain subthreshold without external stimulation, so this is not a DMN self-activation demonstration.
No fixed-slot memory-capacity conclusion follows from increasing stored patterns while changing graph density.

sources.authors: Sebastian Onasch, Christoph Miehl, M. Maurycy Miękus and Julijana Gjorgjieva
sources.title: Assembly-based computations through contextual dendritic gating of plasticity
sources.publication_status: Neuron corrected proof available2026-08-21. Only primary abstract/institutional publication record and released model source reviewed; full article not obtained.
sources.evidence_type: Partial primary article review supplemented by selected author-released model source
sources.read_scope: Published abstract, author institutional record and seven verified repository files including equations, parameters, area construction and Figure4 workflow. No final article or figure-PDF review claimed.
finding: The published abstract proposes dendrite-specific inhibitory gating of plasticity to preserve overlapping assemblies and support context-sensitive associations. Exact effect sizes and all final controls remain unverified without the article.

The released construction assigns several dendrites to each soma and supplies context identifiers. In its non-overlapping-context setting, each context leaves a designated dendrite uninhibited; another setting chooses the spared dendrite randomly per cell/context.

Plasticity depends on local dendritic voltage, filtered voltage and presynaptic traces. Both feedforward and recurrent synapses are plastic; a periodic normalization operates on their combined incoming weight.
Figure4 source schedules contexts and input assemblies externally and compares overlap/recall conditions. It does not establish that semantic context identities are discovered autonomously.
The default model has400 somata, six dendrites per cell and extensive recurrent support, with compartment and synapse state beyond a target identifier and scalar weight.
sources.application_inference: Selective protection of learning is a computational use of dendritic compartmentalization. It is different from assigning physical distance to semantic neurons, and its context source, internal states and feedforward learning would need separate justification.
transfer_limits: Full-text claims and complete final control coverage remain unverified.
Explicit supplied context and context-specific compartments cannot be treated as free consequences of our120 cells per minicolumn.
No model is adopted and no numerical reproduction or application resource estimate is claimed.

sources.authors: Bin Wang, Nicholas J. Audette, David M. Schneider and Johnatan Aljadeff
sources.title: Desegregation of neuronal predictive processing
sources.evidence_type: Primary normative recurrent-network theory and reanalysis of auditory-cortical experiments
sources.read_scope: Primary results on network construction, response desegregation and experimental comparison; full base-network definitions, response classification and statistics; Figure4 visually inspected; five source files audited.
finding: A recurrent model can distribute stimulus representation and prediction-error-like responses across the same cells, with a cell’s response classification differing across stimulus pairs. Higher stimulus dimensionality increases mixed classifications under the modeled assumptions.

The experimental comparison uses expected versus probe sounds during lever-press and passive conditions. Representation similarity is measured in a separate passive presentation window, reducing circularity with the active/passive response contrast.

Probe sounds less similar to the expected sound give less-correlated response contrasts across cells. Figure4 uses five animals; plotted subsamples are not additional animals. The authors explicitly call this an indirect test: animals learned one expected sound, whereas the model comparison includes two learned pairs.

Representation/error labels are operationally defined from match/mismatch responses for each stimulus pair. They are not a measured division into dedicated physical cell classes or static semantic coordinate identities.

The base model derives recurrence from an encoding/prediction objective and changes feedforward/readout vector correlations during learning. Its main analytical limit treats inputs as static or slow relative to neural dynamics; spatial prediction here does not mean anatomical distance.
The normative base uses negative Gram-matrix recurrent feedback. Its input-cancellation computation is distinct from a mechanism for generating autonomous semantic cycles.
sources.application_inference: Assigned semantic participation should not be equated with a universal pure computational response class. Context-dependent recurrent responses can coexist with stable cell identities, but the source’s learned input mappings and paired-stimulus objective do not automatically transfer to our fixed roles.
transfer_limits: The animal comparison is indirect and includes only one learned association per condition.
No physical metric between semantic dimensions is inferred.
Neither predictive response classification nor loose-balance model parameters select FP4 phases, valence behavior or a per-CC activity envelope.

sources.authors: Márton Albert Hajnal, Duy Tran, Zsombor Szabó, Andrea Albert, Karen Safaryan, Michael Einstein, Mauricio Vallejo Martelo, Pierre-Olivier Polack, Peyman Golshani and Gergő Orbán
sources.title: Shifts in attention drive context-dependent subspace encoding in anterior cingulate cortex in mice during decision making
sources.evidence_type: Primary mouse recordings, trained recurrent model and conditional subspace argument
sources.read_scope: Primary sections on suppression, representation geometry, RNN task and context mechanism; RNN methods; Supplementary Information proposition/corollaries on pages2–6; Figure3 visually inspected; four source files audited.
finding: In an audiovisual set-shifting task, irrelevant stimulus identity becomes less decodable in ACC over a trial, especially during behaviorally consistent periods. V1 provides a comparison with much less corresponding suppression. Single-cell changes have mixed signs, so population suppression must not be translated into universal firing-rate decreases.

ACC data include122 neurons from four animals; the V1 comparison uses eight animals. Analyses address recording drift with temporally separated train/test blocks and movement with restricted lick-only comparisons. These controls strengthen the observed contextual association without proving its precise recurrent mechanism.

A30-unit tanh RNN infers context from current stimuli and previous reward/punishment, without an explicit context cue in the standard task. It learns input, recurrent and output weights and reproduces aspects of the context-dependent population response.

All2048 combinatorial five-trial sequences are used for training, with no held-out model evaluation claimed. Histories containing only congruent trials cannot reveal context before a final conflicting trial. The model studies task computation, not novel-language generalization.

The formal subspace argument begins with linear encoding/readout and supplied constant stimulus assumptions. Its nonlinear extension and the interpretation of decoder axes require additional care: smooth monotone response functions do not generally preserve angles, and decoder normals are not automatically encoding directions.

The recurrent weight-power visualization is a linear approximation. Actual tanh dynamics include state-dependent derivatives; matrix powers alone are not a measured anatomical influence kernel or a full nonlinear trajectory.
sources.application_inference: Learned history can modulate the treatment of unchanged inputs without anatomical coordinates or weight changes on each trial. This is useful evidence for context-sensitive computation, while suppression of irrelevant task variables is not automatically appropriate for preserving all legitimate semantic dimensions.
transfer_limits: The standard RNN learns its input weights; fixed weights after training are different from statically assigned semantic roles before learning.
Near-right-angle decoder estimates and nonsignificant tests against90 degrees do not establish exact orthogonality or statistical independence.
The experiment does not identify a distance-dependent partner-selection rule, autonomous semantic cycling, or a new application controller.

sources.authors: Marius Pachitariu, Lin Zhong, Alexa Gracias, Amanda Minisi, Crystall Lopez and Carsen Stringer
sources.title: A critical initialization for biological neural networks
sources.evidence_type: Primary large-scale mouse recordings, random-matrix dynamics and delayed-input decoding benchmarks
sources.read_scope: Primary results, linear stochastic theory, covariance estimation, DMD and simulation methods; Figures3 and5 visually inspected; seven released source files audited.
finding: Near-critical symmetric random linear recurrence gives a covariance rank-spectrum exponent approaching2/3 under its assumptions, versus about1.25 numerically for the compared nonsymmetric model. This is an activity-covariance law, not a neuronal degree or connection-slot capacity law.

Cortical calcium recordings and brainwide electrophysiology show spectra and dominant-mode relaxation broadly consistent with the symmetric model; hippocampal CA1 differs in variance exponent. Large-variance modes have longer timescales, and estimated spontaneous DMD eigenvalues have small imaginary components.

The primary data include18 cortical calcium recordings, eight CA1 recordings and three brainwide electrophysiology recordings. Task datasets provide positive controls for rotational dynamics; they use task-specific time lags rather than a universally identical protocol.

Covariance estimation splits neurons spatially to reduce independent measurement/Poisson noise but does not split training/testing timepoints in the revised SVCA2 analysis. The paper explains this choice using simulation controls; it should not be described as temporal cross-validation.

Sparse-positive, clustered and spatially local symmetric examples preserve the broad variance spectrum when sufficient global positive connections remain. Subtracting the connection probability from all matrix entries introduces a dense negative background; the effective operator is not simply a sparse list of nonzero synapses.

Under ongoing noise, fixed random inputs and fixed recurrence support delayed classification with a trained decoder. Symmetric linear dynamics outperform the compared nonsymmetric and rectified reservoirs for unknown-lag decoding in these benchmarks. Inputs aligned to spontaneous modes use a different inter-trial interval, so the panels are not a single controlled estimate of alignment benefit.

The model unit may represent a neuron or a neuronal group. Spontaneous mouse recordings and a delayed-input task do not establish human DMN, valence-biased drift or self-sustained semantic sequence generation.
sources.application_inference: Long-lived information can arise without assigning a physical distance to semantic coordinates. Retention, noise amplification and autonomous sequence generation remain distinct requirements. The paper supports a candidate dynamical comparison, not an adopted initialization or topology.
transfer_limits: The linear Gaussian-like state is not bounded FP4 three-phase spiking activity.
Random or eigenvector-aligned input maps and a trained output decoder differ from the application’s assigned signed-coordinate roles.
Matched spectral summaries do not uniquely identify anatomical wiring, and truncated/single-lag DMD cannot exclude every hidden rotation.
Dense background inhibition and spectral normalization require explicit mechanisms and resource accounting if ever proposed.

sources.authors: Margot Wagner, Yusi Chen, Arjun Karuvally, Mia Cameron and Terrence J. Sejnowski
sources.title: Balancing stability and flow in hippocampal networks via inductive bias and learned symmetry breaking
sources.publication_status: Published Philos Trans R Soc B381:20250260 in July2026. Detailed review is of April30 preprint v2, DOI10.64898/2026.02.06.704443, its supplement and May22 code; final journal full text unavailable through checked route.
sources.evidence_type: Primary computational fixed-input/output predictive recurrent model and timing-plasticity analysis
sources.read_scope: April30 primary methods, results, biological limitations and ten-page supplement; supplementary equations visually checked;13 released source files inspected at targeted locations. Published abstract/metadata verified separately.
finding: A100-unit recurrent model learns a repeated circular moving-bump sequence while input and output weight maps remain fixed. Random initialization can acquire recurrent structure supporting noise-driven replay and prefix-cued continuation; a task-aligned shifted center-surround initialization improves the reported comparisons.
This is a positive example of learned recurrent sequence dynamics under stable input/output roles. It does not require neurons to acquire arbitrary new input identities during training.

The circular relationship is already present in the input sequence and preferred-position code. Learned banding is examined after sorting neurons by peak response. This representational order is not evidence that semantic dimensions or somata have corresponding physical distances.

The authors explicitly distinguish representational waves from anatomical waves and acknowledge sparse CA3 connectivity with weak anatomical distance dependence. The rate model uses effective signed interactions and does not enforce Dale’s principle; sparse-spiking transfer remains open.

Symmetric and antisymmetric recurrent components are useful descriptions of the learned operator. Their norm ratio is not by itself a universal stability or replay criterion, and a cyclic shift matrix is not purely antisymmetric.

The local timing-plasticity analysis combines a base interaction with its transpose. Its even component depends on the timing-window parameters; the released defaults use unequal potentiation/depression amplitudes and time constants.

Reported outcomes include direct MSE as well as fitted ring decoding, angular-error concentration and residual autocorrelation. The latter metrics have different invariances and cannot each be equated with correct fixed-code replay.
sources.application_inference: Temporal experience can organize functional neighbors without assigning an anatomical metric, while preserving input identities. The evidence is strongest for one repeated continuous ring, not for many overlapping dense signed semantic loops at the application’s sparse budget.
transfer_limits: Fixed identity projections with learned biases are closer to stable roles than fully trained encoders but are not the60+60 stochastic population encoding.
A dense100-unit rate network and one repeated ring do not establish614400-cell CPU performance, FP4 robustness or static slot compliance.
The inspected supplement/source have analytical and evaluation qualifications recorded below; final published corrections were not verified.
No ring, center-surround prior, symmetry target or learning rule is adopted.

sources.authors: W. Jeffrey Johnston, Stephanie E. Palmer, David J. Freedman and Stefano Fusi
sources.title: Nonlinear mixed selectivity supports reliable neural computation
sources.evidence_type: Primary channel-coding theory, finite-code simulations and reanalysis of macaque LIP tuning
sources.read_scope: Main results and discussion, code definitions, energy/population/noise/decoder methods and experimental analysis; Figure2 visually inspected; four pre-publication source files audited.
finding: The paper constructs codes containing all conjunctions of a chosen number O of K categorical features. At fixed raw squared-response energy, squared minimum codeword distance divided by energy is2O/K, so increased conjunction order can improve noise robustness.

Population count for this particular complete code is binomial(K,O)*n^O. Including neuron-maintenance cost or a fixed population ceiling changes the preferred order; the result is not a free gain from adding mixed selectivity at unchanged resources.

The principal channel adds independent Gaussian noise after encoding and uses maximum-likelihood decoding. Supplementary alternatives include Poisson and input noise; the paper explicitly notes that input noise can reduce or reverse some advantages.

Error probability and error magnitude are distinct objectives. Fully conjunctive codes can separate all categories while making errors less related to stimulus similarity; broader receptive fields and intermediate mixing trade fewer distant errors against more frequent nearby errors.

Reanalysis finds both pure and interaction tuning for category and saccade variables among61 analyzed LIP neurons; the categories overlap rather than partitioning the cells. This demonstrates mixed responses even when the extra task combination is not needed for a flexible linear decision, but it does not causally measure the proposed reliability benefit.

Response-space rotations preserve the compared independent-noise channel geometry under the stated transform assumptions. They do not identify neuronal anatomical positions, and the authors acknowledge additional implementation costs for rotated response codes.
sources.application_inference: Stable semantic assignments need not imply that every recurrent response is a pure one-dimensional function. However, any proposed contextual specialization must preserve the assigned semantic meaning and be evaluated at fixed neuronal, connection and state budgets. A generic mixed-selectivity benefit does not authorize re-encoding the semantic vector.
transfer_limits: The full categorical Cartesian code differs from the finite, correlated, dense signed Flash token table.
A channel with independent output noise and an ideal decoder is not an autonomous SNN learning/replay model.
No physical neighborhood, population remapping or optimal mixing order follows for the application.

sources.authors: Pantelis Vafidis and Antonio Rangel
sources.title: Stimulus-to-stimulus learning in RNNs with cortical inductive biases
sources.evidence_type: Primary computational associative-learning model with released implementation
sources.read_scope: Architecture, learning, conditioning, convergence and decoder methods; three supplementary texts; Figure2 visually checked; five pinned source files inspected.
finding: Two-compartment rate neurons learn cue-to-outcome substitution using a somatic teaching signal and a dendritic prediction error. The outcome input mapping and decoder are fixed; cue and recurrent weights learn.
The delay-conditioning result survives removal of recurrent connections. Trace conditioning requires a separate memory network pretrained by backpropagation. Trials reset network state.
The implementation supplies trial timing and the paired outcome index to the surprise calculation. The mechanism does not independently discover every element of its teaching protocol.
Supplementary Oja/BCM comparisons show interference or timing sensitivity for the tested variants; they do not prove that every coactivity-based rule fails.
sources.application_inference: Synapse-local information is distinct from physical proximity. Fixed semantic roles could coexist with learned predictive effects, but the paper also changes cue mappings and uses explicit teaching/memory machinery absent from the current design.
transfer_limits: Separated Boolean patterns, continuous rates and a fixed decoder differ from dense signed Flash input and FP4 states.
Conditioned substitution is not autonomous multi-step semantic recurrence.

sources.authors: Gloria Cecchini and Alex Roxin
sources.title: Locally balanced inhibition allows for robust learning of input-output associations in feedforward networks with Hebbian plasticity
sources.evidence_type: Primary theory and simulations of binary feedforward Hebbian learning
sources.read_scope: Results, binary-plasticity/input-coupling/inhibition methods and discussion; Figure5 visually checked.
finding: A fixed fraction of active output cells can coexist with repeated selection of the same high-input cells, freezing representations despite continued varied inputs.
Subtracting inhibition proportional to each target’s incoming degree prevents freezing in the studied uniform-input regime. Here local refers to the receiving cell, not an anatomical neighborhood.
Too little compensation leaves freezing; too much produces alternating activity. The balanced setting depends on the input coding fraction.
sources.application_inference: A broad per-CC activity envelope and useful diversity of semantic responses are separate properties. Degree compensation needs the source-activity assumptions to be stated; it is not a capacity-allocation parameter.
transfer_limits: The model is binary and feedforward, with homogeneous random input marginals.
Mean compensation alone does not equalize covariance, gain or response probabilities under heterogeneous dense semantic inputs.

sources.authors: Tanguy Cazalets and Joni Dambre
sources.title: Reshaping reservoirs with unsupervised Hebbian adaptation
sources.evidence_type: Primary reservoir-learning benchmarks and explicit algorithm supplement
sources.read_scope: Results, preprocessing, channel duplication, learning, comparison and complexity methods; SI Algorithms/AppendicesA–D and selected result tables; FigureD4 visually checked.
finding: Approximately500 neurons receive one fixed input channel each. Correlation-guided excitatory growth and random pruning adapt recurrence without anatomical coordinates; a supervised ridge readout performs the task.

Dedicated channel groups outperform matched random input mapping in19 of21 reported comparisons; gains vary substantially, with two large cases. Classification benefits are stronger than forecasting benefits.
Per-cell mean or variance targets drive adaptation. Variance control also uses saturation scaling; convergence is not proved.

The supplement explicitly estimates worst-case quadratic pairwise correlation work. Its target-wise pseudocode and the main text’s global-pair description leave a selection-order ambiguity; symmetric scores alone do not establish reciprocal row-wise choices.
sources.application_inference: This is a useful existence example for fixed channel assignment plus nonspatial recurrent adaptation. It does not establish a suitable algorithm at614400 cells or autonomous semantic loops.
transfer_limits: Inputs are normalized nonnegative features, not the current signed encoder.
A maximum-degree parameter, changing continuous weights and statistical windows do not implement the static slot-class contract.

sources.title: Rapid context inference in a thalamocortical model using recurrent neural networks
sources.evidence_type: Primary computational context-inference and continual-learning study
sources.read_scope: Results, two model architectures, input routing, plasticity, training/evaluation and transfer methods; Figure5 visually checked; seven released source files inspected.
finding: Activity traces and competitive Hebbian learning produce stable context-dependent gating in the studied tasks, improving retention across task switches.
Simple cue tasks use disjoint sensory groups. The complex-task model adds a separate context pathway with task-disjoint input routing and supervised learning in the recurrent task network.
Disjoint gating protects tasks but limits forward transfer. The overlapping-gate comparison uses task relationships measured from a separately trained multitask model.
sources.application_inference: Context can regulate responses without physical neighborhoods, but the origin of context information must be explicit. Task-indexed routing is not equivalent to inferring latent context solely from overlapping token vectors.
transfer_limits: The model introduces separate context/thalamic modules and continuous states.

sources.title: Thalamic regulation of switching between cortical representations enables cognitive flexibility
sources.evidence_type: Primary mouse recordings, optogenetic interventions and reservoir model
sources.read_scope: Full results/discussion, cue controls, cell classification, coupling analyses, intervention and computational methods; primary XML figures/captions reviewed.
finding: Cueing contexts can group different sensory modalities; thalamic activity reflects multi-trial cue regularities rather than only modality.

Timed thalamic suppression delays switching and permits out-of-context cortical activity. Suppression during an intervening context also impairs later reuse, consistent with protection of currently irrelevant responses.
The companion reservoir uses explicit context identity to gate disjoint cue groups. Its implementation explains a proposed function rather than discovering all contextual structure.
sources.application_inference: The experiments support selective functional engagement and preservation within unchanged anatomy. They do not provide a physical-distance preference for our semantic populations.
transfer_limits: GLM coupling is functional dependence, not a complete synaptic map.
Regional interventions support circuit functions without proving every modeled cell-to-cell edge or learning rule.

Routing a switch signal through a two-unit context representation uses fewer target connections than the compared direct cortical route. The advantage depends on the supplied architecture and compressed context code.

sources.title: Backpropagation through space, time and the brain
sources.evidence_type: Primary computational learning framework and benchmark study
sources.read_scope: Core postulates, dynamical derivation, temporal approximation, cortical circuit proposal, scaling/noise/symmetry, open questions and benchmark methods; Figure11 visually inspected. Eight source files read at a pinned preprint-era revision.
finding: Retrospective and prospective neuronal operations provide an online approximation to temporal error propagation, with positive teacher-student, classification and time-series prediction results.

Local plasticity receives error signals transported through feedback connections; ideal feedback mirrors forward weights and uses complementary temporal constants. Benchmarks study noisy alignment and other deviations.

Large-task simulations separate teaching-error and representation dynamics using weak somato-dendritic coupling. The published chaotic forecasting benchmark feeds output back to delayed input channels after a teacher-driven prefix.
The authors explicitly leave dedicated treatment of lateral recurrence and sparse spiking extensions for future work; hierarchical temporal processing and autoregressive feedback are distinguished.
sources.application_inference: Local information processing does not imply a spatial partner preference. The useful transfer question is which teacher, error, timing and recurrent-state information is available under fixed semantic roles.
transfer_limits: Learned hidden/input mappings and richer continuous neuron/error states are not the current FP4 fixed-role model.
Equal phase of individual Fourier components does not imply equality of instantaneous signs for arbitrary mixtures.
Published forecasting uses30 overlapping segments with separate training runs, finer time discretization and RK4; average best-epoch results differ from final-epoch results.
No distance rule, auxiliary error population, training objective or learning algorithm is adopted.

sources.title: Emergence of spontaneous assembly activity in developing neural networks without afferent input
sources.evidence_type: Reanalysis of zebrafish calcium activity and computational assembly-learning study

finding: A nonspatial recurrent binary model develops spontaneously active assemblies from random weights and independent background drive, using covariance learning and incoming/outgoing normalization.
The number of assemblies can stabilize while membership continually reorganizes. Stable assembly count is not stable content.
A separate larger model imposes distance-dependent weight limits on a periodic2D grid and obtains spatially organized assemblies. Its size and learning/noise parameters differ from the basic model.
Noise-free perturbations of trained fixed networks support conditional completion: most tested within-assembly triples trigger an event, whereas individual cells rarely do.

sources.title: Graph partitions and cluster synchronization in networks of oscillators
