sources.authors: Elaine Tring, Konnie K. Duan and Dario L. Ringach
sources.title: ON/OFF domains shape receptive field structure in mouse visual cortex
sources.evidence_type: Awake-mouse calcium imaging, receptive-field measurements and fitted local pooling model
sources.read_scope: Full results and discussion, receptive-field/CCA/density methods; complete PDF obtained and Figure6 visually inspected. Released code/data not read.
finding: Cortical ON/OFF density differences correlate with the distribution of receptive-field centers after alignment of cortical and visual coordinates. Mono-contrast cortical receptive fields are assumed to approximate geniculate inputs, not directly measured as their complete synaptic source population.

The observed receptive fields of simple cells are fitted by nonnegative combinations of nearby ON and OFF receptive fields. Figure6 displays five candidate weights for each polarity; reported fit similarity averages0.84 for k=5 in the illustrated dataset.

The two largest fitted weights within each polarity contribute over90% of the normalized fitted input on average. These are regression-model weights, not directly recorded individual synaptic strengths.

The CCA uses paired measurements of anatomical and visual positions; it does not infer geometry from unpositioned semantic labels. ON/OFF classification concerns luminance response, not a universal inhibitory/excitatory taxonomy.
sources.application_inference: Signed response channels can have structured local organization when a meaningful sensory map and physical sampling neighborhoods already exist. That result does not create retinotopy for fixed LLM coordinate/polarity roles.
transfer_limits: Physical cortical positions and visual-space relations are present before the analysis.
The reported neighborhood fits do not establish a complete anatomical connectome, a generally optimal neighbor count or a2D computational advantage for semantic recurrence.
The study assumes mono-contrast cortical cells approximate afferent signals and states that direct thalamic-bouton testing remains future work.
A label-shuffle density control is distinct from a matched alternative-neighborhood computation or held-out synaptic prediction; no such transfer claim is made here.
No60/60 allocation, activity encoder or learning mechanism is changed.
sources.access_notes: Publisher PDF and EuropePMC XML available. Institutional HTML required a robot check. Figshare public-share page identifies example_code.m, but the linked file request returned HTTP202 with an empty HTML response; its contents were not audited.

sources.authors: Christopher Ebsch and Robert Rosenbaum
sources.title: Spatially extended balanced networks without translationally invariant connectivity
sources.evidence_type: Integral-operator theory and spatial integrate-and-fire simulations
sources.read_scope: Model, mean-field construction, theorem/corollary, all simulation-comparison and discussion sections; printed equations on pages5/11 visually inspected. Selected released construction/analysis source read; theorem proof not independently reproduced in full.
finding: The model supplies a one-dimensional domain with position-dependent connectivity; neurons near its center have more connections than those near its boundaries.
Balanced input cancellation requires an external profile in the range of the recurrent operator, a nonnegative rate solution and stability. These are separate conditions.

Its analytical decomposition assumes symmetric spatial kernels sharing an eigenbasis, while the complete E/I operator need not be symmetric. Finite-N approximations and spiking comparisons are supplied.
sources.application_inference: Geometry and mean activity cannot by themselves guarantee compatibility with all input profiles. A supplied spatial organization constrains input-response structure; the application has no such anatomical coordinate map.
transfer_limits: The large-N theory keeps connection probabilities fixed and weights proportional to1/sqrt(N); it is not the application’s fixed sparse-slot capacity model.
E/I rate balance is not a specified bound on FP4 phase occupancy or proof of semantic cycling.

An inspected example has a printed input/code mismatch and an unsupported L2-divergence inference. For the code’s profile, the signed L2 solution exists but violates positive-rate feasibility near boundaries; ANA-141 gives the independent derivation.
No claim that this issue invalidates every theorem, finite-N result or simulation is made.

sources.authors: Yue Wan and Robert Rosenbaum
sources.title: High-Dimensional Dynamics in Low-Dimensional Networks
sources.evidence_type: Asymptotic recurrent-network theory and numerical examples
sources.read_scope: Published PDF main sectionsI–VI, discussionVIII, methodsIX, appendicesB/C and selectedD/E; eigenmode, covariance and frequency-response assumptions inspected. No complete independent proof verification, no author execution, no visually inspected figure.
finding: Strong low-rank recurrent structure need not produce low-dimensional responses to high-dimensional input. Alignment between incoming and outgoing structured subspaces matters.

The theory separates a low-rank component with divergent singular values from a bounded-norm random background under stability and input assumptions. An EP alignment condition is sufficient in the stated setting; it is not claimed necessary.

A supplied one-dimensional periodic spatial example uses strong local negative feedback to suppress smooth inputs more than spatially disordered inputs. Locality does not by itself imply smoothing or denoising.
The frequency-dependent analysis distinguishes slow-input or steady response from temporally fluctuating response. Empirical input covariance and recording duration also affect finite examples.
sources.application_inference: Evaluate recurrence together with input alignment, coupling sign and timescale. Neither anatomical distance, graph rank nor activity dimensionality alone identifies preservation of useful semantic trajectories.
transfer_limits: The spatial coordinates and weights are constructed, not learned under the application constraints. Continuous tanh or linearized dynamics differ from FP4 phase transitions.
The strong-in-network-size scaling is not implied by fixed sparse capacity; capacity is not live degree or weight normalization.
High response dimensionality is not semantic diversity, and stable driven response is not autonomous cycling.
The inspected code predates the final paper. The published text was accessible through web PDF extraction; a separate direct PDF request returned403 and was not retried.

sources.authors: Alan Eric Akil, Robert Rosenbaum and Krešimir Josić
sources.title: Balanced networks under spike-time dependent plasticity
sources.evidence_type: Mean-field plasticity theory and nonspatial spiking simulations
sources.read_scope: Main model, plasticity derivation, equilibrium/transient excitatory and inhibitory results, stimulation and full discussion. Supplement pages6–13,16–17,19–22 read; page13 FigE visually checked. Remaining supplement sections not fully reviewed.
finding: Slow pairwise plasticity can preserve balanced activity for selected rules. Weight-rate correlations can invalidate a first-moment closure and leave multiple final weight distributions.
Firing-rate and covariance contributions are distinguished; observed rate dominance is conditional on update coefficients and operating statistics.
A stable mean weight does not ensure bounded variance; finite-network fluctuations destabilize one example before its mean-field threshold.
sources.application_inference: Separate structural partner selection, weight learning, rate regulation and correlation dynamics. No physical metric is required by these examples.
transfer_limits: Homogeneous connection probabilities, fixed adjacency, dense storage and1/sqrt(N) weight scaling; broad degree distributions require extensions.
Slow-learning separation and E/I assumptions do not define an FP4 activity band or validate semantic recurrence.
ANA-143 shows why a selected positive-coefficient rate-dominance example is not a universal statement about all timing rules.

sources.authors: Ariana R. Andrei, Alan E. Akil, Natasha Kharas, Robert Rosenbaum, Krešimir Josić and Valentin Dragoi
sources.title: Rapid compensatory plasticity revealed by dynamic correlated activity in monkeys in vivo
sources.evidence_type: Macaque V1 perturbation and nonspatial plastic balanced-network model
sources.read_scope: Final abstract, extended-data captions and complete9-page supplement; final main text unavailable. Akil2021 doctoral thesis chapter4 sections4.1/4.2 read as a distinct earlier account; Fig4.1.3 line panels inspected, rendered heatmaps unavailable. Released2021 model source inspected.
finding: Repeated optogenetic stimulation produces state-dependent changes in pairwise correlations while rates remain comparatively stable across trials.
In the tested models, inhibitory-to-excitatory plasticity reproduces the progressive correlation reversal. Changing recurrent strength changes the modeled response between awake/rest conditions.
sources.application_inference: Regulation of mean activity and regulation of coordinated responses can differ without adding geometry.
transfer_limits: Correlations and waveform-based putative cell classes are indirect synaptic evidence, not direct measurements of every connection.
The model’s recurrent weight downscaling defines its rest condition; it does not establish our DMN, valence bias or semantic-loop behavior.
Thesis,2021 code and2023 final supplement differ in details. Limited animal/session replication is distinct from numbers of recorded pairs.

sources.authors: Gabriel Koch Ocker, Ashok Litwin-Kumar and Brent Doiron
sources.title: Self-Organization of Microcircuits in Networks of Spiking Neurons with Plastic Synapses
sources.evidence_type: Weak-coupling timing-plasticity theory and nonspatial excitatory spiking simulations
sources.read_scope: Main results sections003–013, discussion014–016 and main construction/plasticity methods019–020 inspected; derivation appendix not fully reviewed. Broad-degree Fig10 on PDFpage23 visually checked. Eight archived source files inspected in AUD-084.
finding: Expected pairwise updates combine a rate-product term weighted by the learning-window area and a time-resolved covariance term. Nearly balanced windows allow correlations to dominate.
Common input and recurrent motifs can change predictions obtained from isolated neuron pairs. Weighted in/out-degree motifs differ from the binary opportunity graph.
Constructed broad-degree examples largely support the closure, with a reported qualitative failure for strongly positive degree correlation.
sources.application_inference: Temporal and graph relations can organize learned weights without defining anatomical distances. The timing statistic and opportunity graph must still be specified independently.
transfer_limits: The binary graph is fixed and updates are masked; this is not a structural partner-discovery algorithm.

All-excitatory weak-coupling and slow-learning assumptions, first-order response paths and cumulant closure restrict transfer. Reduced theory describes transient evolution without the full hard-bound dynamics.
The piecewise power-law degree distribution is a constructed example, not an empirical estimate or a justification of our capacity exponent.

sources.authors: Gabriel Koch Ocker and Brent Doiron
sources.title: Training and Spontaneous Reinforcement of Neuronal Assemblies by Spike Timing Plasticity
sources.publication_status: Published online2018-02-03; Cerebral Cortex29(3):937–951, March2019 issue.
sources.evidence_type: Nonspatial E/I network, timing-plasticity mean-field analysis and trained assembly coding
sources.read_scope: Final public publisher full HTML: main results, discussion, construction and plasticity methods inspected. SupplementS1 pages1–3,6–8 andS4 pages11–13 reviewed; equation pages12–13 visually checked. Remaining supplement and main figures not fully inspected. An older2016 preprint was cached but is not the review basis; final implementation code was not located.
finding: Assigned within-assembly correlated inputs train strong recurrent weights. Pair-based plasticity can reinforce assembly structure after the training correlation is removed.
The triplet-rule example returns to correlated background input and maintains structure without the same spontaneous reinforcement.
Inhibitory plasticity stabilizes rates under a separation of learning timescales. This does not imply every homeostatic rule or speed is sufficient.
A fixed summed-assembly readout improves its local stimulus information because response gain increases more than noise; the covariance-reset control is explicitly artificial.
sources.application_inference: These are positive examples of maintained learned recurrent structure without a distance kernel, and of separate rate, covariance and coding effects.
transfer_limits: Disjoint prescribed stimulus groups, fixed binary opportunities and comparatively dense connections do not establish learning with dense overlapping signed semantic inputs.
Spatial input correlation denotes correlation across neurons; plotted node positions visualize learned weights and are not anatomical coordinates.
Persistent assembly weights and scalar stimulus coding do not demonstrate ordered autonomous semantic cycles. Distributed coding is explicitly left open.
Printed supplemental gain equations contain inconsistencies identified in ANA-144; they may be typesetting errors and do not establish failure of published numerical findings.

sources.authors: Daniel C. Miner and Jochen Triesch
sources.title: Slicing, sampling, and distance-dependent effects affect network measures in simulated cortical circuit structures
sources.evidence_type: Spatial graph construction with simulated slicing and sampling
sources.read_scope: Complete methods, results and discussion in primary XML. Figure captions inspected; plots and author code not independently audited.
finding: A supplied distance kernel can generate excess reciprocity, common-neighbor association and some triangular motifs. Their measured strength depends on slice and sample geometry.
Correcting the null for reciprocity removes some motif enrichment but not all.
The model does not reproduce the full measured common-neighbor effect or its directional asymmetry, and does not exactly reproduce particular experimental sampling protocols.
sources.application_inference: Distance-conditioned and sampling-conditioned controls are needed before attributing a biological motif to a distinct learning rule. The positive residual evidence remains relevant.
transfer_limits: The Gaussian width and6000-cell spatial slab are illustrative construction choices, not a measured universal cortical scale.
This is a structural study without neural dynamics, semantic encoding or a computational task.
Artificial sampling effects neither supply our absent physical metric nor establish that all biological structure is a sampling artifact.

sources.authors: Marina Vegué, Rodrigo Perin and Alex Roxin
sources.title: On the Structure of Cortical Microcircuits Inferred from Small Sample Sizes
sources.evidence_type: Network inference theory, graph simulations and reanalysis of rat cortical recordings
sources.read_scope: Published13-page PDF: model definitions, construction, sample-degree formulas, classification methods, all results and discussion inspected. Formula/method pages4–5 visually checked; main result plots and implementation not independently reproduced.
finding: Spatial, clustered and heterogeneous-degree graph families can have similar common-neighbor curves and degree histograms in small samples.

Sample in/out-degree correlation combines reciprocal, convergent, divergent and chain probabilities; with stated assumptions it distinguishes selected model families. The paper explicitly notes that identical constituent moments leave higher-order structure unidentified.

The rat data are inconsistent with the tested simple families. A model combining measured distance dependence with an additional asymmetric nonspatial relation fits the tested statistics. Other latent interpretations are explicitly possible.
sources.application_inference: A directed functional relation can be needed beyond a symmetric proximity rule. Neither a fitted latent variable nor a good graph-statistic fit establishes an anatomical map or a learning mechanism for fixed semantic roles.
transfer_limits: Classification is conditional on model-family, exchangeability, degree and sampling assumptions. It does not reconstruct a unique full network or demonstrate dynamics.
The SDC reanalysis uses40 recorded groups of8–12 cells from the earlier dataset; many overlapping subsamples are not independent animals. Bootstrap/dependence controls are described.
The degree-model generator preserves selected moments approximately while adding sampling variance; prescribed expected degree differs from exact realized degree.
The distance-plus-modulator fit is descriptive. No variable is identified as an LLM coordinate or an accepted application parameter.

sources.authors: Vinograd, Nair, Kim, Linderman and Anderson
sources.title: Causal evidence of a line attractor encoding an affective state
sources.evidence_type: Mouse hypothalamic recordings, targeted holographic perturbations and mechanistic models
sources.read_scope: Read main results/discussion and dynamical/model/spatial-decoder methods; inspected extended-data figures7,10,11 visually and relevant captions. No raw dataset or author model execution.
sources.finding: Perturbing identified integration-contributing ensembles yields persistent pulse integration; perturbing an orthogonal response group gives transient excursions with return. Selective influence on non-targeted followers remains after a50-micrometre light-spillover exclusion. A linear spatial classifier did not separate the two groups; the plotted follower-distance regression had R2<0.001 and p=0.475. Slow transmission plus feedback-stabilized recurrence matches the fitted persistence within the explored models.
sources.application_inference: Provides a causal example of persistent population computation without evidence that these functional groups form simply separated physical parcels. Functional influence, interaction timescale and geometry need distinct evidence.
transfer_limits: This is hypothalamic aggression circuitry, not a cortical semantic column, semantic valence measure or DMN negative drift.
A nonsignificant linear spatial classifier does not exclude all nonlinear spatial clustering. Influence can include indirect pathways and is not a monosynaptic connection probability.
The36percent influence threshold is a response-derived statistic; the1000-unit/200-unit-subnetwork model does not establish a live degree law for614400 cells.
Persistence is finite and leaky; model feedback, slow state and background noise are supplied assumptions. No application parameter is chosen.

sources.authors: Mountoufaris et al.
sources.title: A line attractor encoding a persistent internal state requires neuropeptide signaling
sources.publication_status: Published Cell187:5998–6015.e18; final publisher-formatted PDF hosted by author lab.
sources.evidence_type: Cell-type-targeted receptor perturbation, mouse imaging, slice physiology and fitted dynamics
sources.read_scope: Read abstract and targeted main results/discussion/limitations on PDF pp10–15, data/code methodspp21/25–26, supplemental captionspp34–37 and visual S7p36. Earlier molecular methods/figures not fully reviewed. Public referenced visualization notebook inspected in AUD-088.
sources.finding: Co-disrupting oxytocin/vasopressin receptors reduces persistent responses and the fitted slow integration mode while leaving some stimulus/behavior decoding relatively preserved. Unilateral imaging experiments preserve aggressive behavior through the unmanipulated side. Slice peptide application evokes persistent responses; fast-synaptic blockers only partly shorten late responses.
sources.application_inference: Temporal maintenance and immediate response discrimination can depend on different mechanisms. Biological persistence cannot automatically be assigned to physical-neighbor wiring or to firing-rate magnitude alone.
transfer_limits: Between-animal comparisons, incomplete co-infection/editing and simultaneous receptor perturbations limit mechanism identification.
The source explicitly cannot isolate reduced single-cell persistence from loss of a persistent subpopulation. Behavioral effects are not proven to arise only from the attractor change.
Peptide sources are extrinsic to this nucleus; endogenous sources/release dynamics remain unidentified. Slice responses to bath peptide do not establish a fully input-free local network.
The plotted3D landscape is speed magnitude, not an independently measured energy potential. The study also uses vector fields and interventions.
No receptor, slow auxiliary variable, controller, numerical activity band or negative-semantic bias is adopted.

sources.authors: Kennedy, Kunwar, Li, Stagkourakis, Wagenaar and Anderson
sources.title: Stimulus-specific hypothalamic encoding of a persistent defensive state
sources.publication_status: Published Nature586:730–734; inspected HHS author manuscript identifies final publication, available2021-03-16.
sources.evidence_type: Mouse physiology and behavioral perturbations, plus comparison of spiking models
sources.read_scope: Read mainpp1–5, model/metric methodspp13–16, extended-data10p27 and Figure4 captionspp37–38. Visually inspected model equationp15 and extended-data10p27. Six public2021 model/helper files inspected in AUD-089; no execution. Publisher access unavailable, so author-manuscript and code versions remain distinguished.
sources.finding: Persistent stimulus-specific activity survives stimulus removal and has diverse single-cell timing; post-stimulus silencing affects persistent defensive behavior. Among tested models, slow recurrence with global feedback inhibition matches timing and specificity either through a longer slow time constant or through a weak1D distance bias combined with structured input overlap. Excessively separated input/network populations fail to match observed overlap.
sources.application_inference: A positive conditional case for locality helping preserve response distinctions, alongside a nonspatial alternative. Both recurrent organization and input alignment matter; neither spatial dimensionality nor a semantic metric is identified.
transfer_limits: Distance in the model is a supplied neuron-index ordering, not a measured map from its recorded cells or our semantic axes.
The spatial model jointly changes input organization; released scripts also change driven fraction, gain allocation and normalization. This is not an isolated geometry comparison.

Published phenomenology and inspected2021 code settings are distinct; literal Gaussian width/normalization differs between the rendered author methods and helper. Exact figure reproduction is not established.
The1000-unit fixed-probability model, slow-current history, inhibition and external noise do not establish scaling to the application capacity/FP4 contract or learned closed semantic loops.
Tetanus-toxin and slice findings support recurrent contribution while leaving distal feedback possible.

sources.authors: Chen, Wu, Yu, Chae, Tan, Ramot, Aljadeff and Komiyama
sources.title: Targeted stimulation of motor cortex ensembles drives learned movements
sources.publication_status: Published2026-10-14; primary abstract and indexed final extended-data captions inspected. Public Zenodo archive predates publication and retains an under-revision README.
sources.evidence_type: Mouse motor-cortex population imaging and targeted ensemble stimulation
sources.read_scope: Final abstract and indexed captions, particularly extended-data6 anatomical/activity controls and8–10 population analyses. Full final main text/methods unavailable through checked access. Read public plotting README, EDFig4 anatomical controls, EDFig6 PCA controls and Fig5 context code; viewed archiveEDFig4p9 and Fig5p6. Archive numbering differs from final; no raw-analysis replication.
sources.finding: Stimulating about20 early-onset cells can evoke learned movement and related population activity, whereas late-onset cells do not have the same effect. Initial population state predicts outcome; task disengagement prevents learned activity/movement. Learned activity can also occur without movement. Final anatomical controls report no detected early/late differences in depth, AP/ML distributions or nearest-neighbor clustering.
sources.application_inference: Temporal role, state and context can matter beyond response amplitude and measured target proximity. Functional membership, trigger capability and successful behavioral output are distinct; none supplies a metric for fixed semantic coordinates.
transfer_limits: Nonsignificant anatomical contrasts do not establish exact spatial equivalence or eliminate unmeasured geometry.
Stimulation and calcium imaging do not isolate a particular recurrent synaptic pathway or establish indefinitely closed loops.
This trained motor task does not instantiate the three application regimes or identify a learning algorithm.
Archived plotting code reads precomputed data and statistical results. Its version is not asserted to reproduce every final figure.

sources.authors: Yamamoto, Spitzner, Takemuro, Buendia, Murota, Morante, Konno, Sato, Hirano-Iwata, Levina, Priesemann, Munoz, Zierenberg and Soriano
sources.title: Modular architecture facilitates noise-driven control of synchrony in neuronal networks
sources.publication_status: ScienceAdvances9:eade1755,2023-08-25. Final publisher PDF obtained from University of Granada repository; separately inspected2022 arXivv1 is not treated as final.
sources.evidence_type: Patterned rat cortical cultures with optogenetic/chemical perturbations, microscopic spiking simulations and mesoscopic reduction
sources.read_scope: Final main results/discussionpp2–8, experimental/model/analysis methodspp9–10; visually inspected finalFigure4p7. Supplement not reviewed. Public pinned model/topology/parameter source targeted in AUD-091. Earlier arXivv1pp2–13 also read; numerical results use final version.
sources.finding: Highly modular cultures respond more strongly to asynchronous targeted stimulation by reducing network-wide bursting. Chemical excitation and blocked inhibition do not yield the same behavior. Simulated topology comparisons adjust mean incoming degree to approximately30 while varying intermodule bridging. Resource depletion weakens intermodule propagation; the coarse model requires stochastic resource-dependent gates to reproduce desynchronization. Reported synchrony effects are separated from mean firing-rate changes.
sources.application_inference: A positive example of graph organization interacting with input and internal dynamics at a controlled mean-degree budget. Spatial construction can leave its computational effect in adjacency; explicit coordinates do not appear in the inspected subsequent neuron-update equations.
transfer_limits: The160-cell simulation has four prescribed40-cell modules,20percent inhibitory cells and additional recovery/resource states; none is adopted here. Modules are not identified with semantic minicolumns or CCs.
Matching average degree does not match the entire degree distribution, all motifs or input-output alignment. Bridging axon count differs from number of resulting synapses.
The mechanism concerns transient synchrony and burst propagation, not learned semantic trajectories, FP4 feasibility or sustained per-CC activation-band acceptance.
Experimental stimulation is a400ms discrete pattern applied to ten selected cells, not an unspecified white-noise process. The microscopic and mesoscopic noise/input conventions differ.
Some final numerical settings differ from the2022preprint. Pinned2024 code is inspected source, not an executed publication reproduction.

sources.authors: Wright, Chen, Zhou, Wang, Liu, Morales and Komiyama
sources.title: Local plasticity underlies the reorganization of cortical circuit dynamics during motor learning
sources.evidence_type: Mouse motor learning with optical inhibition of CaMKII-dependent plasticity and population imaging
sources.read_scope: Primary published abstract only for biological conclusions; full main text/methods not available through checked public routes. Public archive README and two functional-connectivity analysis files inspected in AUD-092. No data unpickled or author code executed.
sources.finding: The primary abstract reports that blocking CaMKII-dependent plasticity in M1 pyramidal cells prevents normal development of stable learned movements and reproducible movement-related population dynamics.
sources.application_inference: Local learning can contribute to shaping circuit dynamics, but local in this experiment refers to the manipulated brain area/cells and is not a measured pair-distance learning kernel.
transfer_limits: Without full methods this review does not attribute the effect exclusively to recurrent M1-to-M1 synapses rather than inputs onto manipulated cells.
Released functional connectivity is a thresholded inverse-correlation statistic, not an anatomical connectome; direct-edge or distance-law conclusions require separate evidence.
No application CaMKII mechanism, plasticity rule, partner selection or geometry follows from this partial review.

sources.authors: Zeraati, Shi, Steinmetz, Gieselmann, Thiele, Moore, Levina and Engel
sources.title: Intrinsic timescales in the visual cortex change with selective attention and reflect spatial connectivity
sources.evidence_type: Macaque V4 recordings, fitted timescales and binary spatial-network models
sources.read_scope: Final XML results/discussion; targeted model, correlation and timescale methods; pinned model source in AUD-093. No author model or experimental analysis executed.
sources.finding: Attention changes a slow local population timescale while a fast component is comparatively unchanged. Spatial recurrent models link local temporal correlations to connection range; heterogeneous cellular alternatives can fit temporal components but lack the observed spatial dependence.
sources.application_inference: Local and aggregate persistence are different possible computational properties. Their benefit must be related to fixed semantic input/output roles.
transfer_limits: Experimental lateral distance is receptive-field-center separation used as a cortical-distance proxy, not directly measured soma distance.
Binary model units represent local populations/minicolumns; fitted timescales are not semantic loop durations.
Several changes in vertical/horizontal efficacy fit attention effects; stronger horizontal coupling is not uniquely identified.
Near-criticality and input-dependent gain are model assumptions, not application requirements.

sources.authors: Haeusler and Maass
sources.title: A Statistical Analysis of Information-Processing Properties of Lamina-Specific Cortical Microcircuit Models
sources.evidence_type: Data-informed spiking microcircuit simulations with trained linear readouts
sources.read_scope: Author PDF targeted methods/results pp2–3 and7–13; final publisher HTML methods and control comparisons, including final Table2. No source execution.
sources.finding: Preserving neuron degrees and input/output roles nearly preserves mean performance after laminar wiring is scrambled. Final Table2 reports1.6percent overall decrease but12percent decrease on memory tasks. Small-world controls alone perform worse.
sources.application_inference: Degree allocation, role alignment and task-specific temporal processing should be distinguished from generic geometric or motif similarity.
transfer_limits: 560-cell model has richer cellular/synaptic states and predefined laminar input/readout routing.
Only readout weights are trained; recurrence is sampled. It does not establish a coactivity-learning rule.
Average performance can conceal individual task deficits. Published final Table2 supplies the numbers; the author PDF is not assumed identical.

sources.authors: Mosheiff, Ermentrout and Huang
sources.title: Chaotic dynamics in spatially distributed neuronal networks generate population-wide shared variability
sources.evidence_type: Spatial E/I rate-field theory and numerical dynamics
sources.read_scope: Final XML model/results/discussion and targeted numerical/MLE methods; no author simulation executed.
sources.finding: Spatial interaction can produce low-dimensional shared variability and chaos with uniform deterministic drive. Shared versus independent noise affects the dynamics differently. Two-dimensional sheets support richer patterns than the studied one-dimensional rings.
sources.application_inference: Geometry can alter dynamics, but more temporal complexity is not automatically useful semantic computation.
transfer_limits: Gaussian distance-dependent weights, power-law rate responses, E/I widths and time constants are supplied assumptions.
The reported2D and1D simulations use different total unit counts; this is not a fixed-resource proof of2D superiority.
No learned semantic task is demonstrated. Microscopic chaos is neither automatically required nor automatically disallowed by the application.

sources.authors: Wijesinghe, Srinivasan, Panda and Roy
sources.title: Analysis of Liquid Ensembles for Enhancing the Performance and Accuracy of Liquid State Machines
sources.evidence_type: Spiking reservoir classification comparisons
sources.read_scope: Final XML model/readout, ensemble construction, tasks, representation metrics, connectivity controls and limitations; spatial-control supplement not reviewed.
sources.finding: Splitting a fixed neuron count into independent reservoirs can improve selected classification tasks. A sparse equal-E-to-E-edge comparison favors four reservoirs; at denser settings the ordering reverses. Small reservoirs can lose accuracy when split.
sources.application_inference: Graph separation can aid a specified task and communication budget without a physical sheet; no universal modularity advantage follows.
transfer_limits: Connections and input probabilities are tuned; equal-E-to-E counts do not establish every edge/state/input cost is matched.
The readout uses normalized spike counts over a presentation, discarding temporal detail; recurrent weights are not learned.
Reservoir modules are not identified with our CCs or minicolumns. Gaussian spatial baseline parameter coverage is limited.

sources.authors: Shi, Zeraati, Levina and Engel
sources.title: Spatial and temporal correlations in neural networks with structured connectivity
sources.evidence_type: Binary-network analytical theory and simulation comparisons
sources.read_scope: Final publisher PDF extracted text: model pp2–5, correlation modes pp6–9/11–15, nonlinear input analysis pp17–19, discussion and Appendices A/B/C targeted equations. Screenshot unavailable; no claim of figure visual inspection.
sources.finding: Translation-invariant recurrent interactions create a spectrum of correlation times. Increasing connection radius while rescaling weights changes local mode amplitudes while retaining the slow global component. Nonlinear input shifts can alter effective timescales.
sources.application_inference: Useful persistence depends on which modes the fixed encoder excites and the fixed observation reads, not solely the longest network timescale.
transfer_limits: Radius comparisons change degree as well as geometry while normalizing aggregate strength; they do not fix sparse slot counts.
Linearized interaction assumptions and further approximations separating auto/cross-correlations have explicit scope; the beta1=beta2 special case cancels higher-moment terms in AppendixB.
Reservoir-computing benefit is a suggested application, not a task experiment in this paper. Continuous-time analysis and discrete-time simulation are distinct.

sources.authors: Haeusler, Schuch and Maass
sources.title: Motif distribution, dynamical properties, and computational performance of two data-based cortical microcircuit templates
sources.evidence_type: Two data-informed spiking microcircuit templates and matched controls
sources.read_scope: Final author-hosted publisher PDF: abstract, targeted model/input/calibration pp2–6, results pp11–12 and discussion pp13–14. No source execution.
sources.finding: Degree-controlled scrambling largely preserves mean performance for both templates. Removing one feedback pathway improves certain template-memory tasks while hurting rate tasks. Ordinary scrambling worsens one template but improves the other.
sources.application_inference: The computational consequence of a structural feature is conditional on input, observation and task; one average score cannot decide the three semantic regimes.
transfer_limits: Templates omit horizontal neuron locations and differ in biological measurement method, layer makeup and calibrated weights.
Only trained readouts specialize the tasks; findings do not establish learned recurrent organization.
Seven tasks and selected input distributions limit generalization; no universal sufficiency of degree or irrelevance of motifs is established.

sources.authors: Shi, Zeraati, International Brain Laboratory, Levina and Engel
sources.title: Brain-wide organization of intrinsic timescales at single-neuron resolution
sources.evidence_type: Mouse brain-wide recording analysis and recurrent-network theory; preprintv1,2025-08-30
sources.read_scope: PMC primary preprint XML results, estimation/anatomical/power-law methods and linear/nonlinear model derivations. Version1 verified in metadata; no peer-reviewed successor located in checked sources. Code availability promises release upon publication.
sources.finding: Selected single-neuron autocorrelations contain multiple timescales; slow tails are consistent with an exponent near2 and statistically indistinguishable from lognormal alternatives. Regional and cellular-feature associations are reported.
sources.application_inference: A distribution of observed persistence does not identify a connection-capacity law, local physical metric or semantic loop distribution.
transfer_limits: Main multi-exponential analysis retains11468/27960cells; excluded curves include oscillatory/noisy cases. Fits use10min spontaneous recordings and lags through5s.
Within-structure task associations differ from pooled associations; anatomy predictors explain a limited fraction of variance.
Modal reciprocal-eigenvalue distributions and fitted cell timescale distributions are related only under additional assumptions; ANA-153 gives a counterexample to universal identification.
Nonlinear model samples weight values, not sparse degree or slot capacities; no scaling parameter is transferred to the application.

sources.authors: Stern, Istrate and Mazzucato
sources.title: A reservoir of timescales emerges in recurrent circuits with heterogeneous neural assemblies
sources.evidence_type: Rate-network theory and clustered spiking simulations
sources.read_scope: Final XML primary results/discussion; clustered-network/self-coupling and colored-noise methods; full public demonstration notebook source and helper in AUD-094.
sources.finding: Heterogeneous assembly self-couplings produce different switching timescales. Prescribed populations preferentially entrain different frequencies of broadband input; network-generated colored drive changes persistence quantitatively.
sources.application_inference: Functional groups can provide temporal diversity without an explicit physical metric, but their meaning and input alignment must still be justified.
transfer_limits: The rate unit represents an assembly, not one project neuron or automatically one minicolumn. Spatial demixing refers to distinct response populations.
Spiking model uses supplied E/I assemblies, strong within-assembly coupling and connection probabilities0.2–0.5, not the application sparse-capacity regime.
Timescales use half-widths, exponential fits or dwell times in different comparisons; membrane-time calibration is explicit.
Reservoir task training is proposed future work; the inspected release is a two-population rate demonstration, not the full final spiking analysis.

sources.authors: Spitmaan, Seo, Lee and Soltani
sources.title: Multiple timescales of neural dynamics and integration of task-relevant signals across cortex
sources.evidence_type: Single-neuron recordings during a monkey decision task with multi-component temporal modeling
sources.read_scope: Primary PMC main results and methods, including AR/memory components, within-area versus pooled correlations and model selection. Supplement not reviewed.
sources.finding: Intrinsic, task-epoch and reward/choice-memory timescales show parallel regional trends but no detected pairwise correlations within areas after correction. Reward/choice traces relate specifically to corresponding behavioral history effects.
sources.application_inference: Slow spontaneous fluctuation and retention of particular information are distinct measurements; a shared regional hierarchy does not identify their cellular mechanism.
transfer_limits: Observational task-conditioned fits do not establish causal independence or absence of every relation.
Model selection randomly holds out time bins; it is not a demonstration of autonomous prediction on entirely new sequences.
AR decay, task history and input selectivity have explicit definitions, not direct anatomical-distance or synapse measurements.

sources.authors: Wasmuht, Spaak, Buschman, Miller and Stokes
sources.title: Intrinsic neuronal dynamics predict distinct functional roles during working memory
sources.evidence_type: Monkey frontoparietal recordings and temporal decoding
sources.read_scope: Final XML main results/discussion; timescale-selection, cross-temporal/temporal decoding and same-electrode correlation methods. Supplement not reviewed.
sources.finding: Longer baseline timescales accompany stronger stable delay coding in selected prefrontal populations, while short-timescale cells can carry information through dynamic temporal patterns. Relationships vary by area and task epoch.
sources.application_inference: Useful memory requires specifying the observation: stable instantaneous code and reproducible temporal pattern are different possible behaviors.
transfer_limits: Timescale fits use500ms fixation periods and exclude poorly fit or greater-than500ms estimates; retained populations are selected.
Functional coupling is same-electrode spike-count correlation with drift correction, not measured anatomical degree or soma-distance dependence.
Cross-temporal discriminability is not an immutable semantic-coordinate readout; associations do not establish causal necessity.

sources.authors: Zeraati, Engel and Levina
sources.title: A flexible Bayesian framework for unbiased estimation of timescales
sources.evidence_type: Statistical-method theory, synthetic validation and primate recording example
sources.read_scope: Final publisher full HTML results, model comparison, discussion and targeted sample-autocorrelation/OU generative methods. No package execution.
sources.finding: Finite sample means distort autocorrelation and inferred decay times. Matching sampling/noise in a generative model can reduce bias and quantify uncertainty; unknown nonstationarity or insufficient data limits inference.
sources.application_inference: Any future recurrence comparison should distinguish measurement bias, slow fluctuations and retained semantic content.
transfer_limits: OU-mixture fit selects among proposed dynamical descriptions; it does not identify a unique biological wiring mechanism.
Pooling trials with genuinely different means can introduce additional apparent slow components.
No Bayesian estimator or measurement pipeline is adopted as an application requirement.

sources.authors: Zemliak, Pipa and Nieters
sources.title: Continual familiarity decoding from recurrent connections in spiking networks
sources.read_scope: Final primary XML fixed-input/model/plasticity results, familiarity/readout comparisons, input sparseness and genetic-optimization methods; equations1–4 inspected in MathML. Selected released source in AUD-095; supplements not reviewed.
sources.finding: One-to-one fixed inputs and ongoing recurrent Hebbian plasticity support familiarity detection across repeat intervals without positions. Weight normalization and optimized plasticity/readout parameters matter. Main patterns stimulate5,10or20 of100cells; the reported sparseness is an imbalance statistic, not fraction inactive.
transfer_limits: Fully connected excitatory model, externally driven during each observation; not autonomous content recall or semantic cycling.
Genetic optimization and selected stimulated-cell readout remain external assumptions; LSTM/HebbFF comparisons use different representation and training conventions.
Released code contains additional postsynaptic-trace weighting and per-stimulus trace resets; source precision is limited as recorded in AUD-095.
Rsync population-size dependence is already analyzed in ANA-122; no new statistic is adopted.

sources.authors: Fruengel and Oberlaender
sources.title: Sparse connectivity enables efficient information processing in cortex-like artificial neural networks
sources.read_scope: Final primary XML main results and discussion; released notebook setup, MNIST recurrent training, dropout and Dale-constrained example targeted in AUD-096. Other notebook dataset workflows and supplements not fully reviewed.
sources.finding: Sparse random recurrence improves early-epoch and data-limited classification in selected large ReLU networks. Benefits depend on size, activation and E/I initialization; longer training can close differences. The paper separates fixed sparse masks from structural rewiring.
transfer_limits: Inputs/readouts are trained, and equal hidden-edge counts do not equal all-parameter or fixed-neuron budgets.
Sparse means up to10% connectivity in these comparisons; dense masked tensors are used in the release. Training epochs are not CPU wall time.
The reported Dale-delay benefit can disappear with stronger inhibition or a different sign balance. Public notebook sign-enforcement details require reconciliation before quantitative transfer.
Classification/dropout robustness is not recurrence under assigned semantic roles.

sources.authors: Knight, Senk and Nowotny
sources.title: A flexible framework for structural plasticity in GPU-accelerated sparse spiking neural networks
sources.read_scope: Primary arXivv2,2026-01-23, full methods/results/discussion targeted; publication metadata identifies Neuromorphic Computing and Engineering6:014019,March2026, but final publisher body unavailable. Selected author implementation in AUD-097.
sources.finding: Preallocated ragged connectivity permits sparse GPU rewiring without reallocating each change. Supervised sparse classifiers can match dense accuracy; a separate spatial-map model refines prescribed topographic inputs. Update cost depends strongly on learning schedule and reverse-index rebuilding.
transfer_limits: Classifier input/recurrence are learned by e-prop/DEEP R; topographic model already supplies positions and spatially correlated stimuli. Neither assigns geometry to fixed semantic coordinates.
DEEP R uses two full potential-pair bitfields; the topographic method uses one. Ragged rows share a maximum allocation. ANA-154 quantifies a conditional CC-scale transfer cost.
Topographic attempts scale withN while each pair exposure falls as1/N; ANA-155 distinguishes per-neuron learning exposure from aggregate simulator throughput.
GPU timings and proof-of-concept network sizes do not determine CPU feasibility, five-byte slot state or the application degree law.

sources.authors: Janzakova, Balafrej, Kumar, Garg, Scholaert, Rouat, Drouin, Coffinier, Pecqueur and Alibart
sources.title: Structural plasticity for neuromorphic networks with electropolymerized dendritic PEDOT connections
sources.read_scope: Primary XML pulse-overlap/growth model, limited association experiment, classification and reservoir examples, hardware-boundary discussion and targeted material methods. Supplementary simulations and author software not reviewed.
sources.finding: Physical conducting-fiber growth depends on pulse overlap and electrode arrangement. Derived simulations show task-specific sparsity benefits from activity-dependent wiring. A25-cell reservoir has fixed random inputs; its readout and weights are subsequently learned.
transfer_limits: Physical growth demonstrations and simulated computational benchmarks are distinct evidence.
Classification wiring is supervised by output-label drive. Reservoir comparison changes activity-dependent selection together with geometry; it does not isolate physical distance.
Two-dimensional hardware imposes non-crossing constraints because fibers are not insulated; the general simulated graph is not directly realizable by that substrate.
Rate-product coincidence is not automatically centered correlation. None of these material constraints supplies a metric between our semantic-role cells.

sources.authors: Morgan, Devinsky, Doyle, Dugan, Friedman and Flinker
sources.title: Hybrid spatial organization and evidence for magnitude-independent neural coding of linguistic information during sentence production
sources.read_scope: Primary XML sentence/list comparisons, targeted RSA/NMF results and discussion, electrode/HGA/warping/RSA/statistical methods. Selected released R code in AUD-098. Full supplementary analysis and patient datasets not reviewed.
sources.finding: ECoG sentence production shows distributed and focal contributions. Linguistic representational-association statistics need not covary with average high-gamma amplitude across electrodes. NMF groups temporal profiles without supplying electrode coordinates.
transfer_limits: Ten epilepsy patients and1256 electrodes;5–10mm grid spacing and1–2mm contacts do not resolve single neurons or one CC.

RSA uses scalar HGA pair differences, transformed permutation-standardized regression t-statistics and GPT2 sentence-profile distances; it is not mutual information, a fixed semantic-axis map or a firing-fraction measurement.
Failure to detect an amplitude correlation is not a general independence theorem. Active/passive and canonical-sentence semantic predictors retain task confounds.
Learned functional grouping and anatomical localization do not yield distances between the application neurons.

sources.authors: Balwani, Cho and Choi
sources.title: Exploring the Architectural Biases of the Cortical Microcircuit
sources.read_scope: Final primary public article model/task methods, feedback/delay results, predictive-coding objective and appendixE theoretical argument. Targeted author source in AUD-100. Training notebooks and all task results not reproduced.
sources.finding: A supplied hierarchy of six point-neuron RNN populations, sparse interpopulation projections and delayed feedback distinguishes repeated from expected sequence inputs even at initialization; supervised learning and an extra feedback loss alter representational specialization.
transfer_limits: Input projections, neuron meanings and readouts learn; the architecture does not preserve the application semantic assignments. No metric within a population is used.
Temporal-violation labels are correlated with repeated inputs. Distinguishability at initialization is not itself learned expectation or proof of prediction-error computation.
Removing feedback changes edge/parameter resources; the released no-time-delay module also changes the recurrent factorization and update schedule.
ANA-156 identifies printed mathematical-bound problems; empirical findings remain separate. This is not a quantitative guarantee for fixed dense signed inputs.

sources.authors: Bausch, Niediek, Reber, Mackay, Boström, Elger and Mormann
sources.title: Distinct neuronal populations in the human brain combine content and context
sources.read_scope: Final primary XML content/context results, generalization and temporal interaction results, discussion, screening/design/population/decoding/cross-correlation methods. Selected processed-result repository in AUD-099; raw spikes and full original analysis pipeline not inspected.
sources.finding: In49sessions from16patients,3109MTL units include597stimulus-modulated and200context-modulated neurons. Most selected stimulus responses remain context-invariant, while contextual reinstatement and entorhinal-to-hippocampal lagged coactivity emerge during task pairing.
transfer_limits: Pictures were selected to elicit recorded responses; prevalence is conditional on this screening. Context means the comparison question, not every kind of context or a model semantic coordinate.
Lagged shift-corrected coactivity is consistent with learned interactions but does not directly measure or isolate new synapses. The paper explicitly proposes causal follow-ups.
The key directed comparison is40pairs across6sessions;3sessions from2participants individually show the lagged peak. Patient/session and pooled pseudo-population results differ.
MTL cell populations, task coding and broad region labels do not establish cortical minicolumn anatomy or a physical proximity rule.

sources.authors: Kong, Zabeh, Liao, Mihaila, Wilson, Santhirasegaran, Peterka, Geiller and Losonczy
sources.title: Recurrent connectivity shapes spatial coding in hippocampal CA3 subregions
sources.read_scope: Final2026-07-08abstract and publication metadata; final full methods unavailable. Separately reviewed2024-11-07preprintv1 modeling/results/discussion and RNN/Hopfield methods fromPMC11581023. The final intervention is not described by the old preprint.
sources.finding: Proximal low-recurrence and distal high-recurrence CA3 show differing stable/generalized versus context-specific coding. The final abstract reports that local glutamatergic-transmission disruption impaired distal context-specific coding. Earlier models relate recurrent organization to memory discrimination/generalization.
transfer_limits: Final intervention selectivity and controls are not verified from the abstract; do not infer that only recurrent synapses were affected.
The old RNN uses trainable input/outputs and100hidden units with different L1 penalties; changing regularization changes weight scale as well as effective sparsity.
The preprint Hopfield generalization comparison trains each density to its own maximal perfect-recall load; it does not isolate a sparsity benefit at matched stored-pattern count.

Biological location and afferent/inhibitory differences remain confounds for structural interpretation. Neither the abstract nor models prescribe a distance preference or a degree law for the application.

sources.authors: Mackey, Schizas, Deighton, Boothe and Maroulas
sources.title: Geometric sparsification in recurrent neural networks
sources.read_scope: Final primary main theory, methods, applications and discussion; main tables1–9, including visual inspection of PDF pages6–7; supplement architectures/hyperparameters, proofs, parameterizations, inhibitor comparisons, penalty sensitivity and trained-embedding topology. Targeted pre-publication release in AUD-101; no trained models or author programs executed.
sources.finding: Geometric weight penalties plus pruning can outperform both plain L1 and coefficient-shuffled penalties in selected navigation, language and adding tasks. Best global shape depends on task; language results do not clearly select one manifold. Retraining from random weights succeeds in some conditions but mostly fails on the95%-sparse adding task.
transfer_limits: Neuron locations may be fixed while learned input maps, hidden meanings and readouts remain free. That is not fixed semantic-coordinate identity.
Entry shuffling preserves the penalty histogram but changes reciprocal symmetry, diagonal penalties and row exposure; ANA-158 identifies what it does not isolate.
The difference-of-Gaussians low-cost annulus is motivated partly by avoiding collapsed learned embeddings, not by a biological very-near exclusion measurement.
The final supplement finds no clear recognizable learned manifold in the R3 point clouds despite improved task performance.

Main results vary with sparsity and penalty strength; sparse retraining is not universally successful. Dense pretraining/global pruning and dense masked storage differ from bounded candidate learning.
ANA-157 limits conversion from magnitude-kernel arguments to signed recurrent behavior; released scripts have reproducibility mismatches, without establishing that final published runs used them.

sources.authors: Ghosh and Goodman
sources.title: Partial recurrence can enable robust and efficient computation
sources.read_scope: Final primary main architecture/results, task/method definitions, learning and functional metrics, Jacobian-based memory, statistical methods and source version. Selected tagged source in AUD-102. Supplement and trained-object archive not reviewed.
sources.finding: Systematic comparison of128pathway architectures with50trained models each across multisensory maze tasks shows that useful recurrence is circuit- and task-dependent. Many partial architectures match or exceed full recurrence with fewer parameters in dense-cue tasks; sparse cues expose important failures. A parameter-matched feedforward control still fails a task requiring history.
transfer_limits: The main model has8hidden units, trained dense blocks and linear/ReLU/softmax layer roles; no within-layer physical metric is used.
Pathway additions change parameter count and initial scale; the task-controlled comparison does not isolate anatomy or fixed CC roles.
Memory is a normalized lagged input-output Jacobian norm, not a decoding-capacity, semantic-content or autonomous-cycle measure. The finite noisy state distribution is part of its definition.
Counterfactual architecture pairs are separately trained models, not pathway removal in an otherwise unchanged learned circuit.
Parameter savings do not directly measure CPU throughput, energy or our five-byte slot costs. Neither anatomical pathways nor cell classes are adopted.

sources.authors: W. Jeffrey Johnston and Stefano Fusi
sources.title: Modular representations emerge in neural networks trained to perform context-dependent tasks
sources.publication_status: Reviewed2024-10-11preprintv2; primarybioRxivAPI confirms renamedv3 When and why modular representations emerge,2026-01-06,not published. V3fulltext unavailable in this review.
sources.read_scope: V2 input geometry, contextual task, learning-speed decomposition, generalization and context transfer; input/model/clustering/context-fraction/subspace methods; targeted discussion. No supplement or released source reviewed. V3metadata/abstract only.
sources.finding: In the tested learned feedforward representations, explicit context-specific cell groups depend on structured low-dimensional input; implicit context-specific subspaces can occur without explicit groups. Modularity can aid learning related tasks/contexts while more unstructured representations can aid unrelated contexts.
sources.application_inference: Useful grouping can arise from task and input structure without anatomical coordinates. Computational grouping and physical proximity are different, and the usefulness of separation depends on the relation between contexts.
transfer_limits: The600-input/200-hidden ReLU model learns its hidden roles using Adam and labeled classifications. Context is explicitly supplied; no recurrent semantic sequence, sparse partner learning or fixed-role cell model is tested.

The input is a constructed mixture of disentangled and conjunctive binary latent variables, with overall variance controlled. Raw embedding dimension or measured Flash covariance rank cannot be directly substituted for its task-relevant latent dimension.
Explicit modularity uses a chosen response threshold; implicit modularity uses a relative subspace index. Neither gives anatomical distances.

The2024methods contain ambiguous matrix row/column and BIC-convention wording. No implementation is available in the inspected article to resolve these; no claim about actual simulation error follows.
The extensive2026revision has not been inspected, so old detailed results are not attributed to that revision.

sources.authors: Tirthabir Biswas and James E. Fitzgerald
sources.title: Geometric framework to predict structure from function in neural networks
sources.read_scope: Published main structure/dynamics, recurrent-to-feedforward reduction, constrained/semi-constrained/unconstrained solution space, synapse-certainty interpretation, nonorthogonal-pattern limitation and discussion through public manuscriptXML. PublishedPDF metadata and targeted text checked; visualPDF retrieval failed; appendix proofs not reproduced.
sources.finding: Threshold-linear response constraints describe an ensemble of recurrent weights supporting specified fixed points. Under additional incoming-weight bounds, some synapse signs can be necessary across all such solutions. The exact closed-form certainty criterion uses orthonormal response patterns; the paper gives a conservative nonorthogonal extension.
sources.application_inference: Assigned or measured response profiles can constrain connections without specifying cell positions, but fixed response matching alone does not establish stable recurrent behavior.
transfer_limits: The geometry is in weight/response parameter space. The physical basis denotes individual synaptic weights, not anatomical coordinates of cells.

The main construction assumes independent response patterns no more numerous than candidate incoming synapses and complete activity observations. Strongly correlated dense token profiles and hidden context need separate treatment.
The paper explicitly leaves restriction to stable fixed points, Dale constraints, synapse-number limits and wiring-length objectives as further refinements.
The weight-norm bound is a model constraint requiring independent justification, not the static slot-capacity distribution.
No anatomical placement or application learning mechanism follows.

sources.authors: Gray Umbach, Ryan Tan, Joshua Jacobs, Brad E. Pfeiffer and Bradley Lega
sources.title: Flexibility of functional neuronal assemblies supports human memory
sources.read_scope: Main assembly identification, order/phase findings, participation drift and discussion; subject, assembly, spatial-null and semantic methods. Supplementaryfigures1–3captions and visualinspection ofsupplementp1; later supplement figures not reviewed. Custom code available only on request, not obtained.
sources.finding: In human MTL recordings, correlated firing defines45assemblies in15sessions from13subjects; ordered firing and changing participation relate to episodic recall. Pooled member pairs more often share a channel, region and hemisphere, while an aggregate spatial score against within-session random groups is not significant.
transfer_limits: Spatial categories are channel/region/hemisphere, not calibrated soma distance or within-CC semantic coordinates. Same-channel overlap is26%among member pairs versus13%reference; the separate aggregate score uses a different null and is not evidence of zero spatial organization.
203neurons from assembly-positive sessions are analyzed, with5–34simultaneously recorded. The study does not observe a complete local synaptic graph.
Coactivity and lagged firing are not measured physical synapses; the authors explicitly distinguish them. Associations with memory are observational.

Its semantic test groups words by similarity to a single reference word,world. Non-significance on that projection cannot exclude all multidimensional semantic tuning; ANA-161 illustrates the limitation.
Assembly-expression thresholds and25mswindows are analysis definitions, not our FP4phase or per-CC activity-band values. No oscillatory controller or timing contract is adopted.

sources.authors: Robert M. Mok and Bradley C. Love
sources.title: A non-spatial account of place and grid cells based on clustering models of concept learning
sources.read_scope: Common-learning result, grid/environment interpretation, full targeted Discussion, simulation/learning/grid-score methods; pinned source inAUD-103. Supplement not reviewed; no author execution.
sources.finding: A winner-based clustering model yields regular place/grid-like response fields for broadly sampled two-dimensional environments, while structured concept inputs give non-grid clusters. The authors distinguish an algorithmic account from its unresolved neuronal implementation.
sources.application_inference: A regular cognitive or receptive-field map can reflect sampled stimulus structure without being a map of neuron positions. This is evidence about representational geometry, not a source of physical distance among assigned semantic roles.
transfer_limits: Preferred inputs/cluster centers learn. The method does not preserve our fixed per-coordinate roles or simulate recurrent semantic loops.
Spatial coordinates in the algorithm are environment/stimulus coordinates. There is no recurrent neuron-to-neuron metric or Hebbian graph in the inspected implementation.
The test sums closest-cluster match values into a response map, normalizes by visit count and computes autocorrelation/grid scores; a hexagonal plot is not direct anatomical placement.
Task-relevance and feature attention discussed in the paper are further modeling assumptions, not demonstrated automatic inference from dense language embeddings.

sources.authors: Laurens van der Maaten and Geoffrey Hinton
sources.title: Visualizing Data using t-SNE
sources.evidence_type: Primary methodological reference for an independent descriptive input-profile analysis
sources.read_scope: Gaussian conditional probabilities, perplexity, symmetrization, Student-t objective/gradient, optimization and experimental setup. No author implementation or original dataset experiment executed.
sources.finding: A low-dimensional visualization can prioritize local probability relationships while distorting global geometry; the objective and its optimization parameters define what it tries to preserve.
transfer_limits: This is not biological evidence or a neuronal learning rule.
The application analysis uses full cached profile distances rather than the paper experiments PCA30preprocessing.
Map optimization is nonconvex and preserving neighbors does not supply physical meaning, causality or task benefit.

sources.authors: Terrence J. Sejnowski
sources.title: Storing Covariance with Nonlinearly Interacting Neurons
sources.evidence_type: Historical primary theoretical model; not a new experiment
sources.read_scope: Primary author-hosted PDF: model and covariance discussion, motor-learning and memory sections, targeted Appendix2; page319 visually inspected. No author program or complete proof replication.
sources.finding: Separates coincident activity from the independent-mean baseline in an approximate covariance-storage proposal. Background firing changes the effective response dynamics, so matching a covariance alone does not specify the operating state.
transfer_limits: Gaussian-process and small synaptic-change assumptions delimit the derivation; this is not evidence that all cortical plasticity follows the proposed rule.
The cerebellar example uses an additional climbing-fiber signal; it is not a two-neuron-only demonstration of cortical learning.
No mean-subtraction mechanism, neuronal geometry or application encoder is selected.

sources.authors: Robert Gütig, R. Aharonov, Stefan Rotter and Haim Sompolinsky
sources.title: Learning Input Correlations through Nonlinear Temporally Asymmetric Hebbian Plasticity
sources.evidence_type: Analytical single-target plasticity and spiking-input simulations
sources.read_scope: Primary final PDF introduction/methods, selected correlated-group results, delayed-input sensitivity and discussion; PDFpage4 equations8–13 visually inspected. Appendix not fully audited; no source execution.
sources.finding: Weight dependence and temporal filtering change whether input correlations are represented by differentiated or nearly homogeneous synaptic weights. Stable bounded learning and sensitivity to input structure can trade off; the useful parameters depend on input timing and rate.
transfer_limits: Fixed afferents to a target are supplied. The study does not solve recurrent partner discovery or compare anatomical geometry.
Linear-Poisson and conductance-LIF targets differ quantitatively; the latter uses1000plastic excitatory and200fixed inhibitory inputs, distinct from signed semantic populations.
The sensitivity score is based on derivatives of equilibrium weights with respect to input features; the authors explicitly leave readout behavior outside that score.
No STDP window, exponent, biological type split, normalization or application stability criterion is adopted.

sources.authors: James Humble
sources.title: Resource-dependent heterosynaptic spike-timing-dependent plasticity in recurrent networks with and without synaptic degeneration
sources.evidence_type: 200-cell recurrent spiking model with resource-transfer plasticity
sources.read_scope: Published main methods/results/discussion from primary HTML/XML; targeted source and launcher inspection AUD104. Supplement and long-run notebook not fully audited; no published run reproduced.
sources.finding: Activity can persist after an initial stimulation while excitatory synaptic resources compete and weights remain bounded. Recycling resources during connection removal prolongs persistence in the compared model.
transfer_limits: The main model supplies a25percent recurrent mask,50independent Poisson inputs and random1–5ms delays; it does not learn partners outside that mask.
The distance rule acts between ordered afferent synapses on one target, not between somata. This ordering is an extra model assumption.
Resource amounts, time constants, refractory dynamics and a tuned depression factor shape the result. The initial resource multiplier was selected to obtain post-stimulation activity.
The reported persistent active subset is not a test of multiple semantic memories, ordered token context or closed multidimensional loops.
A resource budget limits total weight (ANA165), not slot capacity or a particular active-neuron fraction. No resource array is adopted for this application.

retrieval.title: Resource-dependent heterosynaptic spike-timing-dependent plasticity in recurrent networks with and without synaptic degeneration

sources.authors: Thomas Schibler, Subhash Suri, Jie Xue
sources.title: Embedding Graphs as Euclidean kNN-Graphs
sources.evidence_type: Computational geometry theory
sources.read_scope: Primary full HTML introduction, definitions, section2.1 lemma2 and approximation framework through lemma4. Remaining algorithmic proofs not fully audited.
sources.finding: Ordinal nearest-neighbor realization is different from preservation of all metric distances. Approximate edge-preservation guarantees are conditional on realizability.
transfer_limits: The theorem does not make arbitrary observed neighbor graphs realizable in a plane.
The independent opponent-exclusion bound in ANA166 is derived separately.
No anatomical evidence, application geometry or implementation is inferred.

sources.authors: Miloš Radovanović, Alexandros Nanopoulos, Mirjana Ivanović
sources.title: Hubs in Space: Popular Nearest Neighbors in High-Dimensional Data
sources.evidence_type: Nearest-neighbor hubness theory and computational experiments
sources.read_scope: Targeted primary PDF sections3.1,4.1–4.3,5.2,6; Figure10/PDF28 visually inspected. Full asymptotic proofs and published datasets not reproduced.
sources.finding: Nearest-neighbor popularity can depend strongly on metric and data distribution; centrality helps explain some hubness, while centerless examples limit a universal dimensionality claim.
transfer_limits: Ranking popularity is not biological synaptic degree or semantic importance.
Removing hubs through projection may alter useful relationships; benefit is task dependent.
This input table is not assumed to satisfy the isotropic distribution examples. No hub suppression or new capacity law is selected.

open_comparisons: Wiring-cost optimization is not proof that spatial distance must enter the learning rule.
No physical layout does not imply statistically uniform learned connections.
Nonspatial assembly models may depend on learned input maps, precise set points, dense coupling or silent memories incompatible with our requirements.
Counterexamples to stronger locality do not prove locality never helps; identify task and pattern-structure dependence.
Graph triangle clustering, learned weighted assemblies and sampled recording groups are different objects.
Anatomical absence of a detected distance trend is not evidence of exact spatial independence.
Fixed total synapses with variable neuron count, fixed incoming degree, and fixed stability eigenvalue are different experimental controls.
Human local motif statistics need sampling-group heterogeneity controls before becoming candidate learning principles.
Sparse final connectivity is not evidence that an algorithm learns from a sparse initial candidate graph.
Fixed feedforward roles do not require fixed recurrent assemblies; learned assembly membership need not coincide with minicolumn membership.
A low-cost random absent-pair proposal is not a low-cost useful-partner discovery algorithm; quantify learning work separately from representation size.
Fixed assigned semantic roles, fixed potential edge masks and fixed learned sequence membership are three independent constraints.
A trajectory repeated after each probe is not a closed autonomous cycle, and a stability result after freezing plasticity does not establish stability during continual learning.

Separate recurrence motifs, geometric wiring cost and useful sustained content: LOC-125/AUD-027 confirm a degree-preserving spatial/null contrast, but dynamics are untested; LOC-123 changes strength as well as geometry, LOC-124 separates spatial and task-trained models, and LOC-127 finds transient self-feedback benefits without persistent activity in its tested preparation. No additional mechanism or acceptance metric is adopted.

Distinguish anatomical distance, direct pair selection, hidden-path influence and state-dependent gain when evaluating perturbation evidence; keep causal pattern completion separate from autonomous sequence persistence and from decoder-only feature ablation.

If a future proposal uses coordinate coactivity to define neighborhoods, identify the input/state distribution and compare its added value against the same coactivity already used for learning; ANA-065 provides a measured distribution-sensitivity example without adopting that proposal.

Keep functional modules, causal influence, inferred direct edges and anatomical positions separate. A coactivity rule may be useful without reconstructing biological synapses; evaluate its desired recurrent computation rather than treating anatomical inference limits as a blanket rejection of learning from activity.

Distinguish one-pass propagation, repeated autonomous cycling, driven assembly reliability and nonlinear covariance classification. Each demonstrates a different functional benefit and has different state/recovery requirements; none alone selects physical distance for the fixed semantic arrangement.

Keep unconditional recall probability separate from behavior conditional on successful recall; compare driven recruitment, autonomous persistence, event duration and participating identities rather than treating all as activation strength.

Evaluate coordinate normalization, effective penalty strength, graph-preserving node permutations, independent edge resampling and held-out task evaluation separately before attributing a trained-network gain uniquely to physical geometry.

Distinguish fixed input preference from exclusive coordinate drive when transferring nonspatial assembly-learning examples; broad nonpreferred inputs and extra excitability states are material assumptions.
Keep activity-mass matching, discrete-event occupancy, event counts and conditional transition statistics separate when evaluating spontaneous replay.

Compare fixed whole-stimulus assembly models with fixed signed-coordinate roles explicitly; successful first-order switching without geometry does not already solve overlapping semantic patterns or higher-order context.

findings: simulateTheorem draws one shared Gaussian source and converts it to a common conditional edge probability for each sampled group. It evaluates binomial mixture probabilities, explicitly tying heterogeneity to a shared latent variable.

getTheoremPrediction maps empirical mean and variance onto that restricted model’s lookup table. It is not a general theorem that marginal degree or probability variance determines arbitrary motif correlations.
The higher-order slice routine converts innervation to P=1-exp(-I), samples neuron subsets and multiplies probabilities of present/absent directed edges within each subset.

Its reference is a uniform probability derived from the slice mean. Perin2011 instead describes a null preserving measured positions and distance-dependent uni/bidirectional profiles. Qualitative similarity of overrepresentation does not establish equality of the two residual tests.

Large motif spaces are sampled rather than fully enumerated; the plotting routine applies combinatorial and normalization corrections. The code and paper are statistical architecture analyses, not simulations of recurrent neural activity.
