source_audits.status: targeted read-only public-source audit plus descriptive analysis of plain-text result files
source_audits.read_scope: Targeted HAR DeepR baseline/cost and SET-cost functions, model penalty/gradient code, GRU cell, README and statistical-notebook calculation cell inspected. Eight source/utility/notebook files and72 tiny numerical result files cached. Not every cached source line audited; author programs and notebook were not executed.
findings: The HAR cost variants use dense131×131 weights/masks/distance matrices and enumerate all absent pairs. Sparsity is a parameter constraint, not a demonstrated sparse CPU implementation.

The sampled partner preference is proportional to1-D/Dmax among eligible off-diagonal pairs, rather than literal1/D. Baseline rewiring includes diagonal candidates; geometric rewiring excludes them, while initialization can include self-connections in both.

The optimized penalty is distance-weighted L1; the inspected scripts rescale by the distance RMS. They do not implement the weight-RMS denominator of the optional normalized Equation5. This is a scope distinction, not a claim that Equation4 is invalid.
The total active recurrent weight count is held fixed; per-target incoming capacity classes and static slot migration are not implemented.
The GRU uses learned dense input projections, input-dependent gates, dense matrix multiplication and Adam gradients. It is not a local Hebbian SNN learner with fixed semantic cell roles.

The statistics notebook standardizes jointly within each condition and shuffles treatment labels within that condition, addressing the pooled-z dependence discussed in the supplement. A plain pooled t-test is not the authors’ sole validation.

The current repository contains72 of the96 raw L1/L2 treatment files implied by24 conditions: RNN MNIST and ManteTask data are missing. Two HAR filenames use lower-case l; the descriptive audit matches case explicitly and retains source names.

Available files cover18 conditions per norm:13 positive and5 negative mean differences for both L1 and L2. Equal-condition mean gains are0.166625 and0.262483 percentage points. These figures describe the available subset only.

findings: fig1_model.m draws a new mask, uniform weights and Bernoulli cell signs at every parameter-grid point. The inhibitory count has expectation200, not a fixed200. Diagonal entries are not removed. Mean and variation include the complete50000-step trajectory from a half-active initial state.

fig2_branching_simu.m draws initial states independently with probabilityS, rather than conditioning on exactlyN*S active neurons. Its denominator is the prescribedS; the actual initial count fluctuates.

fig4_balance.m allocates50000 time columns but advances only through column100 before calculating currents/correlations. The remaining columns stay zero. Its tension variable is a ratio of population-averaged currents, whereas equation10 defines one minus a ratio per neuron followed by averaging. An additional plotting transformation would not by itself resolve the averaging-order difference.

source_audits.read_scope: README, estimator core, main spectral-fit script and alternative-spectrum script; exact Git blobs verified. findings: The estimator removes an unknown mean using differences of independent stimulus pairs scaled by1/sqrt(2), then estimates cross-repeat eigenmoments. Its unbiasedness relies on stimulus/trial assumptions; fitting the spectrum is a separate optimization.

The main figure pipeline estimates10 moments and bootstrap covariance, fits a nonnegative-slope single power law and searches50 candidate breakpoints for a two-slope model. The whole n_neur-length spectrum is fitted, including indices beyond stimulus-data rank; these are inferred values, not separately observed singular modes.

Alternative nonparametric fits use7 moments and a10000-bin nonnegative eigenvalue distribution constrained to sum to1. Smooth broken laws and exponentials are also tested. The inspected S3 plot supports different early/tail slopes but shows substantial between-recording tail variation.

The S5 cumulative-variance plot confirms that the fitted curves cross the comparison inverse-rank curve: weaker leading dominance can coexist with faster later coverage. Its reported count selects the last index below75%, rather than the first index reaching75%; quoted source counts should therefore remain approximate.

The cvPCA core projects cross-repeat covariance onto the first repeat’s noisy eigenbasis, consistent with ANA-056. The generic power-law fitter mutates its index array in place; successive weighted/unweighted calls shift the comparison range by one entry. This local observation does not establish a material change to the paper’s principal conclusion.
limitations: The repository commit predates final publication; exact paper-generation provenance beyond the named files/plots is not independently established. No claim that measured neural dimensions select physical positions, connection slots or application encoding.

The EE amplitude varies with IE set to four times EE; a prose reference to an IE value of 0.07/0.11/0.15 should not override the table/code EE values.

The task notebook sets recurrent density to 1, uses 1000 training sequences of 5 seconds at 5 ms steps, and updates every 50 steps. Its integration target is a cumulative average, its differentiation target a filtered discrete difference, and its delay target a shifted input. The differentiation filter decay in the inspected notebook is 30 steps versus 75 in the article methods; exact version reproduction is therefore unresolved.

The customized FORCE class genuinely enables recurrent updates, despite inherited docstrings describing a static kernel. With the default unmasked dense setting, every recurrent-column update is the same vector. This admits the rank-one learning-path derivation in ANA-060.

source_audits.status: Independent descriptive check of one released distance-dependent/configuration graph pair
source_audits.read_scope: Zenodo metadata and two small Holmgren RTF edge-list files, totaling about 1.8 MB; publisher MD5 and local SHA256 verified. Large anatomical graph files were not downloaded. Parsed numeric directed edges only; no author code executed.
findings: Both released graphs contain 58,140 directed edges on 10,201 labeled vertices. Per-vertex source and target counts match exactly, confirming the degree-preserving control for this sample.

The spatial graph has 832 self-edges and 1,138 reciprocal nonself pairs; the configuration graph has 7 self-edges and 12 reciprocal nonself pairs. Fully reciprocal triangles are 1 versus 0, consistent with the reported small Holmgren clique count.

Under the supplied 101x101 lattice, summed edge lengths are approximately 249,930.814 versus 2,991,387.286; mean lengths are 4.29878 versus 51.45145. This confirms a substantial geometric cost difference under the stated cost definition, not an application CPU or memory saving.

The configuration file contains 15 repeated directed pairs, whereas the spatial file has none. Degree preservation is exact for the edge multiset; collapsing repeated pairs into a simple graph changes 15 counts. The sampled difference is small and does not explain the large reciprocal-pair or length contrast.

Rewiring changes self-connections, reciprocal pairs and other motifs together with length. A later dynamical experiment would need to distinguish which of these changes matters; the static comparison alone does not make geometry a uniquely necessary mechanism.
limitations: One graph pair only; published clustering/path algorithms and large high-probability networks were not rerun. Data predate the final paper; exact final-figure provenance is not independently established.

source_audits.read_scope: Eight exact Git-blob-verified MATLAB/README files. Original CRLF endings restored only when the resulting blob hash exactly matched the pinned repository. No binary .mat data, GUI archive execution or author environment setup.
findings: The main solver optionally normalizes each trace by its L2 norm, obtains anchors with K-means, and minimizes squared reconstruction error plus alpha times squared coefficient norm, with each coefficient constrained to [-1,1]. There is no L1 term or explicit coefficient-count constraint in the reviewed path.

It takes abs(Z), computes leading singular vectors and clusters their rows. For fixed anchors, sign-reversed input traces yield identical absolute coefficient vectors under the symmetric strictly convex objective; this is an association representation, not a signed directed edge list.

The demo sets the cluster count to length(unique(id_true)), uses 900 anchors and alpha=0.1, then scores against known labels. This supports a controlled recovery benchmark, not automatic discovery of an unknown cluster number.

GUI helpers use the same quadratic/absolute-coefficient structure. The separate basis-analysis helper selects components by explained energy and a heuristic shared-basis singular-value threshold; it does not reconstruct anatomical connections.

source_audits.status: Read-only source/notebook audit; no author code execution
source_audits.read_scope: All four text/source/notebook files in the six-file repository tree, with exact Git blob verification. Notebook JSON was parsed as text; outputs were not executed and no dependencies were installed.
findings: The principal lag_corr helper computes IFFT(FFT(a)*conj(FFT(b))) at the original signal length, giving circular cross-correlation. It returns argmax(abs(cross_corr))-N+1, which is not a conventional signed lag: identical nonconstant signals with peak index zero return -(N-1).

The main direction decision compares this returned value in both argument orders. The same additive shift cancels, so the preceding observation alone does not prove reversed direction or invalid published reconstruction. Circular wrapping, long/ambiguous delays and the non-FFT branch require separate interpretation.

Edge weights in the principal helper come from zero-lag Pearson correlations after direction selection, matching the paper’s description. A function named partial_correlation actually returns derivative-versus-state covariance; it must not be mistaken for the paper’s scikit-learn L1-regularized partial-correlation baseline, which is not implemented in the inspected notebook.

The six-code-cell notebook demonstrates a ten-node example and forward reconstruction using the same seed. The complete final-paper parameter sweeps, graphical-lasso baseline and all biological controls are not present in this pinned tree.
limits: The release predates publication; a full figure-to-code correspondence is not established. Local naming/index conventions do not justify declaring the entire scientific comparison false.

findings: The geometric base uses real coordinates, optional axis scaling/directional and cell-class biases, then becomes binary before spread. The spread function itself uses the graph and only the number of coordinate rows; this does not remove the geometric assumptions of its base graph.

Layer-4/5 and layer-2/3 configs share dist_neighbors=47 and p_pick=0.029. They change vertical scaling 2.25 to 1.5, directional factor 0.33 to 0.45 and step target 2.52 to 2.325. Both specify 100 steps and six protected steps. These settings substantiate the limited d/p transfer claim.
Protected steps round the requested count and sample without replacement, capped by available positive candidates. They do not implement exactly a noninteger expected count in each realization.

Printed methods exclude every node once it has been a candidate. build_instance instead accumulates selected state in exclusion; a failed candidate can remain eligible through a later frontier. A complete-base-graph hand trace distinguishes the two rules (ANA-073). Therefore the printed one-step Erdos–Renyi limit cannot be assumed to describe this released implementation without reconciliation.

findings: Real coordinates undergo independent axis min–max normalization. WD constructs raw integer grids with np.arange and performs no matching normalization for grid variants. This difference is present in the actual constructors passed to all three task loops.

W.__call__ returns sum(abs(x)) without self.w, although self.w is initialized from regu_strength0.3. WD/WDC do multiply by their coefficient. Their distance diagonal is zero, while W penalizes self-weights too.

W! uses the same permutation for rows and columns, exactly preserving the weighted recurrent graph up to relabeling. The EMD term compares sorted flattened communicability values and does not enforce node correspondence.

The default main field is312 nodes with grid12×13×2. The notebook default simulations=1 is a demo setting, not evidence against the paper’s20-run claim. Biological weights are rescaled after applying a floor; a minimum0.01 after final rescaling is not guaranteed.

The notebook assigns Go/NoGo to task2 and perceptual decision-making to task3, opposite the paper table labels. The first-task dictionary contains8 templates rather than the16 listed in the paper. These discrepancies need provenance resolution before exact numerical reuse.

Fit uses tfdf_test as validation and records final training/validation metrics; an additional tfdf_val dataset is generated but unused in the inspected workflow. No independent held-out test evaluation was found in these cells.

source_audits.status: Read-only exact published repository snapshot; source/paper differences recorded
source_audits.read_scope: README and complete396-line Python sample; exact Git blobs verified. No imports, simulation, notebook, serialized data or package installation executed.
findings: The source initializes dense learned input and recurrent matrices, masks recurrent self-connections, and enforces nonnegative inhibitory weights. It does not implement the later distinct E/I population experiment.

The training loop sets count=0 at each new pattern and tests count==width, but never increments count. Consequently its100ms noise interval is never entered: the selected pattern persists until the next200ms boundary. The evoked-measurement loop does increment count. This differs from the published100ms pattern plus100ms interval protocol.

The somatic activation is g(3*x/max_trace), with g(z)=1/(1+exp(5*(1-z))) and50Hz maximum. Its threshold in normalized potential is1/3. Printed equations5,7,8 instead place the threshold at3; their literal implications are quantified in ANA-077.

The source sorts every finite-correlation neuron into its maximum-correlated evoked stimulus group using a permissive maximum>-1 criterion. It does not require a significance threshold or claim that this grouping maps anatomical synapses.
The spontaneous summary explicitly sums spikes per assembly and separately plots per-cell counts and assembly size. There is no discrete event-transition estimator in this sample.

findings: The base demo uses1000 cells split500/500, Bernoulli0.5 connectivity with self-edges masked, fixed nonoverlapping excitatory input groups, and positive recurrent weights. Only connections onto excitatory cells are modified.

Excitatory learning is presynaptic PSP times somatic-minus-recurrent-prediction error. Inhibitory learning is presynaptic PSP times excitatory-prediction-minus-inhibitory-prediction error. This provides a local functional learning mechanism without a soma-distance input.

Weights are initialized with1/sqrt(p*N_type), scaled by0.1 onto excitatory cells. The PDF visually confirms the square root, which is omitted by the plain XML text extractor. This is not a source/paper mismatch.

The sample training uses input strength2 and learning rate1e-5; the published table/text give1 and1e-4. The source firing response is g(2*u/h), and inhibitory h is fixed at2. Printed equation3 instead places the normalized excitatory threshold at2, unlike the source threshold1/2.

The test script runs100seconds of settling followed by100seconds of recorded spontaneous activity, driven by constant0.3 input and without learning. It records expected firing probabilities as well as spikes; transition estimation reads the expected-rate assembly averages.

At an event start, the detector considers only the assembly with maximum current activity and requires that assembly to cross half its own observed maximum. It follows that assembly until it falls below threshold. Events continuing beyond the trace end are not retained.

Only consecutive detected events of different labels are counted, with absolute gap between predecessor end and successor start below50ms. The absolute value admits short overlaps; the printed method instead says successors within100ms after the end. The first frame compares against index-1, another boundary detail.

Accepted transition counts are normalized within each source row and scored by mean squared error against the target matrix. The script does not report the fraction of all detected endings that produce accepted transitions or sensitivity to the selection window.

The source groups cells using int(N_E/n_patterns) while stimulus boundaries use int(i*N_E/n_patterns). For the500-cell three-state demo this introduces a small grouping-boundary difference; no numerical impact is asserted without rerunning.
source_audits.limits: The inspected release is an explanatory demo, not a reproduction of every paper condition. No trained arrays, simulation or author-code execution performed. Source qualifications do not remove the constructive result or approve an application learning rule.

source_audits.status: exploratory-processed-data-neighbor-conditioning-audit
source_audits.read_scope: Unmodified public cell and connection tables already obtained for AUD-047. New independent standard-library calculations only; no author code, raw recordings or project tests executed.
method: Select complete-distance recorded clusters and choose each target's nearest recorded pyramidal neighbor before reading outcomes. Exclude a candidate when its source is that nearest neighbor, or when the required outcome is unavailable. Repeated equal-outcome endpoints are collapsed; conflicting outcomes are excluded rather than arbitrarily resolved.

Primary subset uses the already count-matched four-e-type/anatomical flags from AUD-047. A declared sensitivity includes all anatomically eligible pyramidal pairs and restricts cluster size to at most10; all complete-distance clusters already satisfy that bound.

For each source, compare the observed number of jointly connected target/nearest-neighbor pairs with uniform permutations of its outgoing outcomes. Additional references preserve counts within target e-type,50-micrometer source-distance bins, or both. Analytic expectations are checked by exhaustive per-source subset enumeration and convolution.
findings: The known-e-type subset contains18 ambiguous directed endpoint pairs. After exclusions,2954 opportunities span673 sources,120 recorded clusters and23 participant labels. Target connection probability is0.140487; conditional on connection to its nearest recorded neighbor it is0.195506.

Those pooled rates correspond to87 jointly connected opportunities. Preserving each source's outgoing count predicts87.792857, with a conditional reference95% interval70–106. Thus pooled enrichment in this subset is not by itself evidence of additional nearest-neighbor organization.

The broader pyramidal subset gives4875 opportunities and189 joint connections; source-only expectation164.046032 and reference interval140–188 retain a modest positive residual. Preserving outgoing counts within50-micrometer source-distance bins raises expectation to179.543056, with reference interval161–199.

Both subset results are retained. They show sensitivity to curation and the conditioning reference, not absence of anatomical locality or a contradiction of the source's separately curated/offset-conditioned analyses.
The narrow e-type-plus-distance strata leave many events fixed and few alternatives. Reduced or increased residuals across references cannot be read as a clean causal decomposition.
limits: This is exploratory secondary analysis of a different released subset, not exact reproduction of Peng2024 or Barros-Zulaica2026.

The conditional reference assumes independent permutations between sources and does not preserve target indegrees, unmeasured cell properties or shared-source dependencies. Its intervals/tails are not participant-level sampling inference.
Scalar distance bins do not reproduce vertical/horizontal offset conditioning, and missing distances/ambiguous outcomes may select the analyzed population.
Nearest recorded neighbor is not nearest anatomical neighbor. No application geometry or proximity kernel follows from these calculations.

findings: The model uses two branches with64 input sites each, distinct pre/post accumulators, Gaussian within-branch interaction and soma-distance attenuation. No interaction kernel links sites on different branches.

The shuffle helper permutes pair correlation values within each dendritic field before pooling distance bins, preserving field-level value distributions. Its interval is a conditional shuffle reference, not an animal-bootstrap confidence interval.

source_audits.status: selected-public-source-audit

findings: Initial excitatory support is random with its diagonal removed. Plasticity changes weights on that fixed support; no physical positions or structural partner search are used.

The displayed code condition uses IE>0.5 for the dendritic-event trigger, while the figure description uses0.7. This is an example-setting discrepancy, not an independently measured effect size.

Mapped-cell cross-day decoding trains a ridge model on one day and scores another; neural features and target traces are standardized within each day. This supports cross-day predictive structure while not establishing preservation of absolute firing or movement amplitude.

source_audits.status: selected-public-source-audit
source_audits.read_scope: Seven Git-blob-verified files: readme, dynamics/DMD helpers, base simulations, structured-connectivity examples and figure2/3/5 analysis. No execution.
findings: The structured covariance examples subtract Bernoulli probability or a spatial inhibition kernel before symmetrization. Sparse positive edges coexist with dense negative effective couplings.

Released structured examples normalize maximum eigenvalue to0.999; primary methods state0.998. Dense/base simulations default to0.998. This small discrepancy matters when translating longest relaxation times and is retained rather than silently harmonized.

The plotted rotation count correctly divides phase angle by2*pi before dividing by negative log10 magnitude. The displayed methods expression omits this factor if angle is in radians; the inspected source does not have that units error.

DMD retains up to1000 principal components, then fits a lagged ridge operator. Orthonormal truncation is not generally an eigenvalue-preserving similarity transform; preservation requires additional invariant-subspace conditions.

Binary decoding in the inspected figure5 workflow uses nearest class centroids after per-trial across-neuron standardization; the article calls it one-nearest-neighbour decoding. The zero-shot workflow fits a ridge map to high-dimensional embedded input vectors and selects the closest held-out target.

The figure5 simulation rescales per-step noise with timestep and tau; the separate base simulate_random helper uses unit per-step noise. Do not treat defaults across these functions as one universal diffusion convention.
Exact saved figure outputs were not reconstructed; these source/prose differences limit literal reproduction claims without invalidating the reported qualitative comparisons.

source_audits.status: selected-public-source-audit
source_audits.read_scope: 13 Git-blob-verified files covering input/init construction, training entry/settings, RNN definition, timing-plasticity calculations and evaluation; targeted reads, no training or checkpoint loading.
findings: Default main training scripts select tanh hidden units, sigmoid output and fixi=fixo=5. The input/output matrices are frozen identities, while the corresponding biases remain trainable; the RNN helper’s softmax default is overridden by the actual entry point.

Inputs are shifted copies of one truncated Gaussian-bump template, sampled at100 timepoints for100 units. The source therefore embeds the circular relation in training activity before learned recurrence is examined.

Replay receives Gaussian noise of default standard deviation.01; prediction receives a10-step true prefix then noise. These evaluations use the stored sequence length, not evidence of indefinitely continuing replay.

Ring R2 fits and evaluates a ridge decoder on the same output timepoints. It is an in-sample representation-fit measure, not held-out fixed-decoder accuracy. Angular resultant length measures consistency of errors, including a constant wrong phase.

The STDP matrix helper uses A+=1,tau+=1,A-=.5,tau-=3. It normalizes the matrix by its operator norm; the default subsequent dynamics renormalize again and use u_next=(W/||W||)*u. The computed tanh Euler candidate is bypassed in this default path.

The inspected Gaussian-integral closed form repeats the v2 supplement’s exponent1/(b*tau^2), whereas completing the square gives1/(2*b*tau^2). Independent quadrature verifies the discrepancy; unequal time constants mean it is not one removable common factor.

The source Fourier imaginary term correctly sums the potentiation/depression contributions, while the inspected supplementary expression shows their difference. Analytic and numerical spectra also have separately chosen scale factors; neither is a verified exact reproduction of the final journal figure.
These scope-specific discrepancies do not negate the trained-RNN positive result; they prevent literal adoption of the displayed plasticity formula or metrics without independent validation.

The helper named code_effective_dimension computes a participation ratio of an uncentered second-moment spectrum, not an exact nonzero-eigenvalue count. Named dimensionality metrics must be interpreted by their definitions.

Continuous response simulations depend on external general-library helpers not included in this audit. The pinned historical files are evidence about their selected paths, not a complete reproduction of the publication or the2026 repository head.

findings: Fig4bc.py uses max(real(eigvals(W))) and accepts R<=1; it computes integrated covariance from (I-W)^-1 times its transpose. The single scalar must be interpreted in the stated continuous-time setting.
Its chain sweep simultaneously changes convergence, divergence and reciprocity. This is not an isolated chain intervention.

source_audits.status: Selected pinned source and compact result audit

findings: Main GLMM construction uses one functional predictor with projection interaction and presynaptic/projection random intercept; conversion includes an exposure offset.

Released results detect total common-input excess in three of four projection groups; axonal and synaptic decompositions have different group patterns. Non-significance is not proof of equality.
Proximity utilities discretize skeletons, find vertex pairs with a KDTree radius and sum associated dendritic edges. This is an anatomical measurement procedure, not a neuron-index neighborhood.

findings: AnisoSin2.m uses c*sin(pi*x)^2+(1-c)*sin(pi*x), c=.15. The printed equation18 omits pi inside its first sine, whereas its Fourier coefficients match the code profile.

analytical_checks.status: agent-derived illustrative probability calculation; no new application mechanism
analytical_checks.question: Can pooled sampling heterogeneity mimic motif enrichment?
assumptions: Equal-sized sampled groups have latent edge probability p=0.1 or 0.3 with equal prior weight.
Edges are independent conditional on the group probability; no geometric or common-neighbor wiring mechanism is present.
The target edge and the two edges of one specified common-neighbor configuration are distinct.
derivation: P(edge)=E[p]=0.2.
P(reciprocal pair)=E[p^2]=0.05, while pooled independent-edge prediction is E[p]^2=0.04.
P(target edge | specified two-edge configuration)=E[p^3]/E[p^2]=0.28.
analytical_checks.result: Apparent reciprocal enrichment of 1.25 and increased connection probability after observing a common neighbor arise from the mixture alone.
analytical_checks.relevance: Use a suitable heterogeneous null before treating an observed motif relation as an independent learning principle. This is not a fit to either human dataset.
analytical_checks.calculation: Exact rational arithmetic using Python fractions; values independently follow from the displayed finite sums.
analytical_checks.qualification: The mixture shares a latent probability across the sampled edges. For reciprocal pairs, shared symmetric opportunity creates E[p^2]; arbitrary unrelated directed propensities do not imply enrichment. AUD-014 confirms a published shared-latent example; marginal variance alone cannot determine motifs outside that restricted family.

analytical_checks.question: Does the assigned coordinate role itself define a useful cross-minicolumn distance?
assumptions: Represent only the coordinate/polarity label of a cell by s*e_d, with s in {-1,+1} and e_d an orthonormal basis vector.
This idealization describes its assigned role, not its complete context-dependent response function or learned connectivity.
derivation: For distinct dimensions d and e, ||s*e_d - t*e_e||^2 = 2 for every polarity pair.
Within one dimension the squared distance is 0 for equal polarity and 4 for opposite polarity.
Thus this role-only Euclidean construction supplies no graded cross-dimension neighborhood.
limits: Orthogonal basis vectors do not imply statistically independent coordinate values across tokens.
The existing embedding statistics already measure nonzero coordinate correlations, uniformly over token types; they do not measure usage-weighted temporal input or neuronal coactivity.
A correlation, learned graph or context representation could contain additional structure, but none is thereby approved as a spatial metric.
Relabeling coordinates together with input/output mappings differs from rotating the fixed semantic basis.

analytical_checks.question: Do fan-in, fan-out and middleman statistics count three distinct global triangle structures?
assumptions: A is a directed adjacency matrix without self-edges. For weighted numerators replace A by the elementwise cube root of nonnegative weights, as in LOC-023.
derivation: The motif numerator sums are tr(A^T A^2), tr(A^2 A^T), and tr(A A^T A).
Cyclic invariance of trace makes these sums equal: they describe different node roles in the same transitive triangle configurations.
For edges 0→1, 0→2, 1→2, numerator vectors are fan-in=(0,0,1), fan-out=(1,0,0), middleman=(0,1,0). Each total is one.
Their nonzero raw local clustering values differ: fan-in=1/2, fan-out=1/2, middleman=1, owing to different possible-triplet denominators.

analytical_checks.question: Can an excitatory direct edge coexist with negative net influence in a stable circuit without any geometry?
assumptions: Small deviations around a positive operating point; three linear units E1, I and E2 with common unit time constant.
Positive coefficients a,b,c and no feedback: E1 excites E2 and I; I inhibits E2.
derivation: dx/dt = -x + u; dy/dt = -y + b*x; dz/dt = -z + a*x - c*y.
The state matrix is triangular in order (x,y,z), with all eigenvalues -1.
At equilibrium, dz/du = a - b*c. For a=0.2, b=c=1, the direct excitatory edge is positive but net influence is -0.8.

analytical_checks.question: Does a fixed assignment of cells to semantic coordinates determine their measured coactivity?
assumptions: For this illustration only, let a_i(t) be a binary input event and p_i(t) its conditional probability given the input/context at time t.
Distinct cells are conditionally independent in the first case; this is an analytical assumption, not the accepted SNN encoder.
derivation: The law of total covariance gives Cov(a_i,a_j)=E[Cov(a_i,a_j | input/context)]+Cov(p_i,p_j).

Under conditional independence, distinct-cell covariance equals Cov(p_i,p_j). Cells with the same assigned probability function have covariance Var(p), even if their individual events are independently sampled.
If instead exactly k of n cells are sampled uniformly in a group, with p=k/n fixed, distinct-cell conditional covariance is -p*(1-p)/(n-1). This follows from E[a_i*a_j]=k*(k-1)/(n*(n-1)).

assumptions: Let X contain one row-normalized population-response vector per word, and K=X X^T.
Let Q be an orthogonal transformation of neuron coordinates, including a permutation as a special case.
derivation: For Y=XQ, Y Y^T=X Q Q^T X^T=K. Centering over words gives the same J K J and the same word-space eigenspaces.
Consequently a difference between word-Gram eigenspaces is not itself an estimate of a pure rotation in neuron space. A neuronal rotation cannot be identified from K alone.

Cosine distance is not invariant to arbitrary linear remixing: x=(1,1) and y=(1,-1) have cosine zero; applying diag(2,1) to both gives cosine 3/5. Orthogonal maps and common uniform scaling preserve cosines; general anisotropic maps do not.
analytical_checks.relevance: A correlation between semantic and response RDMs cannot identify a unique assignment of semantic axes to neurons, much less an anatomical distance rule. Separate identified-neuron or anatomical evidence is required.
limits: LOC-043 also measures identified-neuron tuning and neuron covariance; this check does not negate those separate observations or show that neural rotations never occur.
Arbitrary signed rotations need not preserve nonnegative firing-rate representations. The permutation case alone already establishes non-identifiability of individual-neuron ordering from K.
Fixed semantic roles in this model are a human design premise, not a conclusion that must be inferred from a brain RDM. No role rotation or remapping is selected.

analytical_checks.status: conditional noise-projection calculation; no noise process or readout selected
analytical_checks.question: Does temporally white input specify how noise moves a represented population state?
assumptions: Let discrete-time noise eta_t have zero mean and Cov(eta_t,eta_s)=Q times the indicator t=s. Q describes correlations among neurons at one time.
For a local linear observation z=c^T x, a noise step contributes c^T eta_t. This is an illustrative local observation, not the selected SNN decoder.
derivation: Var(c^T eta_t)=c^T Q c. Temporal whiteness fixes the absence of across-time covariance; it does not require Q to be diagonal or determine the variance along a semantic/dynamical direction.

For an arithmetic average over m equal-variance cells with pairwise correlation rho, variance is sigma^2*(1+(m-1)*rho)/m. Independent cells give sigma^2/m, while perfectly shared fluctuations give sigma^2.

Under isotropic noise, a unit vector receives the same absolute projected variance as any other unit vector; its fraction of total noise energy is 1/N. Claims of 1/N diffusion must also specify state-coordinate normalization and dynamics.
analytical_checks.relevance: The DMN white-noise premise leaves correlation and projection questions open. Noise that maintains activity need not drive semantic exploration effectively, and changing correlation structure need not refer to a physical distance.
limits: The average example does not choose an output decoder, neuron-phase rule, activity controller or a particular covariance.
Observed low-dimensional motion in LOC-047 does not establish the same mechanism in semantic networks.
No dense covariance matrix, new allocation or noise generator is introduced.
analytical_checks.additional_application: The averaging identity also shows why equal-gain synaptic inputs rescaled to preserve mean drive can change fluctuation magnitude when their number changes. This is a conditional training/dynamics observation, not a capacity-allocation weight rule.

filtering_extension.statement: If temporally independent Gaussian input has spatial covariance Q and fixed linear filters are rows of H, the filtered covariance is H Q H^T. Overlapping filters can create cross-channel correlations even when Q is diagonal. For Gaussian projections z_k,z_l and rates lambda_k=a*exp(b*z_k), Cov(lambda_k,lambda_l)=E[lambda_k]*E[lambda_l]*(exp(b^2*Cov(z_k,z_l))-1).
filtering_extension.limits: This identity does not reproduce LOC-171's finite movie, smoothing, Bernoulli sampler or amplitude settings. Its reported white-noise control is protocol-specific. Temporal whiteness alone neither supplies semantic correlations nor prevents filtered/recurrent activity from acquiring them; no noise process or covariance allocation is chosen.

analytical_checks.status: identifiability distinction; no analysis pipeline or acceptance threshold selected
analytical_checks.question: Does a loop in the topology of sampled neural states demonstrate a recurring temporal sequence?
assumptions: Consider a point cloud containing measured population-response vectors, and a topological analysis depending only on those points and their pairwise distances.
derivation: Permuting the time order of all vectors preserves the point cloud, pairwise-distance structure and its persistent-homology result.
The same sampled states can therefore arise in an ordered traversal, a diffusive walk or an irregular succession while producing the same point-cloud topology.
Evidence for repeated temporal traversal additionally requires time-ordered transitions and return behavior; a bounded activity fraction or a nontrivial topological loop alone cannot establish it.

LOC-153 provides a constructive side-by-side recurrent-network example: complex low-rank modes produce ongoing circulation, while nearly degenerate real modes produce a ring-like slow manifold and fixed points. Their activity-state plots are not physical neuron maps.
analytical_checks.relevance: A state manifold, an anatomical ring, a directed circuit cycle and an actual repeating semantic trajectory are four different objects. Grid/head-direction results must not be imported as automatic proof of the intended immersion dynamics.
limits: LOC-047 and LOC-050 also study temporal dynamics; this check does not reduce those studies to topology alone.
No required period, metric, decoder, smoothing window or new runtime bookkeeping is chosen.

analytical_checks.status: conditional common-input counterexample; no diagnostic or learning rule selected
analytical_checks.question: Can directional predictive dependence arise without a direct source-to-target edge?
assumptions: Let independent standard Gaussian variables Z_t, e_t and n_t generate X_t=Z_t+e_t and Y_(t+1)=Z_t+n_t, with independent latent values over time.
Both observations are driven by Z_t; there is no causal edge from X to Y.
derivation: Y_t is independent of X_t and Y_(t+1), so I(Y_(t+1);X_t | Y_t)=I(Y_(t+1);X_t).
The correlation of X_t and Y_(t+1) is 1/2. Their Gaussian mutual information is -0.5*log2(1-1/4), approximately 0.2075 bits.
Thus positive pairwise transfer entropy does not by itself identify a direct connection or exclude delayed common input.
analytical_checks.relevance: Distributed token drive can induce relationships across assigned populations. Observed coactivity may still be useful for learning, but is not equivalent to proof of existing directed transmission.
limits: This counterexample does not invalidate the specific experimental analyses in LOC-055 or show that all observed propagation is common input.
No all-pairs statistic, causal estimator or new storage is prescribed.

analytical_checks.status: conditional delayed-network calculation; no delay representation selected
analytical_checks.question: Does matching connectivity counts and the marginal delay distribution preserve recurrent timing?
assumptions: Consider two disjoint reciprocal pairs with identical edge weights, and a common multiset of four delays {a,a,b,b}, with a and b unequal positive values.
derivation: Assigning one a and one b to each reciprocal pair gives two round-trip delays a+b. Assigning both a values to one pair and both b values to the other gives round-trip delays 2a and 2b.

The same graph, weights and marginal delays therefore have different feedback timing. For a linear delayed pair with equal leak gamma and weight w, the characteristic equation is (lambda+gamma)^2-w^2*exp(-lambda*(tau12+tau21))=0.

Delay-weight-path associations, rather than delay histograms alone, can determine recurrent temporal structure. Coordinates used only to construct those associations are not separately required by the subsequent equations.
analytical_checks.relevance: A meaningful control for a claimed geometry benefit should identify which joint timing/path properties change. This refines the distinction between an explicit physical layout and the dynamics of its resulting circuit.
limits: This does not prove that finding suitable nonspatial weights/delays is easy or equivalent in learning cost.
No delay arrays, geometric coordinates, event queues or implementation changes are adopted.

analytical_checks.status: conditional structural counterexample; no dendritic implementation selected
analytical_checks.question: Can a single global distance between source neurons represent all receiver-specific synaptic locality?
assumptions: Two source neurons A and B contact two receiving neurons J and K.
Their contacts cooperate locally on J but occupy separate, weakly interacting branches on K.
derivation: A rule depending only on one global d(A,B) gives the same distance factor for both receiving neurons.
The stipulated receiver-specific interactions require an additional dependence on receiver/contact placement or state; a global source-pair metric alone cannot express both.
This is a representation distinction, not evidence that our application requires dendrites or that no richer geometric model could represent the circuit.
analytical_checks.relevance: Prevents transferring measured dendritic crosstalk directly into a distance preference among semantic minicolumns.
limits: The counterexample is conditional; it does not claim all biological circuits realize arbitrary interaction tensors.
No additional arrays, branch structures or learning rule are selected.

analytical_checks.status: deduction from published HTM activation equations; no extension adopted
analytical_checks.question: Do the core2016 HTM equations generate spontaneous activity when external winning input columns are absent?
assumptions: Use equations2–3 of LOC-061 as printed, with a positive dendritic threshold and no additional activation pathway.
The externally selected winning column set W_t is empty.
derivation: Both nonzero cases for a_ij(t) require j in W_t; consequently all active-cell entries become zero regardless of the previous prediction.
The subsequent prediction calculation receives zero active presynaptic inputs, so no segment exceeds its positive threshold.
Predictive transitions under continuing external inputs therefore do not by themselves establish input-free recurrent activation.
analytical_checks.relevance: The application's immersion requirement needs evidence beyond inherited HTM phase names; this does not specify how to satisfy it.
limits: This deduction applies to the cited equations, not every later HTM variant or biologically motivated replay mechanism.
No feedback conversion, noise source or activation rule is adopted.
analytical_checks.later_extension_note: LOC-074 supplies a continuous-time replay extension with changed excitability parameters; this does not invalidate the deduction for the original2016 activation equations.

analytical_checks.status: analytical null-model sensitivity illustration; no activation fraction or threshold selected
analytical_checks.question: Is a sparse marginal firing fraction sufficient to justify extremely low dendritic pattern false-match rates?
assumptions: Consider20 binary contacts with activation threshold15 and common marginal probability p.
Compare independent contacts with four independent blocks of five contacts, perfectly correlated within each block; these are illustrative distributions, not measured project encoding.
derivation: Independent contacts give P(match)=sum_{k=15}^{20} choose(20,k)*p^k*(1-p)^(20-k).
In the block model at least three blocks must activate, giving P(match)=4*p^3*(1-p)+p^4.
At p=0.1 these probabilities are approximately9.4813e-12 and0.0037, despite identical contact count, threshold and marginal activity.
The published HTM fixed-size uniform-pattern formula is hypergeometric; this independent-Bernoulli comparison is deliberately a separate illustrative calculation.
analytical_checks.relevance: Global sparsity and an activity-fraction band do not establish the null distribution for fixed-role, correlated semantic input. Dense embedding entries also do not determine neuronal firing probability without an encoder.
limits: Perfect within-block correlation is an extreme counterexample, not an estimate of Flash embeddings or neuronal activity.
No sparsifier, whitening transform, threshold, rate band or branch structure is selected.

analytical_checks.status: probability-mixture calculation and conditional approximation; no connectivity rule adopted
analytical_checks.question: Do90/10 coefficients applied to two peak-normalized maps imply a90/10 split of sampled connections?
assumptions: An initial weighted draw uses q_i proportional to a*G_i+b*F_i, with nonnegative maps G,F.
For illustrative numbers, use an ideal600-by600 periodic grid, Gaussian sigma72 grid steps, equal100-bin angle populations, and peak0.1 for both maps, matching the inspected generator's scales.
derivation: The normalized mass attributable to F is b*sum(F)/(a*sum(G)+b*sum(F)); it equals b/(a+b) only if the component sums are equal.
With a=0.9,b=0.1, sum(G) is approximately3257.001856. For concentration k=1.25, sum(F) is approximately14754.101378, giving an initial-draw component mass0.3348097634.
For k=0,2,3 the analogous masses are approximately0.55119,0.27478,0.22984. Peak normalization makes concentration also change total component mass.
analytical_checks.relevance: Interpret the published coefficient as a probability-map coefficient. A concentration sweep does not isolate preference width at fixed component mass in this construction.
limits: This is not an empirical fraction of long-distance edges: the tuning component can also draw nearby targets.
The generator resamples, deduplicates and trims candidates; final retained-edge proportions and exact binary graph were not measured.
No modification of the authors' code or project learning algorithm is made.

analytical_checks.status: graph-observable counterexample; no graph prior selected
analytical_checks.question: Does a pair-strength distribution identify the distribution of distinct incoming partners?
assumptions: Take six labeled neurons and five arbitrary positive edge weights.
Place exactly those weights either on a directed five-neuron cycle with one isolated neuron, or on five edges from five different neurons into the sixth neuron.
derivation: Both constructions have exactly the same multiset of nonzero pair weights, total strength and edge count.
The cycle has incoming-partner counts1,1,1,1,1,0; the convergent star has counts0,0,0,0,0,5.
Thus the weight distribution alone cannot identify partner-degree heterogeneity. The construction remains valid for any chosen broad weight multiset.
analytical_checks.relevance: An apparent exponent match between a biological pair-strength tail and the engineering capacity-class template does not qualify the latter as an empirical indegree law.
limits: This is an identifiability example, not a claim that either topology is a suitable SNN design.
It does not modify the provisional allocation, which already distinguishes degree from weights.

analytical_checks.status: response-model identifiability check; no encoder or metric selected
analytical_checks.question: Does a response that peaks near a preferred semantic vector identify a physical neighborhood or distinguish all peak and axis response models?
assumptions: For this algebra only, x and p are unit-normalized stimulus and preferred vectors.
A response depends monotonically on distance from p, or on cosine similarity to p; this does not assume DeepSeek vectors or the application encoder are normalized.
derivation: Squared Euclidean distance is||x-p||^2=2-2*p dot x. Consequently, a radial response function on this sphere is also a scalar nonlinear function of projection onto p.
A sigmoid of cosine similarity to a fixed preferred vector is a nonlinear single-direction tuning curve. The preferred direction can mix many embedding coordinates.
For p=(0.6,0.8), the unit stimuli(0,1) and(1,0) have projections0.8 and0.6, and squared distances0.4 and0.8 respectively; the identities agree directly.
None of these quantities contains neuronal anatomical coordinates. A semantic response relation does not determine where cells should be placed.
analytical_checks.relevance: Peak-looking semantic plots and monotone direction tuning can be indistinguishable under restricted stimulus/response assumptions. This preserves the distinction between the geometry of represented concepts and a proposed physical metric.
limits: This does not declare the preprint analyses invalid or claim equivalence for all varying-norm stimuli, multiple response peaks or arbitrary nonlinear models.
It does not normalize, rotate, reduce or relearn the application embedding basis.
It does not establish that all neurons share one preferred direction or that preferred directions are mutually orthogonal.

analytical_checks.status: conditional storage extrapolation; no excitatory/inhibitory allocation proposed
analytical_checks.question: Would the published2014 SORN connectivity translate directly into the provisional CC slot budget?
assumptions: For this calculation only, keep total neuron count614400 and the paper ratio NI=0.2NE, giving NE512000 and NI102400.
Preserve fully connected E-to-I, independent EE probability0.1 excluding self, and I-to-E probability0.2.
Use the favourable application storage cost5bytes per actual edge, ignoring all additional states, learning traces, precision and temporary storage.
derivation: E-to-I alone has52,428,800,000edges and costs262,144,000,000bytes=244.140625GiB.
Expected EE edge count is26,214,348,800; expected I-to-E count is10,485,760,000.
Total expected count is89,128,908,800, costing415.038824GiB at5bytes/edge.
That count is793.797994times the J16 allocation of112,281,600slots.
analytical_checks.relevance: Dense auxiliary connection classes can dominate even when the recurrent class is described as sparse. A successful small-network recurrence result is not itself a memory-feasible CC plan.
limits: This deliberately literal extrapolation is not a lower bound on all SORN-like or coordinate-free sequence mechanisms.
Sparse replacements may work, but their dynamics require separate evidence. No replacement or E/I cell partition has been adopted.
Expected counts are not measurements of a sampled network. Allocated slots are an upper capacity, not a required count of live synapses.

analytical_checks.status: conditional motif-access calculation; no dendritic threshold, graph prior or learning rule selected
analytical_checks.question: Does the successful potential-connectivity regime of LOC-074 automatically transfer to a globally uniform static sparse candidate graph at CC scale?
assumptions: For this comparison only, preserve its20 active source cells and requirement of5 potential contacts per recruited target. These are paper parameters, not our application choices.
Each target independently of its semantic role has k distinct candidates sampled uniformly from614399 other neurons. The prescribed source set is disjoint from target cells.
Use120 possible target cells as a generous illustrative whole-dimension pool; the application has60 cells per signed population. No mechanism for combining the signs is proposed.
The18432 row gives every hypothetical target the largest J16 capacity, an intentionally generous bound that is not the actual capacity allocation.
derivation: For one target, q=P(H>=5), with H hypergeometric over20 marked source cells in a population of614399 and k selected candidates.
Equivalently q=sum_j>=5 C(k,j)C(N-k,20-j)/C(N,20), evaluated with exact rational arithmetic.
For120 targets, E[number qualifying]=120q. Markov bounds P(at least20 qualifying)<=120q/20 without assuming independent target neighborhoods.
For the paper binomial model p0.2,n150: q=0.370351736097331, E[qualifying]=55.5527604145996, and P(fewer than20)=2.23181883584884e-11.
analytical_checks.relevance: The important transfer quantity is access to enough mutually relevant candidates, not simply whether both networks are called sparse. This is one possible computational function of concentrated opportunity, without supplying any physical coordinates for our model.
limits: The calculation applies to a fixed uniformly sampled candidate skeleton, not adaptive rewiring that searches additional partners over time.
Dense semantic patterns can recruit sources across many dimensions. Failure of this specific single-group motif translation does not prove failure of the proposed SNN.
No uniform sampling law, coincidence threshold, synchrony requirement or increase in storage is selected.
Capacity is not live degree. The calculation does not require filling every slot or restoring an abandoned physical metric.

analytical_checks.status: conditional rejection-sampling arithmetic; no candidate sampler adopted
analytical_checks.question: Does uniform sampling of an absent pair inherently require enumerating all absent pairs?
assumptions: There areM=N(N-1) allowed directed nonself pairs andK distinct occupied pairs, with a way to test occupancy. The cost or storage of that membership test is not assumed free.
Draw a uniformly random allowed pair with replacement and retry if already occupied.
Use N614400 and the J16 slot total112281600 only as a generous example with every slot assigned to a distinct occupied pair.
derivation: Conditional on acceptance, each absent pair has equal probability, so a materialized list of absent pairs is unnecessary.
The acceptance probability is1-K/M; the expected number of draws is1/(1-K/M).
analytical_checks.relevance: The size of the mathematical partner universe and the number of simultaneously stored connections are different. Cheap sampling of an absent pair, however, does not imply cheap discovery of a useful connection.
limits: Per-target saturation, forbidden pair classes, weighted proposals, duplicate contacts and capacity migration can change this calculation.
Learning relevance, convergence speed, membership structures and candidate evaluation are unresolved costs.
This arithmetic does not recommend global uniform rewiring or introduce auxiliary storage into the design.

analytical_checks.status: exact moments of a conditional toy model; not an SNN capacity estimate
analytical_checks.question: Can a heterogeneous live-degree distribution be replaced by its arithmetic mean in independent-pattern retrieval noise?
assumptions: Independent standard Gaussian patterns xi^1 through xi^(L+1), a fixed target source set S_i of size K_i excluding self, and bilinear weights J_ij=(1/K_i)*sum_mu xi_i^(mu+1)*xi_j^mu on that set.
The cue equals one stored pattern xi^nu; evaluate the linear field h_i, before nonlinear neural response, against xi_i^(nu+1).
derivation: Writing q_mu=(1/K_i)*sum_j xi_j^mu*xi_j^nu gives E(q_nu)=1 and Var(q_nu)=2/K_i; for mu!=nu, E(q_mu)=0 and E(q_mu^2)=1/K_i.
Independence of target-pattern coefficients and nonself source patterns makes cross terms vanish. Therefore E[(h_i-xi_i^(nu+1))^2]=(L+1)/K_i.

The mean error across targets depends on mean(1/K_i), not1/mean(K_i). Equal groups with degrees100 and1600 have arithmetic mean850 and harmonic mean188.235294; replacing the distribution by850 understates this toy mean error by4.515625 times.
analytical_checks.relevance: Even before real embedding correlations or spiking nonlinearities, a uniform-degree capacity result cannot be transferred using only mean allocated slots.
limits: The example uses actual occupied degree, not capacity-class size.
The formula is not a result for correlated Flash inputs, sign-separated probabilistic encoding, FP4/FP8, recurrently learned weights or firing dynamics.
No per-neuron normalization, degree law or learning formula is adopted.

analytical_checks.status: conditional Lyapunov argument; no dynamics selected
analytical_checks.question: Can changing static connection locality alone generate autonomous cycles in a symmetric passive rate network?
assumptions: C_i*du_i/dt=-u_i/R_i+sum_j W_ij*V_j, with V_i=g_i(u_i), C_i,R_i>0, W symmetric, smooth strictly increasing responses and no time-dependent drive, adaptation, delay or noise.
Use zero external input to avoid relying on the sign convention of the scanned paper's external-input energy term.
derivation: E(V)=-0.5*V^T W V+sum_i(1/R_i)*integral_0^V_i g_i^(-1)(s)ds.
dE/dt=-sum_i C_i*(g_i^(-1))'(V_i)*(dV_i/dt)^2<=0. A nonconstant periodic trajectory would return to its initial energy despite a strictly negative integral, a contradiction.
Selecting different symmetric edges by a geometric rule does not change this conclusion while the assumptions remain true.
analytical_checks.relevance: Desired sustained semantic loops require a dynamical explanation; a distance preference by itself is not such an explanation.
limits: This does not exclude cycles in delayed, adaptive, noisy, asymmetric, spiking or synchronous discrete-state systems.
It does not require asymmetric weights in every possible model; adaptation-based latching is an explicit different case.
No conclusion about all forms of fire-together learning is implied.

analytical_checks.status: information-identifiability argument under restricted observations
analytical_checks.question: Can instantaneous input statistics alone distinguish opposite orders of the same represented states?
assumptions: Compare equal-occupancy cycles A->B->C->A and A->C->B->A for three arbitrary distinct encoded patterns.
The learner uses only the instantaneous input distribution, with the same static graph prior, and has no observed temporal order or history-dependent activity.
derivation: Both sequences have the same instantaneous distribution and every zero-lag moment. Any parameter construction depending only on these quantities produces the same result.

With identical post-learning initial conditions, that result cannot uniquely encode both opposite orders. Lagged statistics, differing retained state or another history-sensitive mechanism can distinguish them.
analytical_checks.relevance: Choosing partners and encoding temporal succession are separate questions. An unchanged physical-distance prior supplies no missing sequence-order information.
limits: Recurrent neural coactivity can already contain temporal history, so this is not a claim that every Hebbian rule fails.
No eligibility trace, asymmetric update, timing window or sequence objective is adopted.

analytical_checks.status: completed full-vocabulary observational calculation on the pinned local input table
analytical_checks.question: How closely do actual Flash inputs resemble isotropic independent-coordinate patterns used in sequence-capacity analyses?
assumptions: Equal weight for127997 ordinary vocabulary entries from pinned revision1bae0e1088993b9b82de08f59de5be5a34e42170;5120 raw embedding coefficients per entry.
Input-table statistics precede the unchosen probabilistic population encoder and do not represent corpus-frequency-weighted or contextual states.
derivation: Float64 full covariance accumulation and eigendecomposition yield participation ratio652.650489 and entropy effective rank2156.122082. These are different spectral summaries, not counts of semantic concepts.
416 principal components contain50% of centered variance;3327 contain90%;4104 contain95%. The largest component contains1.953441%.

Across all13104640 dimension pairs, median absolute Pearson correlation is0.023921569,95th percentile0.071560994, and0.794474% of pairs exceed0.1. Extreme correlations are+0.501467893 and-0.351914662.
Source SHA256 was reverified. Direct diagonal, spectral trace, squared-eigenvalue and matrix-symmetry checks agree to floating-point precision; every covariance eigenvalue is positive.

Keeping only coordinate variances would give participation ratio5111.263733, whereas standardizing variances before computing the correlation-matrix participation ratio gives661.311493. Cross-coordinate covariance, rather than marginal variance inequality, therefore dominates the observed spectral concentration. This is a descriptive decomposition, not a neuron metric.
analytical_checks.relevance: Dense distributed token activation is compatible with statistically structured dimensions. Independent isotropic pattern results require a transfer analysis rather than substitution of our neuron count or mean slot capacity.
limits: Principal components are analytical coordinates only; no basis rotation, compression or neuron remapping is proposed.
Covariance is not a physical distance, causality claim or connection rule.
Neither a task capacity nor a steady-activation probability follows from this calculation.

analytical_checks.status: conditional finite-population sampling calculation; no candidate distribution selected
analytical_checks.question: How many semantic dimensions would uniform distinct neuronal candidates expose to one target?
assumptions: The existing5120 dimensions each contain120 cells, split60/60 by semantic polarity. Select K distinct source neurons uniformly from614399 cells excluding only the target itself.
This is a reference distribution, not an approved proposal rule, minimum coverage requirement or assumption that every capacity slot is occupied.
derivation: For a source group of size g, the probability of no selected source is q_g=choose(M-g,K)/choose(M,K)=product_{r=0}^{g-1}(1-K/(M-r)), with M=614399.

The expected number of represented dimensions is5119*(1-q_120)+(1-q_119); for signed subpopulations it is10239*(1-q_60)+(1-q_59). The target's own dimension contributes on average119*K/M source cells.
K=100 exposes about99.047 dimensions; K=183 exposes179.812; K=10000 exposes4405.543; K=18432 exposes4987.651. These are expectations over distinct source identity, not independent input signals.
analytical_checks.relevance: Incoming edge count, coverage of fixed semantic dimensions and the number of statistically independent signals are different quantities.
limits: A neuron need not directly observe every dimension; distributed computation and multistep paths can contribute.
Cells sharing an input role can acquire different recurrent states, so their activity is not assumed identical.
The full-table covariance and the unchosen input encoder prevent interpreting coverage as a memory-capacity calculation.
No geometry, same-minicolumn exclusion, bookkeeping field or sampler is introduced.

analytical_checks.status: measurement-identifiability distinction; no model mechanism proposed
analytical_checks.question: Does classifying a source–target cell-type pair from molecular features validate prediction of its synaptic connection?
assumptions: T_i,T_j denote cell types, G_i,G_j expression features and A_ij the presence of a synapse.
The assessed classifier predicts (T_i,T_j) from expression products. Its test split excludes training cells but the target is still pair identity rather than A_ij.
derivation: P(T_i,T_j | G_i,G_j) and P(A_ij | G_i,G_j,T_i,T_j) are different statistical objects.

Keeping the same cell types and expression profiles while changing the synaptic graph leaves pair-identity classification unchanged. Thus even perfect identity classification alone does not identify the graph.
An anatomical prior used to select molecular interactions is an input assumption. Agreement with that same assumed structure is not an independent test of the prior.
Perturbation effects and independently measured synapses provide separate evidence; this distinction does not discard the paper’s targeted knockdown results.
analytical_checks.relevance: Evidence for stable cellular identities must not be promoted into evidence for a spatial layout, semantic-distance kernel or wiring algorithm without an additional validated link.
limits: This is a scope distinction, not an allegation that the paper claimed to predict every synapse.
No molecular proxy, classifier or new application state field is introduced.

analytical_checks.status: conditional mathematical counterexamples; no geometry assigned to application neurons
analytical_checks.question: Does a typical nonzero connection length or a spread-out connected group establish very-near avoidance?
assumptions: For illustration only, use uniform spatial density in d dimensions and a decreasing pairwise kernel p(r)=exp(-r/ell), without any exclusion zone.
A second illustration compares valid three-point geometries with independent undirected pair events and ell=1. These coordinates are mathematical examples, not a proposed layout.
derivation: The number of candidate partners in a radial shell is proportional to r^(d-1). Thus the connected-distance density is proportional to r^(d-1)*exp(-r/ell), whose mode for d>1 is (d-1)*ell, despite the maximal pairwise probability occurring at zero distance.
Mean group distance also discards information. An equilateral triangle with side1 has mean distance1 and expected connected-pair count3*exp(-1)=1.1036383.

Collinear points at0,0.01,2 have mean distance4/3 but expected connected-pair count exp(-0.01)+exp(-1.99)+exp(-2)=1.2620805. A larger average separation can therefore coexist with more expected connections under the same strictly decreasing pair kernel.

Perin2011 used measured-position controls, so these generic examples do not explain away that study’s residual clustering. They show why the pair kernel, distance histogram and group statistic must be distinguished.
analytical_checks.relevance: A very-near exemption needs its own operational meaning and evidence; it cannot be read directly from the typical spacing of assemblies or the peak of a connection-length histogram.
limits: No exemption is adopted or removed, and no physical metric is introduced.
These examples do not determine how biological morphology, finite boundaries or cell identities modify a measured connection distribution.

analytical_checks.status: exact denominator reconstruction and conditional sampling calculation; no biological reanalysis or model choice
analytical_checks.question: What do a reported reciprocal percentage and an observed fully reciprocal cell actually measure?
assumptions: For paired directed observations let u, o and b count unconnected, one-way and reciprocal unordered pairs; n=u+o+b.
For a separate illustrative sampling calculation, suppose m recorded partners independently reciprocate with probability q. This is not assumed to describe the biological samples.
derivation: Directed connection probability is (o+2b)/(2n); the reciprocal fraction of all pairs is b/n; reciprocity conditional on any connection is b/(o+b). These have different denominators.
Tarusawa Figure 3 at P18–20: presumed clonal counts (u,o,b)=(50,4,20) give .297297 directed probability, .270270 reciprocal fraction of all pairs, and .833333 conditional reciprocity.
Nonclonal counts (35,13,9) give .271930, .157895 and .409091 respectively. Similar marginal probabilities therefore coexist with different paired structure. No significance test is recomputed here.
For the illustrative per-cell sample, Pr(observed RPV=1)=q^m. At q=.75 this is .421875 with three partners and .31640625 with four; observing only reciprocating partners does not prove q=1.
analytical_checks.relevance: Slot capacity, actual degree, pooled pair probability, reciprocal motif enrichment and sampled per-cell reciprocity must remain distinct when considering biological constraints.
limits: The sampling example neither explains away the intervention effect nor estimates the true biological q or its distribution.

analytical_checks.status: conditional normalization calculation and control analysis; no geometric prior adopted
analytical_checks.question: Does equal eta isolate the contribution of geometry when comparing ordinary and distance-weighted regularization?
assumptions: For illustration, independently uniform points on a unit circle have chord distance D=2*abs(sin(theta/2)).
For the expectation comparison only, edge weights and sampled pair distances are independent. Learning generally breaks that independence.
derivation: E[D]=4/pi and E[D^2]=2. Therefore distance-RMS normalization yields E[D/sqrt(E[D^2])]=2*sqrt(2)/pi=.900316316, not1.

At equal eta, ordinary L1 and this distance-weighted L1 can differ in average shrinkage even before considering heterogeneous edge penalties. Matching one scalar also cannot remove the heterogeneous penalty itself.

The inspected framework changes both the penalty and candidate sampler; those two interventions need separate controls to identify their individual contributions. A shuffled symmetric cost matrix with matched values would test a different hypothesis from ordinary L1, but has not been run here.
analytical_checks.relevance: The source’s positive controlled results should be preserved without treating equal-coefficient comparisons as proof that a geometrically consistent metric is the unique source of benefit.
limits: This is not a reanalysis of trained weights or an explanation of the reported improvement.
It does not declare the comparison invalid, select an alternative regularizer, introduce coordinates or authorize experiments.

analytical_checks.status: completed partial descriptive audit of published control result files
analytical_checks.question: How large and consistent are gains over regularization in the publicly available subset?
assumptions: Treat each plain-text value as the reported independent-run test accuracy, without assuming that same-position trials across treatments are paired.
Keep conditions equally weighted for the descriptive mean; do not generalize the available18-condition subset to all24.

For L1, mean/median differences are+.166625/+.093008 percentage points; the range is-1.156250 to+.861111.
For L2, mean/median differences are+.262483/+.097155 percentage points; the range is-.326452 to+1.041668.

Six conditions per norm lack raw files in this snapshot: RNN MNIST and ManteTask, each with three rewiring methods. Thus the published24-condition counts and pooled surrogate p-values are not independently reproduced by this audit.
analytical_checks.relevance: The result is positive on average in the available controls but neither universal nor by itself evidence for our semantic layout. Effect size and experimental scope remain visible beside significance claims.

The experiment still combines multiple interventions and allows hidden roles to be learned.

analytical_checks.status: completed symbolic model-scope check
analytical_checks.question: Does the successful passive geometric wave model establish self-sustaining recurrence?
assumptions: Use Pang’s stated passive linear equation and Laplace–Beltrami eigenfunctions with Delta psi=-lambda psi, lambda>=0.
Consider neural field dynamics separately from the hemodynamic observation model.
derivation: Each mode obeys a_ddot+2*gamma*a_dot+gamma²*(1+r_s²*lambda)*a=gamma²*q.
With q=0 and lambda>0, roots are-gamma±i*gamma*r_s*sqrt(lambda). With lambda=0, the repeated-root solution is(A+B*t)*exp(-gamma*t). All homogeneous modes decay.
At gamma=116/s, the modal exponential envelope has time constant8.62ms. This is not a BOLD time constant, nor a statement that all distant response peaks occur within8.62ms.
Spatial eigenfunctions alone can also diagonalize other functions of the same Laplacian, including first-order diffusion. Fitting spatial maps does not identify the temporal operator.

In Maran’s geometry-only model, regeneration changes roots to-gamma±gamma*sqrt(nu0-r²*lambda); nu0=.756<1 still leaves every unforced geometric mode decaying. This statement is not extended without proof to all non-symmetric projection configurations.
analytical_checks.relevance: Noise-supported stationary activity, evoked waves and autonomous semantic cycles require separate evidence. A useful spatial reconstruction result cannot by itself supply the proposed SNN recurrent mechanism.
limits: No physiological damping parameter or wave equation is adopted for the application.
This is a derivation from published linear models, not a simulation or a claim that biological cortex lacks self-sustaining dynamics.

analytical_checks.status: completed construction and observable comparison
analytical_checks.question: Which changes are actually compared in the macroscale geometry/connectome claims?
assumptions: Keep source construction, fitted coefficient estimation, measurement filtering and error target separate.
Do not treat geometrically related kernels as identical at finite resolution.
derivation: Pang’s stochastic EDR uses Bernoulli edges with exp(-.12*d) and a binary normalized graph Laplacian. Vohryzek’s weighted baseline retains exp(-.12*d), while its augmented graph uses fitted exp(-.162*d) plus structural exceptions. These are multiple distinct changes.

An exponential exp(-lambda*d) and the small-time Gaussian heat-kernel form exp(-d_geodesic²/(4*t)) have different distance dependence. Surface metric, sampling, normalization and limiting procedure also matter; a shared locality intuition does not prove finite-graph equivalence.

Vohryzek selects structural exceptions from structural data, then evaluates a functionally selected strong-distant FC subset. This is not direct FC-based construction of those edges, but its reported advantage is specific to the evaluation target.

Pang’s whole/resting summaries, Vohryzek’s selected FC/task projections and Maran’s impulse/cosine/time-integrated responses answer different questions. A difference in their conclusions need not be a contradiction.

Mansour’s source code incorporates surface-informed smoothing into a weighted connectome. Thus a comparison involving it is not a clean removal of all geometric information; independent controls are needed to attribute improvements.
analytical_checks.relevance: Any future locality comparison for our model must preserve semantic assignments and expose exactly which graph, parameter, dynamics and observation change. These papers do not choose that comparison or its outcome for us.
limits: No source’s reported empirical result is invalidated solely by these distinctions.
No complete reanalysis of the datasets, model optimization or new topology is performed.

analytical_checks.status: completed exact linear-algebra scope check
analytical_checks.question: What does preserved task behavior establish when a learned sheet is followed by its pseudoinverse?
assumptions: Use the audited row-vector convention z=xW and x_hat=zW_plus.
Assume W has full row rank and exact arithmetic for the identity result; distinguish the square paper case from optional current-code shapes.
derivation: Full row rank gives W*W_plus=I, hence x_hat=x even though the coordinates of z can change substantially as W is trained.

With a frozen backbone and no intervention, the exact unperturbed task output therefore cannot distinguish such full-row-rank mappings. Rank loss, finite precision and pseudoinverse truncation can break this ideal identity; none was measured here.

The paper’s additive sheet intervention z->z+delta yields x_hat=x+delta*W_plus. A hypothetical zeroing mask D would instead yield x*W*D*W_plus; that is not the same intervention as the paper’s negative contrastive addition.
A compact selected region can thus provide a useful intervention basis without proving that its2D geometry is computationally necessary or that physical communication has become local.

Selected-unit ridge-regression brain predictivity need not remain identical under a general basis change: feature selection and regularization break the simple full-feature equivalence. This check does not dismiss the measured neural or intervention results.
analytical_checks.relevance: Preserving whole-model behavior is weaker than preserving each neuron’s assigned semantic role. An added learned basis or inverse projection would be a separate design choice, not a consequence of biological locality evidence.
limits: No transformation of the application’s semantic basis is proposed or performed.
This does not imply that learned recurrent responses are forbidden under fixed input/readout assignments; that compatibility remains an open design question.

analytical_checks.status: completed compression-mechanism interpretation
analytical_checks.question: Does topographic downsampling establish a geometric wiring advantage?
assumptions: Use the source’s linear-layer downsampling and interpolation-before-bias procedure.
Represent the fixed interpolation operation as a linear matrix U.
derivation: The compressed layer evaluates y=U*W_small*x+b. Its effective full matrix is U*W_small, whose rank is at most the reduced intermediate width.

The spatial layout specifies a structured interpolation subspace. Parameter reduction can therefore be understood as structured matrix factorization; it does not require physical neurons to inhabit that geometry.

Improved compressibility under the trained smoothness prior is still a real potential engineering benefit. Comparing against equally budgeted non-geometric factorizations would answer a distinct question from the reported baseline downsampling.

The source reports80% downsampling of targeted layers and about19% reduction of total parameters; full output width is restored by interpolation. Parameter counts, effective rank, actual sparse edges and hardware runtime are different quantities.
analytical_checks.relevance: Preserve the positive compression evidence while separating it from a claim that distance-biased sparse synapse selection is required for our model.
limits: No alternative compression experiment or CPU benchmark was run.
No factorized weights, interpolation arrays or new bookkeeping are introduced into the application.

analytical_checks.status: completed attention algebra and independent published-parameter mask calculation
analytical_checks.question: Does spatial query pooling necessarily identify physical local wiring?
assumptions: Isolate linear queries Q=XW_Q and keys K=XW_K with a fixed feature mask M.
For the numerical check use the public circular-mask definition on a 20x20 torus, matching the paper’s 400-channel IMDB setting; no author code is executed.
derivation: Q M K^T = X (W_Q M) W_K^T X^T. With full-rank M, W_Q maps bijectively to W_Q M, so the isolated bilinear attention family is unchanged; conditioning and optimization can still change.
With rank-deficient M, the effective bilinear form is rank-limited by M. Additional positivity, nonlinearities, local Q/K/V or output reweighting are not removed by this argument.
