For area fraction 0.1, the 20x20 circular toroidal mask has 37 neighbors including self and numerical rank 392/400. For 0.3 it has 121 neighbors and numerical rank 400/400. Nonzero spectral condition numbers are approximately 971.08 and 2171.26, respectively.

The Fourier-spectrum calculation uses a floating numerical-rank tolerance recorded in the artifact. Global Frobenius normalization does not change rank or condition number. These values are not a measurement of trained weights or finite-precision training dynamics.
The computation modifies learned feature-channel interactions and still attends across tokens. Its grid labels are not an inferred anatomical coordinate system for fixed semantic-axis populations.
analytical_checks.relevance: Separate useful optimization/representation biases from an anatomical or sparse-connection claim.
limits: No SNN mechanism or replacement semantic basis adopted.
Expressive-family equivalence is not equality of trained behavior, training speed or biological plausibility.

analytical_checks.status: completed alignment identifiability derivation
analytical_checks.question: Can PLS-SVD brain alignment identify the sheet placement of model features?
assumptions: Centered stimulus-by-feature matrix X and stimulus-by-brain-response matrix Y.
Fit PLS-SVD from X^T Y; compare an orthogonal feature change XQ, including any feature permutation.
derivation: If X^T Y = U S V^T, then (XQ)^T Y = Q^T U S V^T. Singular values are unchanged and model component scores satisfy XQ(Q^T U)=XU, up to sign or degenerate-subspace conventions.

Held-out component-score predictions therefore cannot distinguish spatial feature permutations when the fitted loading vectors transform with them. A separate spatial statistic or constraint supplies spatial information.

This matches LOC-099’s explicit non-topographic control: comparable component alignment can coexist with different spatial visualization. It does not negate the observed smoothness or model/brain predictive correspondence.

General invertible feature changes preserve unregularized linear spans but not necessarily PLS singular vectors or isotropic ridge penalties. The exact invariance claimed here is orthogonal/permutation invariance, not arbitrary transformation invariance.
analytical_checks.relevance: A robust representational alignment is insufficient to select a physical metric for the application’s semantic assignments.
limits: No claim that brain responses lack local organization.
No one-to-one neuron correspondence follows from a distributed voxel projection.

analytical_checks.status: completed expected-degree and placement-counterfactual analysis
analytical_checks.question: Can a neuron-count-driven map transition justify geometry at our fixed sparse budget?
assumptions: Independent uniform orientation preferences on[0,pi), the LOC-102 periodic pair-probability function, and no self-edges.
The extrapolation is diagnostic only: the source does not simulate our CC or assign semantics to Flash dimensions.
derivation: For p=a+b*|cos(delta_theta)|^(2*gamma), E[p]=a+b*Gamma(gamma+1/2)/(sqrt(pi)*Gamma(gamma+1)). Thus E[K]=(N-1)*E[p] when a and b are fixed.

With the figure’s a=0.1,b=0.2 and gamma0.1–0.3, mean pair probability is approximately0.246–0.277. A literal extrapolation to614400 neurons would require about151374–169961 partners per neuron on average, far beyond the J16 allocated mean upper bound182.75. The paper’s original population is much smaller.
The authors’ supporting function p=(a+b*f)/N instead makes E[K]=(1-1/N)*(a+b*E[f]), approximately constant with N. Their FigureS3 reports no visible map change from varying N alone in this control.

Therefore a large CC population does not itself establish a pinwheel/topography transition at a fixed bounded live degree. Selectivity, degree and noise still matter; the source does not prove a universal threshold applicable to our budget.

A post-hoc placement that leaves weights, graph and every state-update term unchanged cannot alter the mathematical trajectory of a model whose update does not read position. To affect dynamics, geometry must enter some additional operation, such as partner selection, delay, weight, input or observation. This is a conditional equivalence, not a recommendation to add any such operation.
analytical_checks.relevance: Separate feature-preserving placement and material wiring economy from claims of improved sparse recurrent dynamics.
limits: Allocated capacity is not measured live degree;182.75 is only an upper-bound average for the pending J16 candidate.
No MDS, XY simulation, SNN training or new application storage is implemented.

analytical_checks.status: Conditional exact counterexample for a historical source-code statistic; no biological result reanalysis
analytical_checks.question: Can core-seeded personalized PageRank distinguish core neurons even on a completely homogeneous graph?
assumptions: Complete directed graph withN vertices, no self-edges, identical outgoing transition weights andm designated core vertices.
Restart probability1-alpha distributed uniformly over the designated core set, as specified by the historical AUD-021 reset argument.
derivation: Stationarity gives r_i=alpha*(1-r_i)/(N-1)+(1-alpha)*v_i. Thus r_i=[alpha+(1-alpha)*(N-1)*v_i]/(N-1+alpha).
Noncore vertices havev_i=0; core vertices havev_i=1/m. The core/noncore ratio is1+(1-alpha)*(N-1)/(alpha*m), despite identical degrees and otherwise symmetric topology.
ForN=100,m=10,alpha=0.85, the ratio is2.7470588235294118. Every designated core outranks every noncore solely because of restart assignment.

Consequently this comparison alone is not independent evidence that designated cores occupy anatomically privileged convergence positions. A uniform-restart or suitable matched-label null addresses a different question.
limits: This is an algebraic counterexample, not an estimate of the actual MICrONS effect.
The final2025CodeOcean implementation has not been inspected; no claim is made that it retains the historical personalization.
Other structural/dynamic findings must be evaluated on their own evidence.

analytical_checks.status: Conditional resource-accounting and identifiability analysis; no addressing mechanism adopted
analytical_checks.question: Does a smaller molecular-address alphabet establish a cheaper or better computational connectivity representation?
assumptions: LOC-108 supplies a potential-neighbor relationH and a label functionf withc labels; the actual binary edgeA_ij equalsH_ij times a deterministic label-pair ruleB[f(i),f(j)].
derivation: A literal arbitrary labeling requires aboutN*log2(c) bits and an arbitrary directed label-pair rule requiresc^2 bits, in addition to describingH. The source’s counting expressionc^N*2^(c^2) reflects these two distinct terms.

Counting candidate descriptions is not a proof that every description is distinct or that a solution exists at the first-moment threshold. Greedy found label counts are feasible encodings, not certified minima.

IfH has a compact geometric or other generative description, reusing labels can economize developmental specification. IfH is separately stored as a large arbitrary graph, its description cost cannot be omitted from total storage.
The source’sD counts allowed partners before edge selection. ReplacingD with theJ16 allocated mean182.75, a neuron’s live incoming degree, or a capacity class is unjustified.

Our explicit source-ID and FP8-weight slots encode learned edges directly. Introducing a label code or implicit neighbor relation would be a separate representation and learning design choice, not a consequence of this biological encoding argument.
limits: No extra table, heap structure, runtime bookkeeping or new compression format is introduced.
A compact developmental generator can still be a useful inductive bias; the accounting does not prove geometry unhelpful.
The argument concerns binary connectivity specification, not task performance, weights, firing-state transitions or autonomous cycles.

analytical_checks.status: Completed empirical conditional coordinate-profile geometry diagnostic; no physical layout or representation change selected
analytical_checks.question: Do the measured Flash coordinate response profiles themselves have a faithful two-dimensional Euclidean correlation-distance representation?
assumptions: Use each of the5120 raw input coordinates as a response profile across127997 equally weighted ordinary vocabulary entries. Center and variance-normalize each profile for analysis only.
Define R as the measured coordinate correlation matrix and squared profile distance as2*(1-R_ij). Center this point set with J=I-11T/5120, giving Gram matrixG=J*R*J.
derivation: The spectral decomposition ofG gives the minimum-Frobenius-error positive-semidefinite rank-d Gram approximation. This is a global Gram-preservation criterion, not a task loss, local-neighborhood criterion or a biological observation.

MeasuredG has numerical rank5119, participation ratio661.2317, and two leading components retain0.02916837 of its trace. Those components retain0.309253 of squared Gram Frobenius energy, leaving relative Gram error0.831112.

The distinct trace and squared-energy percentages are not interchangeable. The two-dimensional trace fraction also equals the fraction of summed squared pair distances retained by this orthogonal projection, because that sum is proportional to the centered Gram trace.

A faithful exact Euclidean realization of these specific distances is therefore not two-dimensional. A deliberately distorted map or a different biological/functional relation can have a different purpose; this analysis does not test its utility.
limits: Raw input-coordinate profiles are not measured SNN neuron responses or biological tuning curves.
Equal vocabulary-type weighting is not corpus frequency, context, or temporal coactivity.
Centering and variance normalization are analytical choices, not accepted learning or encoding operations.
The result concerns this all-pairs distance/Gram preservation criterion only; local-neighborhood maps can have different objectives and biological geometry need not preserve these distances.
A useful geometric prior could distort these distances; this calculation neither supplies one nor proves none can help.
Signed population encoding and nonlinear conditional activation remain unspecified; negative populations are not modeled here.
No runtime arrays or additional application bookkeeping are proposed.

analytical_checks.status: Exact conditional operator counterexample; no biological or project simulation
analytical_checks.question: Does sharing geometric eigenmodes before graph postprocessing imply that the final adjacency shares those eigenmodes?
assumptions: Use the three-vertex path Laplacian L=[[1,-1,0],[-1,2,-1],[0,-1,1]] and static Green operator G=(I+L)^-1.
derivation: Exact rational inversion gives G=[[5/8,1/4,1/8],[1/4,1/2,1/4],[1/8,1/4,5/8]]. The commutator L*G-G*L is zero, as expected for this function of L.

For A obtained by setting only the diagonal of G to zero, L*A-A*L=[[0,-1/8,0],[1/8,0,1/8],[0,-1/8,0]], which is nonzero. All off-diagonal entries remain positive; no clipping or thresholding is needed for this counterexample.

Thus diagonal removal alone can change the eigenbasis. Further clipping and sparsification require their own analysis; final-graph modes and temporal poles cannot simply be read off the original geometric kernel.
limits: This establishes a logical limitation, not the magnitude of basis change in the authors’ cortical graphs and not a refutation of their anatomical predictive performance.
A static Green function is not itself a chosen recurrent neuronal update rule.

analytical_checks.status: Conditional matched-density interpretation; not a reproduction of source data
analytical_checks.question: How informative is75% empirical-edge recovery when model and empirical graphs have the same sparse edge count?
assumptions: Let M be possible undirected edges, both graphs have d*M edges, and t be recovered empirical-edge fraction.
derivation: Precision=recall=F1=t; false-positive rate=d*(1-t)/(1-d). An independently uniform graph at the same density has expected recall d.

Using the inspected demonstration density d=0.046 and reported preprint recovery t=0.75 illustratively gives FPR0.0120545073, balanced accuracy0.8689727463 and recovery16.30435times the random expectation.

This supports interpreting the reported recovery as substantial at that density. It does not identify which model component is responsible or establish that the demonstration settings exactly match the final publication.
limits: Degree/spatially constrained baselines are stricter than independent random edges; the source includes several such comparators.
Sparse-edge classification performance is not an autonomous-dynamics performance measure.

analytical_checks.status: Exact conditional null interpretation for independent-cascade cooperation
analytical_checks.question: Does faster average activation from two seed groups establish a cooperative nonlinear interaction?
assumptions: Each directed contact has a fixed Bernoulli success outcome for a coupled realization; activated neurons get one propagation opportunity and then remain refractory. Compare the same sampled graph and seed groups.
derivation: The independent-cascade process can be represented as shortest arrival in the sampled graph of successful edges. For a target, T(S1 union S2)=min(T(S1),T(S2)), allowing infinite times for unreachable targets.

Consequently E[min(T1,T2)]<=min(E[T1],E[T2]) whenever the expectations are finite. For independent T1,T2 each taking1or3 with equal probability, both single-seed mean times are2 but the joint mean is1.5.

A negative joint-minus-best-single mean arrival difference can therefore arise from ordinary redundant opportunity and extra seeds, without any supra-additive synaptic integration. This does not deny the usefulness of the source’s operational cooperation statistic.
limits: The identity concerns arrival, not competitive color assignment. Conditioning separately on successful activation can change the expectation comparison and must be checked before numerical application.
No author trajectories or project implementation reproduced; this is an analytical interpretation of the model class.

analytical_checks.status: Exact finite-activity bound for permanently refractory cascades
analytical_checks.question: Can the source’s three-state cascade maintain a nonzero steady active fraction?
assumptions: N finite neurons, each active for one step at most once, no recovery or additional neurons.
derivation: Let a_t be the active fraction. Since each neuron contributes at most one active neuron-step, sum_t a_t<=1 over the complete cascade.

Over T steps the mean active fraction is at most1/T; a fixed positive lower mean bound a_min is impossible for T>1/a_min. With no external reactivation, a nonempty active set also cannot persist for more thanN steps.
Graph cycles do not change this result because refractory vertices cannot be revisited. Sustained loops require different transition semantics, not merely more closed paths in the same graph.
limits: The bound applies to this source’s permanent-refractory rule, not biological neurons with recovery or our as-yet unspecified phase transitions. No accepted activity band or update rule is selected.

analytical_checks.status: Exact conditional analysis of signed diffusive Hopf coupling; not a proposed SNN rule
analytical_checks.question: Does a negative diffusive interaction simply suppress amplitude, or can it change which modes become self-active?
assumptions: Use the source model without noise, two identical nodes z1,z2 with intrinsic a<0, angular frequencyomega and symmetric couplingg. The two-dimensional complex oscillator state and cubic saturation are essential assumptions.
derivation: Linear growth at the zero state is a for the symmetric mode and a-2*g for the antisymmetric mode. The latter is enhanced when g is negative.

The subspace z2=-z1 is invariant. There, dz/dt=(a-2*g+i*omega)z-|z|^2*z, yielding a nonzero periodic orbit of amplitude sqrt(a-2*g) when a-2*g>0. With a=-0.02, threshold isg<-0.01; g=-0.02 gives amplitude sqrt(0.02), andg=-0.1 gives sqrt(0.18). This states existence and radial stability within the invariant subspace, not a full-network attractor classification.

Conversely, for any finite network with nonnegative diffusive couplings, no noise and uniformly negativea_i, at a node of maximal amplitude R, the radial derivative is bounded above by a_i*R-R^3 because neighboring amplitudes are no larger. Thus the maximum amplitude decays; apparent persistent oscillation in this setting requires drive/noise or a changed assumption.

Suppressing synchrony and suppressing all activity amplitudes are therefore different effects. Negative diffusive weights can favor differentiated modes while the cubic nonlinearity bounds amplitudes. The rotational i*omega term supplies oscillator structure; a signed one-variable rate graph does not inherit this result.
limits: This is a mathematical special case of the published equation, not a claim that the paper’s fitted networks operate in this particular regime.
No physical metric is needed for the two-node derivation, but it does not solve the application’s semantic learning or FP4 phase semantics.
The paper measures noisy macroscopic dynamics and a separate driven tanh reservoir; neither is replaced by this analysis.

analytical_checks.status: Conditional graph-denominator consistency calculation; unresolved source definitions
analytical_checks.question: Can the contact-density ratio and synaptic filling fraction be interpreted on the same simple-graph universe?
assumptions: Let C be undirected unique contact dyads, U undirected synaptic dyads, D directed synaptic edges, with the same n vertices and U contained in C. Then U<=D<=2U.
derivation: If filling p=U/C, the ratio of two undirected densities is C/U=1/p. If synaptic density is directed but contact density undirected, the ratio is2C/D, hence lies between1/p and2/p.
For p=0.0341 the corresponding range is29.3255–58.6510; for p=0.0281 it is35.5872–71.1744. The reported density ratios11.74 and3.853 fall below these ranges.

Therefore a change between directed and undirected counting alone cannot reconcile these numbers under the stated assumptions. Different vertex sets, pair subsets, edge multiplicities or definitions would need to be established from the queries before combination.
limits: This is not a finding of an erroneous biological result. It identifies assumptions that cannot all be used simultaneously for application sizing. No corrected ratio or inferred synaptic capacity is adopted.

analytical_checks.status: Exact three-variable linearized example, not a selected neural update rule
analytical_checks.question: Can global inhibitory feedback stabilize the total mode while leaving competition between groups unstable?
assumptions: Perturbations around an active operating point satisfy dx1=(a-1)x1+b*x2-c*y, dx2=b*x1+(a-1)x2-c*y, dy=e*(x1+x2)-d*y; c,d,e>0. Negative perturbations do not mean negative firing rates.
derivation: For difference q=x1-x2, dq=(a-b-1)q. Uniform inhibitory feedback cancels exactly. For m=(x1+x2)/2, [dm,dy] has matrix[[a+b-1,-c],[2e,-d]].
Choose a=1.2,b=0.1,c=e=d=1. The mean/inhibitory block has trace-0.7 and determinant1.7, hence both eigenvalues have negative real part. The difference mode instead grows at0.1.

This demonstrates why a control or measurement sensitive only to total activity can miss growing redistribution between groups. Saturation may later bound the trajectory but need not preserve a desired distributed semantic state.
limits: The example does not specify a physical metric, inhibitory cell population, controller, semantic grouping or application parameter. It is a local stability illustration, not a nonlinear attractor classification.

analytical_checks.status: Conditional check of printed Gaussian perturbation, not a replication of published simulations
analytical_checks.question: Does a deterministic column sign guarantee Dale-type signs after untruncated Gaussian perturbation?
assumptions: Read the source’s A_ij as an untruncated Gaussian with the reported variance; G=(H+epsilon*A)/sqrt(N). No undocumented clipping or rejection is assumed.
derivation: For an excitatory off-diagonal weight, P(G<0)=Phi(-mu_E/(epsilon*sigma_E)); for an inhibitory weight, P(G>0)=Phi(-abs(mu_I)/(epsilon*sigma_I)). Every nonzero epsilon gives nonzero wrong-sign probability.
At the reported epsilon=1 example parameters mu_E=.7,sigma_E²=.625,mu_I=-2.8,sigma_I²=2.5, these probabilities are approximately0.1879603 and0.0382907.

Both mean and deviation scale by1/sqrt(N), so increasingN does not reduce these per-edge probabilities. The deterministic epsilon=0 analysis remains sign constrained; the formula alone does not enforce that property for the random examples.
limits: Actual generated matrices and any unreported sampling restriction were not inspected. This distinction does not invalidate the deterministic periodic-orbit analysis or prove that the observed oscillations require wrong-sign edges.

analytical_checks.status: Logical identifiability check for proposed functional distance; no metric adopted
analytical_checks.question: When does a distance preference add information beyond the coactivity already used for learning?
assumptions: Suppose a proposal/retention score uses one scalar coactivity statisticC_ij and a distance constructed solely as d_ij=f(C_ij). Let the combined score beF(C_ij)*K(d_ij).
derivation: Substitution gives a single functionG(C_ij)=F(C_ij)*K(f(C_ij)). Under these assumptions the extra distance supplies a reweighting of the same evidence, not an independently grounded anatomical relation.
Such reweighting could still improve an objective through thresholding or regularization; the point is that an independent locality benefit has not been isolated.

If a distance instead uses broader histories, directed timing, graph neighborhoods, additional covariates or lossy dimensional reduction, the equivalence need not hold. The additional information or imposed constraint must then be identified and compared explicitly.
limits: Fixed semantic roles do not prevent learned response relationships. This check rejects neither coactivity-based learning nor future functional geometry; it prevents relabeling the same statistic as independent biological evidence.

analytical_checks.status: Exact finite Fourier counterexample; no application encoding or physical layout proposed
analytical_checks.question: Does a one- or two-dimensional physical support impose a matching bound on population response-covariance rank?
assumptions: Place n>2K sample cells at x_i=2*pi*i/n on a one-dimensional circle. For a uniform scalar stimulus theta, let r_i(theta)=r0+sum_{k=1..K} a_k*cos(k*(x_i-theta)), with nonzero a_k and r0>=sum(abs(a_k)).
derivation: Every response is nonnegative and smooth in both physical coordinate and stimulus. The centered covariance is C_ij=(1/2)*sum_k a_k²*cos(k*(x_i-x_j)).

Discrete sine and cosine vectors are orthogonal, each with squared normn/2. The2K nonzero eigenvalues are n*a_k²/4, each repeated twice. Thus covariance rank2K can be arbitrarily larger than the physical dimension1.
A numerical arithmetic check with n=17,K=5,a_k=1/k² and64 evenly spaced stimulus samples gives rank10, minimum response0.625 and maximum eigenvalue error1.78e-15 relative to the formula.

Consequently, failure to embed all response-profile distances exactly into2D does not prove that high-dimensional responses cannot be carried by neurons on a physical sheet. It rules out the particular distance-preserving identification being tested.
limits: This counterexample says nothing about a chosen learning law, memory quality, sparse recurrence or wiring efficiency. Applying these tuning functions to the model would be a new encoding decision, which is not proposed.

analytical_checks.status: Exact normalized-spectrum example
analytical_checks.question: Can participation ratio rise while the number of modes needed for75% variance falls?
assumptions: Compare sorted unit-trace spectra A=(3/5,2/45 repeated9times) and B=(1/4 repeated4times,0 repeated6times).
derivation: A has participation ratio1/sum(lambda²)=45/17≈2.6471 and requires5 modes to reach75% variance.
B has participation ratio4 and requires3 modes. Thus B is higher-dimensional by participation ratio and lower-dimensional by the75%-coverage count.
The metrics emphasize different spectral properties. An apparent disagreement between them is not by itself a numerical inconsistency, nor a basis for choosing an application dimension count.
limits: This example illustrates metric dependence; it is not a fit to either biological data or the Flash table.

analytical_checks.status: Exact limiting-covariance illustration of basis contamination
analytical_checks.question: Does unbiased cross-repeat covariance guarantee that variance measured in a noisy PCA basis equals the signal eigenvalues?
assumptions: Let signal covariance Cs=diag(1,0), independent additive-noise covariance Cn=[[1,1],[1,2]], and use eigenvectorsU of Cs+Cn as the projection basis. Both covariance matrices are positive semidefinite; Cn is positive definite.
derivation: Cs+Cn=[[2,1],[1,2]] has45-degree eigenvectors. In that basis diag(U^T*Cs*U)=(1/2,1/2), even though the true signal eigenvalues are(1,0). The trace is correct but the spectrum is not.

More generally, for any orthogonalU and positive semidefiniteCs, sum_i diag(U^T*Cs*U)_i²<=tr(Cs²), because the full squared Frobenius norm also includes off-diagonal entries. A participation ratio formed only from those diagonal projections is therefore at least the true covariance participation ratio.

This isolates the need to distinguish accurate covariance estimation from identification of the signal eigenbasis. It corresponds to the limiting issue discussed in the source’s cvPCA method, without claiming the same bias magnitude for its empirical recordings.
limits: Finite-sample cross-validation estimates have additional dependencies and can be negative; the inequality here concerns the exact limiting positive covariance. It does not undermine the noise-free finite-table Flash eigendecomposition.

analytical_checks.status: Exact conditional weight-sum calculation
analytical_checks.question: Does the mixed normalization in LOC-123 keep recurrent input strength fixed while distance changes?
assumptions: One target has d_local existing intraregional edges and d_external interregional edges, with local weight 1/m and external weight 1/(d_local+d_external), as printed in equation 2.
derivation: The incoming weight sum is d_local/m + d_external/(d_local+d_external). Holding d_local>0 fixed, its derivative with respect to d_external is d_local/(d_local+d_external)^2>0.

For m=100 and d_local=10, external degrees 0, 1, 10, 100 and 800 give sums 0.1, 0.190909, 0.6, 1.009091 and 1.087654. At fixed presynaptic rate this changes expected recurrent drive; spatially varying rates add further effects.

Normalization becomes approximately constant only when external degree already greatly exceeds local degree. Thus a range sweep that moves from nearly isolated regions to well-connected regions is not a pure geometry comparison.
limits: This is a conditional calculation, not a reproduction of the degree distribution or nonlinear simulation. The positive complexity result remains valid for the reported combined parameter manipulation.

analytical_checks.status: Exact Gaussian-complexity counterexample
analytical_checks.question: Does the covariance-based complexity used in LOC-123 necessarily become small as activity approaches synchrony?
assumptions: n stationary jointly Gaussian variables with unit variance and common correlation r in [0,1). Apply equation 12 to this covariance; natural logarithms are used.
derivation: Every k-variable principal submatrix has determinant (1-r)^(k-1)*(1+(k-1)*r). Substitute its log determinant into C_n=0.5*sum_{k=1}^{n-1}[log(det(C_k))-(k/n)*log(det(C_n))].

As r approaches 1, C_n=-(n-1)/4*log(1-r)+O(1), so the metric diverges rather than tending to zero. For n=9, r=0, 0.1, 0.5, 0.9, 0.99 and 0.999 give approximately 0, 0.17643, 1.79574, 5.42429, 10.10954 and 14.72250.

Each r<1 defines a valid nonsingular Gaussian distribution. Perfect synchrony itself is singular and the differential-entropy expression is undefined. A claim that this metric universally rewards a middle ground between independence and synchrony is therefore stronger than its definition supports.
limits: This does not contradict the paper's observed finite-parameter maximum for its particular simulations. It limits using that maximum or metric as an application acceptance criterion without separate checks on correlation, useful content and autonomous dynamics.

analytical_checks.status: Printed-equation consistency check; implementation unknown
analytical_checks.question: Can printed equation 3 of LOC-123 generate the stated excitatory firing from reset?
assumptions: Use the visually verified plus signs before nonnegative external/recurrent conductances, reversal V_E=3, resting/reset V_R=0 and threshold V_T=1. Let g(t)>=0 be their combined conductance.
derivation: The printed subthreshold equation reduces to tau*dv/dt=-v+g(t)*(v-3). At v=0 its derivative is -3*g(t)<=0, so a trajectory starting at reset cannot cross upward through zero to threshold under these terms.

For constant 0<g<1 the equilibrium is -3*g/(1-g)<0; for g>=1 the equation still drives negative from reset. Reversing the driving-force sign would provide the stated excitation, but that correction is not silently substituted into the source.
limits: Likely equation/sign inconsistency, not evidence of the simulation implementation. No code/data were supplied for verifying the implemented sign; do not infer that the reported network behavior was fabricated or reproduced by the printed equation.

analytical_checks.status: Algebraic interpretation of the released default FORCE update
analytical_checks.question: Does the task model in LOC-124 learn an arbitrary full recurrent matrix?
assumptions: Use the inspected notebook's unmasked fully connected setting and one-dimensional output. Its optimized recurrence update is u*ones(N,N), with u=P*h^T*error an N-by-1 vector. Standard arithmetic is assumed; finite-precision rounding can add tiny deviations.
derivation: Each update has the form u_t*1^T. Summing updates gives W(t)-W(0)=v(t)*1^T, of rank at most one, even though every matrix entry is marked trainable. This statement concerns the learned change, not the rank of the initial random matrix.

Output and recurrent P matrices start identically and receive the same h-dependent update. Their weight gradients use the same scalar error. With the zero-initialized output vector w, the idealized update path therefore gives W(t)=W(0)+w(t)*1^T.

Including the fixed feedback row b, the effective recurrent input is h*W(0)+(h*w)*(1^T+b). The learned contribution remains rank at most one. This can support meaningful computation and change sign-split graph metrics, but does not establish arbitrary independently learned synapses or a geometric layout.
limits: Applies to the released default class/settings, not all FORCE variants or unknown paper-generation versions. No training was rerun and no claim that task success is invalid. The result further separates the paper's computational evidence from its independently imposed spatial-sheet model.

analytical_checks.status: Exact pair-propensity calculation
analytical_checks.question: Can reciprocal-edge enrichment arise from a locality kernel even when the two directed edges are sampled independently?
assumptions: For a randomly selected unordered distinct pair, both directional probabilities equal a pair-specific p, and the two edge draws are independent conditional on p. Pair propensities vary, for example through distance. Let mu=E[p]>0.
derivation: The probability of both directed edges is E[p^2]=mu^2+Var(p). Conditional on one direction being present, the probability of the reverse is E[p^2]/mu=mu+Var(p)/mu.

A homogeneous independent-edge null with probability mu therefore underestimates reciprocity whenever pair propensities vary. This is not evidence that a rule explicitly detects reciprocal edges or applies a separate reciprocal reinforcement.

The same identity applies to symmetric heterogeneity generated by other pair properties. It helps explain one route by which geometry changes motifs, but it does not establish that geometry is the only route or prescribe a replacement rule.
limits: A degree-preserving configuration null is not identical to a homogeneous null. This identity explains a mechanism, not the exact enrichment ratio in AUD-027. Directed cell-type asymmetry requires a generalized E[p_ij*p_ji] calculation.

analytical_checks.status: Trade-off definition check
analytical_checks.question: Does the crossing of normalized path length and wiring cost define a universal optimal connection range?
assumptions: Let decreasing path-length curve L(c) and increasing geometric cost C(c) be separately divided by their observed maxima, as in LOC-125 figure 12.
derivation: The crossing solves L(c)/L_max=C(c)/C_max. It is a minimax optimum only for the specifically chosen objective max(L/L_max,C/C_max), under monotonicity and a feasible crossing.

A weighted-sum objective instead satisfies a*L'(c)+b*C'(c)=0 at an interior optimum; equality of normalized levels is not that condition. Other relative weights or constraints can select other ranges.

Changing the sampled range of c can change L_max or C_max and shift the crossing even when the underlying local curves remain unchanged. The reported c=4.87 therefore depends on normalization and sampled domain, not solely on a biological law.
limits: This preserves the genuine cost/path trade-off and numerical coincidence with the fitted widths. It limits transfer of the crossing to an application whose useful computation and hardware costs have not been defined.

analytical_checks.status: Conditional geometry-conversion check
analytical_checks.question: What assumptions are needed to extend the planar rule of LOC-125 to biological density and multiple layers?
assumptions: First consider a cubic lattice with density rho. Separately consider L identical parallel lattice layers, unit vertical spacing and an isotropic Gaussian probability with width c in all three directions.
derivation: rho^(-1/3) is the cubic-lattice spacing. Density alone does not fix the minimum pair distance for an arbitrary point arrangement: close pairs and compensating gaps can preserve density. Applying this spacing to real tissue adds a lattice/packing assumption.

For the three-dimensional Gaussian, a layer pair separated by h has its same-plane expected edge count multiplied by exp(-h^2/(2*c^2)). The total layer multiplier is S=sum_{h=-(L-1)}^{L-1}(L-|h|)*exp(-h^2/(2*c^2)), rather than L^2.

For L=20 and c=5, S=200.8306703 versus L^2=400, a ratio of 0.5020767. The paper's factor of 400 corresponds to treating every layer pair alike in the relevant lateral kernel; it is not the result of simply applying the same isotropic 3D distance decay.
limits: The paper's stack argument is an approximate consistency estimate, not a direct synapse census. A lateral-only or anisotropic kernel could use different scaling; this calculation does not select one or revise application memory sizing.

analytical_checks.status: Exact linear-system distinction
analytical_checks.question: Does stable continuous-time recurrence guarantee convergence of a sum over recurrent paths?
assumptions: Consider dr/dt=(W-I)r+h with one common time constant. This is a mathematical illustration, not an adopted neuronal update rule.
derivation: Asymptotic stability requires max Re(lambda(W))<1. The Neumann expansion (I-W)^(-1)=sum_{k>=0} W^k instead requires spectral radius rho(W)<1; the latter is stronger.

For W=[[0,-2],[2,-1]], the two eigenvalues are -1/2 +/- i*sqrt(15)/2, with modulus 2. The first column is excitatory and the second inhibitory. W-I has eigenvalues -3/2 +/- i*sqrt(15)/2 and is stable, but the path series does not converge.
The exact inverse is (I-W)^(-1)=[[2,-2],[2,1]]/6. Therefore failure of the path expansion does not mean absence of a well-defined small-signal steady response.
For heterogeneous time constants, the relevant dynamical matrix is T^(-1)(W-I). Conditions stated only in terms of W need their time-constant assumptions retained.
limits: This is not a stability guarantee for nonlinear spiking dynamics, delayed circuits or quantized updates. It explains why the weak-coupling interpretation of LOC-129 need not cover the strong-coupling cases of LOC-131.

analytical_checks.status: Independent finite-input-table sensitivity measurement
analytical_checks.question: How stable are Flash coordinate-correlation neighborhoods across different distributions of token pieces?
assumptions: Use the locally verified BF16 input table at deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 commit 1bae0e1088993b9b82de08f59de5be5a34e42170. Its full SHA256 was freshly checked before analysis.

Classify decoded ordinary token pieces by strict UTF-8 and Unicode spelling, stripping only boundary whitespace for classification. ASCII-letter-only and CJK-ideograph-only groups contain 64,054 and 35,185 token types. These are not language or semantic labels.

Within each group and the ordinary-token population, draw two disjoint 8,192-type samples with seed 2026102715. Center separately and compute all 13,104,640 distinct coordinate-pair Pearson correlations. No corpus-frequency weighting or context states are used.
Compare signed correlation maps and top-16 absolute-correlation neighborhoods. Sixteen is a descriptive rank cutoff, not a connection count or adopted metric.
derivation: Within ASCII-letter pieces, correlation between the two estimated correlation maps is 0.92920 and mean top-16 overlap is 48.40 percent. Corresponding CJK values are 0.92681 and 49.59 percent; uniform ordinary-token samples give 0.90357 and 42.52 percent.

Across the ASCII/CJK split pairs, map correlations range approximately 0.44347 to 0.44547 and top-16 overlap 4.92 to 5.02 percent. Differences therefore exceed the sampling sensitivity seen within these groups at the same sample size.

Independent uniform 16-neighbor sets among 5,119 candidates would overlap by 16/5119=0.31256 percent on average. The measured cross-group overlap remains above that baseline, so the result is not absence of shared structure.

This establishes conditionality of the measured coordinate relationships in this fixed input table. It does not tell whether any conditional relationship would improve recurrent learning, which distribution the business should prioritize, or how to assign physical positions.
limits: Absolute correlation includes anticorrelation. Population weights, script composition, tokenization and residual sampling error all affect the result. Four cross-group comparisons share samples and are not four independent experiments.
Fixed semantic role does not freeze a neuron’s learned recurrent response profile. No SNN activity or learned connectivity was measured here; no coordinate basis or layout was changed.

analytical_checks.status: Exact partial-observation identifiability example
analytical_checks.question: Do complete steady perturbation measurements within an observed excitatory population uniquely identify its direct recurrent connections?
assumptions: Partition a stable linear circuit into observed E and unobserved I populations. Perturb only E and assume I-W_II is invertible. This illustration does not choose cell types or a controller for the application.
derivation: Eliminating the unobserved population gives L_EE=[I-W_EE-W_EI*(I-W_II)^(-1)*W_IE]^(-1). Even exact E-to-E steady responses identify only the combined effective operator under these assumptions, not its direct and hidden-path factors separately.

For one E and one I unit, let W=[[a,-b],[c,-d]]. Then L_EE=1/[1-a+bc/(1+d)]. Both parameter sets (a,b,c,d)=(0.2,1,0.4,1) and (0.4,1,0.8,1) give L_EE=1 despite different direct excitation and inhibitory recruitment.

Both examples preserve column signs and continuous-time stability: W-I has positive determinant 2 and negative traces -2.8 and -2.6, respectively. Thus the ambiguity does not depend on choosing an unstable counterexample.

Additional interventions, observations or justified structural assumptions can narrow this ambiguity. The constrained biological models supply such assumptions explicitly; the inference must retain them rather than treating response similarity as a measured direct edge.
limits: This is a limited identifiability statement for partial steady-response measurements. It does not claim that all circuit properties are unidentifiable, that the cited models are wrong, or that transient/full-cell observations carry no further information.

analytical_checks.status: Exact interpretation of an audited quadratic objective
analytical_checks.question: Does the released FRID regularizer impose sparse synapses or distinguish sign-opposite functional roles?
assumptions: For fixed anchor traces H and input trace x, the audited solver minimizes ||H^T z-x||^2+alpha*||z||^2 subject to -1<=z_i<=1, with alpha>0. This is source interpretation, not an application algorithm.
derivation: The L2 penalty is smooth and does not generally set coefficients to zero. For H=I and every x_i=1/2, the unconstrained optimum is z_i=1/[2(1+alpha)], which lies strictly inside the box and is nonzero in every coordinate.

The feasible set is sign-symmetric and the optimum unique. Replacing x by -x replaces the optimum z by -z. Consequently abs(z) is identical for the two traces when the anchor dictionary is held fixed.

The final similarity representation therefore can intentionally group opponent activity profiles. It is not a signed, directed synaptic adjacency or a rule for merging the application’s positive/negative coordinate identities.
limits: Anchors themselves are data-dependent, and changing the dataset can change H. The sign identity concerns comparison within one fixed dictionary. The calculation does not negate useful functional clustering or claim that every empirical coefficient is nonzero.

analytical_checks.status: Exact finite-probability illustration
analytical_checks.question: Does replacing pairwise correlation with pairwise mutual information capture every nonlinear relation?
assumptions: Let X and Y be independent unbiased binary inputs; compare a gate output with one input and with the joint input pair. This is a conditional mathematical example, not a reconstruction of LOC-133 figure 1.
derivation: For Z=1-X, Pearson correlation is -1 and I(X;Z)=1 bit. Strong negative correlation is strong dependence, even though it is not positive coactivity.
For Z=X AND Y, correlation(X,Z)=1/sqrt(3) and I(X;Z)=h2(1/4)-1/2=0.311278 bits; joint input information I((X,Y);Z)=h2(1/4)=0.811278 bits.
For Z=X XOR Y, each individual input has zero correlation and zero mutual information with Z, whereas I((X,Y);Z)=1 bit. The dependence is available jointly and is missed by either pairwise measure.

Thus functional relationship, pairwise synchrony and jointly predictable context are distinct. Merely renaming an activity similarity as distance does not resolve which relationship the desired recurrent computation needs.
limits: Biased or dependent inputs change these numbers. No information estimator, multi-input learning rule, extra storage or revised encoder is selected. H-40’s coactivity-learning direction remains open at the temporal/contextual mechanism level.
analytical_checks.extension_2026_10_27: For independent fair J_t,K_t and I_(t+1)=J_t XOR K_t with independent receiver past, I(J_t;I_(t+1)|I_t)=I(K_t;I_(t+1)|I_t)=0, but I((J_t,K_t);I_(t+1)|I_t)=1bit. Therefore selecting only triples with two individually significant bivariate transfer-entropy edges excludes this pure joint dependency even with infinite data. This qualifies LOC161's selected analysis domain, not its detected associations.

analytical_checks.status: Exact stable fully observed counterexample
analytical_checks.question: Can zero-lag partial correlation miss direct dynamic coupling and retain an indirect pair even with infinite data and complete observation?
assumptions: Consider X_t=A X_(t-1)+epsilon_t with independent unit-covariance innovations and symmetric A=[[0,a,0],[a,0,b],[0,b,0]], where a^2+b^2<1. This is a mathematical process, not an SNN update proposal.
derivation: The stable stationary covariance is Sigma=sum_{k>=0}A^(2k)=(I-A^2)^(-1), as in the symmetric model of LOC-134. Its precision matrix is I-A^2.
The precision entries for directly coupled pairs (1,2) and (2,3) are zero. The unconnected endpoint pair has precision entry -ab and partial correlation ab/sqrt((1-a^2)*(1-b^2)).

For a=b=1/2, spectral radius(A)=sqrt(1/2)<1 and the endpoint partial correlation is 1/3, while both directly coupled pairs have zero partial correlation. This is a dynamical timing effect, not a finite-sample or hidden-node artifact.

Under the same fully observed linear/noise assumptions, lag-one covariance supplies additional information: Cov(X_t,X_(t-1))=A*Sigma. The counterexample therefore distinguishes a particular zero-lag statistic from a claim that connectivity is unknowable.
limits: Nonzero self-coupling, different sampling, nonlinearities, noise structure or lags change the result. Conditional reconstruction successes in LOC-136/137 remain valid within their evidence scope. Failure to infer direct anatomy does not imply that coactivity-based learning cannot serve a business objective.

analytical_checks.status: Exact scope consequence of a one-use population approximation
analytical_checks.question: Does successful passage through an arbitrarily long assembly chain demonstrate repeated autonomous cycling?
assumptions: Use the nonnegative population activity a_i(t) of LOC-138, with cumulative activation sum_t a_i(t) bounded by one because reset is omitted. This is the paper’s replay approximation, not an application update rule.
derivation: A positive periodic trajectory with period T and mass c=sum_{t=1}^T a_i(t)>0 would accumulate kc after k cycles. This violates the one-use bound for sufficiently large k.
An arbitrarily long open chain can keep moving to previously unused groups without violating that bound. Closing its graph alone does not supply recovery/reset dynamics or prove cyclic replay.

The spiking model includes reset/refractoriness but tests an open chain under ongoing baseline input. Its positive pulse-propagation result should be preserved separately from an untested repeated-loop claim.
limits: No reset/refractory rule, time constant, oscillator or cycle-length bound is chosen. The conclusion distinguishes evidence scopes; it is not an impossibility result for recurrent spiking networks.

analytical_checks.status: Exact conditional-probability calculation
analytical_checks.question: Can variable actual degree produce apparent connection association without spatial preference?
assumptions: A node has K actual edges chosen uniformly without replacement among n eligible partners; K varies across nodes. Compare two distinct eligible partners. The calculation applies to outgoing degree or, with arrows reversed, incoming degree. Allocation capacity is not substituted for actual degree.
derivation: Let mu=E[K]. The marginal edge probability is mu/n. Given an edge to one partner, the probability of an edge to another is E[K(K-1)]/((n-1)*mu).
The conditional probability exceeds the marginal exactly when Var(K)>mu*(1-mu/n). Heterogeneity can therefore create positive edge association with no metric or target-nearness preference.

For n=1000 and K equally 100 or 400, the marginal is 0.25 and the conditional probability is 0.339339, a ratio of 1.357357. For fixed K=250 the conditional is instead 249/999=0.249249, slightly below the same marginal.

LOC-140 explicitly compares a configuration control and finds spatially structured excess beyond this global contribution. That positive finding is retained; the calculation explains why the control matters.
limits: The application’s static class distribution bounds capacity, while training determines occupancy and actual in/out degrees. No degree law, target-selection rule or physical layout is inferred from this example.

analytical_checks.status: Independent algebraic check of a conditional clustering theorem
analytical_checks.question: What exactly is optimized by the covariance-block clustering argument in LOC-141?
assumptions: Consider N channels partitioned into blocks of n, unit variance, within-block correlation rho_l and between-block correlation rho_g, with 0<=rho_g<rho_l<1. A branch selects s<=n distinct channels with unit binary weights. This is the theorem’s latent/linearized model, not the nonlinear trained network or measured Flash embeddings.
derivation: If c_b selected channels fall in block b, the target variance is (1-rho_l)*s+rho_g*s^2+(rho_l-rho_g)*sum_b c_b^2.

Uniformly permuting a competing partition makes two distinct selected channels share a block with probability (n-1)/(N-1). Its expected variance is D_s=(1-rho_l)*s+rho_g*s^2+(rho_l-rho_g)*(s+s*(s-1)*(n-1)/(N-1)), independent of the selected input labels.

Moving from counts (s-1,1) to (s,0) increases the target/expected-competitor ratio by 2*(s-1)*(rho_l-rho_g)/D_s. This is positive, while the denominator grows with s, so the gap need not increase with synapse count.
For N=200,n=10,rho_l=.9,rho_g=.3, the gap is .452101 at s=2, .483597 at s=3, and .273818 at s=10. The explicit count dependence agrees with the restricted theorem.
The result identifies nonlinear integration of selected correlated inputs as a possible functional mechanism. It does not require numerical proximity of those input labels.
limits: This is a ratio against an expected random competitor, not an expectation of the ratio or a guarantee against each of three realized competitors. It does not establish universal optimality, biological learnability or recurrent stability. No dendritic subunit, coordinate remapping or training method is adopted.

analytical_checks.status: Hand-derived algorithm correspondence check; author code not executed
analytical_checks.question: Do the printed SGSG candidate-exclusion rule and the pinned released source necessarily generate the same graph family?
assumptions: Use a complete three-node base graph without self loops, source A, other nodes B and C, positive q allowing the event that B alone is selected on the first step, and unprotected spread. This isolates the exclusion rule; it is not an application graph proposal.
derivation: Under the printed rule, both B and C were tested on the first step. They are excluded from all subsequent candidate sets, so C cannot later become selected from this source.

In the released source, exclusion accumulates selected state, not all tested candidates. After B is selected and C rejected, B’s frontier can offer C again. C then has positive probability of being selected on the second step.

The events differ even without geometry, multiplicity or a large dataset. Separately, clipping frontier multiplicity to one removes the printed multiplicity weighting when candidates are reachable through different numbers of frontier nodes.
limits: This identifies a formalism/release mismatch to reconcile, not a measured error in published connectome fits or a refutation of anatomical locality. The supplement and exact figure-generation notebook paths have not yet been fully audited.

analytical_checks.status: Independent finite-grid arithmetic and regularization identity; no training or application geometry selected
analytical_checks.question: How does the released raw-grid coordinate scale alter the distance penalty relative to the normalized real-coordinate condition?
assumptions: Use only the three grid shapes printed in the source paper and the released coordinate-construction formula. Actual MICrONS coordinate arrays are not loaded.
For mean-cost comparisons use equal absolute off-diagonal weights; learned weighted costs need not follow the unweighted mean.
derivation: For a global scaling D→cD, lambda*sum(abs(W)*D) becomes the original penalty with coefficient c*lambda. The same identity holds with an unchanged communicability multiplier.
For distinct pairs in an nx×ny×nz integer grid, mean squared distance is N/(N−1)*sum(n_axis²−1)/6. Exact pair enumeration agrees with this formula.

The312-node grid has mean distance6.5746004 and maximum16.3095064. Any two real-coordinate points after axis normalization have distance at most sqrt(3), so its grid mean exceeds even that universal real-coordinate upper bound by3.7958473.
Normalizing that same grid to[0,1] per axis gives mean0.8713130, a7.5456241-fold change. Corresponding raw/normalized mean ratios are3.5203324 for70nodes and5.1133664 for160nodes.
Axis-wise normalization also changes anisotropy; it is not generally a uniform change of physical units. Matching a mean penalty alone would still not isolate all geometric effects.
limits: These calculations identify a concrete control difference, not the fraction of reported accuracy gain it explains. No model is retrained and no performance correction is asserted.
This is not an application distance proposal. The positive study warrants a matched-scale comparison before treating geometry as the isolated cause.

analytical_checks.status: Exact matrix relabeling argument; no graph prior selected
analytical_checks.question: Does joint row/column permutation test whether only the marginal weight distribution matters?
assumptions: Let P be a permutation matrix and Wprime=P W P^T, matching the released W! construction.
derivation: Wprime^k=P W^k P^T for every positive integer k. Eigenvalues, weighted cycles and graph structure up to labels are preserved, along with the weight histogram.
For nonnegative row-strength-normalized communicability, Sprime=P S P^T and Cprime=P C P^T. Flattening and sorting Cprime yields exactly the same value distribution as C.

With the physical distance matrix held fixed, Wprime breaks the original graph-to-position assignment while retaining graph organization. A successful W! control therefore argues against requiring that exact assignment, but does not prove a weight histogram alone is sufficient.
The paper’s separate ECDF-resampling comparison addresses a different hypothesis and must be retained rather than conflated with node permutation.
limits: This argument does not reproduce trained performance or show that anatomy never helps. It does not authorize relabeling semantic meanings, changing the embedding basis or assigning new coordinates.

analytical_checks.status: Observable identity and counterexample; no event detector or acceptance metric selected
analytical_checks.question: Does matching total assembly firing to a stimulus prior establish matching event visit frequencies?
assumptions: Partition an assembly’s spikes over an observation interval into identified events and any background. Event identification itself remains unspecified for the application.
derivation: For assembly i, integrated activity equals the sum of spike masses of its events plus background. With event frequency nu_i and average event spike mass m_i, the long-run total firing rate is A_i=nu_i*m_i+b_i.

Therefore A_i/A_j=nu_i/nu_j requires equal event masses and appropriately controlled background. Event mass can change with assembly size, rate per cell and duration, all of which are separate variables.

Two assemblies can have identical visit frequencies but a2:1 activity ratio if one recruits twice as many equally active cells per event. Conversely identical activity ratios can conceal different visit counts and durations.

LOC-151 deliberately uses total population firing, and its figures show that size and per-cell rate both contribute. This is a valid coding observable, but it cannot alone certify application loop timing or transition order.
limits: This does not refute neural sampling under an explicitly activity-weighted representation. It identifies a measurement distinction that must remain open until the business observable is chosen.

analytical_checks.status: Exact literal-equation/source comparison; no author model executed or silently repaired
analytical_checks.question: Do the published transfer function and the released sample implement the same firing response?
assumptions: Use printed equations5–8 with g=3,beta0=5,theta0=1,phi0=50Hz and positive h after its maximum-trace update. That update implies u/h<=1 in the ideal equation.
derivation: The printed response reduces to50/(1+exp(15*(3-u/h)))Hz. At u/h<=1 its upper bound is4.6788114844e-12Hz. Even500 independent cells at that bound have a mean waiting time of approximately13.55years for one spike.
The pinned sample instead gives50/(1+exp(5*(1-3*u/h)))Hz. At u/h=0 it gives0.33464255Hz, at1/3 it gives25Hz, and at1 it gives49.99773Hz.

The difference is a threshold/gain placement discrepancy, not roundoff or a choice of milliseconds. The printed literal response cannot account for the displayed active rasters under the stated maximum-trace relation.

The author code provides a plausible intended operational response, but replacing the printed equation would be an interpretation requiring explicit provenance. The source and paper remain separately identified.
limits: The event-wait calculation is a bound under the stated ideal update, not a simulation of the published network. It does not show that the authors actually ran the printed literal equation or invalidate the numerical phenomenon.

analytical_checks.status: Conditional-estimator identity; no application event detector selected
analytical_checks.question: Does a row-normalized short-window transition matrix establish complete or accurately timed replay?
assumptions: For a simplified fully identified event chain let P_ij be the true next-state probability and q_ij the probability that the transition passes a specified timing/detection filter. Ignore ambiguous overlapping detections for this identity.
derivation: Accepted-count row normalization estimates Q_ij=P_ij*q_ij/sum_k(P_ik*q_ik), not necessarily P_ij.

If q_ij is the same for every successor of a given source, Q=P even if only1% of all transitions are retained. Good conditional probabilities can coexist with poor event coverage or very long silent intervals.

If two true successors each have probability1/2 but pass with probabilities0.9 and0.1, the accepted transition probabilities become0.9 and0.1. A short selection window can therefore change apparent probabilities when delay distributions differ by successor.

LOC-152 reports useful switching behavior, but its threshold/window definition and AUD-038’s additional selection conditions must accompany its probability claim. Coverage, dwell time, waiting time and ordering are distinct observables.
limits: This identity does not demonstrate that the paper’s actual estimates are biased, nor does it invalidate the chosen conditional observable. It specifies which additional information is needed before equating that observable with unrestricted application replay.

analytical_checks.status: Exact Gaussian-moment counterexample with independent quadrature; no representation selected
analytical_checks.question: Does a one-dimensional activation subspace imply an exactly one-dimensional linear firing-rate subspace after a nonlinear response?
assumptions: Let Z be standard Gaussian, activation x=kappa*Z, and rate r=1+tanh(x). Consider the fixed population axis w=H3(Z)=Z^3-3Z, which is not jointly Gaussian with Z.
derivation: Gaussian moments give E[w]=0 and E[w*Z]=E[Z^4]-3E[Z^2]=0, so w is orthogonal to both the global and activation axes.
Nevertheless E[w*r]=E[(Z^3-3Z)*tanh(kappa*Z)]=-2*kappa^3+O(kappa^5), because the linear term vanishes and E[(Z^3-3Z)*Z^3]=6.

Independent Simpson integration gives -0.00192324334 at kappa0.1 and -0.124792968 at kappa0.5. Thus a nonlinear firing-rate component can lie outside the activation axis even though the intrinsic latent variable remains one-dimensional.

LOC-153 explicitly restricts its Gaussian projection argument and describes dominant low-dimensional geometry. This counterexample prevents extending that argument to arbitrary axes or exact firing-covariance rank; it does not contradict the reported dominant-mode result.
limits: No biological coordinate map, application dimension reduction, encoder or neural simulation is introduced. Intrinsic manifold dimension, linear covariance rank and physical support dimension remain distinct.

analytical_checks.status: Special-case mean-field derivation and scalar quadrature; constructive example, not a learning prescription
analytical_checks.question: Can recurrent pattern circulation coexist with a constant population mean without assigning physical positions?
assumptions: Use the infinite-N Gaussian rank-two rate reduction with isotropic unit-variance output vectors, zero-offset response1+tanh, overlap matrix[[sigma,-omega],[omega,sigma]], and time constant tau. These are analytical assumptions, not application choices.
derivation: Let kappa=(r*cos(theta),r*sin(theta)) and F(r)=E[sech^2(r*Z)] for standard Gaussian Z. The reduced equations are tau*dr/dt=(-1+sigma*F(r))*r and tau*dtheta/dt=omega*F(r).
F decreases continuously from1 to0. For sigma>1 there is a unique positive radius r* with F(r*)=1/sigma, with negative radial linearization sigma*r*Fprime(r*)/tau.

If omega is nonzero, that radius supports a stable periodic orbit with angular speed omega/(sigma*tau). If omega=0, the same radius is instead a continuum of fixed points in this ideal isotropic limit.
For every radius and phase, symmetry gives mean rate E[1+tanh(r*Z)]=1. Constant mean therefore permits either circulation or settling; it does not distinguish them.

Using sigma2,omega0.8,tau0.1seconds yields r*=1.337108896, radial rate about-7.17055/second, and period1.570796327seconds. These are independent mean-field calculations using the paper’s illustrative rate overlap/time parameters, not a rerun of its spiking network.
limits: A constant mean firing rate is not the application’s phase-specific activation fraction. The example establishes possibility, not semantic sequence content, learning, finite-size robustness, quantization or sparse scalability. No physical topology or new runtime state is selected.

analytical_checks.status: Exact state-aggregation argument; no hidden-cell allocation or encoding selected
analytical_checks.question: Can a fixed semantic observation map coexist with context-dependent successors even when the complete neural state is Markovian?
assumptions: Let a complete internal state S follow a Markov transition matrix P. A fixed observation map assigns each internal state to an observable class, represented by blocks B_a. This is a logical example, not a proposed application decoder.
derivation: Conditional on a particular internal state s in B_a, the next observed class b has probability sum over t in B_b of P_st.

If that block-sum is identical for all s in B_a, the next-class probability is independent of the history-dependent mixture of internal states within B_a. This condition makes the observed process Markov for every initial internal distribution.

If the block-sums differ, two histories can give different next-class probabilities despite the same current observed class. Equality for every possible initial internal distribution would require equal block-sums, as seen by concentrating the initial distribution on either internal state.

For the deterministic internal cycle B→A1→C→A2→B with fixed observations A1,A2→A, the observed sequence is B,A,C,A,B. After observed A, the successor is C when the predecessor was B and B when the predecessor was C. The observation map is unchanged while context changes the successor.

Thus fixed semantic roles do not logically require fixed context-free transition behavior. Conversely, successful first-order replay of disjoint whole-state assemblies does not already demonstrate higher-order behavior of a shared semantic observation.
limits: The argument does not establish which existing FP4 states, neuronal subpopulations or temporal traces can carry the needed context, nor whether the desired learning dynamics will discover it. No new hidden neurons, physical layout or metadata allocation is authorized.

analytical_checks.status: independent-algebra-checked
analytical_checks.question: Does mixed global/local rate homeostasis preserve heterogeneous deterministic stationary rates?
analytical_checks.assumptions: The visually checked LOC157 Eq11, fixed inputs, positive finite rates, alpha∈[0,1], unbounded/interior thresholds and a genuine deterministic fixed point. No stochastic averaging, clipping or extra state is silently included.
derivation: Let tau*dtheta_i/dt=(1-alpha)(1-r0/r_i)+alpha(1-r0/rbar). Subtract stationary equations i,j. For alpha<1 and r0>0, r_i=r_j. The common equation then requires all rates=r0. At alpha=1 only rbar=r0 is required and threshold differences are unchanged.

For identical local response slopes dr_i/dtheta_i=-g<0 near that homogeneous point, the threshold Jacobian is -g/(tau*r0)*[(1-alpha)I+alpha*11ᵀ/N]. The population mode relaxes at g/(tau*r0); each zero-sum contrast mode relaxes at(1-alpha)g/(tau*r0).
Thus alpha0.8 slows contrast relaxation fivefold relative to the mean, and alpha0.99 one-hundredfold. Finite-time heterogeneity and a stationary heterogeneous manifold are different claims.
limits: This is not a proof that the full noisy spatial network loses all heterogeneity, nor a quantitative correction of its results. Threshold bounds, heterogeneous local gains, input changes and nonlinear NO production change the assumptions. The distinction is useful for evaluating any claimed population controller, not a controller proposal.

analytical_checks.status: independent-linear-mode-derivation
analytical_checks.question: What functional effect can diffusive feedback have beyond anatomical nearness?
analytical_checks.assumptions: Illustrative homogeneous continuum linearization: dc/dt=D∇²c-lambda*c+eta*delta_r; dtheta/dt=kappa*c; delta_r=-g*theta; positive D,lambda,eta,kappa,g. This is not a reproduction of LOC157's nonlinear noisy model.
derivation: For a Fourier mode with wavenumber k, the characteristic polynomial is s²+(lambda+D*k²)s+kappa*eta*g=0. All finite modes are stable in this simplified no-delay system.

At large lambda+D*k² the slow root is approximately -kappa*eta*g/(lambda+D*k²). Diffusion therefore weakens rapid correction of fine-scale contrasts relative to a population mode while still acting on them at finite k.

This exposes a temporal/mode-selective regulatory effect, rather than a generic assertion that short connections are computationally better. A physical wavenumber exists only in the source continuum, not among semantic coordinate labels.
limits: No coordinate assignment, alternate graph diffusion, physiological parameter estimate, CC activity band or implementation is selected. Delays, recurrent transfer and boundaries can change the stability calculation.

analytical_checks.status: independent-local-derivative-argument
analytical_checks.question: Can an unconditioned denoiser preserve every valid dense vector and contract every perturbation?
analytical_checks.assumptions: A differentiable deterministic map F:R^D→R^D, exact preservation F(x)=x for all x in an open valid-signal set. This is a conditional mathematical statement, not an assumption that all Flash vectors fill an open set.
derivation: For any interior x and direction v, differentiate F(x+tv)=x+tv at t=0: DF(x)v=v. Hence DF(x)=I and arbitrarily small perturbations in those directions cannot be contracted to first order while preserving every signal exactly.

If valid signals lie on a smooth lower-dimensional manifold, identity is required only along its tangent; contraction in normal directions may coexist with local signal preservation. For a finite codebook, neighborhoods around separate codewords can contract without this open-set restriction.

Thus denoising needs a specified signal/noise distinction, distribution, context or coding prior. The one-active-channel and discretized-scalar tasks in LOC160 supply such structure. An arbitrary coordinate merely being weak does not establish that it is noise.
limits: The real embedding table is finite and may have exploitable structure even with high covariance rank. No impossibility claim for semantic denoising, physical geometry, new encoding or specific denoiser follows.

analytical_checks.status: independent-probability-feasibility-check
analytical_checks.question: How does fixed edge density constrain modular projection probabilities?
analytical_checks.assumptions: A fraction q of all candidate ordered pairs is classed as within corresponding maps; between-map probability p0=(1-m)pc; all edges are simple Bernoulli opportunities. This mirrors the elementary density accounting in LOC160AppendixA, not a new application topology.
derivation: Overall density sigma=pc*q+p0*(1-q)=pc*[1-m*(1-q)]. Therefore pc=sigma/[1-m*(1-q)] and pc<=1 requires m<=(1-sigma)/(1-q), subject to0<=m<=1.
For Nc disjoint equal maps of fraction d on both ends, q=Nc*d². At m=1, feasibility requires d>=sqrt(sigma/Nc), matching the visually checked published square-root equation.
For sigma0.075,Nc10,d0.01, m_max=0.9259259. The Figure6b plotted range to0.92 remains below this bound; no invalid-probability claim is justified from the small-map panel alone.
limits: Overlapping maps require the appropriate distinct-pair count; multapses and fixed-indegree sampling use different distributions. Slot allocation does not determine live edge density or map membership. No parameter is transferred to the CC.

analytical_checks.status: independent-conditional-nearest-spike-drift-calculation
analytical_checks.question: Does a fixed forgetting offset imply one universal memory-decay time under asynchronous firing?
analytical_checks.assumptions: Two independent stationary Poisson spike trains of rates ri,rj; updates at either endpoint use the other endpoint's last spike, as in the inspected nearest-spike convention. Consider a weight away from soft bounds, infinitesimal learning and no feedback of weight on the prescribed spike rates. This is not a reproduction of LOC163's recurrent network.
derivation: The mean kernel contribution per unit time is ri*rj*[integral_0^infinity exp(-rj*t)Lambda(t)dt + integral_0^infinity exp(-ri*t)Lambda(-t)dt]. A constant -f contributes -(ri+rj)*f, not a decay rate determined by f alone.

For equal r=2Hz and the printed excitatory amplitudes5.296/2.949 and20/50ms constants, the mean non-forgetting kernel per endpoint event is0.0177870553 using base e, and0.0297797268 using the archived base2function. The event rate is4Hz in this continuous independent case.

At M2,f0.1, mean drift divided by learning rate is-0.328851779/s for the printed kernel and-0.280881093/s for the code kernel. The linear time to cancel one exactly coincident event of amplitude2.247 is6.8329s or7.9998s, respectively, under these assumptions.

At M10,f0.02, the same fixed-rate calculation gives drift-0.008851779/s for the printed kernel but+0.039118907/s for base2. Thus constant offset scaling does not by itself guarantee net decay between recalled events.

For2Hz independent trains, the probability that the other last spike is more than0.5s old is exp(-1)=0.367879. Independence is not equivalent to every update lying beyond the timing window; this is why the supplementary far-separated-spike estimate and this calculation answer different questions.
limits: Correlations, rate heterogeneity, weight saturation, finite integration, simultaneous-event conventions and recurrent feedback alter these figures. They neither falsify the published finite-network recall examples nor estimate actual application retention. No forgetting law or timescale is selected.

analytical_checks.status: conditional-rate-estimator-timescale-calculation
analytical_checks.question: When can an exponential spike trace stand in for a firing rate?
analytical_checks.assumptions: Stationary Poisson spikes of rate r, unit-jump exponential trace R with decay tau, and normalized estimator R/tau; equations independently obtained by integrating the kernel and its square.
derivation: E[R]=r*tau and Var[R]=r*tau/2, so E[R/tau]=r, Var[R/tau]=r/(2*tau), and CV=1/sqrt(2*r*tau). This agrees with the visually checked LOC164formula.
At2Hz and tau0.1s, CV=sqrt(2.5)=1.5811. Requiring illustrative CV<=0.1 at the same rate requires tau>=25s; this is an arithmetic example, not a proposed threshold.

The expected response to a rate step relaxes with time constant tau. Reducing single-cell rate-estimation noise therefore delays tracking; a reliable slow rate statistic is not an interchangeable representation of rapid temporal coactivity.
limits: Non-Poisson spiking, correlations, bursts, multiple traces and averaging across cells change the tradeoff. No trace representation, extra state, timing window or rate target is selected.

analytical_checks.status: conditional-compensating-weight-counterexample
analytical_checks.question: Do smaller weights at highly active receiving neurons necessarily cancel the effect of more incoming connections?
analytical_checks.assumptions: Illustrative noiseless feedforward rate neuron, K equal-rate independent inputs r, zero-threshold linear response nu=sum_j w_j*r, and the positive equilibrium of a simplified Oja-like rule w_j=g0*r/nu. This isolates algebra; it is not the spiking mean-field model of LOC164.
derivation: Self-consistency gives nu=g0*K*r^2/nu, hence nu=r*sqrt(g0*K) and w_j=sqrt(g0/K). Weights decrease with K while the receiving rate still increases as sqrt(K).

With positive threshold theta and an active output, nu^2+theta*nu=g0*K*r^2; the positive root still increases with K. Weight attenuation alone is therefore insufficient to claim equal activation propensity.

This leaves the earlier biological plausibility direction intact: compensation can be effective, but its achieved gain and fluctuation behavior depend on the rule and operating regime, not on the allocated capacity class.
limits: No recurrent stability, noise tolerance, saturation, capacity utilization or universal inverse-degree exponent follows. Weight scaling remains a training question.

analytical_checks.status: exact-graph-and-linear-response-counterexample
analytical_checks.question: Do matched degree and two-edge motif counts determine the recurrent response of fixed semantic identities?
analytical_checks.assumptions: Compare a directed12-cycle with four disjoint directed3-cycles on the same12labels. Every edge has weight w with0<w<1; continuous linear dynamics are r_dot=-r+w*A*r+u. These small graphs are counterexamples, not candidate CC topologies.
derivation: Both graphs have one incoming and one outgoing edge per cell,12nonbacktracking directed two-edge paths, zero reciprocal pairs, and zero convergent/divergent pairs of distinct edges. Degree and these second-order motif counts agree.
For uniform input u=1, both have stationary response r=1/(1-w) at every cell. Their response to a localized input differs because the walks revisit the source after3or12steps.
The self-response gain is1/(1-w^L) for cycle lengthL. Atw0.8, it is2.0491803forL3 and1.0737903forL12, despite the same uniform gain5. Third- and higher-order path structure distinguishes the graphs.

All eigenvalues of w*A have real part<=w<1, so both continuous systems are stable. The example separates useful higher-order path identity from average response; it does not demonstrate nondecaying autonomous cycles.
limits: No physical arrangement is used or inferred. Matching a finite list of graph statistics is insufficient in general, but this does not invalidate ensemble-specific approximations in LOC165. No application degree or cycle length is selected.

analytical_checks.status: exact-degree-motif-accounting-and-scaling-check
analytical_checks.question: What does chain enrichment establish about degree tails and network-size instability?
analytical_checks.assumptions: A finite simple directed graph without autapses; sample distinct ordered endpoints i,j,k uniformly. Let mu be mean incoming/outgoing degree, D=mean_j(Kin_j*Kout_j), and R=mean reciprocal-neighbor count per cell. This is unweighted graph accounting, not the full typed weighted model.
derivation: Marginal edge probability p=mu/(N-1). The joint nonbacktracking chain probability is q=(D-R)/((N-1)*(N-2)), because each intermediate cell contributes Kin*Kout minus reciprocal returns. The edge correlation is(q-p^2)/(p*(1-p)).

Take100cells in two50cell groups: each cell in one group connects to the next two cells cyclically, and each in the other to the next four. This mathematical construction has no reciprocal edges, degrees only2or4, mu3,D10,R0, and positive chain correlation0.0038265306. Thus chain enrichment does not logically require a heavy-tailed or power-law degree distribution.

With fixed mu,D,R as N increases, the correlation scales as(D-R-mu^2)/(mu*N)+O(N^-2). Holding a nonzero chain correlation fixed while enlarging N is a different graph family. The fixed-count regime in LOC165 explicitly avoids this growth assumption.

For the paper's illustrative real outliers lambda_plus=(lambda0+sqrt(lambda0^2+4*Delta^2))/2 withlambda0<=0, the outlier condition lambda_plus<1 is equivalent toDelta^2<1-lambda0. Size-independent outliers avoid size-driven growth but still require acceptable parameter values and a stable spectral bulk.
limits: Actual degree and typed weight moments are not supplied by reserved slots. The proof uses indexes only to specify a counterexample, not to assign semantic distance. It neither fixes a degree law nor adopts a motif constraint.

analytical_checks.status: exact-steady-response-versus-temporal-response-counterexample
analytical_checks.question: Can an effective interaction preserve stationary response while losing oscillatory temporal behavior?
analytical_checks.assumptions: Two linear deviation variables satisfy x_dot=-x+2y+u and y_dot=-2x-y. Compare a one-variable reduction x_dot=-5x+u. Deviations may be signed around a positive baseline; no cell type or hidden state is proposed for the application.
derivation: The full matrix has eigenvalues-1+2i and-1-2i. Eliminating y in the Laplace domain gives H(s)=X/U=(s+1)/((s+1)^2+4).

Both the full system and the reduction have stationary gainH(0)=1/5. Their impulse responses are respectively exp(-t)*cos(2t) and exp(-5t), so one has damped sign-changing temporal structure and the other does not.

More generally, eliminating a coupled state produces a frequency-dependent interaction. Replacing it by its zero-frequency value need not preserve timings or sequences even when the stationary gain agrees.
limits: This is a stable linear example, not autonomous persistent cycling or a proposed additional state array. It illustrates LOC165's explicit distinction between steady effective connectivity and transient dynamics.

analytical_checks.status: exact-local-quantization-calculation
analytical_checks.question: What does ideal stochastic rounding establish for small online weight updates?
